SLE.short: The justice minister said in September 2026 that no specific AI legislation has been enacted; no draft is named.
SLE.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Sierra Leone has no law on AI. The attorney-general and justice minister told a UNESCO meeting in Riyadh on 16 September 2026 that the country has established a position on AI but has not yet enacted specific AI legislation. The report of his remarks names no bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI, and no date by which one is to be written.

General AI law and the law applied. With no specific AI legislation enacted by September 2026, there is no general AI law to apply. The minister set out a national position on AI to UNESCO without naming a law to carry it, and the report gives no account of what that position requires of anyone. No rule for one sector or one use that names AI is recorded.

Not found.

SOM.short: A May 2026 analysis reports Somalia has no national AI law and no dedicated AI legislation; no source found says whether any draft exists.
SOM.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Somalia has no binding rule on AI in force. Ecofin Agency, writing on 17 July 2026 about the launch of a university AI center, cites an analysis published in May 2026 that reports Somalia has no national AI law. The same report says the country has no dedicated AI legislation. Nothing found records a draft, a bill or a decree on AI, whether published, out for consultation or before cabinet or parliament, so the position reported is that no rule on AI exists at the national level at all, and none is in preparation in any source found.

General AI law and the law applied. With no law on AI, there is no general AI law that applies across sectors, and none has been applied. The nearest fact held is the May 2026 analysis reported by Ecofin Agency, which states that Somalia has no national AI law and no dedicated AI legislation. No regulation or order has been made, and no body has registered, licensed, decided or penalised under such a law.

Not found. Nothing found says whether a sector law or a draft on AI exists, or whether any source later than May 2026 changes the position reported.

SSD.short: In 2025 a cybercrimes bill carried proposed AI provisions; no source found says whether any binding AI rule is in force.
SSD.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. No binding rule on AI is in force in South Sudan; a draft carries some. Digital Rights Frontlines reported on 22 October 2025 that the Cybercrimes and Computer Misuse Bill 2024, which had not yet passed, contains proposed AI provisions. The bill regulates AI among other matters, which makes it a draft of a rule on AI.

General AI law and the law applied. No law on AI itself is recorded for South Sudan. The nearest held fact is the proposed AI provisions in the Cybercrimes and Computer Misuse Bill 2024, which Digital Rights Frontlines described in October 2025 while the bill had not yet passed, so there was no AI law to apply.

Not found. Whether a rule on AI is in force, and whether the AI provisions of the 2024 bill were kept in the law, is not held.

STP.short: UNESCO's 2026 profile and the minister both say the country has no AI-specific laws or regulations; no draft is named.
STP.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Sao Tome and Principe has no law on AI. UNESCO's country profile, published in January 2026, states that the country has no AI-specific laws or regulations governing the development, use or deployment of AI. The minister of education wrote the same in the preface to the country's AI readiness assessment of 2025. Neither names a bill or a draft.

General AI law and the law applied. With no law or regulation specific to AI in January 2026, there is no general AI law to apply. The profile and the readiness assessment both treat the data protection law and its authority as the nearest rules the country has, and neither records a rule for one sector or one use that names AI.

Not found.

SWZ.short: Nothing found names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
SWZ.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

SYC.short: A private member's draft bill covering AI was presented to Assembly members in 2024; no rule on AI is known to be in force.
SYC.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Seychelles has a draft and no rule in force. A private member's draft Pro-Human Technology Bill, covering AI in employment and education among other technologies, was presented to National Assembly members at a seminar on 6 March 2024. The Speaker told the seminar the bill was still far from reaching the Assembly, and it is expected to go to an Assembly working group.

General AI law and the law applied. No law on AI is in force. The only draft held, the Pro-Human Technology Bill, is a private member's bill that covers AI together with other technologies, among them its use in employment and education. It was presented to Assembly members in March 2024, has not reached the Assembly, and is expected to go to an Assembly working group.

Not found. No source found says a law, decree or regulation that sets a rule for AI is in force.

TCD.short: In April 2026 a minister said Chad's digital texts cannot regulate AI and set up a committee; no draft law is known.
TCD.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Chad has no binding rule on AI and no draft. On 27 April 2026 the telecoms minister said that existing digital texts no longer allow AI to be regulated. He installed a 34-member committee and gave it 45 days to propose updated texts for the digital legal framework.

General AI law and the law applied. No law on AI is in force. The article of 27 April 2026 describes the current legal vacuum on AI and names no draft text. The telecoms minister installed a committee of 34 members and set it 45 days to propose updated texts, after saying that the existing digital texts no longer allow AI to be regulated. No draft text on AI is named in the article.

Not found. No source found says what the committee proposed after its 45 days.

TGO.short: Nothing found names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
TGO.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

TUN.short: A draft data protection law including AI use was before a committee in February 2026; no rule on AI is known in force.
TUN.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Tunisia has a draft and no rule in force. Organic law proposal 095/2025 on personal data protection runs to 132 articles in 6 chapters and includes regulation of AI use. It was heard before the Assembly's Rights and Freedoms Committee on 17 February 2026, as a proposal in the Assembly and not yet as a law passed by it. The text reached committee as a data protection reform, with the regulation of AI use as one of its provisions. A lawyer wrote in October 2026 that the proposal was still before the committee and that Tunisia has no law dedicated to AI.

General AI law and the law applied. No law on AI is in force. The proposal under review, the Proposition de loi organique 095/2025, is a data protection law that includes AI use among its subjects, and not a law on AI itself. Its 132 articles in 6 chapters were heard before the Assembly's Rights and Freedoms Committee on 17 February 2026, and the chapters on personal data sit alongside the provisions that regulate AI use.

Not found. No source found says a law, decree or regulation that sets a rule for AI is in force.

TZA.short: Regulations of January 2025 prohibit fabricated AI-generated content online; there is no law on AI itself.
TZA.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Tanzania has a binding rule on one use of AI. Government Notice 57 of 28 January 2025, made under the Electronic and Postal Communications Act, amends the Online Content Regulations of 2020 to add unethical, fabricated and AI-generated video, audio and still pictures to the content prohibited online. It obliges internet service providers and the owners of social media platforms to filter and remove such content.

General AI law and the law applied. The rule covers online content and not AI across sectors. A university centre wrote in September 2026 that Tanzania lacks a dedicated AI law and that the laws used for AI are mostly data protection laws. No bill or draft of a law on AI itself is named, and no order or penalty under the 2025 amendment is on record.

Not found. No source found says a law on AI itself, applying across sectors, is in force.

UGA.short: A review of September 2026 says Uganda has no AI laws in place; a 2025 government assessment found the same.
UGA.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Uganda has no law on AI. A university centre wrote in September 2026 that Uganda has no AI laws in place and uses data protection laws in place of a dedicated framework. An assessment by the ministry responsible for information and communication technology with the International Telecommunication Union, dated 2025, lists the lack of an AI policy and of a legal and regulatory framework among its main findings.

General AI law and the law applied. With no AI laws in place in September 2026, there is no general AI law to apply. The 2025 assessment recommends that Uganda develop a policy and a legal framework for AI. Neither source names a bill or a draft, or a rule for one sector that names AI.

Not found. No bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI has been found.

ZAF.short: Two sources of August 2026 say South Africa has no law or regulations on AI; national rules are expected in 2027.
ZAF.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. South Africa has no law on AI. The chief executive of a technology company wrote in August 2026 that South Africa currently has no law governing artificial intelligence and that national rules are expected in 2027; the same piece ran a week earlier in a second outlet. A research centre wrote the same month that the country has no national AI policy or regulations in place.

General AI law and the law applied. With no law governing AI in August 2026, there is no general AI law to apply. Rules expected in 2027 are an intention; no bill or draft regulation on AI is named in either piece. The research centre's paper says so in a study of automated decisions in social grants, where existing law is the only test.

Not found. No bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI has been found.

ZMB.short: Nothing found names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
ZMB.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

ZWE.short: An analyst wrote in July 2026 that Zimbabwe has no AI law and no draft; no source found says whether one has been introduced since.
ZWE.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Zimbabwe has no AI-specific rule in force. On 27 July 2026 Tashinga Magaya of African Law Matters wrote that the National AI Strategy is not a law, that the proposed regulator has no enabling Act, and that the Cyber and Data Protection Act is the law that applies to AI today. She urged that a draft AI Act be introduced within twelve to eighteen months.

General AI law and the law applied. As at 27 July 2026, no AI act exists in Zimbabwe. The National Digital Regulatory Committee named in the strategy has no enabling legislation, and a draft AI Act is still to be introduced to Parliament. The strategy is the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2026-2030, and the Cyber and Data Protection Act is the law that applies to AI today.

Not found. No source found says whether a draft AI Act has been introduced since July 2026.

AGO.short: The tax authority's AI flagged 15,000 suspect zero-turnover filers in 2026; no single source says AI is in service in several sectors.
AGO.summary:
AI in service. The tax authority AGT has built its own machine-learning tools, tested from 2024. Its chair said in April 2026 that the audit of the 2024 tax year used AI to flag deviations and suspect cases, which then triggered prior-hearing notices, and in July 2026 that the tools cross-checked 2025 corporate income tax filings and flagged irregular filers. In education, the minister said in February 2026 that an AI pilot in selected primary schools was starting, with teacher training first.

Several sectors. Tax is the only sector held with AI in service. The nearest held fact elsewhere is the primary-school pilot, which was only being installed.

Results reported. According to AGT's chair in July 2026, the AI found that 15,000 of the 40,000 companies that filed zero-turnover 2025 income tax returns had in fact recorded transactions.

Not found. No single source says AI is in service in the public systems of two or more sectors.

BDI.short: An AI tool for a public sector's system was under way in 2025; none in service is on record.
BDI.summary:
AI in service. The national malaria programme trained health workers in Cibitoke and Kirundo on 16 July 2025 on an AI app that reads rapid malaria tests, which Enabel calls a pilot. A team is piloting an AI-powered mpox early-warning dashboard in three health districts of Bujumbura. Both are pilots in a few districts, run with outside partners; neither is reported at work across the health system, and no tax, customs, education or agriculture system with AI has been found.

Several sectors. Every AI tool held is in health, and none is in service. The nearest held fact is the malaria test-reading pilot.

Results reported. No measured results of a sectoral AI system have been found. The Enabel account reports the training, not test results.

Not found. No source says an AI tool is in service in a public sector's system.

BEN.short: Customs runs AI risk profiling, by the vendor's account in 2025; no source found reports AI in a second sector and measured results.
BEN.summary:
AI in service. Webb Fontaine, the vendor, says Benin's customs system now bases risk management on AI profiling of importers and goods and detects fraud patterns automatically, and in February 2025 that the system was in use at 44 of the 49 customs offices. In health, the ministry awarded a contract for 20 AI-assisted malaria diagnostic devices for referral hospitals in 2026, and a Japan-funded malaria project launched on 30 June 2026 will use AI mapping to target larvicide spraying in six pilot municipalities. For the tax directorate, an invoice-label classification model was developed in 2025.

Several sectors. Customs is the only sector held with AI in service. The health tools, such as the malaria diagnostic devices and a clinical decision-support system under test, are still being procured or tested.

Results reported. No measured results of a sectoral AI system have been found. The nearest held fact is the vendor's account of customs risk profiling, which gives no figures.

Not found. No source found reports AI in service in a second sector, and measured results of a sectoral AI system.

BFA.short: The TB programme's AI X-ray reading found cases in 2024-25 field campaigns; no single source says AI is in service in several sectors.
BFA.summary:
AI in service. The national TB programme's coordinator said the AI tool CAD4TB was introduced in 2024 to read images from the programme's mobile digital X-ray units in field screening campaigns. In weather forecasting, the digital transition minister and the meteorological agency ANAM signed a research convention on 10 October 2025 to bring AI into forecasting, with ANAM as the pilot body.

Several sectors. Health is the only sector held with AI in service. The nearest held fact elsewhere is the ANAM convention, which covers research, with no tool reported in service.

Results reported. The coordinator reported that from September 2024 to April 2025 the campaigns screened 1,730 people and found 61 TB cases. The AI flagged 50 suspected cases, of which 37 were confirmed and 13 were not TB.

Not found. No single source says AI is in service in the public systems of two or more sectors.

BWA.short: The national TB programme deployed AI chest X-ray reading in 2025; no source found reports AI in a second sector and measured results.
BWA.summary:
AI in service. A vendor partner says the national TB programme deployed AI chest X-ray reading in April 2025 and trained local teams. The U.S. Embassy says PEPFAR donated AI software for TB detection to the Ministry of Health in 2025. The health minister said in February 2025 that trial systems incorporating AI were approved under the ministry's digital health pilot, and an assistant minister said in August 2025 that government is piloting AI for health diagnostics in remote areas.

Several sectors. Every AI tool held is in health. The nearest held fact is the TB programme's chest X-ray reading; no tax, customs, education or agriculture system with AI has been found.

Results reported. No measured results of a sectoral AI system have been found. The embassy's account of the donated software expects better TB case identification but gives no figures.

Not found. No source found reports AI in service in a second sector, and measured results of a sectoral AI system.

CAF.short: An AI X-ray tool at one district hospital helped detect 90 TB cases in 2025; no source shows AI in another sector.
CAF.summary:
AI in service. MSF reports that, with the health authorities, it equipped Batangafo district hospital in 2024 with an AI tool that scores chest X-rays and sends high-score patients for laboratory confirmation. In Bangui, The Union and EPCON built an AI model predicting TB positivity on 100 m grids with the national TB programme, which its manager says helped active screening; the partners plan to validate it with the health ministry. Institut Pasteur de Bangui began a four-year project in August 2024 to build AI-assisted fever diagnostic tools for health centres and community health workers.

Several sectors. Every AI tool held is in health. The nearest held fact is the Batangafo hospital's X-ray scoring.

Results reported. MSF reports that in 2025 the tool helped detect 90 of the 203 TB cases screened in the Batangafo area.

Not found. No source says AI is in service in a public sector other than health.

CIV.short: Côte d'Ivoire's tax administration uses AI to segment taxpayers; no source says AI is in service in several sectors.
CIV.summary:
AI in service. In May 2025 the finance minister said the tax administration uses AI to segment taxpayers by category and has drones that scan buildings to check declarations, presented as tools against tax fraud. Since 5 October 2026, community health workers in Gontougo's five districts have collected data on a platform whose AI gives treatment recommendations and flags inconsistent data, rolled out under the Ministry of Health. In July 2025 the national computing centre said the AI Hub had begun a pilot project on agriculture with the Case Agri. In 2024 the ministry selected 52 health facilities to receive AI-driven forecasts for family planning commodities.

Several sectors. Tax, health and land-cover mapping each have AI in service, in separate accounts. In March 2024 the state technical bureau BNETD presented a land-cover map with AI recognition of forests on satellite imagery, offered as a monitoring tool for the national sustainable cocoa strategy. Customs is deploying AI fraud-detection tools in its Douane Intelligente project, with Huawei.

Results reported. No measured results of a sectoral AI system in service have been found. The minister's account of AI in tax gives no figures for fraud detected or revenue recovered.

Not found. No single source found says AI is in service in several sectors, and no source found reports measured results of a sectoral AI system in service.

CMR.short: An AI tool was in service in a public sector's system in 2026; AI in several sectors is not on record.
CMR.summary:
AI in service. The director general of the social insurance fund CNPS said in February 2026 that the fund runs a symbolic-AI system for automatic processing of old-age pension files, and that its AI tools detect fraud by finding inconsistencies in declarations and contributions and calculate rights in real time. The secondary-education ministry presented the official integration of AI-generated simulations in secondary schools on 17 August 2026. University researchers say a tax fraud detection model was tested at three tax centres, which the tax directorate has not corroborated.

Several sectors. Social security and secondary education each have AI in service, in separate accounts: the CNPS tools and the school simulations.

Results reported. No measured results of a sectoral AI system in service have been found. The tax model's reported gains come from its authors' test, not from a system in service.

Not found. No single source says AI is in service in the public systems of two or more sectors.

COD.short: Measured results of AI in a public sector's system were reported in 2025.
COD.summary:
AI in service. The education minister told the Council of Ministers on 15 August 2025 that an AI system automated State Exam marking in 2025, with results published three days after the exams. The ministry says AI is integrated into grading at the national centre in Kinshasa and at the Lubumbashi branch. WHO says its AI-based preparedness platform is now in use in the country, giving national teams early-warning signals during the Ebola response, as of October 2026. PATH and the Ministry of Health piloted an AI tool reading paper health registers into DHIS2 in 12 health zones.

Several sectors. Education and health each have AI in service, in separate accounts: the exam marking and WHO's epidemic intelligence platform.

Results reported. The minister reported that AI exam processing cut processing time by 30-40% and lifted scanning from 8-10 to 80-100 papers a minute, in August 2025.

Not found. Nothing further is asked of this indicator.

COG.short: Nothing found names AI in a sector's public system or says there is none, so no stage is set.
COG.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether a public sector's system uses AI.

COM.short: An AI tool for a public sector's system was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
COM.summary:
AI in service. WHO says the Comoros adopted an AI-assisted open-source epidemic intelligence system and trained health surveillance staff on it with the Ministry of Health on 22-25 April 2025. A 2026 conference poster says machine-learning models are being developed on routine malaria data to forecast incidence. Neither account describes a tool producing outputs in service, and no tax, customs, education or agriculture system with AI has been found. Both efforts sit within the national health information and surveillance work.

Several sectors. Every AI tool held is in health, and none is in service. The nearest held fact is the epidemic intelligence training.

Results reported. No measured results of a sectoral AI system have been found. The malaria forecasting poster compares models in development.

Not found. No source says an AI tool is in service in a public sector's system.

CPV.short: AI-read heart and eye tests reached all islands with the health ministry in 2026; no source found reports AI in a second sector and measured results.
CPV.summary:
AI in service. The Cabo Verdean American Medical Society, working with the Ministry of Health, says it has distributed cloud ECG devices across all islands that make automatic diagnoses with AI, and that AI lets nurses diagnose cataracts, glaucoma and retinopathy. The account dates from April 2026 and describes the devices as part of the society's medical missions with the ministry. It is the only account held of AI at work in a public sector's system.

Several sectors. Health is the only sector held with AI in service. The nearest held fact is the society's account of AI-read ECGs and eye screening; no tax, customs, education or agriculture system with AI has been found.

Results reported. No measured results of a sectoral AI system have been found. The society's account gives no count of diagnoses or patients.

Not found. No source found reports AI in service in a second sector, and measured results of a sectoral AI system.

DJI.short: The corridor road company's AI logged 2,174 road defects in 2026, with AI weather warnings too; no single source names several sectors.
DJI.summary:
AI in service. The ports and free zones authority says an AI road-monitoring system launched in 2024 uses cameras to detect and locate potholes and cracks along the regional transport corridors. The state corridor-road company said in January 2026 that its system, which reads defects from vehicle video, was in deployment and calibration and had covered over 844 km of its network. In weather, the Chinese Meteorological Administration supplied an AI early-warning system, in service from December 2025, and handed over a new version on 17 July 2026, with forecasts at 3 km resolution.

Several sectors. Road transport and weather each have AI in service, in separate accounts: the road-monitoring system and the early-warning system.

Results reported. The corridor-road company says its system made 2,174 detections across four defect types in its first processing, reported in January 2026.

Not found. No single source says AI is in service in the public systems of two or more sectors.

DZA.short: Trade ministry AI flagged 1,013 importers with identical files in 2026; customs and education also use AI, in separate sources.
DZA.summary:
AI in service. The Ministry of Foreign Trade said in September 2026 that its AI-boosted data analysis and cross-checking system, built into its digital platform, detected anomalies in import programme files. The Ministry of Finance says the customs information system, used at all customs offices and posts, relies on AI techniques for risk analysis of imports and exports. In April 2024 the higher education minister launched an AI platform that simulates study-field choices for new baccalaureate holders. A language model on tax legislation for the Directorate General of Taxes was given a four-month deadline on 20 October 2026.

Several sectors. Trade, customs and higher education each have AI in service, in separate accounts: the trade ministry's cross-checking, the customs system and the orientation platform.

Results reported. The trade ministry's cross-checking flagged 1,013 economic operators whose import files held identical documents, including 278 identical social security declarations and 56 files sharing one tax number.

Not found. No single source says AI is in service in the public systems of two or more sectors.

EGY.short: Egypt has AI in service in justice and in crop mapping, reported separately; no measured results are known.
EGY.summary:
AI in service. The customs head said in November 2025 that Egypt has begun running three smart systems on the Nafeza platform: tariff classification by AI algorithms, automated valuation, and a risk system that scores each shipment before arrival. The health minister's adviser on radiology said in September 2025 that AI applications are used daily in some hospitals and institutes to diagnose breast, prostate and brain tumours. The national AI council's first-half 2026 report lists the launch of a smart judicial assistant. The tax authority's head said in July 2026 that an AI real estate tax app is about to launch, with an AI tax assistant being prepared.

Several sectors. Customs, health, justice and agriculture each have AI in service, in separate accounts. In November 2024 the remote sensing authority NARSS and the agriculture ministry used remote sensing and AI to inventory and classify crops by governorate, producing the 2023-24 winter crop map.

Results reported. No measured results of a sectoral AI system have been found. The nearest held fact is the customs systems' start, reported without figures.

Not found. No single source found says AI is in service in several sectors, and no source found reports measured results of a sectoral AI system in service.

ERI.short: The health ministry's AI chest X-ray units were deployed for TB screening in 2024; no source found reports AI in a second sector and measured results.
ERI.summary:
AI in service. Delft Imaging, the vendor, says the Ministry of Health had 2 portable X-ray units and 6 units of its TB-reading AI deployed in 2024 to detect TB-related abnormalities automatically, and expanded the roll-out with 8 more in 2026. The ministry's work with the vendor goes back to a 2020 plan to use the offline AI chest X-ray reader to screen for TB. The units serve the TB programme; no other use is described.

Several sectors. Health is the only sector held with AI in service. The nearest held fact is the vendor's account of the TB units; no tax, customs, education or agriculture system with AI has been found.

Results reported. No measured results of a sectoral AI system have been found. The vendor's account counts units deployed, not people screened or cases found.

Not found. No source found reports AI in service in a second sector, and measured results of a sectoral AI system.

ETH.short: Agriculture and health AI tools reported yield gains and clinical accuracy in 2025; no single source says AI serves several sectors.
ETH.summary:
AI in service. The Ministry of Revenues and the Customs Commission unveiled an AI-powered passenger risk management system on 12 October 2025, built by the Ethiopian Institute of Artificial Intelligence. CGIAR reports that a fertilizer advisory system run by the Ministry of Agriculture gave AI-based recommendations to 49,000 farmers in 2025. IDinsight says an AI assistant built with the Ministry of Health answers health extension workers' clinical queries in five regions; in April 2026 it was piloted in 15 woredas, with scale-up planned after evaluation. The Ministry of Education completed testing of an AI teacher assistant for grades 9-12 in 2026.

Several sectors. Customs, agriculture and health each have AI in service, in separate accounts: the customs risk system, the fertilizer advisory and the health assistant.

Results reported. CGIAR reports that the fertilizer advisory raised wheat yields by 16-25% and maize yields by 10.5-17.6% among participating farmers in 2025. IDinsight reports 83.3% medical accuracy for the health assistant in real-world use by 2025.

Not found. No single source says AI is in service in the public systems of two or more sectors.

GAB.short: Nothing found names AI in a sector's public system or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GAB.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether a public sector's system uses AI.

GHA.short: Ghana uses AI in tax and, since March 2026, in customs valuation, where it cleared 75.3% of declarations and flagged 24.7% in its first weeks.
GHA.summary:
AI in service. The revenue authority's deputy commissioner said in May 2025 that it uses AI and machine learning to find anomalies in tax filings, expose suspicious trade and trigger audits. Ghana Health Service and Jacaranda Health launched an AI maternal health platform in July 2026 that sorts mothers' SMS questions by urgency and refers emergencies; Ghana Health Service clinicians have staffed its helpdesk since March 2026. A WHO-UNDP programme launched in May 2026 aims to deploy AI early warning for climate-sensitive diseases in national platforms.

Several sectors. Customs is a further sector with AI in service. The Ministry of Finance and the revenue authority said an AI tool that helps customs officers value and classify imports was fully rolled out at ports of entry on 11 March 2026, after a November 2025 pilot.

Results reported. The Ministry of Finance said that by 30 March 2026 the customs tool had endorsed clearing of 75.3% of declarations and flagged 24.7% as below accepted global values. Jacaranda reports the maternal helpdesk handles about 6,500 responses a month, 44% resolved by AI directly.

Not found. No source found reports measured results of the tax analytics, and AI disease surveillance in service.

GIN.short: Nothing found names AI in a sector's public system or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GIN.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether a public sector's system uses AI.

GMB.short: An AI tool was in service in a public sector's system in 2026; AI in several sectors is not on record.
GMB.summary:
AI in service. The Gambia Revenue Authority now uses the Rental Tax Compliance System's ML-estimated rental values and compliance risk scores to prioritise property owner records for audit and visit, per the DIAL case study. The Ministry of Higher Education unveiled the TITA mobile app on 2025-04-24 in Banjul, whose admin panel uses AI to generate institution-wide academic timetables automatically for tertiary institutions. 2 facts are held on the subject: no news story or official notice read for this study says more about it, the documents the earlier cell cited were not read, and the systems themselves were not examined.

Several sectors. No source found since October 2023 says AI is in service in the public systems of two or more sectors. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

Results reported. No source found since October 2023 reports measured results of a sectoral AI system. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

Not found. No source found since October 2023 says AI is in service in the public systems of two or more sectors.

GNB.short: Nothing found names AI in a sector's public system or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GNB.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether a public sector's system uses AI.

GNQ.short: An AI tool for a public sector's system was under way in 2025; none in service is on record.
GNQ.summary:
AI in service. The health ministry officially launched on 6 June 2025 'Guinea Salud', an AI chatbot answering the public on vaccines, medical evacuation, clinic licensing and HIV, in a pilot phase. In July 2025 the transport and AI ministry funded a five-month pilot in which university students build and run the country's first AI-integrated weather station, with a national network of such stations as the stated goal.

Several sectors. No source found since October 2023 says AI is in service in the public systems of two or more sectors. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

Results reported. No source found since October 2023 reports measured results of a sectoral AI system. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

Not found. No source found since October 2023 says: is one in service.

KEN.short: The health insurer's AI blocked Sh12.7 billion of claims by 2026, and AI serves education, farming and health; no source found says how widely.
KEN.summary:
AI in service. The Health Cabinet Secretary told the Senate in October 2025 that the Social Health Authority's claims platform uses AI and machine learning to detect abnormal claim patterns, inflated billing and duplicate submissions in real time; a parliamentary committee report in December 2025 said the system also rejects some legitimate hospital claims as fraudulent. President Ruto said in November 2025 that the revenue authority KRA has AI-powered risk engines integrated into tax compliance. The Digital Health Agency tendered for AI-driven maternal and child health and blood bank systems in 2026.

AGO.short: Angola adopted an ICT White Paper in 2024 resting on a national broadband strategy; no source found reports its money and measurable targets.
AGO.summary:
Plan adopted. Presidential Decree 272/24, published in the Diário da República on 5 December 2024, approved the ICT White Paper 2023-2027 after Council of Ministers review on 30 August 2024. The White Paper's stated objective is universal access to the broadband service for the whole population. It names the National Broadband Strategy and the National Broadband Network (RNBL) as its basis. The White Paper itself, published on the same date, says its measures follow from implementing that strategy.

Money and results. The White Paper describes the strategy as covering the modernisation and expansion of the primary electronic communications network, now called the National Broadband Network, as State-funded public-domain infrastructure. The decree text holds no numeric coverage, speed or price target for the 2023-2027 period, and no delivery figures are given there.

Not found. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan in the last three years is held.

The June 2018 publication is the date held for the strategy, and no later plan or revision has been found.

The strategy sets two coverage targets: 2 Mbps for 50% of citizens by the end of 2014, and 20 Mbps for 90% of the population by 2018. An editorial in La Nation describes the SNHD as aligned with Vision Djibouti 2035, tying the strategy to the country's long-term vision for 2035. The minister said at the launch that the strategy argues for lower tariffs and doubled speeds at no extra cost.

Money and results. The strategy is part of the Djibouti Digital Foundation project, which the World Bank supports. Early results reported at the launch were 250 km of fibre laid in the north and more than 100 administrative buildings connected. The La Nation editorial says the SNHD sets two scenarios for 2027, connecting ten cities or seven.

In a 20 February 2026 message the minister said the government had adopted a comprehensive all-fibre communications strategy. A ministry communique of 30 September 2026 says the strategy aims to bring fibre to the whole territory by 2027, with the copper network phased out by the same date.

Money and results. The Ministry's page of 9 July 2025 sets a goal of 7 million households on fixed internet by the end of 2027, with fibre to the home as the core technology. It reports 6.6 million fixed internet subscribers in the first half of 2025, up from 3.5 million in early 2020, and says the intermediate objectives were reached.

GHA.summary:
Plan adopted. The Ministry of Communications issued the National Broadband Policy and Implementation Strategy as Final Version 1.0 in October 2012. The strategy is the Ministry's national instrument, with targets of 40% household and 40% national broadband penetration by 2015, and of 90% by 2020.

Money and results. Nothing found shows money committed or progress published. The nearest held fact is the targets the 2012 document sets: 40% household and 40% national broadband penetration by 2015, and 90% by 2020. The Ministry of Communications issued that document in October 2012 as Final Version 1.0. The Ministry of Communications is the named owner of the strategy, which is a national plan. Its targets run to 2015 and 2020, and cover household penetration and national penetration. The first set of targets falls in 2015 and the final one in 2020, with the 90% target the highest of the three.

Not found. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan in the last three years is held, and no figures published against its targets.

GIN.short: Nothing found names a national broadband plan or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GIN.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national broadband plan for the country, or says there is none.

GMB.short: A national broadband policy and strategy ran 2020 to 2024 with coverage targets; no successor or report on its targets is known.
GMB.summary:
Plan adopted. The Ministry of Information and Communication Infrastructure issued the National Broadband Policy 2020-2024 in June 2020 for a five-year period ending in 2024. The same month it commissioned the National Broadband Strategy 2020-2024, which covers 2020 to 2024. Neither document names a successor plan, and the strategy's own text refers to a review for the next five-year cycle.

Money and results. The strategy sets targets of broadband coverage to more than 90% of the population by 2024, at least 75% of homes with affordable 5 Mbps download and upload speeds by 2022, and 4G coverage of at least 85% of the population by 2024 (strategy). The policy sets a 5 Mbps minimum for every user and near-100% of homes with affordable 5 Mbps by 2023 (policy).

Not found. Nothing found says a national broadband plan is adopted and still running, or reports its funding or results.

GNB.short: A draft universal-service plan with 2031 coverage targets was dated November 2025; no source found says whether a broadband plan is adopted and running.
GNB.summary:
Plan adopted. Guinea-Bissau's Strategic Plan of the Access and Universal Service Fund (FASU) for 2026-2031 is a consultancy final report for the regulator ARN, dated 24 November 2025. The report states that it is still to be disseminated and validated in a public stakeholder consultation, and so it is a draft rather than a plan in force. ITU's 2019 table of broadband strategies, policies and plans answered no on whether a national broadband policy existed and named none.

Money and results. Nothing is held on funding, spending or results delivered under the plan. The nearest held fact is what the draft itself sets out, its coverage targets before 2031: 99% of the population for 2G, 98% for 3G and 96% for 4G broadband.

Not found. No source found says a national broadband plan is adopted and still running.

GNQ.short: Equatorial Guinea presented a draft telecommunications plan to the World Bank in December 2025; no source found says whether it is adopted, and any funding,.
GNQ.summary:
Plan adopted. On 11 December 2025 the Ministry of Transport and Telecommunications presented to the World Bank a proposal for the Plan Nacional de Telecomunicaciones para la Transformación Digital. The plan includes a competitive network ensuring 100% coverage before 2030. The press article reporting it, published on 12 December 2025, describes the plan as still to be designed, with World Bank technical assistance. The Ministry of Transport and Telecommunications is the owner named for the plan.

Money and results. The nearest held fact is the same December 2025 proposal, which looks to World Bank technical assistance for the design of the plan. It states the 2030 coverage aim as a goal of the proposed plan, with no delivery figure against it. The Ministry of Transport, Telecommunications and Civil Aviation also issued a July-December 2026 half-year action plan, a national plan.

Not found. No source found says a national broadband plan is adopted and still running. Nothing found shows money committed to one.

KEN.short: Kenya has the Digital Superhighway 100,000km fibre plan, announced in 2022 and funded in 2026/27; no source found reports progress against its targets.
KEN.summary:
Plan adopted. In November 2022 President Ruto announced the Digital Superhighway's 100,000km national fibre target. It aims at broadband for the whole country within five years, by 2027. In September 2026 the Nation reported that deadline as still ahead. The National Broadband Strategy 2025-2030 sets the same 100,000km target, against 40,000km of fibre today, Techweez reported in October 2026.

Money and results. The Digital Superhighway is funded through the Universal Service Fund. The Communications Authority and the ICT Authority first signed a Sh5 billion agreement covering 19 counties. Kenya Power had received Sh940.6 million by June 2025 to build the fibre network. The FY2026/27 budget gives Sh1.3 billion to maintain the national fibre backbone. It adds Sh400 million for digital hubs and Sh382 million for the superhighway's cybersecurity.

Not found. No review or report from the last three years giving figures against the plan's own targets is held.

LBR.short: Nothing found names a national broadband plan or says there is none, so no stage is set.
LBR.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national broadband plan for the country, or says there is none.

LBY.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national broadband plan for the country, or says there is none.

LSO.short: Lesotho signed a Broadband Infrastructure Sharing Policy in June 2026, but no budget or delivery results are known, so the main unknown is funding.
LSO.summary:
Plan adopted. Lesotho's Minister of Information, Communications, Science, Technology and Innovation signed the Broadband Infrastructure Sharing Policy on 11 June 2026, according to Lesotho Times; no plan period is given. Before that, the ministry held a second draft of a Broadband and Shared Infrastructure Policy and Implementation Plan, dated 17 February 2025, and the Minister of Finance and Development Planning told Parliament on 19 February 2025 that a broadband policy was among those under development.

Money and results. No budget, fund allocation or delivery report has been found. The nearest held fact is the second draft of the Broadband and Shared Infrastructure Policy and Implementation Plan of February 2025, which includes a monitoring and evaluation framework and states that formal broadband legislation is lacking.

Not found. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan in the last three years is held.

MAR.short: Morocco's national broadband plan reached about 99% of its first-phase target by 2024; a second phase funded by the universal service fund runs to 2026.
MAR.summary:
Plan adopted. Morocco's national broadband plan, the Plan National du Haut Débit (PNHD), is in its second phase. The ministry says PNHD 2 was launched in 2024 for the areas 4G does not reach, and the Minister for Digital Transition told parliament in December 2024 that it is to serve 1,800 rural zones with weak or no coverage by 2026. The ministry's Digital Morocco 2030 brochure of September 2024 lists PNHD 2 among its programmes, and a columnist treats the plan as running in late 2025.

Money and results. The second phase is carried out with the support of the Universal Telecommunications Service Fund, the minister said. The ministry reported that PNHD 1 had covered 10,620 of the 10,740 localities targeted, 98.88 per cent, at the end of March 2024, and the minister told parliament in December 2024 that more than 10,640 rural zones were covered between 2018 and 2024, about 99 per cent of the first phase's target.

Not found. No period beyond 2026 has been found for the second phase.

MDG.short: Nothing found names a national broadband plan or says there is none, so no stage is set.
MDG.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national broadband plan for the country, or says there is none.

MLI.short: Mali's regulator launched a study for a national broadband plan in 2015; no source found says whether a plan was adopted, and any funding,.
MLI.summary:
Plan adopted. In a 2015 article L'Essor reports that the regulator AMRTP held a launch workshop in Bamako for a study on the broadband implementation strategy. The study is to produce a short, medium and long-term broadband development plan, together with the introduction of 4G. The article reports a study under way, not a plan adopted by the government or the minister. The article carries no date, and its published field gives 2015. The study is titled Etude sur la stratégie de mise en œuvre du large bande au Mali.

Money and results. The nearest held fact is the same 2015 report of the launch workshop. It concerns the study that is to write the plan, so it names no budget line, fund allocation or financed programme tied to a plan, and no figures against targets. The report names the regulator AMRTP as the body that held the workshop, in Bamako, and says nothing of who would fund the study or the plan.

Not found. No source found says a national broadband plan is adopted and still running. Nothing found shows money committed to one.

MOZ.short: Mozambique launched an Internet for All plan to 2030 in 2024 or 2025; no source found says whether it is formally adopted and still running.
MOZ.summary:
Plan adopted. In December 2024 the government launched the Internet for All project, which aims to raise internet access in Mozambique from under 25% of the population to 100% by 2030, according to the U.S. International Trade Administration. The Wearetech.africa report of 23 July 2026 also describes an Internet Para Todos programme, with a period running to 2030, which had not ended when it was published in July 2026. Both sources give 2030 as the end of the plan period.

Money and results. No funding or delivery figures have been found. The nearest held fact is the targets: Wearetech.africa reports that the Internet Para Todos programme aims for 80% mobile penetration, 95% territorial coverage and 99% network availability by 2030. All three targets fall on a date that had not arrived when it was published in July 2026, so no result against them has been found.

Not found. Nothing found says a national broadband plan has been adopted and is still running, or reports its funding or results.

MRT.short: A 2019-2025 broadband plan was proposed by the ministry in February 2019; no source found says whether the government adopted it.
MRT.summary:
Plan adopted. The ministry's final study of February 2019 proposes a Stratégie Nationale Haut Débit / Plan National du Haut Débit for 2019-2025, with objectives dated 2020 and 2025. It sets coverage of all Moughataas as the short-term aim and the whole country as the medium-term aim. The study states no adoption by the government or a minister. The same study is titled "Stratégie de promotion du Haut Débit et d'accès Universel" by its authors, and the ministry's January 2019 action plan carries the name Stratégie Nationale de Promotion du Haut Débit.

Money and results. The February 2019 study puts the investment at 623 million US dollars over 25 years, as an estimate. The January 2019 action plan lists actions by theme with phasing and a preliminary calendar, with one action to launch in September 2019. It leaves the action sheets to a follow-up committee and states no broadband coverage, speed or price target.

Not found. No source found says a national broadband plan is adopted and still running. Nothing found reports funding committed or results delivered.

MUS.short: Mauritius issued a National Broadband Policy for 2012-2020 and none is held since, so no source found says whether a current plan is running.
MUS.summary:
Plan adopted. The Ministry of Information and Communication Technology issued the National Broadband Policy 2012-2020 (NBP2012) in January 2012, as the national policy for broadband in Mauritius. Its stated period ran from 2012 to 2020, so the plan's own dates have passed. The document names no successor policy, and it is the only national broadband plan held for Mauritius from any year, including after 2020.

Money and results. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan is held, and no figures published against its targets have been found either. The nearest held fact is the policy document itself, which fixes the period to 2020 and says nothing of a later plan or of delivery after that year.

Not found. No source found says a national broadband plan is adopted and still running.

MWI.short: Malawi's National Broadband Strategy ran 2019-2023 and no successor is on record as of 2025; no source found says whether a new plan is adopted.
MWI.summary:
Plan adopted. Malawi's National Broadband Strategy ran from 2019 to 2023. It aimed to raise broadband penetration from 4.5% to 35% and average speeds from 256 Kbps to 5 Mbps, Ecofin Agency reported in October 2025. The report names no plan that follows it.

Money and results. The regulator, MACRA, launched a national broadband mapping system on 7 October 2025, with support from the International Telecommunication Union and the European Union, to find and fill coverage gaps between 2025 and 2028. Its own figures put 4G coverage at 75.1% by the third quarter of 2024 and mobile broadband subscriptions at 9.4 million, a penetration rate of 47%. Only 18% of Malawians used the internet in 2023. The government licensed Starlink, which began commercial service in July 2023.

Not found. No source found says a national broadband plan is adopted and still running.

NAM.short: Namibia has had a National Broadband Policy since 2020 and a National Digital Strategy since 2025; no source found reports money committed and results published.
NAM.summary:
Plan adopted. The Minister of Information and Communication Technology, Dr P. Mushelenga, signed the National Broadband Policy on 27 July 2020 and issued it to the Communications Regulatory Authority of Namibia as policy guidelines under section 7 of the Communications Act 2009. Government Notice No. 189 in Government Gazette No. 7308 published it on 14 August 2020. The National Digital Strategy, launched in 2025 with the Sixth National Development Plan, charts digital infrastructure for 2025/26 to 2029/30. In January 2026 the minister, Emma Theofelus, said the review of the National Broadband Policy was finished and its new targets would apply from October 2026.

Money and results. The nearest held fact is the National Digital Strategy's target, stated in February 2026, of raising internet use from 53% to 90% by 2030, within a plan period that runs from 2025/26 to 2029/30 and had not ended when it was reported.

Not found. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan in the last three years is held.

NER.short: Nothing found names a national broadband plan or says there is none, so no stage is set.
NER.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national broadband plan, or says there is none.

NGA.short: Nigeria's National Broadband Plan 2020-2025 expired in December 2025 short of its 70 percent target; a successor is being drawn up, not yet adopted.
NGA.summary:
Plan adopted. A committee led by Funke Opeke of MainOne, with Bashir Gwandu as co-chair, was inaugurated in December 2019 to develop a five-year broadband strategy through 2025, which produced the National Broadband Plan 2020-2025. In September 2020 BusinessDay NG referred to the recently updated Nigerian Broadband Plan, and the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) said a grant was in line with it. The plan expired at the end of December 2025, when the NCC's head said talks with the ministry on a third plan had begun. In April 2026 an NCC executive commissioner said the regulator was drawing up a successor; none is reported adopted.

Money and results. Citing NCC data, BusinessDay NG reports broadband penetration of 51.97 percent in December 2025 against the plan's 70 percent target, and 4G at 52.95 percent of mobile subscriptions against a 70 percent goal set for 2023. The only funding held is foreign: a US Trade and Development Agency grant to ipNX, signed on 17 September 2020, to expand fibre to more than 200,000 residences in Lagos, Abuja and Port Harcourt. Its amount is not stated.

Not found. No successor to the National Broadband Plan 2020-2025 has been found as adopted. The money behind the plan is not stated.

RWA.short: Rwanda updated its National Broadband Policy and Strategy in 2022; no source found says whether money is committed to it or results are published.
RWA.summary:
Plan adopted. The government updated its National Broadband Policy and Strategy in 2022, Telecom Review Africa reported in October 2025. The update ended the commitment to a single wholesale network. It introduced technology neutrality, so that mobile operators can reuse spectrum bands for several technologies at once, 4G and 5G among them.

Money and results. To support the change, more spectrum was allocated in the 700 MHz, 900 MHz, 1800 MHz and 2100 MHz bands, opening the way for more than one operator to build advanced networks. The same report estimates 4G coverage reaching 100% by the end of 2025, with 3G coverage at 99.71%. It sets neither figure against a target of the policy, and it names no money committed to it.

Not found. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan in the last three years is held.

SDN.short: Nothing found names a national broadband plan or says there is none, so no stage is set.
SDN.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national broadband plan for the country, or says there is none.

SEN.short: Senegal's ministry presented guidelines for a national broadband plan in 2017; no source found says whether it was adopted, and any funding,.
SEN.summary:
Plan adopted. A ministry slide deck of 2017 presents the guidelines of the Plan national haut/très haut débit, tied to Sénégal Numérique 2025. It sets out objectives, a diagnosis of the infrastructure and proposed investments. The deck presents guidelines and does not state that the plan was adopted. The deck is hosted by the ITU, carries no date of its own, and its published field gives 2017.

Money and results. The nearest held fact is the same 2017 deck, whose proposed investments are put forward as part of the guidelines. It names no budget line, fund allocation or financed programme, and no figures against the plan's targets. The deck links the plan to Sénégal Numérique 2025 and gives a diagnosis of the infrastructure beside the proposed investments, with no statement of who funds them.

Not found. No source found says a national broadband plan is adopted and still running. Nothing found shows money committed to one.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone has a National Broadband Strategy for 2023-2028, reported adopted in January 2025; no source found says what money or results sit behind it.
SLE.summary:
Plan adopted. Sierra Leone has a National Broadband Strategy for 2023 to 2028. The Ministry of Communication, Technology and Innovation held a validation workshop on it on 28 February 2024. ITEdgeNews reported on 31 January 2025 that a government agreement to connect universities by satellite is in line with it.

Money and results. Under that agreement the Ministry of Communication, Technology and Innovation and the Ministry of Technical and Higher Education signed with ELCOME SL to bring Starlink internet to 12 public and private universities, with vocational schools to follow in a second phase. The minister said three local companies were by then providing Starlink services and that its arrival had spurred competition among providers. The report gives no cost for the agreement and no budget line or fund allocation behind the strategy, and it sets no figures against the strategy's targets.

Not found. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan in the last three years is held.

SOM.short: Nothing found names a national broadband plan or says there is none, so no stage is set.
SOM.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national broadband plan for the country, or says there is none.

SSD.short: South Sudan launched a National Broadband Roadmap, reported in 2025; no money or results against it are known.
SSD.summary:
Plan adopted. South Sudan's National Communication Authority, as reported by Eye Radio on 3 July 2025, cited the launch of the National Broadband Roadmap among the developments behind the country's rise in internet users. The Authority names the plan as the National Broadband Roadmap and presents its launch as a development already behind the country, not one still to come. The same report places the roadmap alongside the Authority's own account of how internet use in South Sudan grew between 2024 and 2025.

Money and results. The nearest held fact is the Authority's count of internet users, which Eye Radio reported rose from 1.3 million in 2024 to 1.9 million in 2025. The Authority tied the launch of the National Broadband Roadmap to that rise, and the report gives it as a result of the wider set of developments, not as a figure measured against a target of the plan.

Not found. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan in the last three years is held.

STP.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national broadband plan for the country, or says there is none.

SWZ.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national broadband plan, or says there is none.

SYC.short: Nothing found names a national broadband plan or says there is none, so no stage is set.
SYC.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national broadband plan for the country, or says there is none.

TCD.short: Chad adopted Tchad Connexion 2030 in 2025, with an 80 percent coverage target, but no source found reports money committed or results against it.
TCD.summary:
Plan adopted. Chad's government launched Tchad Connexion 2030, which TechAfrica News reported on 18 July 2025 as a national digital strategy running to 2030, aimed at giving most Chadians quality internet access and extending digital coverage across the country. Biometric Update, on 16 March 2026, reports that the government is implementing it, with targets of at least 80 percent national internet coverage and about 80 percent mobile penetration.

Money and results. The held facts state planned investment and works, not figures against the targets. Ecofin, on 10 December 2025, gives US$1.5bn of planned digital investment. TechAfrica News lists fibre loops, a 509 km fibre link from N'Djamena to the Niger border and satellite coverage as the components of the launch programme.

Not found. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan in the last three years is held.

TGO.short: Nothing found names a national broadband plan or says there is none, so no stage is set.
TGO.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national broadband plan for the country, or says there is none.

TUN.short: Tunisia has a national very high speed broadband strategy dated 2013; no source found says whether money was committed to it or results published.
TUN.summary:
Plan adopted. The communication technologies ministry's fibre optic page names a national strategy for very high speed broadband, the Stratégie Nationale pour le Développement du très haut débit, which dates from 2013. The page sits under the digital infrastructure axis of Tunisie Digitale 2020. It gives no period for the strategy and names nothing that replaces it.

Money and results. Under the strategy the ministry publishes terms of reference for fibre to the home: for network studies, for civil works, for cabling the access network and for cabling buildings, with common annexes. They are meant to set one technical standard for laying fibre in Tunisia and for the studies and works of telecommunications projects. The page states no budget and no figures against the strategy.

Not found. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan in the last three years is held.

TZA.short: Tanzania has a National Broadband Strategy for 2021-2026, with a steering committee first meeting in June 2026; no source found reports its funding and results.
TZA.summary:
Plan adopted. Tanzania's Ministry of Communication and Information Technology reported on 26 June 2026 that the Steering Committee overseeing the National High-Speed Internet Communication Strategy (Mkakati wa Taifa wa Mawasiliano ya Intaneti ya Kasi) held its first meeting on 25 June 2026 in Dodoma. The Ministry's Permanent Secretary chaired the meeting. The same ministry report gives no period for the strategy. A regulator's presentation of March 2026 lists the Tanzania National Broadband Strategy 2021-2026 among the country's digital policies, with results areas on infrastructure, connectivity and devices.

Money and results. The nearest held fact on the plan's delivery is that first meeting of the steering committee, held in Dodoma on 25 June 2026 under the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Communication and Information Technology. It concerns the oversight of the strategy and says nothing of its targets, funding or results.

Not found. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan in the last three years is held.

UGA.short: Uganda has the National Broadband Policy 2018, reviewed in January 2026; no source found reports money tied to it and figures against its targets.
UGA.summary:
Plan adopted. Uganda's National Broadband Policy 2018 is the broadband plan the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance and the ITU describe as under implementation, in a review of it published on 12 January 2026. The review gives no end date for the policy and names no replacement. In June 2025 the ministry validated fibre deployment guidelines meant to support the policy's implementation.

Money and results. The review of the 2018 National Broadband Policy's implementation, published on 12 January 2026 by the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance and the ITU, sets out a matrix covering each of the policy's objectives and strategies. For each it lists the activities undertaken, the outcomes, the level of implementation reported by stakeholders, the challenges met and the measures proposed to mitigate them.

Not found. No figures against the plan's targets have been found. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan in the last three years is held.

ZAF.short: South Africa's SA Connect broadband policy, adopted in 2013, is cited as current in 2026; no source found says whether money is committed to it.
ZAF.summary:
Plan adopted. South Africa's national broadband plan is SA Connect, a policy dating from 2013 that sets "broadband for all". The government gazette page on the IMT Roadmap 2026 names that policy and states no end date or successor for it. In July 2026 the regulator ICASA named the SA Connect Broadband Policy as the existing national policy that its draft IMT Roadmap 2026 supports. A 28 July 2026 report on the same roadmap says ICASA cites the policy for broadband access.

Money and results. The government's SA Connect target, as an August 2026 article puts it, is universal broadband access with an average user experience of 100Mbps by 2030. The article says telecoms licensees' spectrum obligations align with that target, and it gives no figure for delivery against it.

Not found. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan in the last three years is held.

ZMB.short: A December 2025 working group found Zambia lacks a national broadband policy; no source found says whether other plans set broadband targets.
ZMB.summary:
Plan adopted. Zambia has no national broadband policy. The policy working group at the Africa Broadband Maps national event, held in Lusaka with the regulator ZICTA on 9 to 11 December 2025, concluded so and recommended that one be written. The event was part of a project in eleven African countries, run with the International Telecommunication Union and paid for by the European Union.

Money and results. The project is to build a national broadband mapping system in four yearly phases from 2025 to 2028, owned by the government with ZICTA as its custodian, and to train staff in mapping, data management and policy. The report says it is meant to complement the country's digital transformation work and its existing mapping of ICT infrastructure. It states no broadband targets and no budget.

Not found. No source found says whether broadband targets sit inside other government plans.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe launched a National Broadband Plan covering 2020 to 2030 in March 2024; no source found says whether money has been committed or results published.
ZWE.summary:
Plan adopted. Zimbabwe has a National Broadband Plan, which the ICT minister, Dr Tatenda Mavetera, said the government "came up with", as the Herald reported on 12 October 2023. The minister launched the plan on 7 March 2024 at Somabula; it covers 2020 to 2030. The Herald names the Ministry of ICT, Postal and Courier Services as the plan's owner. The minister added that Potraz had been in sync with Government in implementing it, and that the plan covers access for government, business, households and individuals.

Money and results. The nearest held fact on delivery is the minister's statement of October 2023 that Potraz was implementing the plan alongside Government. The plan's stated aim, as the same report gives it, is to provide broadband access at four levels: government, business, household and individual.

Not found. No budget line, universal service fund allocation or financed programme tied to the plan in the last three years is held. No figures against the plan's own targets have been found either.

AGO.short: A government e-procurement system was in service in 2025; no source found reports end-to-end use.
AGO.summary:
E-procurement in service. The SNCP director says public contracting entities publish their procedures and annual plans on the Portal de Compras Públicas, per ANGOP. Angola's national procurement service director said the Sistema Nacional da Contratação Pública Electrónica, launched in April 2018, has processed public purchases online, with over 400 state suppliers on the system (2022, before the three-year window). Presidential Decree 202/17 created the Sistema Nacional da Contratação Pública Electrónica and its regulation for a single state-run electronic platform, to be implemented in phases under a later ministerial decree, with paper and electronic procedures coexisting (2017, before the three-year window).

End to end. No source found since October 2023 says e-procurement runs end to end or is required of all public bodies. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

Use reported. The Serviço Nacional da Contratação Pública director said SNCPE has run 1,959 tender procedures since 2018 and saved Kz 110 billion (25%) against estimated values (2022, before the three-year window).

Not found. No source found since October 2023 says e-procurement runs end to end or is required of all public bodies.

BDI.short: Government e-procurement was under way in 2026; none in service is on record.
BDI.summary:
E-procurement in service. PAFEN issued on 23 September 2026 a World Bank-financed request for proposals to design, build and deploy an end-to-end electronic public procurement (e-GP) system for Burundi, proposals due 13 November 2026. The finance minister said the e-GP e-procurement platform, set up by the Ministry of Finance, Budget and Digital Economy, is due to enter into force from 2027. The public procurement regulator's director general says at least seven of fourteen planned activities for the e-GP system are done and first tests are expected early 2027.

End to end. No source found since October 2023 says e-procurement runs end to end or is required of all public bodies. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

Use reported. No source found since October 2023 gives a figure for e-procurement. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

Not found. No source found since October 2023 says: is an e-procurement system in service.

BEN.short: Figures for government e-procurement were reported in 2023.
BEN.summary:
E-procurement in service. The Treasury (DGTCP) announced on 19 December 2025 that a new 'e-Procurement' platform will replace SIGMAP and the public procurement web portal, under decree 2025-169 of 9 April 2025 setting up the electronic public procurement information system, with its modules presented and implementation at a progress-review stage. ARMP says the e-procurement platform is still being acquired and implemented, under Decree 2025-169 of 9 April 2025, with training of public buyers running 6 October to 28 November 2025.

End to end. No source found since October 2023 says e-procurement runs end to end or is required of all public bodies. The nearest held fact: A 2024 evaluation cited by ARMP found that of 757 calls published in 2023 on SIGMaP only 21 reached the automatic contract page.

Use reported. A 2024 evaluation cited by ARMP found that of 757 calls published in 2023 on SIGMaP only 21 reached the automatic contract page.

Not found. Nothing further is asked of this indicator.

BFA.short: A government e-procurement platform was being piloted in 2025; no source found says whether tenders are published or bid on it.
BFA.summary:
E-procurement in service. The finance ministry's 2025 public-finance report, cited by OuagaNews, says the procurement-planning module was fully configured on the E-Burkindi platform and piloted with ministries and institutions in 2025. A World Bank-backed project set out in 2022 to acquire, adapt and deploy an online e-GP solution for Burkina Faso, with the supplier tender for the solution due that year.

End to end. The nearest held fact is the planning module, piloted on E-Burkindi with ministries and institutions in 2025; nothing found says tenders are advertised, bids taken or contracts awarded on it.

Use reported. The nearest held fact is the 2025 pilot of E-Burkindi's procurement-planning module, which gives no count of tenders, contracts or value passing through the platform.

Use reported. The minister reported 1,173 contracts awarded through Coleps in 2025 from 2,334 notices, against 365 awards from 458 notices in 2024. More than 8,143 contracts worth 1,745 billion FCFA had been programmed and published on Coleps for 2025 by January 2025.

ETH.summary:

Use reported. PPCC executive director Bodger Scott Johnson said in September 2025 that contracts worth US$12,219,000 had been awarded through e-GP. He said in October 2025 that more than US$28 million in contracts had gone to Liberian-owned businesses through it. PPCC reported 127 live processes on e-GP in August 2025, and 132 procurement transactions in October 2025.

The Procurement Policy Office says the web-based e-Procurement System (e-PS), launched in September 2015, covers the procurement process, with use made mandatory by government from July 2020, and 116 of 205 public bodies used it in 2023/24. Licensing providers. The Bank of Mozambique granted PawaPay, through its subsidiary Quidexplus Mozambique, a Payment Service Provider licence, announced by PawaPay on 8 October 2026. The Bank of Mozambique's communiqué of 30 July 2026 says Metix integrates banks, microbanks, electronic money institutions and other payment service providers authorised by the central bank.

Overseeing a switch. Bank of Mozambique launched the Metix instant payment system on 16 March 2026, run by SIMO, and reports its volume (over 11,000 transfers a day) in its Monetary Policy Committee communiqué. The National Single Network (National Switch) has been operated by SIMOrede since 2023 under the supervision and control of the Bank of Mozambique.

Live on PAPSS. Mozambique joined PAPSS in September 2026, with local banks invited to onboard, but none is reported live on it. No source found since October 2023 says the country takes part in PAPSS or a regional payment system in service.

Not found. No source found since October 2023 says the country takes part in PAPSS or a regional payment system.

A later answer places the country above that step. It is the only fact held on the subject: no news story or official notice read for this study says more about it, the documents the earlier cell cited were not read, and the systems themselves were not examined.

The nearest held fact: Bank of Mauritius Governor Thakoor says the bank serves as settlement bank for COMESA's REPSS. A later answer places the country above that step. 2 facts are held on the subject: no news story or official notice read for this study says more about it, the documents the earlier cell cited were not read, and the systems themselves were not examined.

Overseeing a switch. Bank of Mauritius Governor Thakoor says the bank's infrastructure includes the Mauritius Central Automated Switch (MauCAS), whose QR payments are now usable in Mauritius and India.

Live on PAPSS. Nothing found shows the country live on PAPSS. What is held is a regional payment system, which does not count: Bank of Mauritius Governor Thakoor says the bank serves as settlement bank for COMESA's REPSS.
