He spoke of it alongside a data harmonisation act. The report names no instrument, gives no date of approval and sets no date by which data must move, so the policy is counted as one being written. In January 2024 NITA's Director General said a draft National Data Centre and Cloud Computing Regulatory Framework, covering licensing, data localisation, security and competition, was under review at a validation workshop in Accra.

Enforcer named and rule applied. The nearest held fact is the minister's statement, which presents the new data centre as the capacity the policy needs and names no body to enforce it. No source found names a regulator given that job, and none reports the policy applied to any organisation.

Not found. No source found says a rule that data must be kept in the country is in force.

Data classed as sensitive may sit on a government private cloud or on a public cloud hosted in the country. The policy says there is no law on data residence. Its issue date and effective date are blank, pending signature.

Enforcer named and rule applied. The draft gives the job of ensuring agencies comply with its data classification to the government's principal cloud provider, GICTA, with the Gambia Information Commission, and sets up a working group to monitor compliance. None of that has effect until the policy is issued.

Not found. No source found says a rule that data must be kept in the country is in force.

KEN.summary:

A report of 6 August 2026 says the implementation guidelines of the 2025 Kenya Cloud Policy, published by the Ministry of ICT and the Digital Economy, require top secret State data to be held in a data centre within Kenya. They also bar State entities from hosting data in their own server rooms without the authorisation of a Cloud Adoption Committee, and give them 24 months to migrate.

Enforcer named and rule applied. The nearest held fact is the same report, which names a Cloud Adoption Committee that authorises exceptions to the bar on in-house server rooms. No source found counts the State entities that have moved.

LBY.summary:

It binds banks, branches of foreign banks, fintechs, payment providers, exchange companies and leasing companies, from 1 July 2026.

Enforcer named and rule applied. The central bank, which issued the regulation, supervises the institutions it covers and sets a fine of 100,000 dinars for each violation. It may revoke a licence for repeated gross violations, and each institution must appoint a Libyan data officer as its liaison with the bank. No fine, revocation or exemption under the regulation has been found.

Article 49 sets fines of 200,000 to 400,000 dirhams for the heads of vital entities or infrastructures that host such data abroad, and article 53 makes the law operative once its implementing texts are published. A report of June 2025 says a 2021 law mandates that sensitive data be stored locally, which puts the requirement in effect.

Enforcer named and rule applied. The nearest held fact is the law's penalty article, which sets the fines and, in the text held, does not name the body that imposes them. A report of June 2025 on the country's data governance says Banco de Moçambique Notice 4/GGBM/2003 requires data centres to be located in Mozambique, with replicas abroad allowed only with prior approval, and records no repeal. MWI.summary:
Rule in force. The UN Economic Commission for Africa published its digital trade regulatory profile of Malawi in 2022, with data covering 2014 to 2021. The profile states that Malawi has local storage requirements only for health-related data. The requirement is one of local storage, it applies to health-related data and to no other category, and the profile names no instrument for it. The profile gives no date of its own, so 2022 is its publication date.

Enforcer named and rule applied. The nearest held fact is the same profile, the UN Economic Commission for Africa's digital trade regulatory profile of Malawi. It describes the requirement as one on health-related data alone, within data covering 2014 to 2021, and says nothing further about how the requirement is overseen or applied. NAM.summary:
Rule in force. The Bank of Namibia's Determination on Localization of Core Banking Systems (BID 19), signed on 5 August 2008 and effective from 11 August 2008, requires all authorised banking institutions to locate and maintain their core banking systems in Namibia. The determination defines core banking systems as the systems where accounting and other banking records are kept. The requirement binds every banking institution the Bank authorises.

Enforcer named and rule applied. The determination was issued by the Bank of Namibia under section 71(3) of the Banking Institutions Act 1998 for the banking institutions it authorises. On non-compliance the Bank may pursue any remedial measure under that Act. The text also refers to dispensations already granted to individual institutions, so the Bank has exempted named institutions from the requirement.

NGA.short: Nigeria's central bank ordered in June 2026 payment data be stored in Nigeria from January 2027 and says it will enforce; no penalty is known.
NGA.summary:
Rule in force. Nigeria's rule covers payment data. On 15 June 2026 the Central Bank of Nigeria ordered payment transaction data generated in Nigeria to be stored and managed there by 1 January 2027. The circular binds banks, mobile money operators, switches and all licensed payment operators. In September 2026 industry speakers called the deadline too short and asked for more time. In October 2026 deputy governor Lamido Yuguda held banks to the 2027 date. The National Cloud Policy 2025 requires sensitive government and financial data to be hosted in Nigeria, a May 2026 NSIA release says. A wider rule is in draft, covering data on national security, financial services and health.

Enforcer named and rule applied. The circular came from the central bank's Payments System Supervision Department, for the institutions it licenses. Banks and fintechs say the central bank has not told them how hybrid cloud set-ups are treated. The department says the central bank will begin enforcement and review compliance from 1 January 2027. The bank says it will monitor compliance and may impose supervisory sanctions, though the circular sets no penalty schedule. In October 2026 a NITDA survey presented with the central bank found 22 of 44 financial institutions yet to begin. No order, penalty or exemption has been found.

Not found. No organisation is known to have been ordered, penalised or exempted under the rule. No count of those that have moved data to comply is known.

RWA.short: Rwanda requires public sector data in the government data centre or approved sites, a 2025 brief says; the last known penalty was in 2017.
RWA.summary:
Rule in force. Rwanda's rule is partial. A market brief of July 2025 says there is no blanket localisation requirement in Rwanda, but some data must be stored locally depending on the circumstances. It places that under the 2021 Law on Data Privacy and Protection. Public sector data must be hosted in the government data centre or in facilities meeting Rwanda Development Board standards. Digital Policy Alert says the October 2021 law generally requires personal data to be stored in Rwanda, unless the supervisory authority grants a certificate.

Enforcer named and rule applied. The July 2025 brief says local storage of some data depends on certification by the National Cyber Security Authority. That makes the authority the body that decides where such data may be held. No certificate granted or refused has been found. The one penalty found is older: in May 2017 the Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority fined MTN Rwanda FRW 7.03 billion for hosting its IT services outside the country. No order or penalty from the last three years has been found.

Not found. No source from the last three years names an organisation ordered, penalised or exempted under the rule. None counts those that have moved data to comply.

SDN.short: Sudan has no law requiring data to be kept in the country, a July 2026 study says, and none is being written.
SDN.summary:
Rule in force. Sudan has no rule. A study by the Sudanese Center for Policy Studies of 19 July 2026 says mobile banking data transits infrastructure Sudan neither owns nor regulates, with no statutory requirement governing data localisation or cross-border transfer. The study proposes localisation as a first piece of legislation and reports no drafting. An article of October 2023 likewise states that Sudan has no law imposing data localisation.

Enforcer named and rule applied. No enforcer arises without a rule. The 2023 article reports a former senior central bank official saying the bank and other government bodies work under an undeclared localisation policy, and adds that lookups at the time showed several government websites hosted abroad. An undeclared practice is not a rule and no body is named as enforcing it.

Not found. A newer source than those cited saying a rule is being written.

SEN.summary:

An account of September 2025 says that after the Diamniadio National Datacenter opened in June 2021, President Macky Sall instructed his government to migrate all state data and digital platforms to it and to repatriate all national data hosted outside Senegal. The same account says Senegal requires servers to be housed within its borders. It cites secondary sources and names no legal instrument.

Enforcer named and rule applied. The nearest held fact is that account, which describes the instruction and the data centre it names and no body that checks compliance. No source found names a body that checks compliance with the rule or grants exemptions from it. No source found from the last three years names or counts the public bodies that have moved their data to Diamniadio.

Not found. No source found names a body that enforces the rule: a regulator, agency or ministry unit that checks compliance or grants exemptions.

TUN.summary:
Rule in force. Tunisia's rule covers credit information. Article 21 of decree-law 2022-2 of 4 January 2022 bars credit information companies from transferring their databases outside Tunisia, or from setting up sites outside the country to protect the data given to them. The same article bars them from hosting credit information in the cloud. No wider rule on keeping data in the country has been found.

Enforcer named and rule applied. Under the decree-law the Banque centrale de Tunisie licenses credit information companies, and its governor may fine one 10,000 to 50,000 dinars, suspend its activity for three months or withdraw its licence, after formal notice. No fine, suspension or withdrawal for keeping data abroad has been found, and no source names a company ordered to bring data into Tunisia.

TZA.summary:
Rule in force. Tanzania's rules cover critical infrastructure and the financial sector. The Cybercrimes (Protection of Critical Information Infrastructure) Order, 2026, of 19 June 2026, requires owners of critical information infrastructure to host all related data inside the country. Hosting primary or secondary data abroad needs the Minister's approval. The Bank of Tanzania's Cloud Computing Guidelines of August 2025 bar licensed financial providers from hosting mission-critical systems in a data centre or cloud outside Tanzania. They are issued under the banking and payment systems Acts.

Enforcer named and rule applied. Under the 2026 Order the Minister approves offshore hosting, and the ICT ministry keeps the register and audits the infrastructure at least once a year. The bank guidelines make the Bank of Tanzania the body that approves providers' cloud arrangements. It may impose sanctions, including civil money penalties. No approval, refusal or penalty under either rule is on record.

ZAF.summary:
Rule in force. South Africa's rule covers the state's security data. A presentation by the Department of Communications and Digital Technologies to Parliament's communications committee on 24 February 2026 says the National Data and Cloud Policy provides that government data carrying content on national security and the sovereignty of the Republic shall be stored only in digital infrastructure located within South Africa's borders. An earlier draft went further: a 2025 book chapter reports that the draft commented on in 2021 required a copy of data to be kept within South African borders.

Enforcer named and rule applied. The nearest held fact is the department's presentation, which states the storage rule and names no body that checks it. No source found names a body that checks compliance with the rule or grants exemptions from it. No order or exemption under the policy has been found.

ZMB.summary:
Rule in force. A D4D Hub research paper states that Zambia's Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021 requires sensitive personal data (health records, biometrics, religious beliefs and political opinions) to be stored within the country. It quotes Section 70: sensitive personal data can only be stored in Zambia, and other personal data goes on servers in the Republic unless a transfer is approved. The Act is dated 2021.

Enforcer named and rule applied. The same paper says the Data Protection Commission, established in 2023 under the Act and reporting to the Minister of Technology and Science, enforces it. The paper quotes Section 70 as allowing personal data to leave Zambia only with the approval of both the data subject and the Data Protection Commissioner. The Commission is the body that holds that approval power.

Not found. Nothing found from the last three years names an organisation ordered, penalised or exempted under the rule, or counts those that have moved data to comply.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe's data protection authority requires core banking and critical financial systems to be hosted locally and must approve any exception; no application is known.
ZWE.summary:
Rule in force. Zimbabwe's rule covers highly sensitive systems. In its implementation guidelines for the Cyber and Data Protection Act, published in 2025, the regulator POTRAZ, as the designated Data Protection Authority, states that it will not permit highly sensitive information such as core banking platforms and critical financial systems to be hosted outside Zimbabwe, and that such systems must be hosted locally. The guidelines carry no date of their own.

Enforcer named and rule applied. The guidelines name POTRAZ as the body whose prior written approval is required for any exception to local hosting, and say a request must be backed by a risk assessment and a justification. No approval granted or refused has been found, and no source names an organisation ordered to bring a system into Zimbabwe or penalised.

Not found. No source from the last three years naming an organisation ordered, penalised or exempted under the rule, or counting those that have moved data to comply, is held.

AGO.short: Angola has an authority, appointed in 2019, that fined companies in 2025 and 2026; no yearly count of its rulings is known at September 2026.
AGO.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Lei 22/11 of 17 June 2011 created the Agência de Protecção de Dados as a public-law body with a seven-member board. Decreto Presidencial 214/16 set out its statute, and Decreto Presidencial 277/19 of 6 September 2019 appointed a president and two executive administrators. In 2024 its president signed Circular 02/APD/2024 requiring entities to report personal data breaches, and its FAQ page directs citizens to lodge complaints with it.

Rulings and published figures. The authority fined Lizíria, Lda., owner of Hotel Diamante, the kwanza equivalent of USD 115,000 on 10 August 2026. In June 2026 it fined Crescer Tech about USD 505,000 and Fast Digital Center USD 112,000. Its own register lists 15 fines for 2022 to 2026, six of them in 2026, from US$75,000 to US$525,000 each.

Not found. No count of the authority's decisions, fines or complaints settled, for a period ending in the last two years, is held.

BDI.short: Burundi's 2026 law creates an authority, but no appointment, ruling or published figure is known.
BDI.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The law adopted on 15 January 2026 creates an independent administrative authority responsible for enforcing data protection. It also provides a dedicated body to implement and monitor data protection regimes, and the sponsoring ministry was the Ministry of Interior, Community Development and Public Security. The law was promulgated on 10 March 2026. The sources found name no head or member of the authority and report no appointment, so the authority is set out in law only.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling against an organisation and no published figure has been found. The nearest fact is that the adopted law makes the authority responsible for enforcement, and the law took effect by promulgation in March 2026.

Not found. No source found says the authority's head or members have been appointed.

BEN.short: Benin has an authority with a sitting president in 2026, and it published figures for its work in 2025.
BEN.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Book V of the Digital Code, Articles 462 to 473, established the Autorité de Protection des Données Personnelles as an independent administrative authority. It has a sitting head: president Luciano Hounkponou led a delegation to Lomé on 2 and 3 October 2026. It held open days at Kandi on 6 and 7 October 2026. Seventeen of its officers were sworn in on 14 September 2026. The 2026 finance law opens a programme for it at XOF 738,277,000.

Rulings and published figures. The authority's published 2025 report gives 907 files examined, 64 inspection missions, 20 complaints treated and 75 compliance certificates issued. Its 2015 to 2020 report counts 347 decisions, 136 of them in 2020. On 18 August 2016 it refused Spacetel Benin authorisation to collect biometric subscriber data.

Not found. Nothing on the four questions.

BFA.short: Burkina Faso has an authority, active in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known, and no figures it publishes are known.
BFA.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The 2021 data protection law creates the Commission de l'informatique et des libertés (CIL) as the supervisory authority, with nine members appointed by decree. It is at work. Its president led a training for a minister's cabinet on 11 August 2025. In September 2026 the CIL published a form for applications to transfer personal data abroad. The 2024 finance law gives it its own budget section. On 3 August 2026 the legislative assembly adopted a bill merging the CIL into a new regulator, ARCOD. A decree of 16 October 2026 named W. Louis Modeste Ouédraogo president of the merged regulator.

Rulings and published figures. A guide to the 2021 law says the CIL may issue warnings, formal notices, injunctions and fines. No ruling against a named organisation has been found. The only figures found are budget figures. The 2024 finance law appropriated XOF 857,062,000 for the CIL, and 799,459,500 was executed. The mid-year review at 30 June 2025 lists it again.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. No source names ARCOD's members other than its president.

BWA.short: Botswana has an authority, and in July 2026 it ruled against a government body; no figures it publishes are known.
BWA.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Information and Data Protection Commission works under the Data Protection Act No. 18 of 2024. The Minister said it was established in 2022, and in July 2025 its commissioner had three contract officers while the deputy commissioner and two director posts were unfilled. Mmegi reported on 11 February 2026 that Kepaletswe Somolekae is the newly appointed commissioner. In July 2026 it reviewed the E-Payslip portal and guided DPSM through compliance.

Rulings and published figures. In a public notice dated 17 July 2026 the commission issued a Determination and an Enforcement Notice against DPSM for contraventions of the Act. It ordered the ePayslip portal suspended and a data protection impact assessment and revised privacy notice submitted within one month, with an administrative fine possible for non-compliance. DPSM suspended the portal on 22 July 2026. No published figures have been found.

Not found. No count of the authority's decisions, fines or complaints settled, for a period ending in the last two years, is held.

CAF.short: The Central African Republic had no authority appointed in January 2026; no ruling against an organisation and no published figures are known.
CAF.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Article 57 of Loi n° 24.001 gives the ministry in charge of the digital economy twelve months from promulgation to set up the data protection agency, and meanwhile vests the agency's missions in that ministry. The text names no composition, seat or financing. Jurist Laurent-Fabrice Zengue writes in September 2025 that the law gives the agency its missions and powers but does not organise it, with an interim arrangement for its non-operation. Data Protection Africa states that the authority has not yet been appointed, as of 28 January 2026.

Rulings and published figures. The nearest held fact is that, under the same article, the ministry holds the agency's missions in the meantime. The law was promulgated in January 2024. No ruling against an organisation and no published figures have been found, and no agency has yet issued any decision or report that a source records.

Not found. No source found says the authority's head or members have been appointed.

CIV.short: In 2026 Côte d'Ivoire's telecoms regulator acts as its data protection authority; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
CIV.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Law No. 2013-450 of 19 June 2013 governs personal data protection, and a decree of 4 February 2015 names ARTCI as the body that receives declarations and imposes withdrawals and fines under it, with authorisation requests ruled on within one month. A 2022 fact sheet says a data protection authority is appointed, with 7 members serving up to 6 years. On 3 August 2026 ARTCI, styling itself the Autorité de Protection des Données Personnelles, issued a communique inviting controllers to use CERTINUM.

Rulings and published figures. The nearest held fact is the power the 2015 decree gives ARTCI: to rule on authorisation requests within one month and to impose withdrawals and fines. In its 3 August 2026 communique ARTCI says it launched CERTINUM on 2 July 2026.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found, and no published figures.

CMR.short: Cameroon's 2024 law creates a data protection authority, yet to be set up in 2025; no ruling or published figures are known.
CMR.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Law No. 2024/017 of 23 December 2024 sets up the Autorité as an independent public body in charge of data protection. The law names no head or members. A July 2025 commentary says the Authority was yet to be established. In September 2026 the OBS-CC observatory said it was still not installed, and the decree to put it in place had not been taken. The Presidency also publishes the English text of the law.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling or published figure is on record, since the Authority has not yet started work. The nearest fact is its mandate. The law of 23 December 2024 gives it supervision, notification and enforcement powers over those who process personal data.

Not found. No source says the Authority's head or members have been appointed. No ruling or published figure was found.

COD.short: In 2026 the DRC's data protection authority is still not set up; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
COD.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Article 262 of the Digital Code, Ordonnance-loi n° 23/010 of 13 March 2023, creates an independent administrative Autorité de protection des données with legal personality, and says a Prime Minister's decree will fix its organisation and functioning. A ministerial order of 17 August 2024 gave its missions to the telecoms regulator ARPTIC pending its establishment. Articles 267 to 268 set the membership conditions and a four-member bureau. On 13 September 2026, Beto.cd reports that the authority is not installed.

Rulings and published figures. The nearest held fact is a statement by the Minister of Digital Economy, reported on 16 March 2026, that a network of data protection officers precedes the coming creation of a national Data Protection Authority.

Not found. No source found says the authority's head or members have been appointed, and no ruling or published figures have been found.

COG.short: Congo has had a data protection commission since January 2026; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
COG.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Congo's National Personal Data Protection Commission was inaugurated in January 2026 after its members were appointed under Decree No. 2025-538 of 31 December 2025, and its President, Vice President and Rapporteur were elected at the first meeting. On 22 January 2026 the ICT minister installed the members and called it an independent body, so the commission has both a legal basis and sitting members.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling against an organisation and no published figures have been found. The nearest fact is the minister's January 2026 description of the commission as able to advise, warn and sanction, which states a power, not its use. Nothing found shows a decision against a company or public body, a complaint count or an annual report from the commission since it was installed.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found, and no published figures.

COM.short: Comoros law creates a data protection authority, but it was not yet operating in 2024; no appointments, rulings or figures are known.
COM.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The 2014 data protection law institutes a Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés in Article 19, with nine members to be named by decree under Article 24. The text records no appointment. A 2025 review states the law establishes a National Authority for the Protection of Personal Data, which as of 2024 was not yet constituted or operational. The law therefore names the body, but the evidence found shows it on paper only.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling against an organisation and no published figures have been found. The nearest fact is the 2025 review's statement that the authority was not operational as of 2024. An authority that is not operating has issued no decisions, and none has been found, nor any complaint count or annual report.

Not found. No source found says the authority's head or members have been appointed, and no ruling or published figures have been found.

CPV.short: Cabo Verde has an operating data protection commission in 2025, but no published figures; no ruling against an organisation is known.
CPV.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The National Data Protection Commission (CNPD) is in operation, with a decade of existence completed in 2025 under the president, Faustino Varela, and marked its tenth anniversary in March 2025. The Assembly's budget appropriates CVE 36,313,115 for 2025, up from CVE 35,255,451 in 2024, with no own revenue, so it depends on the Assembly's vote. Its head signed a joint statement with 60 other authorities on 23 February 2026.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling against an organisation has been found. The CNPD published no activity report for any year since 2016, so no counts of decisions exist. Its 2024 activity plan, dated 27 December 2023, set out planned inspections, guidance and international meetings, but it is a plan and not a record of rulings.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

DJI.short: Djibouti's 2025 Digital Code creates a data protection authority; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
DJI.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Digital Code's data-protection regime creates the National Commission for the Protection of Personal Data (CNDP), independent with administrative and financial autonomy, as reviewed on 5 November 2025. That review does not say the commission has been constituted or its members appointed, so the law is the only step the sources show. The National Assembly voted the Code on 30 June 2025, and Jones Day reports that the regime establishes the CNDP.

Rulings and published figures. The nearest held fact is from the same 2025 Jones Day report, which frames the competent authorities as still to be put into operation. Nothing in the sources found shows the commission at work in practice. They record no ruling by the commission against an organisation and no figures it has published.

Not found. No source found says the authority's head or members have been appointed, and none records a ruling or published figures.

DZA.short: Algeria has a working authority with a named president in 2026; it has issued decisions but no ruling against an organisation or figures are known.
DZA.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Law 18-07 is enforced by the national data protection authority (ANPDP), and Samir Bourehil is named as its president in July 2026, attending a study day alongside the Justice and Interior ministers. The authority adopted a deliberation at its sitting of 15 July 2026, signed by its president with twelve members named at the foot. It also issues authorisations and receives declarations of processing as of December 2025. The Interior Minister said in December 2025 that infractions over civil status and identity data will be sanctioned in coordination with the authority. An earlier US commercial guide from September 2024 already named it as the enforcer of Law 18-07.

Rulings and published figures. The authority issued a decision in early 2026 on employee and candidate drug test results, and its July 2026 deliberation sets rules on publishing images on digital platforms. No ruling against a named organisation has been found, and no published figures.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found, and no figures it has published.

EGY.short: Egypt has a data protection authority in 2026, still led by an acting chief; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
EGY.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Personal Data Protection Center (PDPC) is confirmed as the supervisory authority for implementation, monitoring and enforcement under the executive regulations of November 2025. A 7 August 2026 report shows it acting under Law 151 of 2020, under an acting chief executive, Susan El-Okbawy, who is described as affiliated to the ICT ministry. In October 2026 it launched its electronic portal for accreditation, licence and permit applications.

Rulings and published figures. The nearest held fact is the licensing and breach-handling role the acting chief executive described in August 2026, with a compliance deadline of November 2026 for organisations covered by the law. The sources describe a body that is licensing and preparing for enforcement. No ruling against an organisation has been found, and no figures published by the centre.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found, and no figures it has published.

ERI.short: Eritrea has no data protection authority and has issued no rulings or figures, as of 2026.
ERI.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Law Lab Africa states that no supervisory authority has been established in Eritrea, as of 1 August 2026. Levellers states, in a page reviewed on 8 June 2026, that Eritrea has no data protection statute and has not appointed a data protection authority. The Horn of Africa Initiative matrix update of June 2025 says Eritrea remains without regulatory oversight for data protection, while Kenya, Somalia and Ethiopia have established authorities.

Rulings and published figures. Law Lab Africa found no enforcement decisions for Eritrea and none published, in its verification pass of 1 August 2026. Levellers states there is no data protection authority to register with or appeal to, so none issues rulings. A Data Protection Africa fact sheet, last updated 24 May 2022, records no authority report and no public report.

Not found. Nothing is held on any plan to set up an authority or pass a data protection law.

ETH.short: Ethiopia has an authority, the Communications Authority, in 2025. No ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
ETH.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The proclamation designates the Ethiopian Communications Authority as the regulator, in an overview of July 2024. By November 2025 Shega described the Authority, whose mandate was extended from telecom regulation to data protection, as enforcing the law. Its Director General, Balcha Reba, said data processors and collectors now need the Authority's permission and that staffing and technical capacity are being expanded.

Rulings and published figures. The Shega article of 15 November 2025 describes enforcement as on a slow path, one year after the law. It names the permission requirement for processors and collectors as the Authority's current step. The overview of the proclamation says only that the Authority is designated as regulator, and names no decision, fine or order against an organisation.

Not found. No ruling against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. No published count of decisions or complaints has been found.

GAB.short: Gabon has an authority and fined a bank 90 million FCFA in 2024. No published figures are known.
GAB.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Article 7 of Loi n°025/2023 creates the APDPVP as an independent administrative authority, with powers to authorise processing, receive complaints and fine from CFA 1 million to 100 million. Its 25 April 2024 plenary sat with a named president, vice-president and six other commissioners, appointed by Council of Ministers decision of 12 July 2023. Its president was still speaking as head of the authority on 4 September 2026.

Rulings and published figures. By deliberation n°073 of 25 April 2024, on a complaint of 27 November 2023, the APDPVP plenary fined Citibank Gabon S.A. 90,000,000 FCFA. It found the bank had diverted employee data from its declared purpose and processed ethnic-origin data, and it added a two-month formal notice.

Not found. No count of the authority's decisions, fines or complaints settled, for a period ending in the last two years, is held.

GHA.short: Ghana's data protection commission directed named unregistered companies to report to the police in October 2026; no source found reports yearly counts of its rulings.
GHA.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Data Protection Commission describes itself as an independent statutory body established under the Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843). In August 2025 the Minister for Communication swore in its new governing board, chaired by Teki Akuetteh. Its 2026 budget estimate is GHS 9,720,400, all from internally generated funds, with 39 staff. The Commission's own page names its Executive Director, Dr Arnold Kavaarpuo, and a board member at a vehicle commissioning on 20 February 2026, and a GNA report says it operates only from its head office. In October 2026 the Commission publicly warned the Minority Caucus, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and media houses over the disclosure of 1,964 evacuees' personal data.

Rulings and published figures. On 7 September 2026 the Communications Minister said the Commission's regulatory activity rose 51.5 per cent and newly registered data controllers 98.4 per cent in the first half of 2026. On 13 October 2026 it said it had registered 2,575 data controllers in 2026 and was adding spot checks, inspections and complaint investigations. It ran a field enforcement exercise in Accra on 12 October 2026 under Act 843. On 14 October 2026 it directed named companies, among them Polytex Ghana Limited, JA Biney Packaging and Menkish Impex Ltd, to report to the police and regularise their registration for operating unregistered or with expired certificates.

Not found. No published yearly count of the Commission's decisions, fines or complaints settled is held.

GIN.short: Guinea's 2016 law provides for a data protection authority, but none is known to be in place, to have ruled, or to publish figures.
GIN.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The 2016 cybersecurity and personal data protection law defines an Autorité de Protection and gives it functions covering declarations, authorisations, transfer approval and investigation. It names no constituted body or members. In June 2024 the National Transition Council's commissions debated a bill to establish the authority, with members' designation and mandates still contested and plenary adoption pending. The CNT page gives the authority's name as Autorité de Protection des Données à caractère Personnel.

Rulings and published figures. The nearest held fact is the 2016 law, which gives the authority power to investigate and to approve transfers, issue guidelines and receive processing declarations, though declarations go to the authority 'designated by regulation'. No ruling or published figure from the authority has been found.

Not found. No source found says the authority's head or members have been appointed, and no ruling or figure has been found.

GMB.short: The Gambia's 2025 law names the Information Commission as its data protection authority, which was acting by 2026; no ruling or published figure is known.
GMB.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2025 (Act No. 11 of 2025, assented 7 November 2025) names the Information Commission established under the Access to Information Act as the Commission, with Part 8 on its functions, powers and fines. A review of 26 December 2025 describes it as an independent oversight Commission. In August 2026 a notice has the Information Commission of The Gambia developing a communication strategy on the Act, alongside the Access to Information Act, 2021.

Rulings and published figures. The nearest held fact is that the Act lets the Commission assess cross-border transfers and impose conditions, a power described in February 2026. No ruling or published figure from the Commission has been found, and no count of complaints or registrations.

Not found. No ruling by the Commission against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

GNB.short: Guinea-Bissau has no data protection authority as of 2026, so it has made no ruling against an organisation and publishes no figures.
GNB.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Guinea-Bissau has no dedicated national data protection authority, a speaker said on 22 September 2026, with these matters handled by several institutions sector by sector. The Data Protection Africa factsheet, published 25 May 2022, states that the country has no data protection law and that its authority is not appointed.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling against an organisation and no published figures have been found for Guinea-Bissau, in 2026 or any earlier year. The nearest held fact is the factsheet of 25 May 2022, which states that the data protection authority is not appointed, so there is no body in place to rule on a complaint, to fine an organisation or to publish a count of its work.

Not found. Nothing is held on any plan or draft to create an authority, or on any ruling or figures.

GNQ.short: Equatorial Guinea's 2016 law creates an authority, but by 2022 it was not appointed; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
GNQ.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Articles 15 and 29 of Law No. 1/2016, dated 22 July 2016, name the Órgano Rector de Protección de Datos Personales as the supervisory body, with a Secretaría Técnica and a Registro General under it. They state that it is to be created by a decree that will fix its structure. Data Protection Africa, in a factsheet published 23 May 2022, states that the authority is not yet appointed or operational.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling against an organisation and no published figures have been found. The nearest held fact is the factsheet of 23 May 2022, which states that the authority created by the 2016 law is not yet operational, so it had no decisions or figures to publish.

Not found. No source says whether the head or members of the authority have been appointed since 2022, and none reports a ruling or figures.

KEN.short: Kenya has had an authority since 2020 and it has fined businesses; its only published count is a running total, not a yearly figure.
KEN.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Office of the Data Protection Commissioner was set up under the Data Protection Act, 2019. Immaculate Kassait has been the first commissioner since 2020, TechTrends KE reports. On 30 September 2026 the Public Service Commission had shortlisted 13 of 152 applicants to succeed her. Its March 2025 bulletin lists offices in seven cities. In April 2026 it opened an investigation into privacy concerns over Meta's smart glasses. The Standard says the office launched an ISO 9001 quality system on 14 July 2026. On 14 October 2026 it hosted a study visit by Sri Lanka's authority.

Rulings and published figures. By September 2024 the office had fined at least nine businesses KES 26,275,000 in all, Cadmus Cyber Solutions states. They include Oppo Kenya in 2022 (KES 5m) and SBM Bank in 2024 (KES 450,000). The office's own bulletin gives running totals to March 2025. It counts 7,128 complaints received, 97 percent resolved, and 215 determinations. Penalties fell on 10 entities, and 103 people won compensation.

Not found. No count of decisions, fines or complaints settled covers a period ending in the last two years. The 215 determinations carry no period.

LBR.short: Liberia's 2026 Act gives the work to an existing commissioner; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
LBR.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act of 2024, printed on 23 March 2026, gives data protection functions to the Independent Information Commissioner in sections 8 and 10 (the printed Act). That body was created by the Freedom of Information Act of 2010. Before the Act, in February 2025, a minister told the Africa-China Reporting Project that Liberia had no national data protection authority, and in June 2025 the Liberian Observer reported that the country still lacked a dedicated data protection law.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling against an organisation and no published figures have been found. The nearest held fact is that the printed Act of 23 March 2026 does not say the Commissioner has begun acting under it.

Not found. Nothing found says the Commissioner or its members have been appointed under the Act, or that any ruling or figures have been published.

LBY.short: SMEX said in July 2026 that Libya has no functioning data protection authority; no ruling or published figure is known.
LBY.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The only held statement is dated 22 July 2026, when SMEX said that Libya currently has no functioning data protection authority. It was made in SMEX's review of Libya's new artificial intelligence strategy, which SMEX says was built without public participation, and it describes the position at that date: no authority is working, so none can be counted as appointed and in office.

Rulings and published figures. Nothing found on rulings or published figures. The nearest held fact is the SMEX statement of 22 July 2026 that Libya has no functioning data protection authority. With no working authority at that date, there is no body to issue rulings, decisions, annual reports or complaint figures of its own.

Not found. Nothing found names a body that was ever set up, or any ruling or published figure.

LSO.short: Lesotho's 2012 law creates a commission, unappointed in 2025; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
LSO.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Data Protection Act (Act 5 of 2012) establishes a Data Protection Commission, but the law firm Z. Mayet and Associates states that the Commission and its Commissioner had not been appointed as at 31 October 2025, so the regulator did not exist in practice. Cenfri said the same of the Commission in an article published on 23 March 2026: the Data Protection Commission under the Act has remained unappointed, with no date given for that statement.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling against an organisation and no published figures have been found. The nearest held fact is the position stated by Z. Mayet and Associates in October 2025, that neither the Commission nor its Commissioner had been appointed, so the regulator did not exist in practice.

Not found. Nothing found says the Commission or its Commissioner has since been appointed, or that any ruling or figures have been published.

MAR.short: Morocco has an authority, the CNDP, active in 2026; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
MAR.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Morocco's CNDP, the national commission for the control of personal data protection, works under Law 09-08. It was installed in 2010, and its president says it began fifteen years ago. In August 2026 it informed parties and citizens of the data rules for the 23 September 2026 elections and opened a 3020 public line. It keeps the national register of processing operations for 2010 to 31 December 2022, and signed a cooperation memorandum with Portugal's authority on 8 February 2026.

Rulings and published figures. The nearest held fact is procedural: on 28 November 2025 the CNDP validated five new deliberations, D-939 to D-943 of 2025, showing it acting as the supervisory body, and the Official Gazette published its members under Law 09-08 in 2012. Its president says its alert system is being strengthened, up to sanctions.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

MDG.short: Madagascar's authority, the CMIL, was sworn in during 2025; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known for 2026.
MDG.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Law 2014-038 provides for the CMIL: article 28 institutes an independent authority of nine members with regulatory and sanctioning powers. It had still not been created in February 2025. Seven members were sworn in at the Cour suprême on 4 August 2025, and the bureau was elected on 14 August 2025. Midi Madagasikara reports the Council of Ministers validated the decree naming its members, and a government announcement of 27 March 2026 says the CMIL is now effectively in place.

Rulings and published figures. The CMIL's own annual report, published January 2026, says no processing declaration has been registered, citizen complaints went untreated for ten years, and it still lacks premises and staff, with 104 posts targeted in the 2026 Finance Law and none yet recruited.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

MLI.short: Mali has an authority, the APDP, which fined a clinic and published figures for 2025.
MLI.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Mali's APDP is an independent administrative authority of 15 members under Article 20 of Law 2013-015. It held its second ordinary session on 3 August 2026 with all commissioners present, and runs regional offices at Kayes, Sikasso, Segou and Mopti. It opened a Ségou antenna on 4 December 2025. On 18 November 2025 its president signed the operational roadmap of the AES coordination framework with Burkina Faso and Niger.

Rulings and published figures. For 2025 the APDP annual report, as summarised by Sahel Tribune, gives about 1,000 formal notices, fines totalling 22 million FCFA and 51 complaints, 28 of them handled. It fined a Bamako clinic 5 million FCFA for obstructing a verification mission linked to an undeclared video-surveillance system. In June 2025 it also fined a company 5 million FCFA for refusing a verification mission.

Not found. No gap is recorded on whether the authority exists, has ruled or publishes figures.

MOZ.short: Mozambique has no data protection authority yet; none has ruled against an organisation or published figures, as of 2025.
MOZ.summary:
Named in law and appointed. A UNECA inception report of June 2025 states that Mozambique has no data regulatory authority, though INTIC, INCM, INAGE and CEDSIF oversee parts of data governance. The World Bank restructuring paper says the Data Protection Office was not yet established as of October 2025. A September 2025 review says the draft law would give the role to the existing Regulatory Authority for ICT, alongside a National Council chaired by the Prime Minister.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling and no published figure has been found, and no body exists to issue them. The nearest held fact is that the Data Protection Office, which the World Bank paper says is not yet established, had its project funding cut from US$18m to US$11m. The same inception report names a Data Protection Bill.

Not found. Whether an authority has been established since October 2025, and any ruling or figure it has published.

MRT.short: Mauritania has a data protection authority, in session in 2026; no ruling against an organisation and no published figures are known.
MRT.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Article 64 of Law 2017-020 creates an independent Authority for Personal Data Protection attached to the Prime Minister, with its composition and the appointment of members left to a decree. Decree 2022-13 of 18 February 2022 is cited for its composition and operation. The authority is in session: it held monthly meetings on 29 April 2026 and 30 June 2026, and its president was sworn in for a second term on 7 October 2026.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling against a named organisation and no published figures have been found. The nearest held fact is that the authority adopted deliberation 005/2025 on 30 July 2025, and met on 14 July 2025 to adopt deliberation 004/2025, both general rules rather than findings against an organisation.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

MUS.short: Mauritius has a data protection authority and published 2024 figures on complaints and breaches; no ruling against an organisation is known.
MUS.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Data Protection Office has operated since 16 February 2009 and enforces the Data Protection Act 2017. Its 2024 annual report is signed by Data Protection Commissioner Drudeisha Madhub. In June 2026 regulations on data protection officers gave the Office roles in receiving notifications, certifying officers and approving training institutions.

Rulings and published figures. The Office publishes annual figures. For January to December 2024 it reports 179 new complaints, 158 of them on CCTV, and 39 complaints closed. It also reports 105 personal data breaches notified, 112 cross-border transfers authorised and 12 rejected under section 36, 10 impact assessments received and four compliance inspections. The figures are the Office's own and cover the 2024 calendar year. No ruling against a named organisation has been found.

Not found. Nothing on the four questions.

MWI.short: Malawi's regulator MACRA has acted as its data protection authority since 2024; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
MWI.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Section 4 of the Data Protection Act, 2024 designates the Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority (MACRA) as the Data Protection Authority, and the Act came into force on 3 June 2024. In November 2025 the World Bank said MACRA had appointed an acting Data Protection Commissioner and recruited staff from its own budget. In July 2026 Daniel Chiwoni was named as its Head of Data Protection, and a World Bank-funded consultancy is developing the authority's institutional structure and policies.

Rulings and published figures. In October 2025 the authority issued guidelines on personal data breach notification and a guideline and checklist on compliance. In July 2026 it consulted stakeholders on proposed registration fees, and in September 2026 GIZ was supporting its work on audits and investigations.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found, and no published figures have been found.

NAM.short: No law names a data protection authority in Namibia; only draft bills of 2020 and 2022 do, and no rulings or figures are known.
NAM.summary: Not found. No law held names an authority, and no source dated in the last three years says the country has none. An authority is named only in draft bills of 2020 and 2022.

NER.short: Niger abolished its data protection authority in June 2026 and repealed the law founding it; no source found says whether the ministries do the job.
NER.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Article 6 of Law 2022-59, as amended by Law 2023-31, creates the Haute Autorité de Protection des Données à caractère Personnel (HAPDP), attached to the Presidency, with ten members named by decree. Its president took office on 18 September 2024, and on 18 November 2025 the HAPDP signed the AES data-protection roadmap with Burkina Faso and Mali. A presidential decree of 8 June 2026 abolished the HAPDP, ending its officials' functions and passing its missions to the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of the Interior, and an ordonnance of the same day repealed the provisions of the 2022 law that founded it.

Rulings and published figures. The HAPDP president said in July 2025 that the plenary deliberates on authorisations and sanctions, and a Le Sahel profile of September 2024 gives it powers of inspection and administrative and financial sanction under articles 92-106.

Not found. Nothing says the Justice and Interior ministries are supervising data protection since the authority was abolished.

NGA.short: Nigeria has a data protection commission that fined Multichoice 766 million naira in 2025; no yearly count of its rulings is known.
NGA.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The 2023 Data Protection Act created a formal Data Protection Commission. It is headed by National Commissioner Vincent Olatunji, who said in September 2026 that it generated over N12 billion in revenue over three years. It keeps a registration list of Data Processors of Major Importance and issued a Notice of Investigation on 1 April 2026.

Rulings and published figures. On 18 February 2025 the Commission issued a Final Order fining Meta $32.8 million. It found violations of the data rights of over 60 million Nigerians. The 58-page Order also covered consent, minors' data and transfers abroad. A consent judgment on 3 November 2025 dropped the fine, and under the court-approved settlement Meta funds a two-year programme. In 2025 the Commission also fined Multichoice Nigeria N766,242,500 for breaching the Act.

Not found. No count of the authority's decisions, fines or complaints settled has been found for the last two years.

RWA.short: Rwanda's cyber security authority is its named data protection supervisor in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
RWA.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The National Cyber Security Authority acts as the supervisory authority for personal data protection and privacy under the Data Protection Act, as an article of 26 January 2026 states. It was published as Rwanda observed Data Privacy Week, held on 26 to 30 January 2026. The Act itself is recorded as introduced on 15 October 2021, and the same article is the source for both facts. The East African Community said in December 2024 that Rwanda is among five of its eight Partner States that had established dedicated data protection authorities.

Rulings and published figures. The nearest held fact is that the authority was the named supervisor under the Act in January 2026. No ruling against a named organisation, no fine and no count of complaints or decisions has been found for the authority in the last three years, so there is nothing further to state here.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

SDN.short: A 2022 factsheet says Sudan has no data protection authority; nothing more recent is known, so no stage is set.
SDN.summary: Not found. No law held names an authority. A factsheet last updated on 24 May 2022 says Sudan has no data protection authority appointed, and no source from the last three years says whether that still holds.

SEN.short: Senegal has an authority, created in 2008. It has ruled against organisations, in 2024 and 2026, and publishes quarterly figures.
SEN.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Commission de protection des données personnelles (CDP) is an independent administrative authority set up by law no. 2008-12 of 25 January 2008. It was acting in the April to June 2026 quarter, holding two plenary sessions and issuing decisions, and in September 2026 its permanent secretary described joint interoperability work with the DAF. Its president has signed a partnership convention with Benin's authority.

Rulings and published figures. In April 2024 the CDP's plenary session served a formal notice on SOLID SA, operator of the Kay Voter platform, and in March 2026 it ordered a company to uninstall a meeting-room camera. It publishes quarterly figures, including 317 files handled in January to March 2026 and 195 files handled in April to June 2026.

Not found. Nothing further is held on the four questions.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone has no authority yet; one is named only in a 2025 bill. No rulings or figures are known.
SLE.summary: Not found. No law held names an authority, and no source from the last three years says the country has none. An authority is named only in a bill of 2025.

SOM.short: Somalia has an authority, inaugurated in 2024. No ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
SOM.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Article 6 of the Data Protection Act establishes the Data Protection Authority as an independent agency, and it was inaugurated on 24 February 2024. The law provides for a General Manager and a Board of up to nine members to be appointed within two years. By June 2026 it was accepting registration applications from controllers and processors.

Rulings and published figures. The nearest held fact is that it issued its Registration Guidelines, version 1.0 of January 2026, issued under Law No. 005 of 2023, setting fees, a 30-day approval timeline and mandatory registration. Its own service page lists the registration forms it issues under Article 10 of the Act. No ruling against an organisation and no published figures have been found.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

SSD.short: South Sudan has no data protection authority as of 2026, so it has made no rulings and published no figures.
SSD.summary:
Named in law and appointed. South Sudan has no data protection authority in place. A 2022 factsheet stated that none had been appointed and that no law established one. In December 2024, the Tanzania Times reported the East African Community as saying South Sudan was yet to form one. In February 2026, Digital Rights Frontlines said the country still lacks a fully operational, independent authority and that the government intends to introduce a Data Protection Bill. Radio Tamazuj reported in late 2025 that a draft bill, once passed, would establish a Data Protection Commission to protect the personal data of South Sudanese online users.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling against an organisation and no published figures have been found, because no authority exists to issue them. The nearest held fact is the February 2026 statement that the country lacks an operational, independent authority, which the 2022 factsheet had said in the same terms four years earlier.

Not found. Whether the draft bill has been passed, and when a commission would be appointed, is not held.

STP.short: São Tomé and Príncipe has had a data protection agency since at least 2022; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
STP.summary:
Named in law and appointed. São Tomé and Príncipe has a National Personal Data Protection Agency, the ANPDP, which the 2022 ALT Advisory factsheet says Law 03/2016 establishes and which has an appointed head. In 2026 Téla Nón described it as the body that by law authorises and supervises all data processing, and Macau's data protection office signed a cooperation memorandum with it, signed for the agency by its president, on 1 June 2026. It was a founding member of the Lusophone Data Protection Network, and its president attended the network's first meeting in August 2025.

Rulings and published figures. The 2022 factsheet calls the agency operational and relatively active in authorisations, resolutions and opinions. A 2024 International Bar Association chapter says the agency imposes fines and ancillary measures under the law, but it names no sanction, decision or count. No ruling against a named organisation and no published figures have been found.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

SWZ.short: Eswatini has a data protection authority and issued enforcement notices to three organisations in 2024 and 2025; no counts of decisions are known.
SWZ.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Data Protection Act 2022 designates the Eswatini Communications Commission as the Eswatini Data Protection Authority, as an authority notice states, with powers to investigate breaches, resolve complaints and impose sanctions. It is acting: in July 2026 it began validation workshops on draft health-data guidelines under an acting chief executive, and in September 2026 it was running an outreach campaign with information desks in major towns. In early 2026 it issued a directive requiring controllers and processors to map their data by 31 March 2026.

Rulings and published figures. The authority's own enforcement page lists enforcement notices under section 41 of the Act, issued in June 2024 to MTN Eswatini and to Liberty Life Swaziland Limited, and in March 2025 to the Royal Science Technology Park. Notice No. 3/2024 found MTN Eswatini in breach and gave it a warning with eleven directed measures. The registration regime for organisations was in place by February 2026.

Not found. No count of the authority's decisions, fines or complaints settled, for a period ending in the last two years, is held.

SYC.short: Seychelles has an authority, active since 2023; no ruling against an organisation and no figures for its rulings are known.
SYC.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Section 5 of the Data Protection Act, 2023 names the Information Commission as the authority, with powers to investigate, audit, issue enforcement notices and impose fines up to SCR200,000. The Commission says it took on the mandate at the end of December 2023. Its 2025 annual report shows a Chief Information Commissioner, two Information Commissioners and a chief executive in post.

Rulings and published figures. The Commission reports each year on the Act: its 2024 annual report notes recruitment and staffing challenges for the new Act, and the National Assembly lists the 2025 report as published on 13 April 2026. It is advertising a Senior Data Protection Analyst post. No ruling against a named organisation has been found.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. No source found says what the annual reports record about enforcement.

TCD.short: Chad's data protection directorate had its director and deputy appointed by decree in June 2026; no rulings or figures are known.
TCD.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Decree 2011/PR/2026 of 1 June 2026 appointed a director, replacing a predecessor, and a deputy director of the Direction du contrôle et de la protection des données personnelles, a directorate of the Agence Nationale de Sécurité Informatique et de Certification Electronique (ANSICE). The directorate carries the control and protection of personal data in its title, and its two senior posts were filled by presidential decree in mid-2026. A July 2026 legal analysis states that Loi n°007/PR/2015 gives ANSICE the formalities for data transfers.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling, fine or order against a named organisation, and no published count of decisions or complaints, has been found. The nearest held fact is the same June 2026 decree filling the senior posts of the personal data directorate, which concerns who leads the body and not what it has decided.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

TGO.short: Togo has an authority, active since 2024; no ruling against an organisation is known, and no figures it publishes are known.
TGO.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Article 55 of the 2019 data protection law creates a national authority, the IPDCP, whose president the President of the Republic appoints by decree. It became operational in 2024 under Colonel Bédiani Belei, who says it holds powers of control, injunction and sanction, and launched its activities on 28 March 2025 in Lomé. On 2 and 3 October 2026 it hosted a delegation from Benin's authority in Lomé for a working session under a cooperation agreement.

Rulings and published figures. Its recent work is training and cooperation. It trained its first 32 data protection correspondents in June 2026, ran a first certification session on 30 September 2026 in Atakpamé, and signed a cooperation agreement with Mali's authority on 23 September 2026. It also signed a cooperation accord with the broadcast regulator on 10 December 2025, and on 19 October 2026 placed a team in that regulator's monitoring service. No ruling against a named organisation has been found.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. No figures the authority publishes are known.

TUN.short: Tunisia has an authority, appointed in 2021, but a 2026 report says it is at a standstill; no ruling or figures are known.
TUN.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The 2004 organic law names a national authority for personal data protection, the Instance. It gives the Instance powers over declarations, authorisations and transfers. A government decree of 16 April 2021 appointed twelve named members for three years. A decree of 15 May 2020 puts the citizen-ID register under its control, and any person may lodge an objection with it. A bill tabled in July 2025 provides for a new personal data protection authority. It passes the 2004 authority's property, files and data to the new one.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling against an organisation and no published figures have been found. In October 2026 the Forum Chawki Gaddes said the authority's activities are at a standstill and called for its reactivation.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found. No renewal of the members appointed in April 2021 for three years has been found.

TZA.short: Tanzania has an authority that is working in 2026 and ruled against organisations in 2025; no published figures are known.
TZA.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Section 6 of the Personal Data Protection Act establishes the Personal Data Protection Commission as a body corporate, with a seven-member Board and a Director General. It is acting. Director General Dr Emmanuel Mkilia announced on-site inspections in Dodoma on 28 August 2026. The Commission ran the eighth phase of its data protection officer training on 7-8 October 2026 for over 300 people. It certifies data protection officers under a programme launched with the Open University of Tanzania on 14 July 2026.

Rulings and published figures. On 19 August 2025 the Commission ruled against an Instagram business page that the report does not name. It awarded the complainant TZS 20 million, fined the page TZS 5 million and ordered a newborn's photos deleted within 14 days. It also ruled in Abdul Said Naumanga v. Mi Casa Company Limited, awarding TZS 20,000,000 and ordering the complainant's data deleted. In October 2026 the Commission was investigating many complaints about lenders selling phones on credit, Mwananchi reports.

Not found. No count of the authority's decisions, fines or complaints settled has been found for the last two years.

UGA.short: Uganda has an authority that is working in 2026 and ruled against Google in 2025 and WhatsApp in 2026; no published figures are known.
UGA.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Personal Data Protection Office, established under the Data Protection and Privacy Act, is headed by director Baker Birikujja, who addressed an ISACA Kampala breakfast on 18 August 2026. It briefed government IT officers on data protection on 13 August 2026. It keeps a register of data collectors, controllers and processors, and a report describes it as an independent office under NITA-U. In December 2025 the director brought a prosecution against a company's finance manager, and NITA-U and the Office launched a six-month data protection campaign.

Rulings and published figures. On 18 July 2025 the Office found Google LLC in breach of the registration and cross-border transfer duties and ordered it to register and document its transfer compliance within 30 days. On 20 February 2026 it partly upheld the AdLegal International complaint and issued five corrective orders to WhatsApp LLC, with no fine. By letter of 17 July 2026 it confirmed that WhatsApp had carried out the measures on time.

Not found. No count of the authority's decisions, fines or complaints settled has been found for a period ending in the last two years.

ZAF.short: South Africa has an authority that has fined and ruled against organisations since 2023, and it published complaint figures for 2024/25.
ZAF.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Information Regulator was established on 1 December 2016 to monitor and enforce POPIA and PAIA. Its annual report for the year to 31 March 2025 describes an independent body under section 39 of POPIA that held 4 ordinary and 40 special meetings. National Treasury appropriated R135.7m for it for 2025/26. On 11 September 2026 Parliament's Justice Committee invited comment on candidates for vacant positions on it. In October 2026 Ampath said it had notified the Regulator of a cyber incident.

Rulings and published figures. The first fine, R5 million on the Department of Justice and Constitutional Development, came in July 2023. It issued WhatsApp LLC an enforcement notice on 10 September 2024. On 20 May 2026 it published an enforcement notice against Central Johannesburg TVET College. In October 2026 it fined the college R500,000 for ignoring that notice, and First National Bank R1 million. A R500,000 fine on Blouberg Local Municipality was reduced to R250,000 by the Polokwane High Court in April 2026. It reports 1,355 POPIA complaints in 2024/25, 745 of them resolved.

Not found. Nothing on the four questions.

ZMB.short: Zambia has an authority, in post in 2026; no ruling against an organisation and no published figures are known.
ZMB.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Data Protection Commission of Zambia is treated as an existing body in a World Bank tender dated 10 August 2026, which describes it as conducting investigations, issuing determinations and enforcing the law. Its first Data Protection Commissioner was appointed in June 2023. The Commissioner, Likando Luywa, spoke on oversight and registration of data controllers in June 2026. A Commissioner and a Deputy Commissioner took part in a September 2025 review of a draft health data statutory instrument.

Rulings and published figures. The nearest held fact is that the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner had issued regulations and guidelines and opened online registration for controllers and processors, with a 30 April 2025 deadline. No ruling against a named organisation and no published figures have been found beyond that.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe has an authority, acting in 2026; no ruling against an organisation and no published figures are known.
ZWE.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Section 5 of the Cyber and Data Protection Act makes the Postal and Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (POTRAZ) the Data Protection Authority. Section 6(2) says it is not subject to the direction or control of any person. It is at work: POTRAZ says it has trained data protection officers. In March 2026 it said it had received 1,123 data controller licence applications that year. In October 2026 a panellist said it was the regulator Parliament's committee took data protection concerns to. The 2024 licensing regulations have it issue licences within 14 days and keep a register.

Rulings and published figures. The nearest held fact is that POTRAZ issued Regulatory Notice 2 of 2026 on compliance inspections, which start on 1 September 2026. In June 2025 it was handing over data controller licences and planning inspections triggered by complaints and unlicensed processing. Its Business Times interview lists powers to audit, investigate, warn, direct and initiate prosecutions. On 23 October 2026 the ICT minister directed POTRAZ to investigate unlawful processing of personal information.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

AGO.short: Angola's 2011 data protection law is in force and its agency fined named companies in 2025 and 2026; no source found counts its decisions.
AGO.summary:
Authority. Lei n.º 22/11 creates the Agência de Protecção de Dados (APD) as a public-law body of seven members. Its organic statute was approved on 10 October 2016, and three board members were appointed on 6 September 2019. Its board took a sanction decision on 10 August 2026.

Standing. Lei n.º 22/11, the Lei da Protecção de Dados Pessoais, was published on 17 June 2011 and entered into force that day. On 25 June 2026 the Assembleia Nacional rejected a UNITA bill to amend it.

Regulations. Decreto Presidencial n.º 60/21 of 10 March 2021 sets the fees the APD charges for registering files and authorising processing. Decreto Presidencial n.º 214/16 approves the APD's organic statute.

Application. The APD fined Lizíria, Lda., owner of Hotel Diamante, the kwanza equivalent of USD 115,000 on 10 August 2026 for breaching articles 30 and 31 of the law. Valor Económico reported on 26 June 2026 fines of about USD 505,000 on Crescer Tech and USD 112,000 on Fast Digital Center, and fines of USD 100,000 on TAAG and USD 75,000 on Banco de Desenvolvimento de Angola, disclosed in September 2025.

Last twelve months. The law is under revision: an APD administrator said on 17 June 2026 that the public consultation was complete and the bill would go to the Assembleia Nacional in the next legislative year. On 21 April 2026 terms of reference were issued for drafting a new organic law for the APD. In October 2026 the APD warned of critical PHP flaws.

Not found. No count of the APD's decisions for a stated period ending by 30 September 2026. The companies it sanctioned in June and July 2024 are not named.

BDI.short: Burundi promulgated its first personal data protection law in March 2026; when it took effect, and any decision under it, are unknown.
BDI.summary:
Authority. The law establishes an independent administrative authority to oversee the protection of personal data. The bill the National Assembly adopted in January 2026 makes that authority responsible for enforcement.

Standing. The National Assembly unanimously adopted a bill on personal data protection on 15 January 2026. It governs the collection and processing of personal data in the public and private sectors. The head of state promulgated the law on 10 March 2026.

Regulations. The law as the National Assembly approved it on 15 January 2026 is structured in eight chapters.

Application. The law sets up a dedicated body to implement and monitor data protection regimes.

Last twelve months. Burundi validated a National Data Governance Strategy on 7 November 2025. It adopted its first personal data protection law on 15 January 2026 and promulgated it on 10 March 2026.

Not found. The date the law takes effect, any regulation made under it and any decision taken under it. No appointment to the authority the law names is reported.

BEN.short: Benin's data protection law is in its 2018 digital code and was applied in 2025; no source found says how many regulations are in force.
BEN.summary:
Authority. The Autorité de Protection des Données Personnelles (APDP) is constituted: seventeen of its officers were sworn in before the Court of First Instance of Cotonou on 14 September 2026. It succeeds the CNIL, whose members were installed in October 2010.

Standing. The data protection rules are Book V of the Code du numérique, Law no. 2017-20, promulgated on 20 April 2018. It replaced Law no. 2009-09 of 22 May 2009 and was amended by Law no. 2020-35 of 6 January 2021. In September 2026 La Nation treated the Code as the framework governing personal data processing.

Regulations. Decree 2022-107 of 16 February 2022, taken under the Code, authorises the interior ministry's national video-protection data processing. Decree 2020-187 of 11 March 2020, also taken under it, authorises the national police to collect traveller identity and fingerprint data at borders.

Application. For 2025, La Nation's account of the APDP's annual report gives 907 files examined, 793 validated, 64 inspection missions and 20 complaints treated. The authority counted 347 decisions from 2016 to 15 December 2020, among them a 2020 injunction to a controller to guarantee a complainant's right of deletion.

Last twelve months. The swearing-in of seventeen APDP officers on 14 September 2026 was done under Article 468(2) of the Code. The APDP's president spoke at a regulators' forum in Johannesburg on 1 to 3 September 2026.

Not found. How many regulations are in force under the Code, and the date the Code commenced, are not stated. The 2025 figures are held through a newspaper's account, not the APDP's report itself, and no ratification of the Malabo Convention is stated.

BFA.short: Burkina Faso has a 2021 data protection law; its commission warns and inspects, but no source found says whether any sanction has been imposed.
BFA.summary:
Authority. The Commission de l'informatique et des libertés (CIL) was created by a 2004 law and has worked since December 2007. The 2021 law makes it the supervisory authority, with nine members appointed by decree. It held its sixth plenary session of the year on 26 June 2025.
