A bill adopted on 3 August 2026 merges the CSC and the CIL into a new regulator, ARCOD, whose first college is still to be formed.

Standing. Law n°001-2021/AN was adopted on 30 March 2021, repeals the 2004 law and gives one year from entry into force for all processing to comply. On 1 July 2025 the CIL president recalled that it makes data protection compulsory. The legislature adopted a new data protection bill on 3 August 2026.

Regulations. The 2021 law itself sets the declaration duties and the fines.

Application. By communiqué of 24 December 2024 the CIL warned that repeatedly posting people's images on social media without consent violates the law. On 26 June 2025 it validated its public report for 2024, covering compliance controls and the handling of complaints and authorisation requests. On 1 July 2025 the Prime Minister launched its awareness sessions for ministries and public institutions.

Last twelve months. The bill voted on 3 August 2026 indexes fines to turnover and bans the transfer of sensitive data abroad, and requires prior consent for commercial prospecting. The law organising ARCOD as the single authority for communications regulation and personal data protection was adopted the same day.

Not found. No regulation under the 2021 law, no named sanction and no published count of decisions or complaints. No source found says whether the bill voted on 3 August 2026 has been promulgated.

BWA.short: Botswana's Data Protection Act 2024, in force since January 2025, was applied in July 2026; no source found says whether regulations exist under it.
BWA.summary:
Authority. The Information and Data Protection Commission was established in 2022, and in July 2025 its commissioner had employed three contract officers while the deputy commissioner and two director posts were unfilled. Kepaletswe Somolekae was the newly appointed commissioner in February 2026.

Standing. The Data Protection Act, 2024 (Act No. 18 of 2024) came into operation on 14 January 2025. It was published on 29 October 2024 and repeals the Data Protection Act No. 32 of 2018. It applies to all organisations processing personal data, public entities included.

Regulations. Statutory Instrument No. 4 of 2025, made by the Minister for State President on 13 January 2025, sets the Act's commencement date.

Application. In a public notice dated 17 July 2026 the Commission issued a Determination and an Enforcement Notice against DPSM for contraventions of the Act. It ordered the ePayslip portal suspended, and a data protection impact assessment and a revised privacy notice submitted within one month. DPSM suspended the portal on 22 July 2026.

Last twelve months. In February 2026 the new commissioner vowed firmer enforcement against non-bank financial institutions. The July 2026 notice left an administrative fine possible if DPSM did not comply.

Not found. No regulation made under the Act has been found. No published count of decisions for a stated period has been found.

CAF.short: The Central African Republic adopted a data protection law in 2024; when it took effect, and any regulation or decision under it, are unknown.
CAF.summary:
Authority. Loi n° 24.001 provides for a personal data protection agency. It gives the ministry in charge of the digital economy twelve months from promulgation to set it up. That ministry holds the agency's missions meanwhile. Data Protection Africa stated on 28 January 2026 that the authority had not yet been appointed.

Standing. Loi n° 24.001 on the protection of personal data was adopted in mid-January 2024 and promulgated. Its text gives no commencement date and no compliance period. Data Protection Africa stated on 28 January 2026 that the country has a data protection law in place. The World Bank recorded in December 2024 that the law was adopted in January 2024.

Regulations. The World Bank reported in December 2024 that activities were planned to support drafting of the law's implementing decrees. The law's text names no composition, seat or financing for the agency.

Application. Until the agency is set up, its missions rest with the ministry in charge of the digital economy.

Last twelve months. On 28 January 2026 Data Protection Africa recorded the authority as not yet appointed.

Not found. No regulation made under the law, and no decision, sanction or count of decisions, has been found. The date the law came into force and any appointment to the agency are not held.

CIV.short: Côte d'Ivoire has a 2013 personal data protection law, with compliance checks made in 2022; no source found says whether any controller has been sanctioned.
CIV.summary:
Authority. Decree no. 2015-79 names ARTCI as the body that receives declarations, rules on authorisation requests within one month and imposes withdrawals and fines under the law. ARTCI was handling compliance and authorisation requests in July 2026.

Standing. Law no. 2013-450 of 19 June 2013 on personal data protection is the general law, and the 2015 decree made under it sets filing fees, prior authorisations and fines of up to FCFA 500 million on repeat breach. On 18 May 2026 the digital minister cited the 2013 law as the country's existing framework.

Regulations. Decree no. 2015-79 of 4 February 2015, signed by the President, sets the filing, authorisation, withdrawal and fine-recovery procedures under the law.

Application. The minister listed compliance control operations carried out in 2022 and national awareness campaigns launched from 2015. In July 2026 ARTCI was handling about 100 paper compliance and authorisation files each month.

Last twelve months. On 2 July 2026 ARTCI launched Certinum, an online platform for compliance and processing-authorisation requests, with the Treasury and ONECI the first two bodies to use it. The minister said a national register of data protection correspondents was created in 2026.

Not found. No named decision or sanction on a controller, and no published count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled for a stated year. The 2022 control operations carry no count and no sanction.

CMR.short: Cameroon's 2024 data protection law came into force in June 2026, with its authority not installed; no source found reports a decision under it.
CMR.summary:
Authority. The law defines the Autorité as an independent public body in charge of data protection and gives it supervision, notification and enforcement functions. The OBS-CC observatory reported on 12 September 2026 that the authority had not yet been installed.

Standing. Cameroon's general law is Loi n° 2024/017 of 23 December 2024 on the protection of personal data. The Minister of Posts and Telecommunications told the National Assembly in April 2025 that it had been adopted. A July 2025 review describes an 18-month grace period from enactment. The finance ministry's budget directorate states that the law came into force on 23 June 2026.

Regulations. The implementing decree called for by article 53 had not been taken by 12 September 2026, the OBS-CC observatory reported. The law itself sets principles, controller obligations and data subject rights.

Application. The law has been in force since 23 June 2026. Enforcement under it is a function of the Autorité.

Last twelve months. The law entered into force on 23 June 2026, which the budget directorate reported on 6 July 2026.

Not found. No decision, sanction or judgment applying Loi n° 2024/017 has been found.

COD.short: The 2023 Digital Code, in force, covers personal data; a data protection officers' network launched in 2026; no source found reports any decision under it.
COD.summary:
Authority. Article 262 of the Digital Code creates an independent Autorité de protection des données with legal personality and its own budget. A ministerial order of 17 August 2024 provisionally transferred its missions to the telecommunications regulator, ARPTIC. In March 2026 the Minister of Digital Economy described the authority's creation as forthcoming.

Standing. Ordonnance-loi n° 23/010 of 13 March 2023, the Digital Code, sets the rules on the protection of personal data in its Book III. It entered into force in 2023.

Regulations. The Code provides that a Prime Minister's decree will fix the authority's organisation and functioning. On 6 August 2024 the think tank Law & Technologies called on the government to draft and sign it.

Application. On 12 March 2026 the Ministry of Digital Economy launched a national network of data protection officers in Kinshasa, to standardise personal data practice and support compliance in the public and private sectors, backed by RUDI International and Droit-Numérique.cd.

Last twelve months. The network launched in March 2026 was reported as part of plans to establish a dedicated Data Protection Authority. On 20 April 2026 the co-author of a book on personal data protection said the Code's Book III replaces the embryonic provisions of the 2020 telecommunications law.

Not found. No decision, sanction or count of decisions under the Digital Code has been found, and no regulation made under it. No source shows the authority constituted, or ARPTIC acting in its place.

COG.short: Congo has a 2019 personal data protection law with a commission inaugurated in January 2026; no source found reports a decision under it.
COG.summary:
Authority. The National Personal Data Protection Commission was inaugurated after its members were appointed under Decree No. 2025-538 of 31 December 2025, as reported on 22 January 2026.

Standing. Congo's general law is Law No. 29-2019 of 10 October 2019 on personal data protection. It was in force in January 2026, when the Commission it provides for was inaugurated.

Regulations. Decree No. 2025-538 of 31 December 2025 completes the institutional framework the law established, by appointing the Commission's members.

Application. The Commission elected its President, Vice President and Rapporteur at its inaugural meeting, reported in January 2026.

Last twelve months. The Commission's members were appointed by decree of 31 December 2025 and the Commission was inaugurated with its leadership elected, reported on 22 January 2026.

Not found. Whether any regulation made under Law No. 29-2019 is in force, and any decision, sanction or count of complaints under the law. The date the law commenced.

COM.short: Comoros enacted a personal data protection law in 2021; no decision under it is on record, and no source found says it is in force.
COM.summary:
Authority. The law institutes a supervisory body, which its Article 19 names the Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés, with nine members. As of mid-2024 the authority had not been formally constituted or made operational.

Standing. The Assembly of the Union adopted Loi n°14-029/AU on the protection of personal data, in 68 articles, in plenary session on 26 June 2014. The Union of Comoros enacted its Protection of Personal Data Law on 29 June 2021, as a comprehensive framework.

Regulations. Under Article 24 of the law, the nine members of the commission are named by decree.

Application. The authority that the law gives the task of supervision was not operational as of mid-2024.

Last twelve months. The latest dated position is that of mid-2024, when the authority had not been formally constituted.

Not found. Whether the law has commenced, and from what date, is not held, nor is any regulation made under it or any decision applying it. Nothing dated in the twelve months to 30 September 2026 is held, including whether the authority has been constituted since mid-2024.

CPV.short: Cabo Verde's 2001 data protection law, amended in 2021, is in force and cases reach its authority; no source found says any was decided.
CPV.summary:
Authority. The Comissão Nacional de Protecção de Dados (CNPD) began work in 2015–2016 and completed a decade in 2025, under its president, Faustino Varela. The National Assembly's own budget gave it CVE 36,313,115 for 2025, with no revenue of its own.

Standing. Law 133/V/2001 is the general data protection regime, applying within the country and to the processing of data of people located in it. The CNPD's president dates the base law to 2001 and says the commission has worked from it since 2015–2016.

Regulations. The law was amended in 2013 and again in 2021: the first amendment led to the CNPD being set up, and the second added the obligation to appoint a data protection officer.

Application. The CNPD's president said in February 2025 that cases involving artificial intelligence and big data have reached the commission, among them two of images manipulated with generative AI and a first image-manipulation case in 2021. Cases that may be criminal are sent to the Ministério Público.

Last twelve months. In March 2025 the CNPD held an international conference on personal data protection for its tenth anniversary, opened by the Prime Minister.

Not found. Whether any regulation has been made under the law, and any dated decision, sanction or published count of decisions under it. Nothing dated in the twelve months to 30 September 2026.

DJI.short: Djibouti enacted a data protection law in June 2025; when it took effect, and any decision under it, are unknown.
DJI.summary:
Authority. The Digital Code's data-protection regime creates the National Commission for the Protection of Personal Data (CNDP). The commission is independent, with administrative and financial autonomy. Jones Day reported at the National Assembly's vote that the competent authorities were still to be operationalised.

Standing. The National Assembly passed Djibouti's first Digital Code on 30 June 2025, with a data-protection regime embedded in it. The Code was to be promulgated by the President and published in the Journal Officiel. TechHive Advisory states that the regime was enacted in June 2025.

Regulations. The data-protection regime runs to 156 articles and sits within the Digital Code.

Application. The Code's embedded data-protection regime establishes the CNDP, as reported at the Assembly's vote on 30 June 2025.

Last twelve months. TechHive Advisory, writing on 5 November 2025, described the regime as enacted in June 2025. It described the commission as created by the regime.

Not found. The date the Code was promulgated or came into force has not been found. Nor has any appointment to the CNDP. No regulation or decision under the law has been found, nor any event in the past twelve months.

DZA.short: Algeria's 2018 data protection law has been in force since 2023 and its authority issues rules; no source found reports a sanction on a controller.
DZA.summary:
Authority. The Autorité nationale de protection des données à caractère personnel (ANPDP) adopted a deliberation by a majority of its members on 15 July 2026, signed by its president. Samir Bourehil was its president in July 2026. It issues authorisations and receives declarations of processing.

Standing. Law n° 18-07 of 10 June 2018 came into force on 10 August 2023, the US International Trade Administration states. Law 25-11, promulgated in July 2025, amended it, adding duties to appoint a data protection delegate, keep a processing register and log automated operations. The law was in force in July 2026.

Regulations. Délibération n° 04 of 15 July 2026, in eleven articles, sets conditions for processing and publishing images and recordings of natural persons. In the months before it the ANPDP published rules on workplace video surveillance and on appointing data protection delegates. A compliance package of guidelines and four templates was released in 2025.

Application. The authority decided in January or February 2026 that a positive or negative test result alone is standard health data, so employers need no prior authorisation. It runs an online complaint service for data subjects, and by December 2025 it had held its first study day and a series of training meetings with national bodies.

Last twelve months. Délibération n° 04 treats publication on foreign-run platforms as a transfer abroad. A study day at the national police college in July 2026 announced a unified guide for administrative, security and judicial procedures.

Not found. No decision or sanction on a named controller has been found. No count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled is published for a stated period.

EGY.short: Egypt's 2020 data protection law is in force and its authority opened a licensing portal in 2026; no decision under it is known.
EGY.summary:
Authority. The supervisory authority is the Personal Data Protection Center, which the executive regulations confirm as responsible for implementation, monitoring and enforcement. In November 2025 it was run by an acting chief executive, Soussan El-Okbawy, and in early October 2026 it launched an electronic portal for accreditation, licence and permit applications.

Standing. Egypt's general law is the Personal Data Protection Law, Law No. 151 of 2020, which the Cairo Review treated in June 2025 as the country's operating data protection law. Shura Law Firm said on 13 October 2026 that it entered into force in October 2020, with a transitional period under the executive regulations expiring on 31 October 2026.

Regulations. The executive regulations were still pending in February 2025. They were issued by ministerial decree on 1 November 2025 as Executive Regulations No. 816/2025.

Application. In January and February 2026 the Personal Data Protection Center published guidelines on consent, lawful bases, direct marketing, data protection officers, records of processing, licences and permits and privacy notices, with templates for notifying a breach. Its portal also publishes guidelines and frameworks for controllers and processors.

Last twelve months. The executive regulations were issued on 1 November 2025, and the Center's guidelines followed in January and February 2026. It launched its licensing and permit portal in early October 2026.

Not found. No sanction, order or decision on a named controller under the law, and no published count of cases settled.

ERI.short: Eritrea has no data protection law as of 2026 and no supervisory authority; no source found says whether a bill is being drafted.
ERI.summary:
Authority. No supervisory authority has been established in Eritrea, as of 1 August 2026. The Horn of Africa Initiative's update of June 2025 recorded the country as without regulatory oversight for data protection, while Kenya, Somalia and Ethiopia had supervisory authorities.

Standing. Eritrea has no comprehensive data protection law in force, as of 1 August 2026. The Horn of Africa Initiative's update of June 2025 placed it at a nascent stage, without data protection legislation, and a UNECA country profile published in 2022 said it lacked a comprehensive legal framework for data protection.

Regulations. No comprehensive data protection law is in force, as of 1 August 2026.

Application. No enforcement decisions are published and none could be found, as of 1 August 2026.

Last twelve months. The position was unchanged at 1 August 2026: no law, no regulator and no enforcement.

Not found. No bill or draft of a data protection law is on record, and whether one is in preparation is not held. Nothing is held on regulations.

ETH.short: Ethiopia published a data protection proclamation in 2024 and its regulator approved about 10 data transfers by 2025; no source found reports decisions on controllers.
ETH.summary:
Authority. The proclamation designates the Ethiopian Communications Authority as the regulator. In November 2025 the Authority, whose mandate was extended from telecom regulation to data protection, was enforcing the law and expanding its staffing and technical capacity, its Director General Balcha Reba said.

Standing. Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024, the country's first comprehensive personal data protection law, was approved on 4 April 2024 and published in the Federal Negarit Gazette on 24 July 2024. It took effect on publication.

Regulations. In November 2025 four directives were expected to be approved in the coming months, and delays in issuing them had slowed implementation.

Application. The Director General said in November 2025 that the Authority had received about 10 requests to transfer data abroad and approved them as a temporary measure, and that data processors and collectors now need its permission.

Last twelve months. At a workshop co-hosted with Huawei in November 2025, Authority officials previewed a digital portal for registering data controllers and processors.

Not found. No sanction or order on a named controller has been found, and no published count of decisions for a stated period. No directive under the proclamation has been found as approved.

GAB.short: Gabon has a 2011 data protection law, amended in 2023, and its authority fined a bank in 2024; no source found says regulations exist.
GAB.summary:
Authority. The Autorité pour la Protection des Données Personnelles et de la Vie Privée (APDPVP) is created by article 7 of Loi n°025/2023 as an independent administrative authority. Its commissioners were appointed by a Council of Ministers decision of 12 July 2023 and its bureau was elected on 6 September 2023. Its president gave an interview as head of the authority in September 2026.

Standing. Gabon's data protection law is Loi n°001/2011, amended by ordinance in 2020 and again by Loi n°025/2023 of 12 July 2023, published in the Journal Officiel on 15 July 2023 with no grace period for compliance. The authority applied it as law in force in April 2024.

Regulations. Loi n°025/2023 was promulgated by Décret n°166/PR.

Application. On 25 April 2024 the authority's plenary fined Citibank Gabon S.A. 90,000,000 FCFA for diverting employee data from its declared purpose and processing data on ethnic origin, with a formal notice of two months. The decision answered a complaint of 27 November 2023.

Last twelve months. On 20 January 2026 the authority supervised the destruction of the personal data of unsuccessful 2022 bidders held by the public procurement directorate. It accompanied a data centre project for several months before commissioning, reported in June 2026. Its president said in September 2026 that it had logged about 715 declarations of conformity, issued about 50 reasoned opinions and received about 30 complaints from individuals.

Not found. Whether any regulations have been issued under Loi n°025/2023. The authority's counts carry no year or period, and nothing dated in the twelve months to 30 September 2026 shows the law being strengthened or weakened.

GHA.short: Ghana's 2012 Data Protection Act was applied by a court in 2024 and against named companies in 2026; no source found reports regulations under it.
GHA.summary:
Authority. The Minister for Communication swore in a new Governing Board, chaired by Teki Akuetteh, reported on 1 August 2025. In October 2026 the Commission was conducting compliance checks and enforcement under the Act.

Standing. The Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843) is in force: a circuit court treated its sections 17 to 30 and 43 as binding on a data processor on 18 September 2024, and in February 2026 the Minister for Communication called on all institutions that process personal data to comply with it.

Regulations. Amendments to the Act are in process and a draft Data Protection Act, 2025 has been published, according to a roundup by Digital Policy Alert and Tech Hive Advisory of 11 January 2026.

Application. On 18 September 2024 a circuit court in Accra found Bolt Holdings OU in breach of sections 20, 21, 28 and 30 of the Act and awarded GHC1,900,000 in compensation and GHC20,000 in costs. On 14 October 2026 the Commission cited six named companies for operating unregistered or with expired certificates and directed them to report to the CID by 15 October, after inspecting a clinic and two hospitals on 12 October.

Last twelve months. In January 2026 the Commission announced that 2026 would be a year of enforcement. On 12 October 2026 it directed Nyaho Medical Centre to report to the police CID over an expired registration certificate. On 20 October 2026 it warned a ministry and media over disclosing evacuees' personal data.

Not found. No regulation made under the Act has been found, and no source says there is none. No published count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled in a stated year has been found; the 2026 figures given are registrations and training.

GIN.short: Guinea has a 2016 cybersecurity and personal data protection law, said in 2025 to be in place; no decision under it is on record.
GIN.summary:
Authority. The 2016 law defines an Autorité de Protection and names no constituted body or appointed members. On 20 June 2024 the CNT's commissions debated a bill to establish the Autorité de Protection des Données à caractère Personnel, with the designation of members and their mandates contested and plenary adoption pending.

Standing. Loi L/2016/037/AN on cybersecurity and personal data protection was adopted by the National Assembly and promulgated by President Alpha Condé in 2016, and covers personal data processing by individuals, companies and public institutions. Part Two of the text is a full personal data protection regime. In October 2025 the ministry's secretary-general said Guinea has put in place the law on cybersecurity and protection of personal data.

Regulations. Article 5 of the law sends processing declarations to the competent authority "designated by regulation".

Application. The law gives the Autorité de Protection the functions of receiving declarations, granting authorisations, approving transfers, investigating and issuing guidelines.

Last twelve months. On 19 November 2025 Minister Rose Pola Pricemou said Guinea is strengthening its regulatory framework with a new data-protection law. The ministry reported for 2025 that texts on personal data protection are in progress.

Not found. Any regulation made under the 2016 law, any decision applying it and the constitution of its authority. The date the law came into force. The stage and timetable of the new law announced in November 2025.

GMB.short: The Gambia enacted its first general data protection law in 2025; no source found gives its commencement date or reports a decision under it.
GMB.summary:
Authority. The Act establishes an independent oversight Commission. A notice published on 17 August 2026 has the Information Commission of The Gambia preparing a communication strategy to raise awareness of the Access to Information Act, 2021 and the Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2025.

Standing. The National Assembly passed the Personal Data Protection and Privacy Bill 2025 in its Third Ordinary Session, and President Barrow assented to the Act on 7 November 2025. It is Act No. 11 of 2025. It is the country's first comprehensive data protection law and has no grace period before it becomes enforceable.

Regulations. In February 2026 regulations and guidance under the Act, on research purposes, the income base for fines and transfers, were still to be issued.

Application. Paradigm Initiative called in January 2026 for the relevant authorities to implement and enforce the law.

Last twelve months. Parliament's passage of the bill was reported on 6 October 2025, when it awaited presidential assent, and assent followed on 7 November 2025.

Not found. The date the Act commenced is not stated, and no source says the Commission's members have been appointed. No decision, sanction or count of complaints under the Act is on record.

GNB.short: Guinea-Bissau has no data protection law; the cabinet approved a bill with amendments in May 2026, and no source found says it has reached parliament.
GNB.summary:
Authority. Guinea-Bissau has no dedicated national data protection authority. A professor at the Bissau Faculty of Law said so on 22 September 2026.

Standing. The country does not yet have specific data protection legislation, the same speaker said. The government's February 2025 report to the Universal Periodic Review lists a data protection bill among several awaiting discussion in the National People's Assembly. That month a WARDIP coordinator said the country urgently needs a data protection law.

Regulations. The bill leaves the organisation of the body it would create to a decree.

Application. Data protection matters are handled by several institutions, sector by sector.

Last twelve months. On 8 May 2026 the Council of Ministers approved the Data Protection Law with amendments. It told an interministerial commission to make the changes. On 22 September 2026 the professor said the bill would create a "Data Protection Agency". The professor added that its membership puts its independence at risk.

Not found. No law is enacted, and no source found says the bill approved in May 2026 has gone to the National People's Assembly. Nothing is held on regulations or on any decision.

GNQ.short: Equatorial Guinea has had a personal data protection law since 2016; whether it has been applied, or its supervisory body created, is unknown.
GNQ.summary:
Authority. Articles 15 and 29 of the law name the Órgano Rector de Protección de Datos Personales as the supervisory body. A Secretaría Técnica and a Registro General sit under it. The law states that the body is to be created by a decree fixing its structure.

Standing. Ley Núm. 1/2016, de Protección de Datos Personales, was sanctioned and promulgated by the President on 22 July 2016. It sets rules for the processing of personal data in the public and private sectors. It enters into force twenty days after its publication in the Boletín Oficial del Estado.

Regulations. The law leaves the structure of the Órgano Rector to a decree.

Application. The law places the power to sanction with the Minister of Telecommunications and New Technologies.

Last twelve months. The law in force is the one dated 22 July 2016.

Not found. Whether the decree creating the Órgano Rector was issued, whether any regulation was made under the law, and whether any decision or sanction has been taken under it. Nothing dated after 22 July 2016 is held.

KEN.short: Kenya's 2019 Data Protection Act is in force and its commissioner has fined businesses; no source found gives the number of decisions in a year.
KEN.summary:
Authority. The Office of the Data Protection Commissioner was established under the Data Protection Act, 2019. Its first commissioner has been in office since 2020. In March 2025 it had offices in Nairobi, Kisumu, Mombasa, Eldoret, Machakos, Nyeri and Nakuru.

Standing. The Data Protection Act, 2019 is in force. The ICT Cabinet Secretary told the Senate in May 2026 that the Act is being enforced, and the office has issued fines under it since 2022. In October 2026 a trade report described organisations in Kenya as facing growing compliance demands under the Act.

Regulations. The Data Protection (Registration of Data Controllers and Data Processors) Regulations, 2021 are in force under the Act. They set 24-month registration certificates and make processing on an expired certificate an offence.

Application. As at September 2024 the office had fined at least nine businesses a total of KES 26,275,000. Its bulletin states that by March 2025 it had issued 215 determinations and imposed penalties on 10 entities.

Last twelve months. In August 2026 the office published a draft guidance note on transfers of personal data to offshore AI providers. On 28 August 2026 it gave holders of expired registration certificates until 11 September 2026 to renew or face enforcement. In April 2026 it announced an investigation into privacy concerns over Meta's smart glasses.

Not found. No count of decisions or sanctions for a single stated year: the figures to March 2025 are cumulative. The date the Act commenced is not given.

LBR.short: Liberia approved a data protection act in March 2026; it has no recorded decision, and no source found says whether the Commissioner has begun acting.
LBR.summary:
Authority. The Act confers data protection functions on the Independent Information Commissioner, the oversight body created by the Freedom of Information Act of 2010.

Standing. The Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act of 2024 was approved on 9 March 2026 and printed on 23 March 2026. It takes effect on publication into handbills, and existing businesses have one year from the effective date to comply. President Boakai's promulgation of the law was announced on 19 August 2026.

Regulations. The Act requires implementing rules within 24 months of its taking effect.

Application. The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection said on 13 September 2026 that it is aware of its responsibilities under the Act, and that it took part in validating the legal framework.

Last twelve months. The House of Representatives had referred the President's bill to committee on 10 June 2025. The Act was approved on 9 March 2026, and its signing was reported on 20 August 2026.

Not found. Any regulation issued under the Act, and any decision, sanction or count of decisions under it. Whether the Independent Information Commissioner has begun acting under the Act is not held.

LBY.short: Libya's government was drafting a data protection law as of July 2026, with adoption targeted for 2026; no bill before parliament is known.
LBY.summary:
Authority. SMEX said on 22 July 2026 that Libya has no functioning data protection authority. The same source places the country's data protection law still at the drafting stage, so there is no law for an authority to administer.

Standing. In January 2024 the General Information Authority reported a committee drafting a national personal data protection law. The committee was formed under a 2023 decision of the National Council for Public Freedoms and Human Rights. SMEX reported on 22 July 2026 that the law remains in draft, with adoption targeted for 2026.

Regulations. None has been found. A committee was still drafting the law itself in January 2024.

Application. None has been found. SMEX reported in July 2026 that the law remains in draft.

Last twelve months. In March 2026 a working group led by the Annir Initiative with Internet Society Libya published an informal draft law for consultation. It is marked unofficial and is not a government bill. In July 2026 SMEX reported the official law still in draft. On 26 October 2026 the National Council and a House of Representatives committee began a joint review of the council's draft. The draft had gone to the House as an initial proposal.

Not found. No source says a government bill has been tabled or when one will be. No regulations or decisions under a law are on record.

LSO.short: Lesotho has a Data Protection Act of 2011 with no commission appointed; no source found says whether it has ever been applied or has regulations.
LSO.summary:
Authority. The Data Protection Act has a Data Protection Commission under it. Cenfri, in an article published on 23 March 2026, says the Commission has remained unappointed.

Standing. Lesotho's general law is the Data Protection Act, which Cenfri dates to 2011. Cenfri says, in the article it published on 23 March 2026, that the Act has been law for over a decade.

Regulations. The nearest dated position is Cenfri's, published on 23 March 2026: the Data Protection Act has been law for over a decade.

Application. The nearest dated position concerns the body under the Act: Cenfri says, in its article of 23 March 2026, that the Data Protection Commission has remained unappointed.

Last twelve months. The latest dated position is Cenfri's article of 23 March 2026, which says that the Act has been law for over a decade and that its Commission has remained unappointed.

Not found. No regulation made under the Act and no decision applying it has been found, nor is any event in the twelve months to 30 September 2026. The source that says the Commission is unappointed gives no date for that position beyond its own publication on 23 March 2026.

MAR.short: Morocco's 2009 data protection law is in force and its authority issues guidance; no source found says whether any controller has been sanctioned.
MAR.summary:
Authority. The Commission nationale de contrôle de la protection des données à caractère personnel (CNDP) was installed in 2010 and acts under Law 09-08. Its president, Omar Seghrouchni, said on 4 August 2026 that it is strengthening an alert system that can go as far as sanctions.

Standing. Law 09-08 on personal data is in force: the CNDP cited ten of its articles to political parties in August 2026, and its president spoke that month of a law more than fifteen years in force.

Regulations. The CNDP validated five deliberations on 28 November 2025 setting model declaration and authorisation forms for cookies, newsletters, patient follow-up, healthcare video surveillance and workplace access control.

Application. The CNDP published a national register of notified processing operations in January 2023. On 28 August 2026 it issued guidance to political parties and voters for the legislative elections of 23 September 2026. It runs a programme with public and private controllers that it calls Data-Tika, and in October 2026 agreed a pilot to train 20,000 young people in data privacy.

Last twelve months. A proposed recast of Law 09-08, prepared with the Justice Ministry, has been sent to the Secrétariat général du gouvernement, the CNDP president said on 4 August 2026. A draft framework law on AI, data governance and digital identity, called Digital X.0, was under review by the same secretariat in November 2025. The CNDP signed a cooperation memorandum with Portugal's data protection authority on 8 February 2026.

Not found. No decision on a named controller and no published count of decisions, sanctions or complaints has been found. No regulation under Law 09-08 has been found, and no source found says what a 2023 amendment to the law changed.

MDG.short: Madagascar has a data protection law of 2015 and an authority seated in 2025; no source found says whether the law has been applied.
MDG.summary:
Authority. Article 28 of the law institutes the Commission Malagasy de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CMIL) as an independent authority of nine members named by decree in the Council of Ministers. Seven members were sworn in at the Cour suprême on 4 August 2025, and the commission elected a president and two vice-presidents on 14 August 2025.

Standing. Loi n° 2014-038 on the protection of personal data was adopted by the Assemblée nationale on 16 December 2014 and promulgated on 9 January 2015. The commission's procedures manual, approved in October 2025, takes the law as its legal basis.

Regulations. Décret n°2023-1541 of 6 December 2023 sets the commission's attributions, organisation and operation and governs the processing of personal data; Décret n°2025-696 of 18 June 2025 amended it. The commission's report of January 2026 cites a significant delay in adopting the law's application decrees.

Application. The commission reported in January 2026 that no processing declaration had been registered, that citizens' complaints had gone untreated for ten years and that it had neither premises nor staff. Its manual sets procedures for declarations, authorisations, audits, complaints and administrative sanctions, with a decision on a complaint due within 30 working days.

Last twelve months. The commission approved its first procedures manual on 17 October 2025, published on 3 December 2025. It joined the AFAPDP on 24 November 2025 and obtained a budget line of Ariary 2,411,579,000 in the 2026 Finance Law.

Not found. No decision, sanction or count of cases under the law. The date the law came into force is not stated.

MLI.short: Mali has a 2013 data protection law, applied by its authority with fines and complaints handled in 2025; no source found gives its commencement date.
MLI.summary:
Authority. Article 20 of the law institutes the Autorité de Protection des Données à caractère Personnel (APDP) as an independent administrative authority of 15 members. It sat in ordinary session on 3 August 2026 with all commissioners present and runs regional offices in Kayes, Sikasso, Ségou and Mopti.

Standing. Law no. 2013-015 on the protection of personal data was adopted by the National Assembly on 9 May 2013 and promulgated on 21 May 2013. On 3 August 2026 the APDP's president cited the law, as amended, as the basis for the authority's sanctions.

Regulations. Decree no. 2024-0300/PT-RM of 14 May 2024, made under the law, sets the fees payable to the APDP for declarations, authorisations and certification, and exempts non-profit public services.

Application. For 2025 the APDP's annual report, as summarised by Sahel Tribune, counts fines totalling 22 million FCFA and 51 complaints received, of which 28 were handled and four referred to the cybercrime prosecutor. The fines include 5 million FCFA on a Bamako clinic for obstructing a check of its video surveillance and 5 million FCFA on Société Aminata Konaté SARL for refusing a verification mission.

Last twelve months. The APDP opened an extraordinary session on 6 October 2025 to review about 2,000 declaration files and opened a regional office at Ségou on 4 December 2025. Its session of 3 August 2026 had over 1,000 files to examine.

Not found. The date the law came into force is not held: its text states none. The APDP's 2025 annual report is held only through a press summary, and no figure has been found for sanctions issued in 2026.

MOZ.short: Mozambique has no data protection law; its bill was on parliament's agenda in October 2026, and no source found says when it will pass.
MOZ.summary:
Authority. No data protection authority exists. The Data Protection Office was not yet established in October 2025, and a June 2025 report found no data regulatory authority. The draft law reviewed in September 2025 gives the role to the existing Regulatory Authority for ICT.

Standing. Mozambique has a bill before parliament and no law. In April 2026 the ministry said the government had approved the bill and sent it to the Assembly of the Republic. On 1 October 2026 the Assembly's Standing Commission put it on the agenda of the session opening 28 October. On 26 October it set the plenary debate for 6 November 2026.

Regulations. A June 2025 report says Mozambique has drafted a Data Protection Bill. It has not enacted a comprehensive law.

Application. A World Bank and African Development Bank diagnostic of spring 2025 recommends adopting a data protection law.

Last twelve months. In October 2025 the bill had not been approved by Cabinet or sent to Parliament. On 25 August 2026 the head of INTIC said the authorities were preparing to submit it. A round table that month discussed the proposed law.

Not found. When the bill reached parliament: an April 2026 statement says it had, and August 2026 reports describe it as still being prepared. There is no law, so no regulations or decisions under one.

MRT.short: Mauritania's 2017 data protection law is applied by its authority through opinions and rules; no source found says whether any controller has been sanctioned.
MRT.summary:
Authority. The Autorité de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel (APD) was created by article 64 of the law as an independent body attached to the Prime Minister, and decree 2022-13 of 18 February 2022 governs its composition and operation. It met on 30 June 2026 under its president, with its members and the Government Commissioner present.

Standing. Law 2017-020 on the protection of personal data was promulgated on 22 July 2017. The APD's 2023-2026 strategic plan places itself under the law's entry into force, and its deliberation 002/2026 of 24 March 2026 applies articles 7, 11, 27, 37 and 40.

Regulations. Deliberation 004/2025 of 14 July 2025 requires the APD's prior authorisation for transfers to countries not on its list and lists 105 countries as adequate. Deliberation 005/2025 of 30 July 2025 requires it for public and private controllers using cloud services abroad.

Application. On 24 March 2026 the APD gave a favourable opinion, conditional on its remarks, on the joint decision authorising the system Maaden Mauritanie calls Maadeni. On 19 November 2025 it examined complaints 004-2025, 006-2025 and 007-2025, one of them with a bank's reply.

Last twelve months. On 19 November 2025 the APD approved a control reference framework and empowered its sworn agents to take part in inspection missions. On 29 April 2026 it approved amendments to deliberations 004/2025 and 005/2025 and discussed complaints 008-2025 and 001-2026. Its 30 June 2026 session had authorisation requests and ministries' compliance answers on its agenda.

Not found. No source gives a sanction, order or decision on a named controller, or a published count of decisions for a stated year, and the outcomes of the APD's sessions are mostly not stated. The law's commencement date, whether Mauritania has ratified the Malabo Convention and whether the law is under revision are not held.

MUS.short: Mauritius has the Data Protection Act 2017, and its office reported complaints closed and transfers decided in 2024; no source found reports figures for 2025.
MUS.summary:
Authority. The Data Protection Office has been operational since 16 February 2009 and enforces the Data Protection Act 2017. Drudeisha Madhub is the Data Protection Commissioner.

Standing. Mauritius adopted its current data protection regime in 2017, after a first law in 2004 that was partly implemented in 2009. The Office reports on its enforcement of the Data Protection Act 2017 during 2024.

Regulations. Controllers and processors register under the Data Protection (Fees) Regulations 2020. Registrations since 1 August 2020 reached 21,219 controllers and 1,157 processors by 31 December 2024.

Application. For 2024 the Office reports 179 new complaints and 39 closed. It also counts 105 breaches notified, 112 cross-border transfers authorised and 12 rejected, and four inspections. In May 2026 the Commissioner said her office issues 3,000 enforcement actions a year. Of these, 99 per cent are resolved without prosecution.

Last twelve months. On 17 June 2026 the Minister made regulations requiring every controller to designate a data protection officer, from 1 January 2027. In May 2026 the Commissioner said Mauritius is going for the EU adequacy assessment in 2026. She said amendments to bring in administrative fines are being introduced. In September 2026 the Office told management companies to register as controllers and designate their own officers.

Not found. No figures for 2025 have been found. The draft bill to amend the Act for EU adequacy carries no date beyond 2024, and the 2026 regulations are not yet in operation.

MWI.short: Malawi's Data Protection Act of 2024 is in force and applied through guidance only; no source found reports a decision or sanction under it.
MWI.summary:
Authority. Section 4 of the Act designates the Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority (MACRA) as the Data Protection Authority. MACRA issued guidance in that role in October 2025, and in March 2026 the Authority operated under the regulator, which was working to make it an independent institution.

Standing. The Data Protection Act, 2024 (Act No. 3 of 2024) was passed on 7 December 2023, assented to on 31 January 2024 and published on 2 February 2024. The Authority's guideline of October 2025 says the Act applied at once to foreign controllers and to Malawian controllers with over 10,000 data subjects, and to all others from 3 June 2026.

Regulations. MACRA drafted the Data Protection (Data Processors Engagement) Regulations, 2025 under section 52 of the Act, dated 6 October 2025. In July 2026 the draft regulations it put to consultation were still to be finalised.

Application. The Authority published a compliance guideline and checklist on 17 October 2025, with a registration requirement for controllers of significant importance, and breach notification guidelines on 22 October 2025, setting a 72-hour notice to the Authority and to data subjects.

Last twelve months. In October 2025 the Public Private Partnership Commission issued terms of reference for a consultancy to operationalise the Authority and draft regulations. In March 2026 the World Bank announced renewed technical assistance to MACRA for data protection. On 13 July 2026 MACRA consulted stakeholders in Blantyre on draft regulations carrying annual registration fees of K50,000 to K7 million by turnover.

Not found. No decision, sanction or published count of decisions under the Act has been found, and no regulation in force. No commencement notice for the Act has been found.

NAM.short: Namibia has no data protection law; a cabinet committee approved the bill in 2026, and no source found says when it reaches Parliament.
NAM.summary:
Authority. The 2020 draft of the Data Protection Bill sets up a Data Protection Supervisory Authority of Namibia in section 25. The revised draft dated 2022 provides for the same authority and its powers.

Standing. The Data Protection Bill is a draft. The ICT minister, Emma Theofelus, said on 13 July 2026 that Namibia was finalising it.

Regulations. The ICT ministry published a revised 59-page draft for comment in 2022. Its gazette notice number is left blank.

Application. An opposition MP, Rodney Cloete, said in August 2026 that Namibia has no data protection statute. He said that leaves no legal definition of a data controller and no rules on cross-border transfers.

Last twelve months. In August 2025 the minister said the bill, about 12 years in preparation, would be tabled in September 2025. In January 2026 she said it was ready for resubmission to the Cabinet Committee on Legislation. The 2026/27 budget estimates say the committee approved it and sent it to the justice ministry. In July 2026 the minister said it was being finalised.

Not found. No source states that the bill has been tabled in Parliament, passed or enacted. Nothing dated since the 2022 draft says the supervisory authority has been set up, and no regulations or decisions have been found.

NER.short: Niger's 2022 data protection law is in force, with compliance files and inspections in 2025; no source found reports a decision under it.
NER.summary:
Authority. The law creates the Haute Autorité de Protection des Données à caractère Personnel (HAPDP), attached to the Presidency, with ten members named by decree. Its president said in July 2025 that he took office on 18 September 2024 and that the plenary deliberates on authorisations and sanctions. Africa Data Protection reported on 13 June 2026 that the government had abolished the HAPDP by decree and split its powers between the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of the Interior. The government's own communiqué confirms the decree of 8 June 2026 and the transfer of the authority's missions to the Justice and Interior ministries.

Standing. Law no. 2022-59 of 16 December 2022 on personal data protection is the general law, held in the HAPDP's consolidated text of April 2026. It repealed laws 2017-28 and 2019-71.

Regulations. The law has been amended by Law 2023-31 of 4 July 2023 and by Ordinances 2024-16 of 26 April 2024 and 2024-29 of 24 June 2024.

Application. The HAPDP's president said in July 2025 that the authority had processed 139 compliance files since September 2024, covering declarations, video-surveillance declarations and processing and transfer authorisations, and had run four control missions on mobile operators in 2025.

Last twelve months. The abolition of the HAPDP and the transfer of its powers to two ministries was reported on 13 June 2026.

Not found. No regulation made under the law has been found, and no decision, sanction or count of complaints settled under it. The date the law came into force and the date of the decree abolishing the HAPDP are not held.

NGA.short: Nigeria's Data Protection Act of 2023 is in force and applied through fines and court orders; no source found counts decisions since mid-2024.
NGA.summary:
Authority. The Nigeria Data Protection Commission supervises the Act. National Commissioner Vincent Olatunji heads it, and it keeps a register of data processors of major importance.

Standing. President Tinubu signed the Nigeria Data Protection Act on 12 June 2023, and the High Court of the Federal Capital Territory applied it in a judgment of 29 July 2026. A Nigeria Data Protection (Amendment) Bill, 2026 was before the National Assembly in July 2026.

Regulations. The minister's office names the General Application and Implementation Directive 2025 as the operating framework under the Act for all tiers of government. The Commission's Guidance Notice on Registration designates data controllers and processors of major importance.

Application. The Commission fined Multichoice Nigeria N766,242,500 in July 2025. On 29 July 2026 the court ordered Stanbic IBTC Bank to pay two former customers N15 million and erase their data. A Commission order fining Meta $32.8 million was set aside when the Federal High Court adopted a settlement, by consent judgment on 3 November 2025. By 11 June 2024 the Commission said sanctions on seven firms had brought in N400 million. By October 2026 41,000 organisations had registered, against 630 in the first year.

Last twelve months. The Federal High Court upheld the Commission's power to register controllers and processors of major importance, and on 28 July 2026 the Commission directed every unregistered one to register. It opened investigations into Temu in February 2026 and Remita and Sterling Bank on 1 April 2026.

Not found. No count of decisions or sanctions for any period ending after 11 June 2024. How far the Amendment Bill has gone in the National Assembly.

RWA.short: Rwanda's 2021 Data Protection Act is in force and the authority registers and trains controllers; whether any sanction or decision has been made is unknown.
RWA.summary:
Authority. The National Cyber Security Authority acts as the supervisory authority for personal data protection and privacy under the Data Protection Act.

Standing. Rwanda's Data Protection Act was introduced on 15 October 2021. It is in force: its two-year grace period ended on 15 October 2023, the date from which controllers and processors are held to it.

Regulations. Under the Act the authority issues registration certificates to data controllers and processors.

Application. By January 2026 the authority had registered data controllers and processors, trained over 100 Data Protection Officers in the public sector and run sector workshops for pharmacists and local government entities, all over the previous four years.

Last twelve months. For Data Privacy Week, 26 to 30 January 2026, the authority adopted the theme "Compliance is Beyond Registration". It moved from the awareness phase of 2022 to 2024 to capacity building, and now expects controllers to prove that they comply.

Not found. No source says whether regulations under the Act have been issued or are pending. No dated sanction or decision under the Act is on record, and no count of decisions is published.

SDN.short: Sudan had a data and artificial intelligence bill in draft in August 2026, with no law yet to apply; no source found reports its content.
SDN.summary:
Authority. The draft law that would carry data protection is being prepared by the Justice Ministry together with the digital transformation ministry.

Standing. A data and artificial intelligence bill is in draft. On 6 August 2026 the Council of Ministers discussed it and directed further study before approval by the interim parliament, a joint sitting of the Sovereignty and Ministers councils. On 11 August 2026 the Justice Ministry's under-secretary named it the 2026 Law on Regulating Data and Artificial Intelligence, meant to provide the legislative framework, data protection included.

Regulations. The bill is one of several draft bills from the digital transformation ministry that the Council of Ministers discussed on 6 August 2026.

Application. The law is one of three draft laws the Justice Ministry said on 11 August 2026 it is preparing.

Last twelve months. Both steps fall in August 2026: the Council of Ministers' direction of further study on 6 August, and the Justice Ministry's statement that the draft is in preparation on 11 August.

Not found. What the bill provides, whether it has gone to the interim parliament, and any date for a vote or commencement. No supervisory authority acting under a data protection law, no regulations and no decisions have been found.

SEN.short: Senegal's 2008 data protection law is in force and applied, with figures published for April to June 2026; whether regulations exist under it is unknown.
SEN.summary:
Authority. The Commission de Protection des Données Personnelles (CDP) is constituted: it held two plenary sessions and issued decisions in April to June 2026. The law set it up as an independent administrative authority, and its president, Ousmane Thiongane, signed a partnership convention with Benin's authority in Cotonou, reported on 17 April 2026.

Standing. Law no. 2008-12 on the protection of personal data was enacted on 25 January 2008 and has been in force since 2014. On 27 March 2026 an expert told APS it is the current law, and the CDP issued receipts, authorisations and a rejection under it in April to June 2026.

Regulations. A workshop reported in July 2026 worked to finalise a draft data protection law and its implementing decree.

Application. For April to June 2026 the CDP reported 195 files handled, 153 declaration receipts and 39 authorisations issued, one processing rejected, and eight complaints and one report received and handled. Its plenary served a formal notice on SOLID SA, operator of the Kay Voter platform, for unsolicited prospecting by SMS, reported on 20 April 2024.

Last twelve months. The CDP relaunched the updating of the law at a two-day workshop at Saly, reported in July 2026, with the ministry committed to finalising the draft law and decree. In March 2026 an expert said a bill was reported to be in the circuit and that the National Assembly must vote it.

Not found. Whether any regulation is in force under Law no. 2008-12 is not stated. How far the bill to replace the law has got is not stated either.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone has no data protection law, only a bill Cabinet approved in April 2026; no source found says whether it has reached Parliament.
SLE.summary:
Authority. The Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill would establish a single independent authority for data protection and access to information. It would be the first such body in the country.

Standing. The law is a bill. In November 2025 the Information Minister said the Bill had concluded its final national validation. On 21 April 2026 he announced that Cabinet had authorised enactment of a new Data Protection and Right to Access Information Act. Cabinet also approved the repeal of the Right to Access Information Commission Act.

Regulations. On 21 April 2026 the Bill was still to be finalised and tabled in Parliament. That work fell to the Ministry of Information and Civic Education and the Attorney-General's office.

Application. In November 2025 the Bill had submission to Cabinet and then to Parliament still to come.

Last twelve months. The Bill moved from final national validation in November 2025 to Cabinet approval on 21 April 2026.

Not found. No law is enacted, and whether the Bill has been tabled in Parliament is not held. No regulations and no decisions have been found, and no source says there are none.

SOM.short: Somalia's 2023 data protection law is in force and its authority opened registration in 2026; no source found says whether any decision or sanction followed.
SOM.summary:
Authority. The Data Protection Authority was inaugurated on 24 February 2024. The Act sets it up as an independent agency under a General Manager, with a Board of up to nine members.

Standing. Law No. 005 of 2023, the Data Protection Act, was ratified by both chambers of parliament and signed by the President in March 2023. A notice from the Authority, reported on 2 June 2026, requires registration under Article 32 of every entity that collects, stores, processes or shares personal data in Somalia.

Regulations. A review published on 11 June 2024 says the Authority issued an Implementation Regulation, guidance and an Alternative Dispute Resolution Procedure under Article 41. The Council of Ministers approved the Regulatory Framework for the Public Data Protection Law by majority vote, reported on 8 January 2026.

Application. The Authority published guidelines for implementing the law at the beginning of February 2024. By 2 June 2026 it had begun accepting registration applications from controllers and processors, and said it will issue certificates only to those meeting the conditions.

Last twelve months. The Regulatory Framework was approved after the Ministry of Communications and Technology said it had cleared constitutional, legal and technical procedures, reported on 6 February 2026. The Authority opened registration of controllers and processors, reported on 2 June 2026.

Not found. No named and dated decision, sanction or order under the law, and no published count of decisions for a stated period. The date the 2023 Act came into force.

SSD.short: South Sudan has no data protection law; a bill was still being prepared in September 2026, and no source found says it has reached parliament.
SSD.summary:
Authority. The draft bill would set up a Data Protection Commission to guard the personal data of online users. Radio Tamazuj reported this on 20 November 2025.

Standing. South Sudan has no data protection law. The World Bank's identity diagnostic of 1 May 2026 says the country has no national data protection or privacy law. A bill is being drafted. In October 2025 digital security experts finished what Radio Tamazuj calls the first Data Protection Policy Bill. A post of 5 May 2026 reports a two-day workshop of over 30 people to validate the Data Protection Bill, 2025. On 8 September 2026 the ICT ministry's undersecretary said the bill was still in preparation.

Regulations. Koneta's Executive Director said in a release dated 17 October 2025 that existing ICT regulations are limited.

Application. The World Bank diagnostic states that South Sudan has no national data protection and privacy regime.

Last twelve months. In October 2025 Paradigm Initiative and Koneta Hub met lawmakers and officials in Juba to seek a commitment to table the bill. In December 2025 the ICT minister, Ateny Wek Ateny, said the bill would be introduced in 2026. The validation workshop was reported on 5 May 2026. At a Juba workshop in September 2026 the deputy minister urged the legislature to speed the bill's passage.

Not found. Any bill tabled in parliament or any law enacted. No regulation and no decision on a controller was found.

STP.short: São Tomé and Príncipe enacted a data protection law in 2016; no source found reports a decision or regulations under it.
STP.summary:
Authority. The Agência Nacional de Protecção de Dados Pessoais (ANPDP) is, in Téla Nón's words, the body that by law authorises and supervises all data processing; its president is José Manuel Costa Alegre. Portugal's data protection commission received an ANPDP delegation on 16 June 2025 and names the agency a founding member of the Lusophone Data Protection Network.

Standing. Lei n.º 03/2016, on the protection of personal data of natural persons, was published in Diário da República n.º 39 of 10 May 2016. An International Bar Association chapter published in 2024 names it as the primary instrument of a framework that applies to processing by controllers headquartered or established in the country.

Regulations. The law itself provides for fines and criminal sanctions, and leaves the agency's organic law, staff and members' statute to a later law of the National Assembly.

Application. The IBA chapter says the ANPDP imposes fines and ancillary measures under the law. On 14 April 2026 its president met the president of the National Assembly to plan the agency's oversight of personal data in the automatic electoral roll.

Last twelve months. On 1 June 2026 the ANPDP signed a cooperation memorandum with Macau's data protection office, which Macau executive orders had authorised by 27 May.

Not found. Whether any regulation has been made under Law 03/2016, the date it came into force, and any named sanction, decision or published count under it. Nothing dated in the twelve months to 30 September 2026 bears on the law itself.

SWZ.short: Eswatini has a Data Protection Act of 2022, applied through enforcement notices in 2024 and 2025; no source found reports the number of decisions made.
SWZ.summary:
Authority. The Data Protection Act designates the Eswatini Communications Commission as the Eswatini Data Protection Authority. In June 2026 the Authority had powers to investigate breaches, resolve complaints and impose sanctions, and took complaints by website, email and phone.

Standing. The Data Protection Act, 2022 (No. 5 of 2022) was assented to and gazetted on 4 March 2022. In June 2026 the Commission's acting chief executive said the Act binds public and private bodies, ministries included, and requires a breach to be notified to the Authority within 72 hours. The deadline for organisations to comply was 31 March 2026.

Regulations. Notice No. 1/2024, issued in February 2024, made registration mandatory from 1 March 2024 for controllers and processors handling the data of more than ten people. General Notice No. 4/2024 directed every data controller to appoint a data protection officer by 30 May 2024.

Application. The Authority lists enforcement notices under section 41 of the Act issued to MTN Eswatini and Liberty Life Swaziland Limited in June 2024 and to the Royal Science Technology Park in March 2025. In June 2026 it opened a formal investigation into the Ministry of Home Affairs over unblurred national identity documents posted online.

Last twelve months. By February 2026 the Authority had launched its 2026 awareness campaign, "Take Control of Your Data". In September 2026 it was setting up information desks in major towns, after its own survey found 55.2% of the public finding the Authority difficult to access.

Not found. No count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled is published for a stated year, and the newest enforcement notice on record is from March 2025. The outcome of the investigation opened in June 2026 is not reported.

SYC.short: Seychelles' Data Protection Act 2023 is in force and its commission handled 14 cases in 2025; no source found says any ended in a decision.
SYC.summary:
Authority. The Act names the Information Commission, established under the Access to Information Act, as the competent authority, with powers to investigate, audit, issue enforcement notices and impose administrative fines of up to SCR200,000. The Commission took on the mandate at the end of December 2023 and in 2025 had a Chief Information Commissioner, two Information Commissioners and a chief executive in post.

Standing. The Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 24 of 2023) was assented to on 19 December 2023 and bears the operative date 22 December 2023; it repeals the former Data Protection Act. The Commission administered it during 2025.

Regulations. The Act itself gave controllers and processors already processing data 18 months from commencement, to 22 June 2025, to conform.

Application. The Commission received four data protection cases in 2024, mostly from the non-banking financial sector, and 14 in 2025: six on data transfers, five breaches, two refused deletion requests and one consultation. It handled the 2025 cases by guidance, assessment and corrective advice.

Last twelve months. In January 2026 the Commission advertised a Senior Data Protection Analyst post. The National Assembly lists the Commission's annual report for 2025 as published on 13 April 2026. In that report the Chief Commissioner states that the Act remains at risk of being largely unenforced because the one budgeted technical post is unfilled.

Not found. No decision or sanction on a named controller and no count of cases settled has been found, only cases received and handled. Whether regulations have been made under the Act is not held.

TCD.short: In 2026 Chad's 2015 personal data law is treated as in force, with a replacement being drafted; no decision under it is known.
TCD.summary:
Authority. Under Loi n°007/PR/2015, transfers of personal data abroad need notification to or prior authorisation from ANSICE, the National Agency for Information Security and Electronic Certification, a law firm's analysis of July 2026 says; it adds that the agency's operational effectiveness is not documented.

Standing. A July 2026 analysis by the Cabinet Thomas Dingamgoto applies Loi n°007/PR/2015 to personal data and treats its articles 29 to 32 as the transfer rules in force. A replacement is being prepared: the minister said on 9 December 2025 that authorities were finalising a digital law carrying international data protection standards, and a report of 16 March 2026 described the Digital Code as under development since December 2025.

Regulations. The nearest held fact is the July 2026 analysis, which reads the rules for sending personal data abroad from articles 29 to 32 of the 2015 law itself.

Application. The same analysis says the law makes transfers abroad subject to notification to ANSICE or its prior authorisation, and that how far the agency acts on this is not documented.

Last twelve months. On 27 April 2026 the minister installed a committee of 34 members with 45 days to propose modernised digital texts, among them on personal data protection, which he called inadequately covered by the current rules.

Not found. Whether a body is constituted to supervise data protection, whether any regulation is made under the 2015 law and whether any decision has been taken under it are not held.

TGO.short: Togo has a 2019 data protection law; its authority trained correspondents in 2026, but no source found says whether any sanction has been issued.
TGO.summary:
Authority. Article 55 of the law creates a national authority, the Instance de protection des données à caractère personnel (IPDCP). The IPDCP officially launched its activities on 28 March 2025 in Lomé, and its head says it holds powers of control, injunction and sanction.

Standing. Loi n° 2019-014 of 29 October 2019 on the protection of personal data was adopted by the National Assembly and promulgated; article 95 gave State and public-service processing two years to comply and all other processing one year. On 15 September 2026 the IPDCP briefed ministry cabinet directors and secretaries-general on their obligations under it as data controllers.

Regulations. Article 58 of the law has the President of the Republic appoint the IPDCP's president by decree from its steering committee.

Application. The IPDCP gave attestations to 32 data protection correspondents on 24 June 2026 after three days of training in Adétikopé. On 15 September 2026 it convened public administrations in Lomé on prior formalities, declaration of existing processing and designation of correspondents.

Last twelve months. The IPDCP and the broadcast regulator HAAC signed a cooperation memorandum on 10 December 2025 that gives the IPDCP access to HAAC's monitoring room. The IPDCP opened its first evaluation and certification session for correspondents in Atakpamé on 30 September 2026, with 32 professionals. On 19 October 2026 the IPDCP placed a team in the media regulator HARC's monitoring service. It set a first national data protection day for 29 October 2026.

Not found. No regulation made under the law has been found. No named sanction or decision under it has been found, and no published count of decisions.

TUN.short: Tunisia's 2004 data protection law is in force and a replacement has been before parliament since 2025; no source found says the law is applied.
TUN.summary:
Authority. The 2004 law names the Instance nationale de protection des données à caractère personnel and gives it the powers to receive declarations and to authorise processing and transfers. Government decree no. 2021-230 of 16 April 2021 appointed twelve members to it for three years: two members of parliament, two judges, ministry representatives, a human rights committee member and an ICT expert.

Standing. Organic law no. 2004-63 of 27 July 2004 on the protection of personal data sets the general regime for processing, consent and rights, and was the operative statute in September 2026. A draft organic law, no. 95/2025, was deposited before the Assembly of the Representatives of the People on 14 July 2025 and would repeal the 2004 law six months after publication.

Regulations. The law itself has the authority receive declarations and authorise processing and transfers.

Application. A representative of the authority was scheduled to be heard by the Assembly's Rights and Freedoms Committee on 25 February 2026, on the proposed new law.

Last twelve months. The Rights and Freedoms Committee scheduled a hearing of the sponsoring deputies on 17 February 2026 and began examining the articles of the bill's first title that month, a text that adds rules on artificial intelligence, surveillance cameras and health data. Tech Hive Advisory lists Tunisia among countries moving to amend an existing law in January and February 2026.

Not found. No regulation made under organic law no. 2004-63 is held, and no dated sanction, decision or count of decisions under it. The three-year term of the members appointed in 2021 has run out and no later appointment has been found.

TZA.short: Tanzania's Personal Data Protection Act 2022, in force since 2023, was applied in a 2025 ruling; no source found counts its decisions.
TZA.summary:
Authority. The Act establishes the Personal Data Protection Commission as a body corporate, with a seven-member Board and a Director General. The Commission delivered a ruling on a complaint on 19 August 2025, and its Director General, Dr Emmanuel Mkilia, announced on-site inspections in Dodoma on 28 August 2026.

Standing. The Personal Data Protection Act, 2022 (Act No. 11 of 2022, Chapter 44) commenced on 1 May 2023 and applies to Mainland Tanzania and, for union matters, Zanzibar.

Regulations. The Personal Data Protection (Collection and Processing) Regulations, Government Notice No. 449C of 2023, apply alongside the Act. The Commission's ruling of 19 August 2025 applied regulation 17, on erasure, and regulation 18, on children's data in commercial advertisements.

Application. On 19 August 2025 the Commission ruled in Complaint No. PDPC/CMP/002/2025 against the operator of an Instagram business page, awarding the complainant TZS 20 million in damages, imposing a fine of TZS 5 million and ordering a newborn's photographs deleted within 14 days. Its preliminary assessments, reported on 28 August 2026, found inaccurate registration data and unlawful transfers of data abroad.

Last twelve months. On 8 January 2026 the Minister of Communication and Information Technology gave unregistered institutions a final three months to register and told the Commission to prepare nationwide compliance audits. On 11 February the Commission announced inspections from 9 April, on 12 June it gave institutions with incomplete registration seven days to finish, and on-site inspections began on 31 August.

Not found. No published count of the Commission's decisions for a stated year has been found. The report of the August 2025 ruling does not name the respondent.

UGA.short: Uganda's Data Protection and Privacy Act is in force and was applied in decisions of 2025 and 2026; no source found reports yearly decision counts.
UGA.summary:
Authority. The Personal Data Protection Office is established under the Data Protection and Privacy Act and headed by a director, Baker Birikujja. It keeps a register of data collectors, controllers and processors.

Standing. The Data Protection and Privacy Act, Cap 97, is in force. The office's director said in August 2026 that it requires data collectors and processors to register and makes failure to register a criminal offence. The office has held that the Act applies to foreign entities serving persons in Uganda.

Regulations. The office's decision of 20 February 2026 was made under the Data Protection and Privacy Regulations, 2021. Its decisions apply Regulation 15 on registration, Regulation 30 on cross-border transfers, Regulation 46 on appeal and Regulation 48 on offences.

Application. On 18 July 2025 the office found Google LLC in breach of the Act's registration and cross-border transfer duties and ordered it to register within 30 days. On 20 February 2026 it partly upheld a complaint and issued five corrective orders to WhatsApp LLC, with no fine.

Last twelve months. On 3 December 2025 a magistrate fined the finance manager of Vuka Africa Ltd sh100,000 for failing to register with the office. By letter of 17 July 2026 the office confirmed that WhatsApp LLC had implemented the corrective measures. In August 2026 its director said 14,697 of an estimated 50,000 entities required to register had done so.

Not found. No count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled for a stated period. The year the Act was passed and the date it commenced are not given.

ZAF.short: South Africa's Protection of Personal Information Act, 2013 has been in force since 2021 and is applied; no source found reports the planned amendment's text.
ZAF.summary:
Authority. The Information Regulator was established on 1 December 2016 to monitor and enforce the Act. Its annual report for the year to 31 March 2025 describes an independent body under section 39 of the Act.

Standing. The Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 was signed into law in 2013. It has been in force since 1 July 2021, with fines of up to R10 million.

Regulations. Regulations on processing health information, under section 112(2)(c) of the Act, were published in Government Gazette 54268 on 6 March 2026. They commenced on publication. An enforcement notice of 21 February 2024 cites earlier regulations under section 112(2).

Application. The Regulator reports that in 2024/25 it received 1,355 complaints under the Act and resolved 745. Its first fine, in July 2023, was R5 million on the Department of Justice and Constitutional Development. It issued an enforcement notice to WhatsApp LLC on 10 September 2024.

Last twelve months. On 20 May 2026 the Regulator published an enforcement notice against Central Johannesburg TVET College. On 26 October 2026 it fined the college R500,000 for not complying, and First National Bank R1 million over security safeguards. In August 2026 it issued an enforcement notice to the South African Bureau of Standards over a 2024 ransomware attack. On 18 August 2026 a commissioner said work is under way with the justice department to amend the Act. The amendment would cover artificial intelligence and privacy by design.

Not found. No bill or draft of the amendment to the Act. The dates of the fines on the Electoral Commission and Lancet Laboratories are not given.

ZMB.short: Zambia's Data Protection Act of 2021 is in force, applied so far through registration and training; no source found reports a decision under it.
ZMB.summary:
