Authority. The Data Protection Commissioner, Likando Luywa, spoke in June 2026 on oversight and the registration of data controllers and processors. A tender of 10 August 2026 seeks a firm to build a compliance management system for the Data Protection Commission of Zambia.

Standing. The law is the Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021, which a tender of 10 August 2026 names as the Act being implemented. It was described in July 2026 as part of the legal framework businesses must comply with, and a World Bank appraisal document published on 5 September 2024 gives it as the standard for the Department of National Registration's personal-data procedures.

Regulations. A tender of 10 August 2026 seeks consultants to help the Commission develop regulatory instruments for implementing the Act.

Application. Data controllers and processors had until 30 April 2025 to register under the Act. UNDP, writing on 17 September 2024, listed training staff in more than 145 offices across 10 provinces on the Act as a requirement of the digital ID rollout. Lusaka Star reported on 7 June 2026 that enforcement and compliance remained a challenge.

Last twelve months. A World Bank-financed tender opened on 10 August 2026, with expressions of interest due on 21 August, for a three-month assignment to review and develop national data protection guidelines and compliance frameworks. The Office of the Data Protection Commissioner joined Zambia's delegation to the ID4Africa conference in Abidjan, which ended on 15 May 2026.

Not found. No regulation made under the Act is on record, and the date the Act came into force is not stated. No decision, sanction or count of cases under the Act is on record; registration and training are the only application shown.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe has the Cyber and Data Protection Act of 2021, applied through licensing and notices; no source found says whether any controller has been sanctioned.
ZWE.summary:
Authority. Section 5 of the Act designates POTRAZ, the Postal and Telecommunications Regulatory Authority, as the Data Protection Authority. In May 2026 it had a Director for Data Protection. Its powers include audits, investigations, warnings, directions and prosecutions.

Standing. The Cyber and Data Protection Act, No. 5 of 2021, was gazetted on 11 March 2022. It applies to all public and private organisations. In May 2026 it provided criminal sanctions for accountable officers, including up to seven years in prison.

Regulations. In September 2024 the ICT minister made licensing regulations, Statutory Instrument 155 of 2024, under section 32 of the Act. Organisations processing the data of 50 or more people must hold a data controller licence. Fees run from US$50 to US$2,500 a year, and the first deadline was 12 March 2025.

Application. POTRAZ handed the first data controller licences to 570 companies in June 2025, and 721 were licensed by 15 October 2025. In March 2026 POTRAZ reported 1,123 licence applications so far that year and more than 60 breaches notified. Its Director for Data Protection said in May 2026 that administrative sanctions were not yet in place.

Last twelve months. Regulatory Notice 2 of 2026, published in July 2026, announced mandatory compliance inspections of data controllers from 1 September 2026. In September 2026 POTRAZ consulted on guidelines under the Act and on amendments to the regulations covering administrative fines.

Not found. No named and dated sanction or decision on a controller. No count of decisions for a stated period.

AGO.short: Law in force since 2011; the authority is appointed and working, and fined a hotel company in August 2026.
AGO.summary:
Law in force. Lei n.º 22/11 on personal data protection was published on 17 June 2011 and enters into force on the date of its publication. In June 2026 the Assembleia Nacional rejected a bill to amend it.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Angola ratified the Convention on 21 February 2020 and deposited its instrument on 11 May 2020.

Authority appointed. The Agência de Protecção de Dados was set up by Decreto Presidencial n.º 214/16 and Decreto Presidencial n.º 277/19 of 6 September 2019 appointed a president and two executive administrators to its board. In August 2026 its board took a sanction decision.

Implementing and acting. On 10 August 2026 the authority fined Lizária, Lda., owner of Hotel Diamante, the kwanza equivalent of USD 115,000 under Deliberação n.º 006/2026. Its register of fines lists 15 fines for 2022 to 2026, of US$75,000 to US$525,000 each.

Not found. No gap is recorded against the four questions.

BDI.short: A law was promulgated in March 2026; no source found says whether it is in force, nor an appointed authority or any ruling.
BDI.summary:
Law in force. Burundi's National Assembly unanimously adopted a bill on personal data protection on 15 January 2026, covering the collection and processing of personal data across public and private sectors. It is structured in eight chapters, and the head of state promulgated the law on 10 March 2026, per Community Voice.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Burundi.

Authority appointed. The law establishes an independent administrative authority to oversee data protection, responsible for enforcement, and a dedicated body to implement and monitor data protection regimes.

Implementing and acting. DLA Piper's guide of 17 January 2024 described only sector confidentiality provisions in Burundi, before the 2026 law was adopted, and stated that no national data protection authority existed then.

Not found. Whether the law has entered into force, whether the authority has been constituted and whether it has ruled on any organisation are not established.

BEN.short: Law in force since 2018; the authority is appointed and working, and published figures for its decisions in 2025.
BEN.summary:
Law in force. Personal data protection in Benin sits in Book V of the Digital Code, law no. 2017-20 of 20 April 2018, which the APDP's 2015-2020 report gives as its legal framework. The code is amended by law no. 2020-35 of 6 January 2021, and La Nation of 5 September 2026 treats it as the current framework.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Benin ratified the Malabo Convention on 14 May 2024 and deposited its instrument on 12 November 2024.

Authority appointed. The Autorité de Protection des Données Personnelles is established by Articles 462 to 473 of the Digital Code. Its president, Me Luciano Hounkponou, spoke at a forum in Johannesburg on 1 to 3 September 2026, and its 2026 budget programme is XOF 738,277,000.

Implementing and acting. The APDP's 2025 report gives 907 files examined, 64 inspection missions, 20 complaints treated and 75 compliance certificates issued. Its 2015-2020 report records 347 decisions rendered over 2016 to 2020, including the CNIL's refusal on 18 August 2016 of Spacetel Benin authorisation to collect biometric data.

Not found. No gap is recorded against the four questions.

BFA.short: Law in force since 2021; authority appointed and working; no ruling against an organisation is known.
BFA.summary:
Law in force. Law no. 001-2021/AN of 30 March 2021 abrogates law no. 010-2004/AN and gives one year from entry into force for all processing to comply. The CIL invoked it in a communiqué of 24 December 2024, and the CIL president recalled on 1 July 2025 that data protection is compulsory under it.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Burkina Faso.

Authority appointed. The Commission de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CIL) is led by its president, Dr Nassa, and was funded in 2024 under its own budget programme, XOF 857,062,000 appropriated and 93.3 percent executed. On 18 November 2025 its president signed the operational roadmap of the AES data protection authorities' coordination framework with Mali and Niger.

Implementing and acting. By communiqué of 24 December 2024 the CIL warned that repeated posting of people's images on social media without consent violates the law. On 1 July 2025 the Prime Minister launched CIL awareness sessions on personal data protection for ministries and public institutions, and on 26 June 2025 the CIL validated its public report for 2024.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

BWA.short: A data protection law has been in force since 2025, the commission is working, and it ruled against an organisation in 2026.
BWA.summary:
Law in force. The Data Protection Act No. 18 of 2024 came into operation on 14 January 2025. It applies to all organisations processing personal data, including public entities, Mmegi states.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Convention by Botswana.

Authority appointed. Mmegi reports Kepaletswe Somolekae as the newly appointed Information and Data Protection Commissioner on 11 February 2026. The Commission was established in 2022, and in July 2025 it had three contract officers, with the Deputy Commissioner and two director posts unfilled.

Implementing and acting. On 17 July 2026 the Commission issued a Determination and an Enforcement Notice against DPSM, ordering the ePayslip portal suspended and a DPIA and revised privacy notice submitted within one month. Mmegi reports DPSM suspended the portal on 22 July 2026.

Not found. Nothing further on the four questions is held.

CAF.short: A data protection law is in force, but no authority is appointed, so none has ruled against an organisation, as of 2026.
CAF.summary:
Law in force. Data Protection Africa states in its factsheet of 28 January 2026 that the Central African Republic has a data protection law in place. The promulgated text of Loi n° 24.001, adopted in January 2024, gives no commencement date and no compliance period. Jurist Zengue writes in September 2025 that the law is promulgated and applied, with a compliance period running and no suspension of its execution.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Convention by the Central African Republic.

Authority appointed. Data Protection Africa states the data protection authority had not yet been appointed as of 28 January 2026. Article 57 gives the ministry in charge of the digital economy twelve months from promulgation to set up the data protection agency, and names no composition, seat or financing for it.

Implementing and acting. The law's text vests the agency's missions in the ministry in charge of the digital economy until the agency is set up.

Not found. No source found says the Malabo Convention has been signed or ratified, or that an authority has been appointed. Nothing is held on how the law is applied or on any ruling.

CIV.short: A data protection law is in force and its authority is working, but no ruling against an organisation is known as of 2026.
CIV.summary:
Law in force. The law of 19 June 2013 on personal data protection is the framework under which a 2015 decree sets filing fees, prior authorisations and fines of up to FCFA 500 million on repeat breach. The digital minister cited the same law as the country's existing framework on 18 May 2026.

Malabo Convention. The African Union Commission's status list of 2 February 2026 records Côte d'Ivoire as having ratified or acceded to the Convention on 8 March 2023, with the instrument deposited on 3 April 2023.

Authority appointed. ARTCI, styling itself the Autorité de Protection des Données Personnelles, issued a communique on 3 August 2026 inviting controllers to use CERTINUM. A fact sheet of 23 May 2022 says a data protection authority is appointed, with 7 members serving up to 6 years.

Implementing and acting. ARTCI launched Certinum on 2 July 2026, an online platform for compliance and processing-authorisation requests, replacing about 100 paper files handled each month. The minister listed compliance control operations carried out in 2022 and national awareness campaigns launched from 2015.

Not found. No ruling by the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

CMR.short: A data protection law came into force in 2026, but no authority is appointed, so no ruling against an organisation is known.
CMR.summary:
Law in force. The Direction Generale du Budget (Ministry of Finance) states that the deadline set for the entry into force of Law No. 2024/017 of 23 December 2024 on personal data protection was reached on 23 June 2026, and that the law is now officially in force. The authors of an African Law & Business article of 17 July 2025 say the law becomes enforceable after an 18-month grace period from enactment.

Malabo Convention. The African Union Commission's status list of 2 February 2026 records Cameroon as having signed the Convention on 12 August 2021, with no ratification or deposit date. A Direction Generale du Budget article of 24 September 2024 likewise says Cameroon signed on 12 August 2021 and that ratification is awaited.

Authority appointed. The law defines the Autorité as an independent public body in charge of data protection and gives it supervision, notification and enforcement functions. The African Law & Business authors said in July 2025 that the authority the law provides for was yet to be established.

Implementing and acting. The Minister of Posts and Telecommunications told the National Assembly on 8 April 2025 that Cameroon had adopted the law of 23 December 2024, setting principles, controller obligations and data subject rights.

Not found. No ratification of the Malabo Convention has been found, and no source found says an authority has been appointed. Nothing is held on how the law is applied or on any ruling.

COD.short: Since 2023 a data protection law is in force; no authority is appointed yet and no ruling against an organisation is known.
COD.summary:
Law in force. The Digital Code, Ordinance-Law No. 23/010 of 13 March 2023, entered into force in 2023 and provides for the Autorité de Protection des Données.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that the Democratic Republic of the Congo ratified the Malabo Convention on 6 March 2025 and deposited its instrument on 27 June 2025.

Authority appointed. Beto.cd reported on 13 September 2026 that the Autorité de protection des données is not installed. A ministerial order of 17 August 2024 provisionally gave its missions to ARPTIC pending its establishment. Its organisation and operation await a Prime Minister's decree.

Implementing and acting. On 12 March 2026 the Ministry of Digital Economy launched a national network of data protection officers in Kinshasa, backed by RUDI International and Droit-Numérique.cd, to standardise personal data practice and support compliance. No sanction or decision is reported.

Not found. No source dated in the last three years shows an appointed authority registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting.

COG.short: A data protection law is in force and an authority was appointed in 2025; no ruling against an organisation is known.
COG.summary:
Law in force. Law No. 29-2019 of 10 October 2019 on personal data protection is in force as of 22 January 2026, and Decree No. 2025-538 completes the institutional framework it established.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Congo ratified the Malabo Convention on 24 September 2020 and deposited its instrument on 23 October 2020.

Authority appointed. The National Personal Data Protection Commission was inaugurated in January 2026 after its members were appointed under Decree No. 2025-538 of 31 December 2025. Its President, Vice President and Rapporteur were elected at the inaugural meeting.

Implementing and acting. On 22 January 2026 ITWeb Africa reported that Congo-Brazzaville has established the Commission, whose members were installed by ICT minister Leon Juste Ibombo, who described it as an independent body able to advise, warn and sanction.

Not found. No source dated in the last three years shows an appointed authority registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting.

COM.short: Comoros passed a data protection law in 2021; no source found says it is in force, and no appointed authority or ruling is known.
COM.summary:
Law in force. TechHive Advisory states the Union of Comoros enacted its Protection of Personal Data Law on 29 June 2021 as a comprehensive framework. The Assembly adopted Loi n°14-029/AU on personal data protection, 68 articles, in plenary session on 26 June 2014.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Comoros signed the Malabo Convention on 29 January 2018 and had not ratified it.

Authority appointed. TechHive Advisory states the law establishes a National Authority for the Protection of Personal Data but that as of mid-2024 it had not been formally constituted or made operational. Article 19 of the 2014 law institutes a Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés whose nine members are named by decree under Article 24.

Implementing and acting. As of mid-2024, TechHive Advisory states the authority had not been formally constituted or made operational.

Not found. The evidence does not establish whether the law has commenced, whether the authority has been constituted since mid-2024, or any ruling against an organisation.

CPV.short: A data protection law is in force and an authority is working in 2025; no ruling against an organisation is known.
CPV.summary:
Law in force. The CNPD president says the base data protection law dates from 2001 and was amended in 2013 and in 2021, in an interview published 2 February 2025. The IBA chapter states Law 133/V/2001 is Cabo Verde's general data protection regime, applying within the country and to processing of data of people located in it.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Cape Verde ratified the Malabo Convention on 13 November 2020 and deposited its instrument on 5 February 2022.

Authority appointed. The CNPD, led by president Faustino Varela, started in 2015-2016 and completes a decade of existence in 2025. Resolução n.º 160/X/2024 appropriates CVE 36,313,115 for the CNPD in the Assembly's own budget for FY2025, up from CVE 35,255,451 in FY2024.

Implementing and acting. The CNPD president says cases have arrived involving AI and Big Data, including two generative-AI image manipulation cases, with cases that may be criminal sent to the Ministério Público; no decision or count is given. The CNPD's 2024 activity plan, dated 27 December 2023, covers planned inspections, guidance and international fora.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

DJI.short: A data protection law was passed in 2025 but is not in force; no authority is appointed or has ruled against an organisation.
DJI.summary:
Law in force. The National Assembly passed Djibouti's first Digital Code, with a data-protection regime embedded in it, on 30 June 2025. It was still to be promulgated by the President and published in the Journal Officiel. TechHive Advisory describes the regime as 156 articles in all, within the Code.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that Djibouti signed the Convention on 12 May 2023 and had not ratified it.

Authority appointed. The Code creates the National Commission for the Protection of Personal Data, independent with administrative and financial autonomy. Jones Day frames the competent authorities as still to be operationalised.

Implementing and acting. TechHive Advisory states that the regime was enacted in June 2025 as part of the Digital Code, and gives no promulgation or commencement date.

Not found. The date the Code was promulgated or took effect, whether the commission has been constituted, and any ruling by it.

DZA.short: The law is in force and the authority is working in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is reported.
DZA.summary:
Law in force. The US International Trade Administration states that Law No. 18-07, enacted on 10 June 2018, came into force on 10 August 2023. El Moudjahid reports that law 25-11, promulgated in July 2025, amends it with data protection delegate, processing register and operations log duties. The Interior Minister said on 8 December 2025 that the law governs and sanctions illegal use of the national identification number.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Convention by Algeria.

Authority appointed. The national authority, the ANPDP, adopted a deliberation on 15 July 2026 by a majority of its members, signed by its president, with twelve members named. El Moudjahid names Samir Bourehil as its president in July 2026.

Implementing and acting. The ANPDP's deliberation says it has put an online complaint service at the disposal of data subjects. Tech Hive Advisory reports a decision in early 2026 on employee drug test results, and a 2025 roundup reports a compliance package of guidelines and four templates.

Not found. Any ruling by the authority against a named organisation in the last three years.

EGY.short: The law is in force and an authority is appointed and issuing guidance in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is reported.
EGY.summary:
Law in force. Shura Law Firm says Law No. 151 of 2020 entered into force in October 2020 and its regulations' transitional period expires on 31 October 2026. Baker McKenzie says all data users must be in full compliance by that date, and Access Partnership says enforcement is expected from 1 November 2026.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Convention by Egypt.

Authority appointed. A 7 August 2026 report says the Personal Data Protection Centre, affiliated to the ICT ministry, is acting under Law 151 of 2020 with an acting chief executive. Baker McKenzie says it launched its electronic portal in early October 2026 for accreditation, licence and permit applications.

Implementing and acting. Tech Hive Advisory says the Centre published guidelines on consent, lawful bases, direct marketing and licences, and breach-notification templates, in January and February 2026. Baker McKenzie says its portal also publishes guidelines and frameworks setting out requirements for controllers and processors.

Not found. Any ruling by the Centre against an organisation, and any inspection it has carried out.

ERI.short: No data protection law is in force and no authority is appointed in 2026, so none has ruled against an organisation.
ERI.summary:
Law in force. Law Lab Africa states that no comprehensive data protection law is in force in Eritrea, as of a verification pass on 1 August 2026. A June 2025 Horn of Africa Initiative update says Eritrea remains without data protection legislation.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Eritrea.

Authority appointed. Law Lab Africa states that no supervisory authority has been established in Eritrea, as of 1 August 2026. Levellers, reviewed on 8 June 2026, states that no data protection authority has been appointed.

Implementing and acting. Law Lab Africa states that no enforcement decisions could be found for Eritrea and none are published, as of the 1 August 2026 verification pass by that source.

Not found. Any draft data protection law, and any body with data protection duties.

ETH.short: Ethiopia published a data protection law in 2024 and its communications regulator oversees it; no ruling against an organisation is known.
ETH.summary:
Law in force. Ethiopia published its Personal Data Protection Proclamation in the Federal Negarit Gazette on 24 July 2024, and Shega reported in November 2025 that it took effect on publication.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Ethiopia.

Authority appointed. The Ethiopian Communications Authority is the regulator under Article 5 of the Proclamation, per the Tech Hive review; its Director General said in November 2025 that data processors and collectors now need the Authority's permission and that staffing and technical capacity are being expanded.

Implementing and acting. The Authority told Shega it had received about 10 requests to transfer data abroad and approved them as a temporary measure, and officials previewed a registration portal for data controllers and processors at a workshop co-hosted with Huawei.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

GAB.short: Gabon's data protection law was published in 2023, its authority is working, and it fined Citibank Gabon in 2024.
GAB.summary:
Law in force. Loi n°025/2023 of 12 July 2023 amended the 2011 data protection law with rights, controller duties, data protection officers, breach notification and sanctions, and was published in the Journal Officiel on 15 July 2023.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Gabon.

Authority appointed. The APDPVP sat in plenary on 25 April 2024 with a named president, vice-president and six other permanent commissioners, appointed by a Council of Ministers decision of 12 July 2023; its president, Joel Dominique Ledaga, spoke as its sitting head on 4 September 2026.

Implementing and acting. By deliberation n°073 of 25 April 2024, the APDPVP imposed a sanction of 90,000,000 FCFA on Citibank Gabon S.A. for diverting employee data from its declared purpose and processing ethnic-origin data. Its president said in September 2026 it had logged about 715 declarations of conformity and about 30 complaints from individuals.

Not found. Nothing is outstanding on the four questions.

GHA.short: Ghana's data protection law is in force and its commission was registering controllers and referring organisations to police in October 2026; no ruling is known.
GHA.summary:
Law in force. The Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843) is the law the Data Protection Commission enforces, and a Circuit Court in Accra applied it in a judgment of 18 September 2024.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that Ghana ratified the Malabo Convention on 13 May 2019 and deposited its instrument on 3 June 2019.

Authority appointed. The Data Protection Commission is led by Executive Director Dr Arnold Kavaarpuo, according to the Ghana News Agency in October 2026. A new Governing Board chaired by Teki Akuetteh was sworn in in August 2025, and the 2026 budget estimates appropriate GHS 9,720,400 to the Commission, which has 39 staff.

Implementing and acting. The Commission said in August 2026 that enforcement actions have begun and it had declared 2026 the "Year of Enforcement". It registered 2,575 data controllers in 2026 and is running inspections, and on 12 October 2026 it directed Nyaho Medical Centre to report to the Police CID over an expired registration certificate. The Communications Minister reported a 98.4 per cent rise in newly registered data controllers in the first half of 2026. On 20 October 2026 it warned a ministry and media over disclosing evacuees' personal data.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

GIN.short: Guinea's 2016 data protection law is in force and the Malabo Convention ratified, but no authority is appointed and no ruling is known.
GIN.summary:
Law in force. The 2016 cybersecurity and personal data protection law, Loi L/2016/037/AN, was adopted and promulgated by President Alpha Condé, and the ministry's secretary-general said in October 2025 that it is in place. At the closing of the Transform Africa Summit on 19 November 2025, Minister Rose Pola Pricemou said Guinea is strengthening its regulatory framework with a new data-protection law.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that Guinea ratified the Malabo Convention on 31 July 2018 and deposited its instrument on 16 October 2018. A presidential decree of 26 July 2017 had ratified it.

Authority appointed. The 2016 law defines an Autorité de Protection and sets its functions, including declarations, transfer approval and investigation. The CNT reported on 20 June 2024 that its commissions debated a bill to establish the authority, with the designation of members and their mandates still contested.

Implementing and acting. The bill to establish the authority was awaiting plenary adoption, the CNT reported on 20 June 2024.

Not found. No authority constituted or appointed has been found, and no source dated in the last three years shows one registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting.

GMB.short: A law was enacted in 2025 but no start date is known; an authority is working; no ruling against an organisation is known.
GMB.summary:
Law in force. President Barrow assented the Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2025 on 7 November 2025, with no grace period before it becomes enforceable and no commencement date given.

Malabo Convention. The Gambia signed the African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection on 2 December 2022 and the minister reiterated the government's commitment to ratify it. In April 2024 the minister told a UN commission that the government ratified it in March 2024; the African Union's list of 2 February 2026 records no ratification.

Authority appointed. The Information Commission of The Gambia is to develop a communication strategy raising awareness of the Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2025, per a notice published on 17 August 2026.

Implementing and acting. Paradigm Initiative says the Gambia enacted data protection legislation in September 2025 and calls for implementation and enforcement by the relevant authorities, in a press release dated 29 January 2026.

Not found. A commencement date for the Act, and any ruling against an organisation.

GNB.short: Guinea-Bissau has no data protection law in force in 2026 and no authority appointed; no ruling against an organisation is known.
GNB.summary:
Law in force. A professor at the Bissau Faculty of Law said on 22 September 2026 that Guinea-Bissau does not yet have specific data protection legislation, and a national report of 18 February 2025 lists a personal data protection bill awaiting discussion.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Guinea-Bissau signed the Malabo Convention on 31 January 2015 and had not ratified it.

Authority appointed. The professor said Guinea-Bissau has no dedicated national data protection authority, these matters being handled by several institutions sector by sector; a Data Protection Africa factsheet of 25 May 2022 gave the same finding.

Implementing and acting. The professor said a bill provides for creating a 'Data Protection Agency', with independence risks in its membership and in leaving its organisation to a decree.

Not found. The stage of the bill, and any ruling against an organisation.

GNQ.short: A law has been in force since 2016, but its authority was not appointed as of 2022 and no ruling is known.
GNQ.summary:
Law in force. Ley Núm. 1/2016 of 22 July 2016 sets rules for personal data processing in the public and private sectors and enters into force twenty days after its publication in the Boletín Oficial del Estado.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's Infrastructure and Energy Department reports that Equatorial Guinea's foreign minister signed the Malabo Convention in Addis Ababa on 28 July 2026, as a step towards ratification.

Authority appointed. Articles 15 and 29 name the Órgano Rector de Protección de Datos Personales as the supervisory body, to be created by a decree that will fix its structure.

Implementing and acting. Data Protection Africa (ALT Advisory) states that Law No. 1/2016 creates the Governing Body for the Protection of Personal Data as the data protection authority, but that it is not yet appointed or operational.

Not found. Ratification of the Malabo Convention is not held, nor is any appointment to the authority or any ruling against an organisation.

KEN.short: A data protection law is in force and the authority is appointed and working; it has fined businesses since 2022.
KEN.summary:
Law in force. The Office of the Data Protection Commissioner enforces the Data Protection Act and Regulations and has issued fines under it since 2022, and in a Senate statement on 13 May 2026 the ICT Cabinet Secretary said the Data Protection Act, 2019 is being enforced.

Malabo Convention. Citizen Digital reported on 8 September 2026 that Kenya had not yet formally joined the Malabo Convention: Cabinet approved it in 2025 and ratification awaits National Assembly approval.

Authority appointed. The Office of the Data Protection Commissioner was established under the Data Protection Act, 2019, with inaugural commissioner Immaculate Kassait in office since 2020; the ODPC bulletin of March 2025 shows the Office registering data handlers from offices in Nairobi, Kisumu, Mombasa, Eldoret, Machakos, Nyeri and Nakuru.

Implementing and acting. The ODPC bulletin states that as of March 2025 the Office had received 7,128 complaints, issued 215 determinations and imposed penalties on 10 entities, and Cadmus Cyber Solutions states the Office had fined at least nine businesses KES 26,275,000 in total by September 2024.

Not found. A completed ratification of the Malabo Convention.

LBR.short: A data protection law is in force from 2026; no authority is known to be working and no ruling against an organisation is known.
LBR.summary:
Law in force. Liberia's printed Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act, approved on 9 March 2026 and printed on 23 March 2026, takes effect on publication into handbills (s.44), and existing businesses have one year from the effective date to comply (s.41).

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Liberia.

Authority appointed. Sections 8 and 10 of the Act give data protection functions to the Independent Information Commissioner, the oversight body created by the Freedom of Information Act of 2010; the Act does not state that the Commissioner has begun acting under it.

Implementing and acting. On 13 September 2026 the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection said that it is aware of its responsibilities under Liberia's Data Protection and Privacy Act, and that it took part in validating the legal framework.

Not found. The country has not ratified the Malabo Convention, and no source found says an authority has been appointed.

LBY.short: Libya's data protection law was still a draft in 2026, no authority is known, and Libya has not signed the Malabo Convention.
LBY.summary:
Law in force. Libya's National AI Strategy, adopted on 1 June 2026, concedes that the Data Protection and Privacy Law is still in draft, and sets its adoption as a 2026 target under the strategy's second pillar. Until it passes, no general law governs the collection and use of personal data.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification by Libya, so the Convention's data protection rules do not bind it either.

Authority appointed. SMEX reported in July 2026 that Libya has no functioning data protection authority. The draft law, not yet adopted, is the instrument that would create one.

Implementing and acting. None: with the law still a draft and no authority in place, no body registers organisations, takes breach reports, issues guidance or rules on complaints.

Not found. No data protection law in force has been found, and no authority.

LSO.short: A data protection law is in force; the authority it creates has not been appointed, and no ruling against an organisation is known (2026).
LSO.summary:
Law in force. Cenfri says that Lesotho's Data Protection Act has been law for over a decade, in a document published on 23 March 2026.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that Lesotho ratified or acceded to the Malabo Convention on 5 February 2025 and deposited its instrument on 16 February 2025.

Authority appointed. Cenfri says that the Data Protection Commission under Lesotho's Data Protection Act has remained unappointed, in its document published on 23 March 2026.

Implementing and acting. The law firm Z. Mayet and Associates states that the Act establishes a Data Protection Commission, but that the Commission and its Commissioner have not been appointed, in a document published on 31 October 2025.

Not found. No source dated in the last three years shows an appointed authority registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting.

MAR.short: Law 09-08 is in force and the CNDP authority is working, issuing guidance in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
MAR.summary:
Law in force. The president of the CNDP, interviewed on 4 August 2026, speaks of Law 09-08 as in force for more than fifteen years, with its paradigms still applicable.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Morocco.

Authority appointed. The CNDP, Morocco's national commission for the control of personal data protection, validated five new deliberations on 28 November 2025, acting as the supervisory body.

Implementing and acting. In a communiqué dated 28 August 2026, the CNDP gave guidance on Law 09-08 to political parties and voters for the 23 September 2026 elections, and opened a 3020 information line. It published a national register of notified processing operations in January 2023.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

MDG.short: A 2015 law is in force and its authority was sworn in during August 2025; no ruling against an organisation is known.
MDG.summary:
Law in force. Loi n° 2014-038 on the protection of personal data was promulgated on 9 January 2015, and the procedures manual of the data protection commission, dated December 2025, treats it as the operative legal basis for its work.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that Madagascar ratified the Malabo Convention on 17 July 2025 and deposited its instrument on 15 September 2025.

Authority appointed. Seven members of the Commission Malagasy de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CMIL) were sworn in at the Cour suprême on 4 August 2025. Its bureau was elected on 14 August 2025, and in March 2026 the Unité de Gouvernance Digitale announced the CMIL is now effectively in place.

Implementing and acting. The CMIL's annual report of January 2026 says no processing declaration has been registered yet, that citizens' complaints went untreated for ten years, and that the commission has no premises or staff, with 104 posts targeted in the 2026 Finance Law.

Not found. No source dated in the last three years shows the authority registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting.

MLI.short: Law 2013-015 is in force and its authority works; it fined a Bamako clinic and a company in 2025.
MLI.summary:
Law in force. Law no. 2013-015 of 21 May 2013, as amended, is the basis the authority's president cited for its sanctions when opening its session on 3 August 2026. A decree of 14 May 2024 is made under it.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Mali.

Authority appointed. The Autorité de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel (APDP) held its second ordinary session on 3 August 2026 under president Pr Mamoudou Samassekou with all commissioners present. It opened regional offices at Kayes, Sikasso, Segou and Mopti and a Ségou antenna on 4 December 2025.

Implementing and acting. In 2025 the APDP fined a Bamako clinic 5 million FCFA for obstructing a verification mission and fined Société Aminata Konaté SARL 5 million F CFA for refusing one. Sahel Tribune, summarising the 2025 annual report, reports fines totalling 22 million FCFA.

Not found. Nothing further on the four questions is held.

MOZ.short: No law is in force and no authority is appointed; a draft law is on parliament's October 2026 agenda. No ruling is known.
MOZ.summary:
Law in force. DLA Piper states, in a guide last modified on 17 February 2026, that Mozambique has no specific data protection legislation. The World Bank says the Data Protection Act had not been approved by Cabinet or submitted to Parliament as of October 2025, and on 1 October 2026 the Assembly's Standing Commission placed a draft law on the agenda of the session opening 28 October.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that Mozambique ratified the Malabo Convention on 2 December 2019 and deposited its instrument on 21 January 2020.

Authority appointed. A June 2025 inception report states that Mozambique has no data regulatory authority. A review of the draft law says it designates the existing Regulatory Authority for ICT as the National Authority for the Protection of Personal Data.

Implementing and acting. The World Bank's October 2025 paper says the Data Protection Office is not yet established, which prevents its operationalisation, and that the project envelope for it was cut from US$18m to US$11m.

Not found. A law in force, an appointed authority and any ruling are not held.

MRT.short: A 2017 law is in force and its authority met monthly and took decisions in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
MRT.summary:
Law in force. Law 2017-020 of 22 July 2017 on personal data protection is applied in the authority's deliberation 002/2026 of 24 March 2026. Deliberation 005/2025 of 30 July 2025 is issued under it and requires controllers using foreign cloud services to seek authorisation.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that Mauritania ratified the Malabo Convention on 19 April 2023 and deposited its instrument on 9 May 2023.

Authority appointed. The Autorité de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel (APD) held its ordinary monthly session on 30 June 2026 under its president, with its members and the Government Commissioner present. Its site lists monthly meetings of 25 March, 29 April and 6 May 2026, and its president was sworn in for a second term on 7 October 2026.

Implementing and acting. On 24 March 2026 the APD gave a favourable opinion, conditional on its remarks, on the joint decision authorising Maaden Mauritanie's Maadeni system. At its 29 April 2026 meeting it approved amendments to its transfer and cloud deliberations, and on 19 November 2025 it examined complaints 004-2025, 006-2025 and 007-2025.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

MUS.short: A law is in force and the authority is working; in 2024 it reported rejecting 12 cross-border transfers and closing 39 complaints.
MUS.summary:
Law in force. The Data Protection Office reports on its 2024 enforcement of the Data Protection Act 2017. It cites the Act's sections on complaints, transfers, registration, certification and appeals. Commissioner Madhub describes the 2017 regime as the current law. A first law of 2004 was partly implemented in 2009. The Office has also sent the ministry a draft bill to amend the Act for European Commission adequacy.

Malabo Convention. Mauritius ratified the Malabo Convention on 6 March 2018. It deposited its instrument on 14 March 2018, the African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records.

Authority appointed. Drudeisha Madhub is named as Data Protection Commissioner. The Data Protection Office has been operational since 16 February 2009. In January 2026 it co-led the launch of the National Data Strategy 2025-2029 with the ministry. Regulations of June 2026 give it roles: receiving notice of data protection officers within 14 days, and certifying them.

Implementing and acting. For 2024 the Office reports 179 new complaints and 39 closed. It also counts 105 breaches notified, 112 transfers authorised and 12 rejected, and four inspections. It issued guidelines for the insurance sector and 3,076 registration certificates in 2024. In September 2026 it told management companies to register as controllers and name their own officers. It said it may make site visits.

Not found. Nothing further on the four questions.

MWI.short: A law is in force and an authority is working; no ruling against an organisation is known as of 2026.
MWI.summary:
Law in force. The Data Protection Act, 2024 (Act No. 3 of 2024) was assented to on 31 January 2024 and published on 2 February 2024. The Authority's compliance guideline says it applies at once to non-Malawi controllers and to Malawi controllers of significant importance, and that other Malawi controllers and processors must comply from 3 June 2026.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Malawi.

Authority appointed. The guidelines state that the Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority, MACRA, is the designated Data Protection Authority under the Act. Nyasa Times reports it convened a stakeholder consultation on draft regulations in Lilongwe in July 2026, with Daniel Chiwoni as Head of Data Protection. The World Bank said in November 2025 that MACRA had appointed an acting Data Protection Commissioner.

Implementing and acting. In October 2025 the Authority published guidelines on personal data breach notifications, with a 72-hour notice to the Authority and to data subjects, and a compliance guideline and checklist covering the Act's duties, data subject rights and cross-border transfers. GIZ ran a training-of-trainers programme with the Authority in September 2026.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

NAM.short: Namibia has no law in force and no authority appointed, so none has ruled against an organisation; a bill is being finalised in 2026.
NAM.summary:
Law in force. Minister Theofelus said in July 2026 that Namibia is finalising the Data Protection Bill. In January 2026 she said the bill had been through consultation and drafting and was ready for resubmission to the Cabinet Committee on Legislation for onward processing by Parliament. An opposition MP told the Windhoek Observer in August 2026 that Namibia has no data protection statute.

Malabo Convention. Namibia ratified the Malabo Convention on 25 January 2019 and deposited its instrument on 1 February 2019, according to the African Union's status list of 2 February 2026.

Authority appointed. The ministry's revised draft Data Protection Bill of 2022 provides in its long title for establishing a Data Protection Supervisory Authority and its powers, duties and functions. Section 25 of the 2020 draft establishes the Data Protection Supervisory Authority of Namibia, with Part VII running to section 37.

Implementing and acting. Minister Theofelus said on 14 August 2025 that the ministry would table a Data Protection Bill in September 2025. In 2018 the Minister of ICT told Parliament that Namibia had embarked on developing Personal Data Protection and Cyber Security Bills.

Not found. No law in force, no appointed authority and no activity by one have been found.

NER.short: A law is in force, but its authority was abolished by decree in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
NER.summary:
Law in force. The president of the High Authority for the Protection of Personal Data, HAPDP, said in an interview published on 28 July 2025 that law no. 2022-59 of 16 December 2022 repealed and replaced the 2017 law as amended in 2019. The authority's consolidated text of April 2026 presents the law as the operative general law, amended by Law 2023-31 of 4 July 2023.

Malabo Convention. Niger ratified the Malabo Convention on 22 February 2022 and deposited its instrument on 16 March 2022, according to the African Union's status list of 2 February 2026.

Authority appointed. Africa Data Protection reports that the government has by decree abolished the HAPDP and split its powers between the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of the Interior, in a report published on 13 June 2026. In July 2025 the HAPDP president said the authority had ten members and that its president took office on 18 September 2024.

Implementing and acting. The HAPDP president said in July 2025 that the authority processed 139 compliance files since September 2024, covering declarations, video-surveillance declarations, and processing and transfer authorisations, and ran four control missions in 2025 on mobile operators.

Not found. No authority appointed after the decree has been found, and none registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting.

NGA.short: A data protection law is in force and the authority is working; it fined Multichoice Nigeria in 2025.
NGA.summary:
Law in force. The Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 was signed by President Tinubu on 12 June 2023. In July 2026 the Federal High Court treated the Act as operative in a case against the Commission, and a federal circular dated 27 July 2026 directed all federal ministries, departments and agencies to comply with it.

Malabo Convention. Nigeria signed the Malabo Convention on 23 January 2024 and had not ratified it at the African Union's status list of 2 February 2026.

Authority appointed. The Nigeria Data Protection Commission is a full data protection authority under the Act, according to its National Commissioner on 14 September 2026, when its new Abuja headquarters was commissioned. Voice of Nigeria names Vincent Olatunji as National Commissioner and CEO.

Implementing and acting. The Commission fined Multichoice Nigeria N766,242,500 in 2025 for violating the Act. Premium Times reports its Final Order against Meta imposed a $32.8 million fine, later set aside when the Federal High Court adopted a settlement. In August 2026 it opened an investigation into the University of Lagos, Lotus Bank and Hackerbella Ltd. In February 2026 it served a compliance notice on 649 higher-education institutions. In October 2026 its National Commissioner said 41,000 organisations had registered with the Commission in 2026 and 362 compliance organisations were licensed.

Not found. Nothing on the four questions is outstanding.

RWA.short: A data protection law has applied since 2023 and an authority registers controllers (2026); no source found reports a ruling against an organisation.
RWA.summary:
Law in force. Rwanda's Data Protection Act was introduced on 15 October 2021, and its two-year grace period ended on 15 October 2023, marking the transition to enforcement and accountability, according to a legal adviser writing in The New Times.

Malabo Convention. Rwanda ratified the Malabo Convention on 14 November 2019 and deposited its instrument on 21 November 2019, according to the African Union's status list of 2 February 2026.

Authority appointed. The National Cyber Security Authority acts as the supervisory authority for personal data protection and privacy under the Data Protection Act, as Rwanda observed Data Privacy Week in January 2026. In July 2026 CIPESA stated that Rwanda's AI policy positions the Authority to oversee data protection compliance relevant to AI systems. Template clauses published in February 2024 name it the supervisory authority under Law No 058/2021, receiving breach reports and settling disputes.

Implementing and acting. The New Times reported in January 2026 that over the last four years the Authority has registered data controllers and processors with registration certificates, trained over 100 public sector data protection officers, and run sector workshops for pharmacists and local government entities. In February 2024 its Data Protection and Privacy Office published template standard contractual clauses for transfers abroad under Article 49 of Law No 058/2021, which also set 72-hour breach reporting to the authority.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

SDN.short: Sudan has no data protection law in force in 2026; two authorities set up by decree in 2025 have issued no binding rules.
SDN.summary:
Law in force. On 6 August 2026 the Council of Ministers discussed a draft data and artificial intelligence bill and directed further study before approval by the interim parliament. On 11 August 2026 the Justice Ministry's under-secretary said the ministry is preparing a 2026 Law on Regulating Data and Artificial Intelligence with the digital transformation ministry. The Sudanese Center for Policy Studies says Sudan has no privacy law governing personal data and that a 2018 draft bill was never enacted.

Malabo Convention. Sudan signed the Malabo Convention on 15 March 2023 and had not ratified it at the African Union's status list of 2 February 2026.

Authority appointed. The Sudanese Center for Policy Studies says the Sudanese Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority and the Sudanese Cybersecurity Authority were both established by a November 2025 decree.

Implementing and acting. According to the same Center, citing the AI Regulation Tracker, neither of those two authorities had issued binding rules as of mid-2026.

Not found. Any ruling by an authority against an organisation, and the content of the draft bill.

SEN.short: A 2008 data protection law is in force and the authority is working; it ordered a company to remove a camera in March 2026.
SEN.summary:
Law in force. A reference summary states that Law No. 2008-12 on the protection of personal data was enacted on 25 January 2008 and has been in force since 2014. In April to June 2026 the Commission issued receipts, authorisations and a rejection under that law. An expert told APS in March 2026 that a bill to replace it is reportedly in the circuit.

Malabo Convention. Senegal ratified the Malabo Convention on 3 August 2016 and deposited its instrument on 16 August 2016, according to the African Union's status list of 2 February 2026.

Authority appointed. The Commission de protection des données personnelles (CDP) is an independent administrative authority set up by Law No. 2008-12. It held two plenary sessions in April to June 2026, and its president signed a partnership convention with Benin's authority in April 2026.

Implementing and acting. On 12 March 2026 the CDP, after a complaint, inspected Digicommunication International unannounced and ordered the meeting-room camera uninstalled. For April to June 2026 it reported 195 files handled, 39 authorisations issued and one processing rejected. In 2024 it served a formal notice on SOLID SA, operator of the Kay Voter platform.

Not found. Nothing on the four questions is outstanding.

SLE.short: In 2026 the data protection law is still a draft bill and no authority is appointed; no ruling against an organisation is known.
SLE.summary:
Law in force. Sierra Leone has a Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill, which the Information Minister said in November 2025 had finished its final national validation, with Cabinet and Parliament still to come. In April 2026 Cabinet approved a National Data Protection Policy and authorised a new Data Protection and Right to Access Information Act.

Malabo Convention. Sierra Leone signed the Malabo Convention on 29 January 2016, and the African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that it had not ratified it.

Authority appointed. The 2025 Bill would establish for the first time a single independent authority for both data protection and access to information, and that authority is not yet constituted because the Bill is unenacted.

Implementing and acting. Cabinet's April 2026 decision left the Ministry of Information and Civic Education and the Attorney-General's office to finalise the Bill and table it in Parliament.

Not found. Whether any authority is constituted or acting is not held, and neither is any ruling against an organisation.

SOM.short: Somalia's data protection law is in force and an authority is appointed and taking registrations since 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
SOM.summary:
Law in force. Somalia's Data Protection Act, Law No. 005 of 2023, was enacted on 23 March 2023 and became effective immediately, according to TechHive Advisory. In June 2026 the Authority's notice required registration under Article 32 of the Act from all entities that collect, store, process or share personal data in Somalia.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Somalia.

Authority appointed. Somalia inaugurated its Data Protection Authority on 24 February 2024. Its own service page of 2 June 2026 lists the registration forms it issues, and its January 2026 Registration Guidelines set fees and a 30-day approval timeline.

Implementing and acting. On 2 June 2026 the Authority began accepting registration applications from controllers and processors and said it will issue certificates only to those meeting the conditions. In February 2024 it published guidelines for implementing the law.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

SSD.short: In 2026 South Sudan's data protection law is still a draft bill; no authority is appointed and no ruling against an organisation is known.
SSD.summary:
Law in force. A two-day workshop of over 30 stakeholders, convened by Digital Rights Frontlines with the NCA, reviewed the Data Protection Bill, 2025 in a post dated 5 May 2026. The ICT Minister said in December 2025 the government will introduce its first Data Protection Bill in 2026. The World Bank's 2026 diagnostic states there is no national data protection or privacy law.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by South Sudan.

Authority appointed. Digital Rights Frontlines states in February 2026 that the country lacks a fully operational, independent Data Protection Authority. Radio Tamazuj reports the draft bill, once passed, will establish a Data Protection Commission.

Implementing and acting. In October 2025 Paradigm Initiative and Koneta Hub held a two-day Juba convening of lawmakers, civil society and officials to seek parliamentary commitment to table the draft Bill.

Not found. No enacted data protection law, no operating authority and no ruling against an organisation has been found.

STP.short: The 2016 data protection law is in force; the authority, appointed, signed a cooperation agreement in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
STP.summary:
Law in force. The IBA chapter of 2024 names the Personal Data Guarantee and Protection Law, Law 03/2016, as the primary instrument, covering processing by controllers headquartered or established in the country. Lei n.º 03/2016 was published in the Diário da República of 10 May 2016.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that São Tomé and Príncipe ratified or acceded on 25 September 2023 and deposited its instrument on 15 February 2024.

Authority appointed. The Agência Nacional de Protecção de Dados Pessoais has a president, José Manuel Costa Alegre. In April 2026 he met the National Assembly president to plan oversight of personal data in the electoral roll, and on 1 June 2026 the agency signed a cooperation memorandum with Macau.

Implementing and acting. The IBA chapter describes the fines and criminal sanctions the law provides and says the agency imposes fines and ancillary measures. In January 2025 its president described working with Facebook on fake profiles.

Not found. No source dated in the last three years shows the authority registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting. No ruling against an organisation has been found.

SWZ.short: A data protection law is in force and the authority is working; it has ruled against named organisations, most recently in 2025.
SWZ.summary:
Law in force. The Data Protection Act, 2022 was gazetted on 4 March 2022. The Ministry of ICT referred to its implementation and enforcement as current in August 2026, and enforcement notices under section 41 of the Act run to March 2025.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Eswatini. In July 2026 the Minister of ICT presented to a Senators' workshop on the importance of ratifying it.

Authority appointed. The notice of 2024 states the Act designates the Eswatini Communications Commission as the Eswatini Data Protection Authority. The Ministry of ICT vests oversight of compliance in it, and it has powers to investigate breaches, resolve complaints and impose sanctions. In September 2026 it was led by an acting chief executive.

Implementing and acting. The Authority issued enforcement notices under section 41 in June 2024 to MTN Eswatini and Liberty Life Swaziland Limited; the notice to MTN Eswatini was a warning with eleven directed measures and in March 2025 to the Royal Science Technology Park. Registration of controllers and processors became mandatory on 1 March 2024. Its transfer form bars unregistered organisations from transferring personal data. In June 2026 it opened a formal investigation into the Ministry of Home Affairs.

Not found. Nothing further is held on the four questions.

SYC.short: A data protection law is in force and the authority is working, handling 14 cases in 2025; no ruling against an organisation is known.
SYC.summary:
Law in force. The Data Protection Act, 2023 was assented to on 19 December 2023 and bears the operative date 22 December 2023. The Commission's page states the Act came into effect, and Appleby reports an 18-month transition for controllers and processors from that date.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Seychelles.

Authority appointed. The Information Commission is named in section 5 as the competent authority, with powers to investigate, audit, issue enforcement notices and impose administrative fines up to SCR200,000. In 2025 it had a Chief Information Commissioner, two Information Commissioners and a CEO in post, and it took on the mandate at the end of December 2023.

Implementing and acting. The Commission handled 14 cases under the Act in 2025: 6 on data transfers, 5 breaches, 2 refused deletion requests and 1 consultation. In 2024 it received four data protection cases, mostly from the non-banking financial sector. In 2026 it marked Data Protection Day with guidance to organisations and the public.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

TCD.short: Chad's 2015 personal data law is treated as in force and the security agency holds data protection duties; no ruling is known.
TCD.summary:
Law in force. Chad's personal data law of 2015 is treated as in force: a Chadian law firm's analysis published on 6 July 2026 applies Loi n°007/PR/2015 to personal data, including its articles 29 to 32 on transfers abroad. A replacement is being written: the minister announced on 9 December 2025 that authorities were finalising a digital law incorporating international standards on cybersecurity, data protection and internet governance, and Ecofin reported in March 2026 that the Digital Code was still under development.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Chad signed the Malabo Convention on 14 June 2015 and had not ratified it.

Authority appointed. Ecofin reported on 16 March 2026 that a reform law ratified by the Senate on 13 March 2026 broadens the mandate of ANSICE, the National Agency for Information Security and Electronic Certification, to personal data protection, cybersecurity, cybercrime and AI oversight.

Implementing and acting. The reform of March 2026 gave the security agency data protection duties, but no source found shows it registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting, and no ruling against a named organisation is known.

Not found. No source dated in the last three years shows an appointed authority registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting.

TGO.short: A data protection law is in force and the authority is working in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
TGO.summary:
Law in force. Loi n° 2019-014 of 29 October 2019 on personal data protection was adopted by the National Assembly and promulgated. In September 2026 the IPDCP briefed ministry cabinet directors and secretaries-general on their obligations as data controllers under it, and in June 2026 it said 35 data protection correspondents had been designated under the law.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Togo ratified or acceded to the Malabo Convention on 30 September 2021 and deposited its instrument on 19 October 2021.

Authority appointed. The IPDCP became operational in 2024 and, per its head, holds powers of control, injunction and sanction. It officially launched its activities in Lomé on 28 March 2025, and in 2026 it ran the June correspondent training and signed a cooperation agreement with Mali's APDP on 23 September.

Implementing and acting. The IPDCP ran a three-day training for 35 data protection correspondents from 22 to 24 June 2026 and opened its first evaluation and certification session for correspondents in Atakpamé on 30 September 2026, with 32 professionals. On 15 September 2026 it convened a compliance meeting for public administrations. It launched a public-awareness campaign in March 2025. On 19 October 2026 it placed a team in the media regulator's monitoring service.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

TUN.short: A 2004 law is in force; an authority appointed in 2021 is reported at a standstill in 2026, with no ruling against an organisation known.
TUN.summary:
Law in force. Organic law no. 2004-63 of 27 July 2004 sets the general processing, consent and rights regime, and a Forum Chawki Gaddes statement of 3 October 2026 cites it as the law guaranteeing personal data protection. A Tunisie Numérique article of 17 February 2026 also calls it the current law. A replacement bill, no. 095/2025, was deposited before the Assembly on 14 July 2025. It would repeal the 2004 law six months after publication.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records that Tunisia signed on 23 April 2019 and had not ratified.

Authority appointed. Government decree no. 2021-230 of 16 April 2021 appointed twelve named members to the national personal data protection authority for three years. Decree no. 2020-312 of 15 May 2020 puts the citizen-ID register under its control.

Implementing and acting. The Forum Chawki Gaddes says in a statement of 3 October 2026 that the activities of the authority, INPDP, are at a standstill and calls for its reactivation.

Not found. No source dated in the last three years shows the authority registering organisations, taking breach reports, issuing guidance or inspecting. No ruling against an organisation has been found.

TZA.short: A data protection law has been in force since 2023, the Commission is working, and it ruled against a company in 2025.
TZA.summary:
Law in force. The Personal Data Protection Act, Chapter 44, commenced on 1 May 2023 and applies to Mainland Tanzania and, for union matters, Zanzibar. The Citizen reported on 28 August 2026 that the Commission will inspect compliance with the Act from 31 August 2026.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Tanzania.

Authority appointed. Section 6 of the Act establishes the Personal Data Protection Commission as a body corporate. Director General Dr Emmanuel Mkilia announced on-site inspections in Dodoma on 28 August 2026. The Commission ran the eighth phase of its DPO training in Morogoro on 7-8 October 2026.

Implementing and acting. PDPC figures cited in October 2026 show 15,146 institutions registered and 445 complaints received by August 2026. A ruling reported in August 2025 awarded TZS 20,000,000 against Mi Casa Company Limited and ordered deletion of personal data. FB Attorneys reports a ruling of 19 August 2025 with TZS 20 million damages, a TZS 5 million fine and deletion of a newborn's photos within 14 days.

Not found. No sanction is named in the 2026 registration and inspection reports.

UGA.short: A data protection law is in force, the Personal Data Protection Office is working, and it ruled against Google in 2025.
UGA.summary:
Law in force. The Data Protection and Privacy Act, Cap 97, was applied by the Personal Data Protection Office in its decision of 18 July 2025 as law in operation, including its reach over foreign entities handling Ugandans' personal data. The PDPO director says the Act requires registration of data collectors and processors and makes failure to register a criminal offence.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature and no ratification of the Malabo Convention by Uganda. Police forensic-services director Andrew Mubiru said on 12 August 2026 that Uganda has not ratified it and needs to domesticate it.

Authority appointed. The Personal Data Protection Office is headed by director Baker Birikujja, who addressed an ISACA Kampala breakfast on 18 August 2026. It briefed government IT officers on data protection on 13 August 2026.

Implementing and acting. The PDPO's decision of 20 February 2026 partly upheld a complaint against WhatsApp LLC and Meta Platforms and issued corrective orders; on 17 July 2026 it confirmed WhatsApp had implemented them. On 18 July 2025 it found Google in breach and ordered it to register within 30 days. In July 2026 the Office supervised more than 13,400 registered data controllers and processors, and carried out inspections and investigations.

Not found. The director names no case taken to court.

ZAF.short: A data protection law has been in force since 2021; the Information Regulator is working and issued an enforcement notice to a college in 2026.
ZAF.summary:
Law in force. ITWeb reports that the Protection of Personal Information Act came into force on 1 July 2021 after a year-long grace period, with fines up to R10 million and up to 10 years' imprisonment.

Malabo Convention. The African Union status list of 2 February 2026 records South Africa as having signed on 16 February 2023, with no ratification or accession date.

Authority appointed. The Information Regulator was established on 1 December 2016 and its chairperson Pansy Tlakula spoke for it in September 2026. Parliament's Justice Committee published candidate names for vacant positions on 11 September 2026. National Treasury appropriated R135.7m for 2025/26 to the Regulator.

Implementing and acting. The Regulator received over 8,000 security-compromise reports to date, 1,220 of them since April 2026. It issued the South African Bureau of Standards an enforcement notice in August 2026 giving it 90 days to revise policies and implement security measures. Its first fine, R5 million, was imposed on the Department of Justice and Constitutional Development in July 2023.

Not found. The Regulator's work with the justice department to amend POPIA for artificial intelligence has no bill or draft described.

ZMB.short: A data protection law is in force and an authority is appointed and working; no ruling against an organisation is known in 2026.
ZMB.summary:
Law in force. The Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021 is the law a World Bank tender notice of 10 August 2026 treats as being implemented. A July 2026 report describes it as part of the operating legal framework beside the Cyber Security Act and Cyber Crimes Act.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records Zambia as having ratified the Malabo Convention on 15 December 2020 and deposited its instrument on 24 March 2021.

Authority appointed. The first Data Protection Commissioner was appointed in June 2023. In September 2025 the Commissioner and a Deputy Commissioner took part in a review of a draft health data statutory instrument.

Implementing and acting. The Commissioner's office opened online registration for controllers and processors, with a 30 April 2025 deadline. UNDP lists training staff in over 145 offices across 10 provinces on the Act as a requirement of the digital ID rollout.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

ZWE.short: A data protection law is in force and an authority is appointed and working; no ruling against an organisation is known in 2026.
ZWE.summary:
Law in force. The Cyber and Data Protection Act [Chapter 12:07] is applied through SI 155 of 2024, which took effect in September 2024 and made a Data Controller Licence mandatory. Business Times states the Act provides criminal sanctions for accountable officers.

Malabo Convention. The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records no signature of the Malabo Convention by Zimbabwe. It records no ratification either.

Authority appointed. POTRAZ states it is the designated Data Protection Authority under section 5 of the Act and is acting as such. Section 6(2) says it is not subject to the direction or control of any person in exercising its functions.

Implementing and acting. POTRAZ handed over the first Data Controller Licences to 570 companies in June 2025. In March 2026 it reported 1,123 licence applications so far that year and 1,218 data protection officers trained. In December 2025 it reported 831 organisations recognised as compliant. Its Regulatory Notice 2 of 2026 announces mandatory compliance inspections from 1 September 2026. A September 2026 account says POTRAZ held a national consultative workshop on guidelines under the Act and on amendments to SI 155 of 2024 on administrative fines.

Not found. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years has been found.

AGO.short: Angola's 2011 law requires notice or the regulator's authorisation to send data abroad; a firm was fined in 2026; no source found reports guidance.
AGO.summary:
Rule in force. Angola's Law 22/11 on personal data protection came into force on publication, 17 June 2011. Articles 33 and 34 make sending personal data abroad to a country with adequate protection subject to notification to the data protection agency (APD), and to a country without it subject to APD authorisation on stated grounds such as the data subject's written consent. Hunton reported in 2011 that the APD must approve transfers to countries without adequate protection. The APD's fee regulation, Presidential Decree 60/21 of 10 March 2021, lists an act of authorisation for international data transfer at Kz 350,450.

Means of complying published and rule applied. The APD fined Crescer Tech US$505,000 in 2026 for failing to notify it and obtain authorisation for the international transfer of personal data to a cloud located abroad. Valor Económico reported on 26 June 2026 a fine of about USD 505,000 (c. 549 million kwanzas) on the company for no notification or prior authorisation and an unauthorised international transfer to foreign cloud servers.

Not found. No published list of approved countries, model contract terms, application form or guidance on transfers is held. The dates of the deliberations behind the fines are not given.

BDI.short: Nothing found names a rule on sending personal data abroad or says there is none, so no stage is set.
BDI.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a rule on sending personal data abroad, or says there is none.

BEN.short: Nothing found names a rule on sending personal data abroad or says there is none, so no stage is set.
BEN.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a rule on sending personal data abroad, or says there is none.

BFA.short: The data authority took applications to send personal data abroad in 2026 and published its form; no grant or refusal is known.
BFA.summary:
Rule in force. Burkina Faso's CIL takes applications for authorisation to transfer personal data to a foreign country. Its annex form, dated September 2026, is the application for that authorisation, and it asks the applicant to give details of the recipient, the destination authority, the consent obtained and the security measures that protect the data. A transfer abroad is therefore made on the CIL's permission, which the applicant requests in writing.

Means of complying published and rule applied. The CIL published the blank application form for authorisation of a transfer of personal data abroad in September 2026, so an organisation wishing to send data out of Burkina Faso has a procedure and a document to complete. The form is the CIL's own.

Not found. No source from the last three years names a country approved to receive data, or an organisation given or refused permission, ordered to comply or penalised for sending data abroad. The law that sets the rule is not named in what is held.

BWA.short: Botswana's Data Protection Act, in force since January 2025, allows data abroad only to approved countries; no source found says how it has been applied.
BWA.summary:
Rule in force. The Data Protection Act has been in effect since January 2025. Mmegi reported on 25 November 2025 that it allows data transfers abroad only to approved countries. The Act was published in the Extraordinary Gazette of 29 October 2024 as the Data Protection Act, 2024.

Means of complying published and rule applied. Botswana keeps a list of countries that data may go to. A DIAL expert comment published on 15 June 2026 says the list held only two African countries. Under the rule Mmegi reported in November 2025, data may go to the countries on that list and to no others. A country that is not on the list cannot receive data sent from Botswana under the Act.

Not found. No source from the last three years names a country approved to receive data. None names an organisation given or refused permission, ordered to comply or penalised for sending data abroad.

CAF.short: A 2025 source says the law conditions transfers outside CEMAC and ECCAS on sufficient protection in the recipient state; no source reports means of complying.
CAF.summary:
