GNQ.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national identity law or bill, or says there is none.

KEN.short: Kenya's digital identity system rests on a 2018 executive order and 2020 regulations, added to a 1947 act; it has no law of its own.
KEN.summary:
Law in force. Kenya has no stand-alone digital identity law. Its digital identity system, the National Integrated Identity Management System, began under executive order no. 1 of 2018, in which the president directed a central master population database to be built. The government then wrote the system into the 1947 Registration of Persons Act by an omnibus amendment, and no Act of its own was passed for it. The High Court ruled in January 2020 that an appropriate and comprehensive regulatory framework should be enacted before the system was rolled out.

Digital identity covered and rules made. With no identity law of its own in force, none provides for a digital identity. The system is anchored on the Huduma Namba regulations of 2020, and civil society organisations objected that regulations cannot create a system of that weight. The inserted section 9A has the system keep a national population register and assign each person a unique number. Kenya therefore answers the first question only.

Not found. No source found says a national identity law is in force.

LBR.short: Liberia's 2011 National Identification Registry Act sets up a biometric identification system. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
LBR.summary:
Law in force. Liberia's National Identification Registry Act was approved by the President on 1 August 2011 and published on 8 August 2011. It repeals a 1983 decree that had established the earlier identification system and sets up the National Identification Registry as the body in charge. The Act took effect on publication.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The Act sets up a National Biometric Identification System and a biometric card for each person, enrolled with a fingerprint and a photograph. The Registry the Act creates is the body that runs that system. The Act is therefore a law for a biometric identity from its first day, and no later amendment to it is on record. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not found. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

LBY.short: Libya's 2014 national number law gives each citizen a unique number in a biometric database. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
LBY.summary:
Law in force. Libya's Law No. 8 of 2014 on the National Number was issued by the General National Congress on 24 March 2014 and took effect on issue. It sets up the national number and a national database, run with the Civil Registry Authority. It is an ordinary law and no amendment to it is on record.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The law provides for a twelve-digit national number unique to each citizen and a national database completed with ten fingerprints, an iris print, a photograph and a signature. The number and the biometric database are both in the law's own articles, the second and the third, and the database is the reference the number is checked against. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not found. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

LSO.short: Lesotho's 2011 identity cards law, in force since 2013, sets up a biometric register and unique number. No rules since 2023 are known.
LSO.summary:
Law in force. Lesotho's National Identity Cards Act, 2011 was published in the Government Gazette on 21 March 2011 and commenced on 1 July 2013. It repealed the National Identity Cards Act, 2004. It is an Act of Parliament and has been the law for the identity register and the card since its commencement.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The Act establishes a National Identity Register that records fingerprints and an image for everyone aged sixteen and over. It assigns each entry a unique national identity number and provides for an identity card with a chip that holds the fingerprints. The register, the number and the chip card are all set out in the Act itself. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not found. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

MAR.short: Morocco's 2020 law creates a population register against which identity is checked online. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
MAR.summary:
Law in force. Morocco's law no. 72-18, on the targeting of beneficiaries of social support programmes, was promulgated on 8 August 2020 and published in the Bulletin officiel on 7 January 2021. It creates the national population register and the national registers agency that runs it. It is a statute and no bill to replace it is on record.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The law's second article defines authentication as checking declared data online and in real time against the national population register. An identity entered in the register is therefore one that can be checked electronically, which is what the law provides the register for. The register and the agency are the law's two creations. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not found. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

MDG.short: Madagascar's parliament passed an identification law in July 2025 and the constitutional court cleared it. No source found says whether it has been promulgated.
MDG.summary:
Law in force. Madagascar's law no. 2025-019 on the identification of natural persons was adopted by the National Assembly on 3 July 2025 and the Senate on 4 July 2025. The President referred it for review before promulgation, and on 26 August 2025 the High Constitutional Court ruled that it conforms to the Constitution.

Digital identity covered and rules made. No source says the law has been promulgated, so it is counted as passed and not yet in force. The court's decision is the last step on record: a law adopted by both houses, referred on 28 July 2025 and cleared a month later. What the law provides for the identity itself is not stated in the decision. The law is numbered 2025-019 and carries the year of its adoption.

Not found. No source found says a national identity law is in force.

MLI.short: Mali's 2006 law gives each person a unique identification number; the last rule known under it is a decree of November 2022.
MLI.summary:
Law in force. Mali's law no. 06-040 of 11 August 2006 institutes the national identification number and a national identification register. It was adopted by the National Assembly on 13 July 2006 and promulgated by the President. A decree of 3 November 2022 instituting the biometric national identity card cites it as its basis.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The law gives each person a unique number held in a national register, to be shown on the identity card, the passport and civil status records. A decree of 18 October 2006 fixes the fourteen-digit number and obliges public services to use it. The 2022 decree requires the number for any biometric identity card application. Those rules all date from before September 2023, and none made under the law since then is on record.

Not found. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

MOZ.short: A civil identification and identity card bill passed first reading in March 2022; no source found says whether it became law.
MOZ.summary:
Law in force. On 16 March 2022 the Assembly of the Republic approved in first reading, by consensus, the Council of Ministers' bill setting the legal regime for civil identification and the national citizen identity card, the Bilhete de Identidade. The bill is meant to replace colonial-era legislation.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The nearest held fact is the same bill, which covers civil identification and the citizen identity card. The existing biometric card, the Bilhete de Identidade, dates from Decree 11/2008 of 29 April. In May 2026 a tender was launched for a consultancy on a mobile digital identity and signature system, and a partner was being sought for a mobile digital ID and e-signature rollout. The Interior Ministry's national directorate of civil identification runs an electronic civil identity system, described in a March 2023 document.

Not found. No source says a national identity law is in force.

MRT.short: Mauritania's civil status code, amended in February 2025, provides for a national biometric population register. No rules made under it since are known.
MRT.summary:
Law in force. Mauritania's identity system rests on its Civil Status Code, law no. 2011-003 of 12 January 2011, which covers the national population register and secure identity documents. Law no. 2025-011 of 24 February 2025 replaced three of its articles after adoption by the National Assembly and promulgation by the President.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The code as amended provides for the national biometric population register in its new article 31. Its new article 15 provides for applications for secure identity documents, and for digital civil status acts, through information systems the administration adopts. The 2025 amendment is thus the text that writes the biometric register and digital acts into the code. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not found. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

MUS.short: Mauritius's 1985 identity card law is in force; 2024 regulations under it set a new card with a digital seal and fingerprints.
MUS.summary:
Law in force. Mauritius's identity card rests on the National Identity Card Act, No. 60 of 1985, which the identity card unit lists as the law behind the card system. The Act is an Act of Parliament, and regulations made under its section 10 came into operation on 19 February 2024, when the new card began to be issued.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The National Identity Card Regulations 2024 were made by the minister on 16 February 2024. They set the new identity card, its digital seal and an application made with fingerprints, and they revoke the regulations of 2013. Through them the 1985 Act now provides for a card that is biometric and can be checked electronically. The new card has been issued since 19 February 2024.

Not found. Nothing on the four questions.

MWI.short: Malawi's 2010 National Registration Act founds its digital identity system; no rule applying it since 2023 is known beyond a fee change.
MWI.summary:
Law in force. Malawi's National Registration Act of 2010 mandates the registration bureau to run the national registration and identification system, according to the Principal Secretary. The Act is in force: on 23 July 2026 the Homeland Security Minister made amendment regulations under it, and the registration bureau runs the national identity card under the Act. In July 2026 a stakeholders' meeting was held to review the Act under the Digital Malawi Acceleration Project.

Digital identity covered and rules made. A 2025 presentation on the financial sector's use of the national identity says the National Registration Act No. 13 of 2010 was enacted as the legal foundation for the national digital identity system, with the registration bureau set up under it. The regulations of 23 July 2026 raised registration fees, and the July 2026 meeting reviewed the registration laws, with no bill on record since.

Not found. No regulation applying the Act, or rule that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held; the 2026 regulations change fees.

NAM.short: Namibia's 2024 Civil Registration and Identification Act provides a unique number and electronic identity documents. No rules made under it are known.
NAM.summary:
Law in force. Namibia's Civil Registration and Identification Act, No. 13 of 2024, is the statute for civil registration and legal identity. It sets up a civil register that includes an identity register under a Registrar-General. In July 2026 officials said the electronic identity card is legally recognised under the Act.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The Act assigns each person a unique identity number, authorises physical or electronic identity documents and governs how register data is authenticated and verified. In July 2026 an official of the Office of the Prime Minister said it allows institutions to accept either the physical card or its digital version, which the ministry said can be verified electronically. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not found. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

NER.short: Niger's cabinet adopted a draft ordinance in April 2026 adding a unique identifier and biometrics to its registers. No source found says whether it was signed.
NER.summary:
Law in force. Niger's Council of Ministers adopted a draft ordinance on the civil status regime on 22 April 2026. It amends law no. 2019-29 of 1 July 2019 to clarify the national civil status register and the national population register. It is a draft adopted by cabinet; no source says it has been signed.

Digital identity covered and rules made. No identity law is in force. The draft ordinance would add biometric parameters and a unique identifier to the registers the 2019 civil status law set up, which is what would make it the country's identity law. Until it is signed, the unique identifier and the biometric register are proposals, and the 2019 law stands as a civil status law. The 2019 law is numbered 2019-29.

Not found. No source found says a national identity law is in force.

NGA.short: Nigeria's NIMC Act 2026, signed in June, makes the identity number foundational and provides for electronic verification. No rules made under it are known.
NGA.summary:
Law in force. Nigeria's National Identity Management Commission Act 2026 was signed into law on 26 June 2026, repealing the 2007 Act. The bill had passed second reading in the Senate in July 2024. A civil society speaker said on 29 July 2026 that the gazetted text was not yet available.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The Act reaffirms the national identification number as the foundational identity and makes the Commission responsible for verifying electronic identities. It makes the Commission the national repository for biometric data and, by one account, makes the number compulsory across fourteen sectors. The Commission described its work in September 2026 as in compliance with the Act. The Act was three months old at the end of September 2026, and no regulation made under it is on record.

Not found. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

RWA.short: Rwanda's single digital identity law, reported in 2026, ends old identity cards by June 2027. No rules made under it are known.
RWA.summary:
Law in force. Rwanda has a law governing registration into its single digital identity system. In March 2026 The New Times reported that the law sets a June 2027 deadline after which existing national identity cards are no longer valid, and that under it citizens cannot hold two government-issued identities. The law's number and date are not given.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The system the law governs is built on a unique single digital identification number, a derived token and a card with a QR code, with authentication that relies on biometric data. Enrolment under it takes fingerprints, a facial image and an iris scan, carried out by the national identification agency. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not found. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

SDN.short: Sudan's 2011 Civil Registry Act gives each citizen a unique national number in an electronic register. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
SDN.summary:
Law in force. Sudan's Civil Registry Act 2011 was signed by the President, repealed the 2001 Act and came into force on signature. It sets up the civil registry, run by the Ministry of Interior, which issues the national number and the identity card. It is an act of the National Assembly, and no later amendment is on record.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The Act defines the national number as a unique number given to each citizen on registration, never to be repeated. It provides for civil registry records to be stored electronically on computer and for a central database. The number and the electronic register are both in the Act's own text, which gives only the year 2011. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not found. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

SEN.short: Senegal's 2016 law institutes a biometric identity card; a bill to extend card validity was before parliament in September 2026.
SEN.summary:
Law in force. Senegal's identity card rests on a 2016 law instituting the ECOWAS biometric identity card. On 29 April 2026 the Council of Ministers adopted a bill to amend it and extend how long cards are valid, and on 29 September 2026 that bill, numbered 21/2026, was before the National Assembly.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The 2016 law is a law for a biometric identity card, which is how the reports of the amending bill name it. The bill concerns the card's period of validity; an Interior Ministry official said on 24 September 2026 that the amending text would extend the 2016 cards. It had not been passed by the end of September. The law in force is the one of 2016, unamended at that date.

Not found. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone validated a draft civil registration and identification bill in November 2025; it had still to reach Cabinet and Parliament.
SLE.summary:
Law in force. Sierra Leone's National Civil Registration Authority held the final national validation of the draft National Civil Registration and Identification Bill and its regulations on 17 November 2025. The bill has still to go to Cabinet and then to Parliament. It is the draft that would replace the present registration law.

Digital identity covered and rules made. No source found says a national identity law is in force, so nothing is counted beyond the bill. The validation of November 2025 covered the draft regulations together with the bill, which means the rules are being written with the law and not after it. What the bill provides for the identity itself is not stated in the report. The validation was the last step before the bill leaves the Authority.

Not found. No source found says a national identity law is in force.

SOM.short: Somalia's 2023 identification law is in force; a 2024 regulation applies it and sets rules for banks and phone companies checking identity.
SOM.summary:
Law in force. Somalia's Public Identification and Registration Law, Law No. 009 of 20 March 2023, is in force. On 8 June 2024 the Prime Minister signed an implementing regulation made under it, following a Council of Ministers decision of 6 June 2024. The regulation took effect on signature.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The regulation defines the digital national identification system as the system the 2023 law established. It applies the law and sets rules for relying parties, among them banks and phone companies, which check identity against the system. The regulation of June 2024 is thus both the rule made under the law and the text that says the law's system is digital. The regulation is numbered 158 and was made a little over a year after the law.

Not found. Nothing on the four questions.

SSD.short: South Sudan's 2018 Civil Registry Act and 2024 regulations provide for a personal identification number; the World Bank calls them under-implemented.
SSD.summary:
Law in force. South Sudan's Civil Registry Act of 2018, with the Nationality Act of 2011, is the legal foundation of its identification system, a World Bank diagnostic of May 2026 says. The Bank says the Act and regulations made under it in 2024 have established the legal foundation for the country's identity system, and calls the framework under-implemented.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The Civil Registration and National Identity Regulations, 2024, were made under sections 33 and 39 of the Act and regulate the issue of legal documents. The Bank says the Act and the regulations lay the foundation for an interoperable digital identity system based on a personal identification number. Both are in force on paper, by the Bank's account.

Not found. Nothing on the four questions.

STP.short: São Tomé and Príncipe had a new identity law in draft in September 2025. No source found says whether it has been approved.
STP.summary:
Law in force. São Tomé and Príncipe has a new identity law in draft. A World Bank mission of 8 to 12 September 2025 flagged as urgent its review, public consultation, finalisation and approval. The mission's note calls it the aggregated identification document law and treats it as drafted and not yet approved.

Digital identity covered and rules made. No source found says a national identity law is in force. The mission warned that without the law's approval the collection of data could be constrained, which is the reason it gave for urgency. No later report says the law has been consulted on, finalised or approved, and what it provides for the identity itself is not stated. The mission's note is dated September 2025.

Not found. No source found says a national identity law is in force.

SWZ.short: Nothing found names a national identity law or bill for Eswatini, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
SWZ.summary: Not found. Nothing found names a national identity law or bill, or says there is none.

SYC.short: Seychelles' identity cards law, amended in 2023, is in force. No source found says whether it provides for a digital identity.
SYC.summary:
Law in force. Seychelles' National Identity Cards Act, Cap. 294, is a statute in force. The Miscellaneous Amendments Act 2023, assented to on 8 November 2023, amended it. The amending Act is Act 22 of 2023 and changes several laws at once, the identity cards law among them.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The 2023 amendment adds a card for non-resident citizens and new rules on disclosing card information. The first is a new section 4A of the identity cards Act. Those are the changes to the law on record, and neither is described as setting up a biometric register or an identity that is checked electronically. The Act is the country's identity law and has no replacement bill on record. The 2023 Act is the newest amendment to it.

Not found. No source found says the law in force provides for a biometric register, an identity number unique to each person, or an identity that can be checked electronically.

TCD.short: A 2020 ordinance, ratified by law, sets up a biometric population register and unique national number; no source found reports rules made since 2023.
TCD.summary:
Law in force. Chad's Ordinance 002/PR/2020 of 14 February 2020 on civil status, ratified by Law 006/PR/2020 of 29 May 2020, sets up the integrated population and secure titles system (SIGPTS), run by the national agency for secure titles, ANATS. The system issues a unique national identification number (NNI) through the national biometric population register.

Digital identity covered and rules made. Under article 8 of the ordinance the register holds the biographic and biometric data and the NNI of everyone on the territory, and article 2 obliges every resident or visitor to register. Article 10 makes the NNI unique, unintelligible and non-sequential. Because the register covers everyone on the territory, the number reaches citizens, foreign residents and visitors alike. These are the 2020 provisions as the UNHCR describes them in an April 2026 study of refugee inclusion in the system.

Not found. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

TGO.short: Togo's 2020 biometric identification law, amended in 2022, sets up a unique number; the last rule known under it is a September 2022 decree.
TGO.summary:
Law in force. Togo's law no. 2020-009 of 10 September 2020 on the biometric identification of natural persons created the national identification agency. Law no. 2022-010 of 24 June 2022, adopted by the National Assembly and promulgated by the President, amended several of its articles.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The amended law defines a unique identification number issued after verification of demographic and biometric data, and a central database against which the number and the data are authenticated electronically. A decree of 9 September 2022 sets the rules for registering and updating the data and the conditions for using the number. Those rules all date from before September 2023, and none made under the law since then is on record. The agency the law created issues the number.

Not found. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

TUN.short: Tunisia's organic law of March 2024 provides for a biometric identity card with an electronic certificate. No rules made under it are known.
TUN.summary:
Law in force. Tunisia's Organic Law No. 2024-22 of 11 March 2024 amends and completes the 1993 law on the national identity card; it was published in the official journal on 12 March 2024. Parliament had adopted it on 6 March 2024. A ministerial session on 22 April 2024 decided to start using the biometric card in the first half of 2025.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The organic law provides that the identity card carries an encrypted electronic chip holding the card number, a fingerprint and a photograph, and an electronic certificate that allows identity to be verified and documents signed electronically. It leaves the model of the card to a decree and the rules for the certificate to a joint ministerial order. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not found. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

TZA.short: Tanzania's 1986 registration and identification law is in force. No source found says whether it provides for a digital identity.
TZA.summary:
Law in force. Tanzania's Registration and Identification of Persons Act, first passed in 1986, is recorded as still in force in the 2023 revised edition of the laws. It provides for the registration of persons and the issue of identity cards. In January 2026 the government said it would table an Infant Registration Bill in the session starting 27 January 2026.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The 1986 Act is the law in force, and no source found says it provides for a biometric register or a unique number. The bill announced in January 2026 would let the identification authority register children from birth and give each a unique identification number. No report says it has been tabled or passed. The Act is numbered Cap. 36 in the revised laws.

Not found. No source found says the law in force provides for a biometric register, an identity number unique to each person, or an identity that can be checked electronically.

UGA.short: Uganda's 2015 Registration of Persons Act provides a unique number and biometric register; regulations were made under it in August 2024.
UGA.summary:
Law in force. Uganda's Registration of Persons Act, 2015 was assented to on 26 March 2015. It sets up the National Identification and Registration Authority, the national identification register and national identification cards. A Parliament release of 20 August 2026 describes the Authority as working under the Act.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The Act has the Authority assign a unique national identification number to every person registered and defines identity data to include fingerprints. Regulations made under it on 12 August 2024 set the card's validity at eleven years. In June 2026 the Authority said registered foreigners are given a unique identification number under the Act. The 2024 regulations amend the Registration of Persons Regulations, 2015, and are deemed in force from 20 November 2015.

Not found. Nothing on the four questions.

ZAF.short: South Africa's 1997 Identification Act is in force; a replacement bill is due in 2027 or 2028. No source found says whether it covers digital identity.
ZAF.summary:
Law in force. South Africa's Identification Act, 1997 is in force: the Minister of Home Affairs made the fourteenth amendment of the regulations under it on 23 June 2025, in operation from 1 July 2025, and the Department of Transport states that it makes Home Affairs the sole authority maintaining the National Population Register and issuing identification documents. Under section 15, anyone aged 16 or over must apply for an identity card, the Minister replied in November 2025. Its replacement, the National Identification and Registration Bill, is due in Parliament only in 2027 or 2028, a September 2026 report says. Home Affairs' first-quarter report to Parliament says it did not submit the bill for public comment, as it had to revise it in line with the Digital Identity Policy framework.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The 1997 Act is the law in force, and no source found says it provides for a digital identity. In May 2026 Home Affairs gazetted draft amended regulations under the Act for comment until 6 June 2026, which would regulate access to identity information. They were drafts at the end of September 2026. The Act of 1997 remains the law the population register and the identity document are kept under.

Not found. No source found says the law in force provides for a biometric register, an identity number unique to each person, or an identity that can be checked electronically.

ZMB.short: Zambia's National Registration Act is in force, with regulations of 2019. No source found says whether it provides for a digital identity.
ZMB.summary:
Law in force. Zambia's National Registration Act is in force. The National Registration Regulations, 2019 were made under its section 14; the Act provides for the national registration card, with a Chief Registrar and registrars. The regulations are Statutory Instrument No. 34 of 2019.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The 2019 regulations prescribe the registration procedure: an application, a photograph, the capture of ten rolled and ten plain fingerprints and a birth certificate, and the forms of the card with its number. They are the newest rules under the Act on record, and no source found says the Act provides for a register held digitally or an identity checked electronically. The Act is Cap. 126 of the laws of Zambia, and no amendment to it since 2019 is on record.

Not found. No source found says the law in force provides for a biometric register, an identity number unique to each person, or an identity that can be checked electronically.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe's 1976 National Registration Act is in force. No source found says whether it provides for a digital identity.
ZWE.summary:
Law in force. Zimbabwe's National Registration Act commenced on 24 September 1976. It sets up the Registrar-General of National Registration, a register of residents and identity documents, and its consolidated text is up to date to 31 December 2016. A statutory instrument gazetted on 30 January 2024 was made under its section 11.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The 2024 instrument amends the registration fees, which is not a rule on how identity is held or checked. The Act itself provides for the registration of residents and a register kept by the Registrar-General. No source found says the Act, or an amendment to it, provides for a biometric register or an identity checked electronically. The Act is Chapter 10:17 of the laws of Zimbabwe.

Not found. No source found says the law in force provides for a biometric register, an identity number unique to each person, or an identity that can be checked electronically.

AGO.short: A national digital-skills programme was under way in 2026; how many it trained is not on record.
AGO.summary:
Training for the public. In October 2026 President João Lourenço authorised US$20 million for specialised centres, hired by public tender, to raise the digital skills of the working population at three levels, especially young people and public servants. Presidential Despacho n.º 324/26 authorised US$5 million, World Bank-financed under PADA, for the National Programme for Training Local Agents in Basic Digital Skills, Inclusion and Digital Citizenship, implemented by IMA with FAS support. The PADA terms of reference say Subcomponent 3.2 supports the Government in developing and implementing a national strategy for basic, intermediate and advanced digital skills for young and underemployed people, starting with a needs assessment. A May 2024 memorandum plans a Digital Governance Academy that will also run digital literacy programmes for citizens.

Share measured. No source found since October 2023 gives a measured share of people with basic digital skills. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

Half or more. No source found since October 2023 gives a measured share of half or more of adults with basic digital skills. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

Not found. No source found since October 2023 says: is one in service and counted.

BDI.short: A national digital-skills programme was under way in 2025; how many it trained is not on record.
BDI.summary:
Training for the public. The ministry in charge of the digital economy, with UN Women Burundi and Belgian funding, launched phase III of the AGCCI coding camps on 25 September 2025, training 102 girls aged 17-25 from all provinces in digital literacy and coding, with telecentres supported at Bubanza, Kirundo and Ruyigi. The PAFEN project launched 12 September 2024 includes development of digital skills for the population among its priority components, per its coordinator. In September 2026 PAFEN's coordinator said a basic digital skills programme to train 10,000 young people within a year would start soon.

BEN.summary:
Training for the public. The Government of Benin, through the School of Digital Professions, launched a national call for applications for OIF D-CLIC digital skills training for young people, per TechAfrica News. It is the only fact held on the subject: no news story or official notice read for this study says more about it, the documents the earlier cell cited were not read, and the systems themselves were not examined.

BFA.summary:
Training for the public. Burkina Faso's digital skills work runs through PACTDIGITAL, a World Bank-financed project. Its appraisal document of 22 December 2023 gives US$22 million to a component on developing digital skills, and sets the project the aim of widening access to digital skills programmes. Agence Ecofin reports that the digital ministry's results for 2025, set out with its plans for 2026, included strengthening the digital skills of 169 young girls.

BWA.summary:
Training for the public. The EU, Expertise France and HAUS Finland project, ongoing 2024-2027 with Botswana's Digital and Innovation Hub, supports and expands digital innovation programmes to enhance digital skills, in particular for women and youth entrepreneurs. BOCRA's incident response team is running ICT training and cybersecurity awareness sessions for students and teachers at four named schools, following its Digital Centres handover. SmartBots (Government of Botswana) says the ongoing EU-funded programme, started August 2024, includes targeted programmes that enhance digital skills for women and youth entrepreneurs. A later answer places the country above that step.

Share measured. Statistics Botswana's 2024 Household Access and Individual Use of ICTs Survey found 59.2% of individuals reported having e-skills, basic skills more prevalent than advanced.

Cote d'Ivoire's digital minister and ITU discussed efforts to expand digital skills programmes for workforce development and digital inclusion. The Ministry of Digital Transition's draft 2025 budget lists digital skills for women, young people and vulnerable people among the activities of a digital support project funded at FCFA 1.5 billion. CIPESA says ANSUT's universal access efforts include digital literacy and skills programs.

Femintech, an institution launched in 2017 with partners including Unicef, teaches digital literacy, AI and programming, and about a thousand girls have received the training since its start (Femintech's outgoing president). COG.summary:
Training for the public. The EU part of the government's digital transformation project, launched on 17 June 2025, aims to develop the digital skills of the population, especially young people and women. UNESCO's project 3210652071 (USD 166,800, 66% progress, 2024-2025) on digital skills and media and information literacy for populations is on going, with an allocation to this country (Congo 10%). The Congo Digital Transformation Project, launched by the government in January 2023, provides for 3,000 people to acquire certified digital skills from basic to advanced (2023, before the three-year window).

CPV.short: A national digital-skills programme was under way in 2026; how many it trained is not on record.
CPV.summary:
Training for the public. Resolução 72/2026 recognises as progress digital-inclusion and skills-training initiatives developed for citizens and public servants.
