Last twelve months. The latest held row is the November 2021 workshop presenting the plan's studies.

Not found. Nothing after November 2021 is held on the plan, and no adoption or public text has been found. Its stated period, 2020-2025, has ended.

CIV.short: Côte d'Ivoire has a published digital strategy for 2021-2025, now past its period; no source found says its 2025 successor has been adopted.
CIV.summary:
Governance and finance. The published text has the Commission Nationale de Développement de la Société de l'Information steer the Stratégie nationale de développement du numérique 2021-2025, with a monitoring committee led by the digital ministry. Paradigm Initiative ties national allocations of about USD 91 million for 2024 and USD 101 million for 2025 to its cycle.

Standing. Fraternité Matin reports it adopted in January 2022. Its successor, the Stratégie nationale de transformation numérique 2025-2035, was validated at a workshop on 19-22 August 2025.

Text. The ministry published the strategy's own text, version 1.4 of 26 January 2022, on its site.

Period. The strategy covers 2021-2025, with 2025 targets for its 36 strategic indicators. The successor is named for 2025-2035.

Delivery plan. The action plan for seven pillars lists projects with start date, priority and budget in million FCFA, such as 95,000 million FCFA to connect public administrations to the national broadband network.

Reporting. We Are Tech Africa credited the strategy on 15 July 2025 with over 5,207 km of fibre, several online service portals and an operational National Cybersecurity Agency.

Last twelve months. A workshop on 3 September 2026 opened work toward 700 digital public services and a paper-free state by 2030.

Not found. No adopting act is on record for the strategy or for its successor. No source found says whether the successor's text is public.

CMR.short: Cameroon's 2016 digital plan has lapsed, and a new digital economy strategy was being finalised in October 2026; no source found reports progress reports.
CMR.summary:
Governance and finance. The Plan stratégique Cameroun numérique 2020 gives delivery to the postal and telecommunications ministry. It works with the other ministries, ANTIC, ART and CAMTEL. The plan draws its money from the public investment budget, the telecommunications special fund and the State budget. External financing comes on top.

Standing. The plan, dated May 2016, calls itself the adopted strategic plan and names no adopting act. A workshop on 3 July 2025 discussed the diagnostic for updating it, with the next step to follow government approval.

Text. The plan's full text, 72 pages, is published on the ministry's site.

Period. The plan began in 2016 and, on both its own text and the ITU repository, ended by 2025.

Delivery plan. The priority action plan lists projects for each axis, with indicators and 2020 targets. Each carries an amount in FCFA. A broadband backbone extension, for one, is costed at 125,000,000,000.

Reporting. The plan assigns monitoring and evaluation to the PPBS committees of each administration and their monitoring-evaluation cells.

Last twelve months. In October 2026 the minister said a draft national strategy for the digital economy was being finalised. It builds on the national AI consultations. Its pillars are infrastructure, data governance, skills, research and responsible AI. The ITU repository still listed Digital Cameroon 2020 in its 2025 edition.

Not found. The new strategy has no adopted text or period yet. No report against the 2016 plan has been found.

COD.short: DR Congo adopted a national digital plan in 2019, now past its period; no source found says its 2026 successor has been adopted.
COD.summary:
Governance and finance. Paradigm Initiative lists the Presidency, the posts and telecommunications ministry and the regulator ARPTC as lead institutions of the Plan National du Numérique Horizon 2025, and reports public digital budget allocations of USD 103.7 million in 2025. The plan leaves its own budget to the Government and the ADN.

Standing. The national validation workshop of 3-5 September 2019 validated the plan, and no cabinet act is named; the ADN coordinator said in November 2023 that it was adopted in 2019, with 69 projects. Its successor, the Politique sectorielle de l'économie numérique 2026-2030, was validated on 4 August 2026 and is due before the Council of Ministers.

Text. The full text, dated September 2019, is on the Presidency's site.

Period. The plan carries the strategy to the horizon 2025, with target years from 2020 to 2025.

Delivery plan. Its timetable gives 68 priority projects with indicators, baselines and targets dated 2020 to 2025.

Reporting. Agence Ecofin reported on 11 October 2025 that the ministry estimates the plan is about 60% complete.

Last twelve months. The Government's action programme for 2024-2028 sets putting the plan's remaining projects into action, and the successor was technically validated on 21-22 July 2026.

Not found. No adopting act is on record for the plan or for its successors, including the 2026-2030 plan reported as launched in October 2026. The successor has no action plan, steering body or monitoring yet, and the plan's progress is a ministry estimate.

COG.short: Congo adopted Vision Congo Digital 2025 by decree in 2019; no source found reports its successor awaits approval, and its action plan and monitoring.
COG.summary:
Governance and finance. The Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy is mandated to implement Vision Congo Digital 2025, coordinated by an inter-ministerial committee, according to the World Bank appraisal of 11 May 2022. The Digital Strategy 2030 document was completed with World Bank financial support in October 2025.

Standing. Décret n° 2019-150 of 17 June 2019 approves the strategy. A successor, Stratégie numérique 2030, was reported complete on 13 October 2025 and awaits review and final approval by decree.

Text. The decree was published in the Journal officiel of 4 July 2019.

Period. The ITU repository gives the time frame as 2021 to 2025, while the successor is named Vision Congo digital 2030.

Delivery plan. A December 2020 World Bank diagnostic says the action plan was still being drawn up with consultants.

Reporting. The May 2022 appraisal lists monitoring and evaluation mechanisms among the requirements for implementing the strategy.

Last twelve months. A digital identity workshop in July 2025 was described as a milestone in implementing Congo Digital 2025.

Not found. No public text of Vision Congo Digital 2025, no monitoring and no domestic budget line for it are shown. Its successor is validated at ministry level but not adopted by decree, with World Bank finance only.

COM.short: Comoros adopted a public, costed digital strategy to 2028 in 2018; no source found reports results against its targets.
COM.summary:
Governance and finance. ANADEN, the national digital development agency created in 2019, has the implementation of Comores Numérique 2028 as its first mission, and the strategy itself designs a national digital council and an observatory.

Standing. The digital health strategy says the Government drew up Comores Numérique 2028 and adopted it in 2018.

Text. The text is public on ANADEN's site.

Period. Its roadmap runs from 2018 to 2028.

Delivery plan. The strategy costs its six axes at 52,995,160,485 KMF, planned costings of 2018, and a 2025 report gives a target of 5% of GDP for the digital sector by 2028.

Reporting. The strategy designs a national digital observatory to measure sector performance.

Last twelve months. On 25 August 2026 the minister said ANADEN is to contribute to implementing the strategy across the economy.

Not found. No published report on results against the strategy's targets, no domestic budget line for it and no adopting act are shown.

CPV.short: Cabo Verde approved a digital economy strategy to 2030 in 2024; no source found reports its public text, plan and reporting.
CPV.summary:
Governance and finance. On 25 November 2025 the Estratégia para a Economia Digital de Cabo Verde was presented to the Conselho Consultivo da Economia Digital, chaired by the Vice-Prime Minister.

Standing. Resolução 72/2026 lists it as approved in September 2024. The Agenda Digital de Cabo Verde 2035 is in preparation, as that resolution only establishes its bases.

Text. The same resolution lists the strategy with a focus on competitiveness, innovation and the digital economy.

Period. It covers 2025 to 2030.

Delivery plan. NOSi's March 2020 action plan names three hubs for the strategy: connectivity, capacity-building and service provision.

Reporting. The same NOSi plan says implementation is under way with African Development Bank and World Bank support.

Last twelve months. The strategy was presented to the digital economy council on 25 November 2025, and the 2035 agenda's consultation followed on 6 August 2026.

Not found. No public text of the strategy and no plan, reporting, body or finance for it are shown. The Agenda Digital de Cabo Verde 2035 is in preparation and not adopted, and the 2019 to 2021 Agenda has ended.

DJI.short: Djibouti's cabinet heard a digital economy roadmap in March 2023; no source found says whether it was adopted.
DJI.summary:
Governance and finance. The minister delegate for the digital economy presented the roadmap to the Council of Ministers in March 2023.

Standing. The government spokesperson's record of that session notes a communication on the "Djibouti Smart Nation: Feuille de Route pour l'Economie Numérique" and records no adoption. The Council of Ministers of 7 October 2025 listed drawing up a national digital strategy among the main challenges left.

Text. The nearest held statement is the March 2023 record's account of the roadmap.

Period. The nearest held statement is the communication of March 2023 on the roadmap.

Delivery plan. The roadmap is built on four pillars, smart administration, digital economy, smart trades and smart civil society, with structuring projects identified.

Reporting. The Council of Ministers record of 7 October 2025 follows the ministry's digital-maturity diagnostic of the administration.

Last twelve months. On 7 October 2025 the Council of Ministers listed a national digital strategy and sectoral roadmaps as still to be drawn up.

Not found. No adoption of the Smart Nation roadmap is on record, and no text, period, delivery plan or report has been found for it. In October 2025 the Council of Ministers still listed a national digital strategy as to be drawn up.

DZA.short: Algeria adopted its national digital transformation strategy for 2025 to 2030 in May 2025, but no source found reports costs and results against its targets.
DZA.summary:
Governance and finance. The High Commission for Digitalisation, created by presidential decree 23-314 of 6 September 2023, designs the strategy and follows its implementation, and on 4 May 2026 it signed a project with UNDP, supported by the Government of Japan to support its implementation.

Standing. El Chaab says the National Digital Transformation Strategy 2025-2030 was adopted, approved and published in May 2025, and on 12 May 2025 the High Commissioner called it the approved strategy. Digital Policy Alert says the government updated the strategy in 2025, with over 500 digital projects planned for 2025-2026.

Text. The text is published on the High Commission's site, in an August 2024 version with twenty-five strategic objectives.

Period. The ITU repository gives its time frame as 2025 to 2030.

Delivery plan. The minister said on 4 May 2026 that the implementation plan for 2025-2026 is under way, with an executive plan for 2027-2030 in preparation.

Reporting. The High Commission published a review of April 2024 to September 2026 listing its projects, and said on 2 September 2026 that the second national data centre at Blida implements its first axis.

Last twelve months. The National Digital Services Centre was inaugurated on 5 July 2026, and the Council of Ministers of 12 July 2026 gave administrations one month to connect to the National Data Center. On 20 October 2026 the solidarity ministry launched an investment-tracking platform under the strategy's action plan.

Not found. No adopting act is named; approval is stated by the press and the High Commissioner only. No cost for the plan, no domestic budget line and no results against the strategy's own targets have been found.

EGY.short: Egypt's Digital Egypt strategy, running from 2016, is listed as adopted in 2025, but no source found reports its text, plan and recent progress.
EGY.summary:
Governance and finance. The ITU repository names the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology as lead of the Digital Egypt Strategy.

Standing. The ITU repository's 2025 listing records the Digital Egypt Strategy as adopted, and on 13 March 2024 the Prime Minister named approval of a National strategy for building a fully digital state among the Supreme Council for Digital Society's objectives.

Text. The ITU repository's 2025 listing names the Digital Egypt Strategy as the country's strategy.

Period. The same repository gives its time frame as 2016 onward.

Delivery plan. At Cairo ICT'24 on 17 November 2024 the ICT minister briefed the Prime Minister on its four pillars: digital services, jobs in the digital economy, digital creativity and infrastructure.

Reporting. At the same briefing of 17 November 2024 the minister gave implementation figures, including 8 million registered on the Digital Egypt platform and 23 of a targeted 32 creativity centres built.

Last twelve months. The latest held figures are those of the 17 November 2024 briefing, when 8 million were registered on the Digital Egypt platform.

Not found. Adoption rests on a general listing with no adopting act, body or date, and no public text has been found. No delivery plan, domestic budget line or reporting after November 2024 has been found, and no approval of the fully digital state strategy is recorded.

ERI.short: Eritrea has no national digital transformation strategy, according to a June 2026 legal-status page; no source found says whether any is in preparation.
ERI.summary:
Governance and finance. Levellers, in a legal-status page reviewed on 8 June 2026, states that Eritrea has no national digital transformation strategy.

Standing. The same Levellers page states that Eritrea has no national digital transformation strategy, alongside no published national AI strategy.

Text. The nearest held row is Levellers' statement of 8 June 2026 that no national digital transformation strategy exists.

Period. The nearest held row is Levellers' statement of 8 June 2026 that no national digital transformation strategy exists.

Delivery plan. The nearest held row is Levellers' statement of 8 June 2026 that no national digital transformation strategy exists.

Reporting. The nearest held row is Levellers' statement of 8 June 2026 that no national digital transformation strategy exists.

Last twelve months. Levellers, reviewing on 8 June 2026, states that Eritrea has no national digital transformation strategy.

Not found. The only statement of absence is a third-party legal-status page, not an Eritrean government source. No instrument in preparation is on record.

ETH.short: Ethiopia's Council of Ministers approved Digital Ethiopia 2030, running to 2030, in November 2025, but no source found says whether its text is public.
ETH.summary:
Governance and finance. The National Digital Transformation Council, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Temesgen Tiruneh, met on 30 July 2026 and was said to provide strategic leadership for the Digital Ethiopia Strategy. Public ICT and digital allocations rose from about USD 250 million in 2020 to USD 500 million in 2024, which Paradigm Initiative attributes to the predecessor, Digital Ethiopia 2025.

Standing. The Council of Ministers approved Digital Ethiopia 2030 on 29 November 2025 and the Prime Minister launched it on 20 December 2025, as the successor to Digital Ethiopia 2025. On 9 September 2026 the Minister of Innovation and Technology reaffirmed the Ministry's work towards the objectives of the strategy.

Text. The Ethiopian News Agency describes Digital Ethiopia 2030 as a comprehensive national blueprint building on the Homegrown Economic Reform Agenda.

Period. Digital Ethiopia 2025 covered 2020 to 2025, and the Prime Minister said on 20 December 2025 that it had been completed. The Ministry of Innovation and Technology describes Digital Ethiopia 2030 as a five-year journey to 2030.

Delivery plan. CIO Africa, on 27 January 2026, lists the targets for 2030: 100 percent 5G coverage in 100 cities, 128 million mobile subscribers, a Fayda digital ID for every adult and digital payments up sevenfold.

Reporting. On 30 July 2026 the Council reviewed progress on the Digital Ethiopia Strategy, Fayda and the 5 Million Coders initiative.

Last twelve months. Digital Ethiopia 2030 was launched on 20 December 2025, succeeding Digital Ethiopia 2025.

Not found. No public text has been found for Digital Ethiopia 2030. No domestic finance line is tied to the 2030 strategy, and reporting is activity only, with no published results.

GAB.short: Gabon's minister presented a national digitalisation strategy in April 2026 after the 2020-2025 plan ended; no source found says whether it has been adopted.
GAB.summary:
Governance and finance. The digital economy minister announced a permanent consultation framework with state IT directors on 3 April 2026. The earlier plan, Gabon Digital 2025, had ANINF as its lead and was financed by the African Development Bank, as reported in November 2020.

Standing. On 3 April 2026 the minister presented the main orientations of the national digitalisation strategy to state IT directors, with no adoption stated.

Text. The report of that meeting gives the strategy's orientations and no text.

Period. The International Telecommunication Union's repository gives the time frame of the earlier Gabon Digital strategy as 2020 to 2025.

Delivery plan. The strategy is built on five axes, regulatory framework, infrastructure, public services, local skills and data governance, and its sector master plans are still to be drawn up.

Reporting. The nearest held statement is the minister's presentation of 3 April 2026.

Last twelve months. The minister presented the five-axis strategy on 3 April 2026 and announced progressive sector master plans.

Not found. No adoption, text or period has been found for the national digitalisation strategy presented in April 2026. No governing body, finance or report has been found for it.

GHA.short: Ghana's Digital Economy Policy and Strategy was adopted in 2024 with a 2028 target; no source found says whether any progress report exists.
GHA.summary:
Governance and finance. The 2024 text of the Ghana Digital Economy Policy and Strategy names government budgetary support, development partner support and public-private partnerships as its funding sources, with no allocation or budget line.

Standing. The Ministry of Communications and Digitalisation adopted the Digital Economy Policy in October 2024, and the World Bank records the strategy and policy as approved in April 2024. A successor, the National Digital Transformation and Emerging Technology Strategy, was begun by the ministry in April 2025 and is in preparation.

Text. The policy and strategy text is public, published in 2024.

Period. The text sets a target timeline of 2028 for its objectives and a review every four years.

Delivery plan. The implementation framework lists strategic actions with assigned responsibilities, phased as quick wins within 6 months, medium term at 6 to 18 months and long term at 18 to 48 months, with no cost stated.

Reporting. The policy text assigns responsibilities for each strategic action and sets a review every four years.

Last twelve months. The latest dated event held for the policy is its adoption by the ministry in October 2024.

Not found. No progress report against the policy's own actions and no mandated body have been found. The successor strategy is only begun, and no budget line is given for the policy.

GIN.short: Guinea's 2023-2027 digital strategy is public and costed, with a lead ministry named, but no source found says whether any progress report exists.
GIN.summary:
Governance and finance. The Stratégie nationale de digitalisation de l'État et de développement de l'économie numérique 2023-2027 names the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy as lead ministry, and its financing table puts the State at USD 209,711 thousand, 12 percent of USD 1,747,590 thousand, with development partners at 60 percent.

Standing. The strategy, titled Guinée Digitale 2027 in its own text, is the Transition Government's strategy in version 1.2 of 11 June 2024, validated in national workshops with UNDP and the African Development Bank.

Text. The full text is published as a PDF on the site of the state digitalisation agency, issued by the ministry.

Period. The strategy is titled 2023-2027 and sets 14 result indicators against 2022 references for a 2027 horizon. It follows the 2016-2020 ICT and digital economy strategy, which has ended.

Delivery plan. The roadmap sets 245 initiatives under 41 orientations and six axes, each with a responsible body, a cost in thousand US dollars and a duration.

Reporting. The lead ministry is responsible for drafting, coordinating, implementing and evaluating the strategy, with a national steering committee to be set up.

Last twelve months. The latest dated row is a round table on 4 and 5 December 2024, where the minister said the strategy had been in implementation since 2022.

Not found. No implementation or results report has been found, and no adopting act is named for the strategy. The period reads 2027 in the title and 2026 in one article.

GMB.short: The Gambia's Digital Economy Master Plan 2024-2034 is published and reported adopted in 2024; no source found reports its delivery plan and any progress report.
GMB.summary:
Governance and finance. The National Digital Economy Master Plan 2024-2034 is issued by the Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy.

Standing. The Digital Cooperation Organization reports that the government adopted the master plan, with data current to September 2024. A separate National Digital ID and Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2028 was validated at a workshop on 16 and 17 May 2024.

Text. The plan's PDF is published on the ministry's website, with 2024 as its published year.

Period. The ministry's own document gives the plan's period as 2024 to 2034.

Delivery plan. The ministry's published plan document sets out the plan for 2024 to 2034.

Reporting. The Digital Cooperation Organization lists the master plan, 2024 to 2034, among the guidelines it consulted.

Last twelve months. An article of 7 October 2026 gives the master plan as running 2024-2034.

Not found. The master plan has no governance, delivery plan or reporting row of its own. Its adoption rests on one third-party report naming the government and September 2024, and some sources date the plan 2023-2033.

GNB.short: Guinea-Bissau adopted a 2025-2030 digital transformation strategy by decree in March 2025, with a public text, but no source found reports any report on results.
GNB.summary:
Governance and finance. UNDP's record of the Mais Digit@l programme shows a US$3,360,500 grant for 2025-2030 to implement the strategy, and its 2024 annual report says the strategy was launched with financing from the Government of Japan.

Standing. Decreto 10/2025, published in the Boletim Oficial on 28 March 2025 after Council of Ministers approval on 13 March, approves the ENTD.GW 2025-2030, which the government had launched on 29 January 2025.

Text. The full text is public as the annex to the gazetted decree.

Period. The stated period is 2025-2030.

Delivery plan. The strategy sets 55 interventions under six strategic objectives, each with a stated start, end and duration in months, and no cost is given for them.

Reporting. UNDP's 2024 annual report says the strategy has six pillars and 55 priority interventions with clear implementation milestones.

Last twelve months. UNU-EGOV reported on 23 September 2026 that a Project Document for implementing the strategy, to set priorities, define governance structures and identify partners and resources, was discussed with a ministry delegation on 9 September 2026.

Not found. No published report against the strategy's targets has been found, and no cost is given for its actions. No mandated body is stated.

GNQ.short: Equatorial Guinea's national digital economy strategy was in drafting with World Bank support in September 2026; no source reports its adoption or a published text.
GNQ.summary:
Governance and finance. The Ministry of Transport, Telecommunications and Civil Aviation, led by Minister of State Honorato Evita Oma, opened a World Bank-supported working week on 2 September 2026 to finish the strategy.

Standing. The Estrategia Nacional de Economía Digital was in drafting on 2 September 2026, when a four-day working week opened in Malabo with eight World Bank Group specialists to complete and validate it. The earlier ADIGE digital agenda was launched by the ministry in 2019 for 2019 to 2025.

Text. The government press office of 2 September 2026 describes the strategy as still to be completed and validated.

Period. On 2 September 2026 the ministry expected a consensus roadmap at the close of the working week.

Delivery plan. The World Bank-supported working week of 2 September 2026 aims to complete the strategy.

Reporting. The government press office reported the opening of the working week on 2 September 2026.

Last twelve months. The working week to finish the strategy opened on 2 September 2026, with the ministry expecting a consensus roadmap at its close.

Not found. No adopting act, period, plan or reporting has been found for the strategy, and no text is published. No body or finance is stated.

KEN.short: Kenya published a costed national digital master plan for 2022-2032, but no source found reports any published report against its targets.
KEN.summary:
Governance and finance. The plan names the ICT Authority as the main coordinating and implementing agency, under an inter-ministerial committee and an oversight committee chaired by the Cabinet Secretary (2022).

Standing. The Kenya National Digital Master Plan 2022-2032 is issued by the Ministry of ICT, Innovation and Youth Affairs with a Cabinet Secretary foreword, and was unveiled and launched by ICT Cabinet Secretary Joe Mucheru on 12 April 2022.

Text. The full plan is published as a PDF on the ICT Authority site.

Period. The plan states its period as 2022-2032 and is the successor to the 2014-2017 master plan. Its predecessor as national strategy is the Digital Economy Blueprint of 2019.

Delivery plan. Table 6.1 gives a resource requirement per theme for each year 2022-2032 in Ksh millions, and Annex 1 a budget per key project, for example Ksh 118.0B for 52,000 km of government fibre in 2022-2030.

Reporting. The ICT ministry's 2026 Budget Policy Statement, presented to the National Assembly committee on 17 February 2026, was aligned with the plan.

Last twelve months. An ICT Authority tender of 15 September 2026 cites the plan's national target of 100,000 km of fibre network.

Not found. No published report against the plan's targets has been found, and no domestic budget line is stated. No dated event in the last twelve months changes the plan's standing.

LBR.short: Liberia has a National Digital Strategy 2025-2029, adopted per a March 2026 policy, with a costed plan, but no source reports results against its targets.
LBR.summary:
Governance and finance. The Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications developed the strategy and is responsible for implementing it, according to the National Data Governance Policy of March 2026, and the strategy's costs are to be met from government, multilateral donor and other sources.

Standing. The National Data Governance Policy of March 2026 lists the National Digital Strategy (2025-2029) among the instruments Liberia has adopted, after a validation workshop on 11 December 2024.

Text. The strategy's full text is published on the ministry's website.

Period. The strategy covers 2025 to 2029.

Delivery plan. In the text published on 3 February 2026, Chapter 6 estimates US$151.813 million over 2025-2029 from government, multilateral donor and other sources, and a separate US$776.250 million for about 1,500 cell towers through public-private partnership. Chapter 7 sets an implementation roadmap with timelines.

Reporting. The Digital Transformation Working Group, activated in October 2025, is to coordinate Liberia's digital activities.

Last twelve months. The strategy was officially launched at the National Coordination Session of Digital Liberia Week, held during 28-30 October 2025.

Not found. No progress report against the strategy's targets has been found. No adopting act or date is named for the strategy, and no budget line for it is named.

LBY.short: Libya's Prime Minister approved a government digital transformation strategy in April 2025, to 2030, but no source found reports its approved text.
LBY.summary:
Governance and finance. Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dabaiba of the Government of National Unity approved the National Strategy for Government Digital Transformation, prepared by the Supreme Committee for Digital Transformation.

Standing. The Prime Minister approved the strategy on 21 April 2025, following the General Information Authority's December 2022 proposal.

Text. The General Information Authority publishes the December 2022 proposal for the strategy, marked as a proposal on its cover.

Period. The vision is that by the end of 2030 everyone in Libya will enjoy world-class government services, with 2030 targets set against 2022 baselines.

Delivery plan. The proposal sets 2030 targets against 2022 baselines, such as a rise in Libya's e-government development index rank from 162 to 100, and lists eleven action areas with initiatives. It says a national plan of projects and the budgets are still to be set.

Reporting. At the April 2025 launch the General Information Authority chairman said some of the strategy's plans had already been implemented in a number of ministries and bodies. On 19 November 2025 the Authority announced pilot phases of the second level of the national digital identity system as part of implementing the strategy.

Last twelve months. On 19 April 2026 the General Information Authority described Level 3 biometric digital identity trials as part of implementing the National Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030, the name it also uses for the strategy.

Not found. The text of the strategy as approved in April 2025 is not held, only the December 2022 proposal. No budget, mandated body or results report has been found for it.

LSO.short: Lesotho's digital transformation strategy to 2030 was approved in February 2025 and is published, but no source found reports its action plan and results.
LSO.summary:
Governance and finance. The strategy's text makes the Chief Digital Office in the ICT ministry, under the Chief Digital Officer, accountable for developing the strategy and its implementation plans and for its monitoring and evaluation, with ministries reporting progress to it.

Standing. The finance minister told Parliament on 19 February 2025 that the Digital Transformation Strategy had been approved, without naming an approving act or body.

Text. The strategy's text is published on the government's website.

Period. The strategy is catalogued as Lesotho's national digital transformation strategy to 2030, self-dated 2024, and the 2027/28 Budget Strategy Paper of October 2026 commits government to fast-track the 2024-2030 strategy.

Delivery plan. The text sets initiatives by priority, the highest to start within about 12 months of operationalisation and medium ones within three to five years, and states no cost. The National Digital Policy lists development of a detailed action plan for the strategy as a task for 2024-2025.

Reporting. A government news item of 29 September 2026 says Lesotho is advancing the strategy, with priorities including connectivity, digital skills, innovation and technology for public services.

Last twelve months. On 29 July 2025 the minister said the memorandum of understanding with India was signed in the wake of the strategy's launch.

Not found. No adopting act or date is named for the strategy, and no finance or results report has been found for it. Its initiatives carry start windows and no calendar dates or costs, and no detailed action plan has been found.

MAR.short: Morocco has Maroc Digital 2030, listed as adopted in 2025, with MAD 11 billion for 2024 to 2026, but no source reports a public text.
MAR.summary:
Governance and finance. The ITU repository names the Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform as lead of Maroc Digital 2030, and Morocco World News says MAD 11 billion was allocated for 2024-2026.

Standing. The ITU repository lists Digital Morocco 2030 among the strategies it says countries have adopted, and the Government Council heard a presentation of its general orientations on 25 January 2024. It follows Maroc Numeric 2013 and Maroc Digital 2020.

Text. We Are Tech Africa says Maroc Digital 2030 was launched in September 2024.

Period. The ITU repository gives its time frame as 2024-2030.

Delivery plan. Morocco World News pairs the MAD 11 billion for 2024-2026 with targets of 3,000 start-ups, 100,000 people trained a year and 240,000 jobs by 2030.

Reporting. In its declaration to the African Telecommunications Union conference in Abuja, Morocco highlighted progress under Maroc Digital 2030, without figures.

Last twelve months. On 17 July 2026 the ministry signed a memorandum with Capgemini Maroc on AI skills, and on 4 June 2026 one with Orange Morocco, both presented as implementing it.

Not found. No public text of Maroc Digital 2030 has been found, and its adopting act and date are not stated. Results against it are not given beyond a general account of progress.

MDG.short: Madagascar has the Plan Stratégique Numérique 2023-2028, presented in 2024 with a USD 800 million estimate, but no source reports its adoption and public text.
MDG.summary:
Governance and finance. UNDP says the Plan Stratégique Numérique 2023-2028 is coordinated by the digital ministry, supported by the Unité de Gouvernance Digitale attached to the Presidency, and the ministry estimates its budget at USD 800.169 million, of which USD 152.334 million is available.

Standing. Newsmada reports the digital minister presented the plan on 19 January 2024, and UNDP calls it formalised and in implementation in December 2025. A national digital roadmap is in preparation after the Digital Readiness Assessment report was handed over on 17 December 2025.

Text. 2424.mg reports the ministry delivered a national Plan stratégique du numérique 2023-2028 on 26 October 2023.

Period. UNDP names the plan as the national digital strategy for 2023-2028, and GSMA said on 16 October 2026 that its priorities support the plan.

Delivery plan. The ministry costs implementation at USD 800.169 million, with USD 647.835 million still to find, across four axes: legal framework, telecommunications, human capital, and digital and financial inclusion.

Reporting. UNDP says the plan is in implementation, in a consolidation phase.

Last twelve months. The digital ministry and UNDP handed over the final Digital Readiness Assessment report on 17 December 2025, as the basis for a national roadmap. Tia Tanindrazana wrote on 8 September 2026 that the plan aims to raise the digital sector to 6% of GDP by 2028.

Not found. No source states that the Plan Stratégique Numérique 2023-2028 was adopted or approved, and no public text has been found. No reporting against it has been found.

MLI.short: Mali has a digital economy policy validated in 2024 with an action plan to 2029, but no source found reports its adoption.
MLI.summary:
Governance and finance. Le Matin reports that the Ministry of Communication, Digital Economy and Administrative Modernisation, with the Direction nationale de l'économie numérique, held the workshop that validated the policy.

Standing. The Politique nationale de développement de l'économie numérique (PNDEN) was validated at a workshop on 24 October 2024. It follows Mali Numérique 2020.

Text. The ministry reports that the launch ceremony of the study to prepare the policy document was held on 29 December 2023.

Period. Malijet describes the policy as covering 2021-2034, and its action plan covers 2025-2029.

Delivery plan. The validated policy comes with an action plan for 2025-2029.

Reporting. The minister is quoted giving an execution rate of 27.30% for the previous version, 2015-2020.

Last twelve months. On 2 October 2025 Malijet reported the African Girls Can Code Initiative phase III as anchored in the policy.

Not found. The policy's adoption is not stated, and no public text has been found. Its periods differ between sources.

MOZ.short: In 2019 Mozambique approved a national information society plan running to 2028, but no source found reports its delivery plan and published results.
MOZ.summary:
Governance and finance. Decreto n.º 4/2026, approved on 10 March 2026, creates the Agência de Transformação Digital e Inovação, whose Technical Council is to ensure execution and permanent monitoring of the plan's projects. Paradigm Initiative says execution depends heavily on donor cycles, with World Bank projects financing broadband and governance work.

Standing. The Council of Ministers approved the Plano Estratégico para a Sociedade de Informação 2019-2028 and its Plano Operacional by Resolução n.º 52/2019, on 26 February 2019. A National Digital Transformation Strategy entered drafting when the process was launched on 12 February 2026.

Text. The text is printed in the Boletim da República I Série n.º 199 of 16 October 2019, hosted on the INTIC site.

Period. The plan sets its priorities for the horizon 2019-2028.

Delivery plan. The resolution approved the plan together with its Plano Operacional.

Reporting. INTIC's 2022 activity report has a section on evaluating the degree of implementation of the plan.

Last twelve months. Decreto n.º 4/2026 of 10 March 2026 tasks the new agency with mobilising resources for the Information Society Policy and its Strategic and Operational Plans.

Not found. No delivery plan is stated for this plan in the evidence, and no published report against its targets has been found. The National Digital Transformation Strategy is still in drafting and would replace it.

MRT.short: Mauritania approved a costed national digital agenda for 2022 to 2025 that has now ended; no source found reports results against its targets.
MRT.summary:
Governance and finance. The agenda states that the State has set up a Haut Conseil du Numérique to follow its execution. In August 2025 the ministry of digital transformation, created in 2021, was described as the institutional lever for the digital transformation, working from the agenda, then under evaluation and update. The digital ministry says the World Bank-supported WARDIP is to attract private investment and co-financing for the agenda's activities.

Standing. The government drew up and approved the Agenda national de transformation numérique 2022-2025 in 2022. On 4 December 2025 the digital ministry announced the start of preparation of an Agenda National de la Transformation Numérique 2030.

Text. The ministry hosts the agenda's text on its official site, dated June 2022.

Period. The agenda is a four-year strategy for 2022-2025 with a calendar of projects. Agence Ecofin refers to it in the past tense on 30 June 2026.

Delivery plan. The agenda is broken into 25 initiatives and 77 projects for a global investment of 400 million dollars, with cost, funding mode and owner given for each project.

Reporting. At a workshop on 4 December 2025 evaluating the agenda, the ministry's secretary general said it brought considerable advances in digital infrastructure, electronic platforms and access to public services.

Last twelve months. On 4 December 2025 the digital ministry opened preparation of the 2030 agenda, with the World Bank taking part by video link.

Not found. No domestic budget line has been found for the agenda, and no report against its own targets has been found, only accounts of activity. The Agenda National de la Transformation Numérique 2030 has no adopted text.

MUS.short: Mauritius launched a national digital transformation blueprint for 2025 to 2029 in 2025; no source found reports its cost or results against targets.
MUS.summary:
Governance and finance. The Blueprint says a National Digital Transformation Bureau is to execute ICT projects and a Steering Committee will oversee implementation. At its first meeting on 26 August 2025 the Inter-Ministerial Committee was reported as mandated to monitor, coordinate and guide the projects, with monthly reports to Cabinet.

Standing. L'Express reports that the ministry officially launched the Digital Transformation Blueprint 2025-2029 on 26 May 2025, at a launch presided over by the President of the Republic.

Text. The full text is published on the MITCI site.

Period. The Blueprint is titled 2025-2029. It follows the Digital Mauritius 2030 Strategic Plan, published in 2018 with a horizon of 2030.

Delivery plan. The Blueprint lists actions per pillar and enabler and contains a phased roadmap with milestones and indicators.

Reporting. On 26 August 2025 the minister said an online motor vehicle licence renewal project under the Blueprint was already deployed, among around 84 projects.

Last twelve months. A government notice of 1 September 2026 names the Digital Transformation Blueprint (2025-2029) as the instrument the Digital Service Framework will help implement.

Not found. The Blueprint states no cost, and no report against its own targets has been found, only accounts of activity. No adopting act is named for it.

MWI.short: Malawi has a National Digitalization Policy for 2023 to 2028, approved by Cabinet, but no source found says whether its text is public.
MWI.summary:
Governance and finance. The NRB Strategic Plan 2025-2030 describes the National Digitalization Policy (2023) as setting the national direction for digital transformation across all sectors.

Standing. The National Digitalization Policy 2023-2028 was approved by Cabinet, per a MACRA presentation of October 2023, and the Open Government Partnership action plan of June 2025 lists its adoption and operationalisation. Its successor, a draft National Digital Transformation Strategy, went to a validation workshop on 18 and 19 February 2026.

Text. The National Local Government Finance Committee describes the 2023 policy as addressing country-wide ICT challenges and priorities.

Period. GSMA gives the policy as running 2023 to 2028.

Delivery plan. The Times said in January 2026 that principal secretaries' appraisals should be tied to the Malawi Digitalisation Policy 2023-28, measured by services online.

Reporting. The Open Government Partnership action plan of June 2025 lists the policy's adoption and operationalisation among the digital governance achievements of 2023 to 2025.

Last twelve months. In May 2026 the Local Government Finance Committee was reported saying Malawi has one ICT policy for the nation, the National Digitalization Policy.

Not found. No source says the text of the National Digitalization Policy is public or describes its scope. No delivery plan or reporting on it has been found, and a National Digital Transformation Strategy is still being validated.

NAM.short: Namibia launched its National Digital Strategy 2025-2029 in August 2025 with a public text; no source found reports any delivery plan or progress report.
NAM.summary:
Governance and finance. The Paradigm Initiative report lists the Ministry of Information and Communication Technology as lead institution for the National Digital Strategy.

Standing. The Namibian reports that the ICT minister officially launched the National Digital Strategy 2025-2029 on 5 August 2025.

Text. The International Science Council paper of February 2026 cites the strategy's text on the ministry's website.

Period. Ecofin Agency gives the strategy as covering 2025 to 2029.

Delivery plan. In the 2025/26 budget speech of 7 May 2025 the minister said the strategy will be implemented in partnership with stakeholders.

Reporting. ITWeb reported in June 2026 that a national datacentre is a core pillar of the strategy, with no dates set for it.

Last twelve months. The national public key infrastructure DigiNam was launched on 31 August 2026 and described as aligned with the strategy.

Not found. No source names the body or act that adopted the strategy, and no cost or financing has been found. No progress report on it has been found.

NER.short: Niger's digital development policy for 2026 to 2035 was validated in March 2026 and awaits an approving decree; no source found reports its text.
NER.summary:
Governance and finance. The drafting committee handed the Politique nationale de développement du numérique 2026-2035 to the Minister of Communication on 13 October 2025.

Standing. A national validation workshop opened on 11 March 2026, and in June 2026 the minister listed the decree approving the policy among coming prospects. It follows the Politique nationale du numérique 2021-2030, which the ministry said in May 2026 a survey would help update.

Text. ANP reports the text was submitted to the workshop participants for validation on 11 March 2026.

Period. The minister gives the policy as running 2026 to 2035, and the earlier policy covered 2021 to 2030.

Delivery plan. The policy comes with a Plan d'Action Sectoriel 2026-2030 whose planned actions the workshop was to enrich.

Reporting. The minister said in March 2025 that the action plan was already drawn up and would be rolled out once the policy is adopted.

Last twelve months. The validation workshop opened on 11 March 2026, five months after the document was handed over.

Not found. No adoption of the policy is on record and its text is not held. No cost, reporting, governing body or financing has been found.

NGA.short: Nigeria has a ten-year digital economy strategy unveiled in 2019, but no source found reports results against its targets and its funding.
NGA.summary:
Governance and finance. The Federal Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy was assigned its development and implementation, and the March 2020 broadband plan says a National Digital Economy Council was established to oversee it, but the text ties no budget line to it.

Standing. President Buhari unveiled the National Digital Economy Policy and Strategy on 28 November 2019, and a 2025 ITU repository lists it as the country's strategy.

Text. The full text is held on the NITDA site.

Period. The strategy is titled and dated for 2020 to 2030.

Delivery plan. It sets eight pillars with listed government actions and dated targets, among them 70% broadband penetration in four years and 95% digital literacy in ten, with no cost stated.

Reporting. At the 20 December 2022 commissioning of the National Shared Services Centre, implementation was said to have produced "giant strides", with no figure against a target.

Last twelve months. NITDA's National Cloud Investment Strategy of August 2026 says the strategy continues to provide the overarching national policy framework.

Not found. No source found reports results against the strategy's targets: reporting is statements of progress only. The plan states no cost, and no funding source is known.

RWA.short: Rwanda's Smart Rwanda plan, issued in 2015, ended in 2020, and a successor was in preparation in 2023, but no source reports its current status.
RWA.summary:
Governance and finance. The Ministry of ICT and Innovation, supported by the Rwanda Digital Acceleration project under the World Bank, is working on its successor, Smart Rwanda Master Plan II.

Standing. The Government of Rwanda issued the Smart Rwanda Master Plan in October 2015, which INCLUDE in September 2022 says was adopted in 2015, and the October 2023 sector review lists Smart Rwanda Master Plan II among policies under development.

Text. The nearest held row is the October 2015 issue of the plan by the Government of Rwanda.

Period. The sector review names the Smart Rwanda Master Plan I as covering 2016 to 2020, and a Digital Transformation Strategy for Rwanda (ICT Master Plan 2021-2025) is listed with that period.

Delivery plan. INCLUDE gives the plan's aims as broadband for all and digital literacy for all by 2020.

Reporting. The nearest held row is the World Bank's March 2023 brief, which calls the 2020 Smart Rwanda Masterplan dated.

Last twelve months. The latest held row is the 26 October 2023 sector review listing Smart Rwanda Master Plan II, a five-year ICT strategy, among policies under development.

Not found. No source found says whether the plan's text is public, and any delivery plan or reporting against it,. No source found says whether Smart Rwanda Master Plan II succeeds the 2021-2025 ICT Master Plan, and its status since October 2023,.

SDN.short: Sudan's digital transformation ministry announced a strategy in 2025, but no source found says whether it was adopted or its text published.
SDN.summary:
Governance and finance. The Central Bank of Sudan's request for proposals of 7 April 2026 refers to the digital transformation strategy announced by the digital transformation ministry in 2025.

Standing. The same request for proposals says the strategy was announced by the digital transformation ministry since 2025.

Text. The nearest held statement is the central bank's April 2026 reference to the strategy the ministry announced in 2025.

Period. The nearest held statement is the April 2026 request for proposals, which refers to the strategy announced in 2025.

Delivery plan. The nearest held statement is the central bank's reference of April 2026 to the strategy the ministry announced in 2025.

Reporting. The nearest held statement is the request for proposals of 7 April 2026, which mentions the strategy announced in 2025.

Last twelve months. The nearest held statement is the April 2026 request for proposals, which refers to the ministry's 2025 announcement of the strategy.

Not found. No source found says whether the strategy was adopted by any act, and whether its text is public,. No period, plan, reporting or governance fact has been found.

SEN.short: Senegal launched its New Deal Technologique for 2025 to 2034 and published the text, but no source says whether results are measured against its targets.
SEN.summary:
Governance and finance. The government created the digital governance committee GouvNum among the first decisions under the New Deal Technologique, and the digital ministry's 2026 budget rose 38.7 percent to CFA 81.06 billion.

Standing. President Bassirou Diomaye Faye launched the New Deal Technologique on 24 February 2025, replacing the Stratégie Sénégal Numérique 2025.

Text. The New Deal Technologique text, titled Horizon 2034, is published on the Presidency site.

Period. The strategy runs to 2034, after a predecessor whose period was 2016 to 2025.

Delivery plan. The Digital Master Plan sets 12 priority programmes and 50 priority projects costed at FCFA 1,105 billion, of which 950 billion is identified.

Reporting. At the first anniversary in March 2026, authorities said significant progress had been made after one year of implementation.

Last twelve months. On 24 March 2026 Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko launched the New Deal's structuring projects, including e-Consulat and the sovereign cloud. On 16 October 2026 the Prime Minister installed the digital governance committee GouvNum to coordinate the state's digital initiatives under the New Deal, with the digital ministry as its secretariat.

Not found. No source names an act adopting the strategy or creating the governance committee. Reporting covers first-year activity and is measured against no targets.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone approved its National Digital Development Policy in 2021 and publishes the text, but no source found says who approved it.
SLE.summary:
Governance and finance. The policy proposes a National Digital Development Council under the President and a National Digital Development Agency, and lists an objective to allocate a proportion of the national budget to e-government systems.

Standing. The National Digital Development Policy 2021 was approved in 2021, and a draft National Digital Transformation Roadmap is in preparation.

Text. The policy text is hosted on the Ministry of Communication, Technology and Innovation site.

Period. The policy states no end date, a vision of middle-income status by 2039, and says it shall be reviewed every five years.

Delivery plan. The policy contains no action plan and no costs, and instructs the Ministry to develop the implementation plan.

Reporting. The policy reports no progress against itself and instructs the Ministry to develop a monitoring, evaluation and learning framework.

Last twelve months. The Ministry of Health's 2024-2026 roadmap says the Universal Access Development Fund was established through the policy.

Not found. No act or body is named for the 2021 approval, and the policy text only recommends approval. Nothing dated in the last twelve months is held on the policy.

SOM.short: Somalia launched a Digital Transformation Strategy for 2025 to 2030 after a consultation in October 2025, but no source found says whether it was adopted.
SOM.summary:
Governance and finance. The Ministry of Communications and Technology, with the ITU, hosted the October 2025 national consultation to validate the Digital Transformation Strategy.

Standing. The government launched the Digital Strategy 2025-2030, after a two-day consultation on 12-13 October 2025 to validate it.

Text. The ITU's 2025 review says the Digital Transformation Strategy for Somalia was developed in 2025.

Period. The strategy runs 2025-2030, as the Communications Minister named it in July 2025.

Delivery plan. The October 2025 consultation was to review and refine the proposed roadmap.

Reporting. The Hiiraan report on the launch of the Digital Strategy 2025-2030 quotes the Communications Minister.

Last twelve months. On 12 October 2025 the National Communications Authority reported the consultation kicked off to validate the strategy.

Not found. No source reports adoption of the strategy, and no act or body is named for the launch. The Council of Ministers approved a separate Inclusive Digital Policy in January 2025, with no period or text given. No text, governance, delivery plan or reporting has been found for the strategy.

SSD.short: South Sudan was still developing its digital road map and master plan in June 2024; no source found says whether it has been adopted.
SSD.summary:
Governance and finance. A consulting firm was developing the Digital Development Road Map and Master Plan for the Government, according to the World Bank aide-memoire of 3-7 June 2024.

Standing. The same aide-memoire records the Road Map and Master Plan as in development in June 2024, after consultations on draft recommendations.

Text. The June 2024 aide-memoire describes the Road Map and Master Plan as being developed, with private-sector and public-sector consultations held on drafts.

Period. The aide-memoire dated 7 June 2024 places the Road Map and Master Plan as support to the Government in preparing its future digital development strategy.

Delivery plan. The June 2024 aide-memoire records the firm's draft recommendations as the stage the work had reached.

Reporting. The World Bank mission record of June 2024 states that the firm "has been developing" the Road Map and Master Plan.

Last twelve months. The last dated row, the aide-memoire of June 2024, says the Road Map and Master Plan was still being developed.

Not found. No adopting act, body, text, period, plan or reporting has been found for the Road Map and Master Plan, and the last dated record is from June 2024. A South Sudan Digital Transformation Strategy and a Digital Government Strategy are named without further description.

STP.short: The government of São Tomé and Príncipe had launched a national digital transformation strategy by March 2026; no source reports its adoption, text and period.
STP.summary:
Governance and finance. The World Bank program document of 11 March 2026 attributes the national digital transformation strategy to the government.

Standing. The same document says the government "has launched" it, and it follows the 2020 Estratégia Nacional para a Governação Digital, approved by the Council of Ministers.

Text. The March 2026 World Bank document describes the strategy as expanding broadband connectivity, modernising the legal and regulatory framework and investing in digital public infrastructure.

Period. The World Bank document of 11 March 2026 is dated the day the launch is recorded, while the predecessor strategy covered 2020/2024.

Delivery plan. The March 2026 document names digital IDs and data exchange platforms as the digital public infrastructure to be invested in.

Reporting. The World Bank program document of 11 March 2026 is the one record of the strategy, stating that it has been launched.

Last twelve months. The government had launched the strategy by 11 March 2026, according to the World Bank.

Not found. The strategy's title, adopting act, date, body, text, period, plan and reporting are not held, and a launch alone does not show adoption. The 2020 digital governance strategy is a separate, earlier instrument.

SWZ.short: Eswatini has a 2024-2028 digital strategy named in sources, but no source found reports its standing, text and plan, so no stage is set.
SWZ.summary: Not found. No instrument could be staged for Eswatini. An Eswatini Digitalisation Strategy (2024-2028, 'Government in Your Hand') and a Digital Transformation Roadmap in procurement are named, with nothing that sets their standing, text, period, plan or reporting.

SYC.short: Seychelles validated a 2026-2031 digital and AI strategy in July 2026; no source found reports its adoption and text.
SYC.summary:
Governance and finance. The World Bank says the Inter-Ministerial Digital and AI Coordination Committee and the Department of Information and Communications Technology are mandated to lead the digital transformation agenda. No budget line is stated.

Standing. A consultant on the drafting team says the National Digital & AI Strategy 2026-2031 passed its national validation workshop by July 2026; no adoption is recorded.

Text. The same consultant's account describes its scope: infrastructure, government services, AI, skills, innovation and the digital economy.

Period. The strategy is titled 2026-2031.

Delivery plan. The World Bank says the strategy is still to be operationalised.

Reporting. The nearest held fact is the World Bank's statement that the strategy is still to be operationalised.

Last twelve months. The national validation workshop concluded by July 2026.

Not found. No adoption, public text, delivery plan, reporting or finance has been found for the 2026-2031 strategy.

TCD.short: Chad has a 2020 to 2030 digital transformation strategy, but no source found reports its adoption and public text, so no stage is set.
TCD.summary: Not found. No source found says whether the Stratégie nationale de transformation numérique 2020-2030 was approved, adopted or launched, nor is whether its text is public. The World Bank in 2023 both cites it and says Chad has no comprehensive national digital strategy, and no reporting has been found.

TGO.short: Togo's president said in 2022 the Togo Digital 2025 strategy was adopted, but no source reports its text and its 2025 to 2030 successor's progress.
TGO.summary:
Governance and finance. In an April 2021 presentation the Ministry of Digital Economy and Digital Transformation is shown leading 6 projects and 1 reform of the Togo Digital 2025 portfolio. A World Bank paper of 29 April 2021 says the World Bank's WARCIP project financed its preparation, at US$1.36 million against a US$0.6 million budget.

Standing. In his independence address of 27 April 2022 the President said Togo had adopted the Stratégie Togo Digital 2025. A successor, Togo Digital 2025-2030, was in preparation from 22 May 2025, when the ministry began recruiting a consultant.

Text. The Minister of the Digital Economy referred to the 2020-2025 roadmap at the opening of the Lomé data centre on 8 June 2021.

Period. Togo Officiel said on 27 May 2025 that the current strategy ends at the end of 2025, and that the new one is to cover 2025 to 2030.

Delivery plan. The April 2021 presentation says the strategic roadmap for Togo Digital 2025 had been launched, with three parts and nine programmes.

Reporting. A WeAreTech.Africa article of 28 May 2025 says the 2020 framework had enabled advances, naming the e-Gouv platform, digital service centres and cybersecurity and data protection laws.

Last twelve months. The government portal reported on 4 May 2026 that under the Stratégie nationale Togo Digital 2025, 181 classrooms were connected, reaching 8,500 pupils.

Not found. No public text of Togo Digital 2025 and no delivery plan have been found, and reporting is activity counts only. The successor, Togo Digital 2025-2030, is held only at consultant recruitment in May 2025.

TUN.short: Tunisia's National Digital Strategy 2021-2025 ended in 2025 and no named successor has been found, so no stage is set.
TUN.summary: Not found. The National Digital Strategy 2021-2025 ended in 2025, and no named successor has been found, only a broader national vision for 2026-2030. No text, delivery plan or governance rows have been found for the strategy.

TZA.short: Tanzania's Digital Economy Strategic Framework 2024-2034 was launched in 2024 and is public; no source found reports its cost and any report on its targets.
TZA.summary:
Governance and finance. The government, through the Tanzania Business Council, created a Digital Transformation Committee of public and private members to drive the Digital Economy Strategic Framework 2024-2034.

Standing. The President, Dr Samia Suluhu Hassan, launched the framework on 29 July 2024, and the ministry's catalogue page gives the same date.

Text. The Ministry publishes the framework on ictc.go.tz, with a statement from the President.

Period. It runs for ten years, 2024 to 2034, and a ministerial statement of 13 May 2026 cites it as in force.

Delivery plan. The Citizen lists its dated targets: ICT at 3% of GDP, 80% broadband and internet penetration and 90% digital literacy, all by 2029.

Reporting. The Ministry presented 758 towers built by December 2025 as supporting the strategy.

Last twelve months. At the 9th Tanzania Annual ICT Conference on 19 January 2026, Minister Angellah Kairuki said delivery must meet the framework's targets on time.

Not found. No finance line tied to the framework has been found, and no published report against its targets. Its plan states dated targets without a cost.

UGA.short: Uganda published its Vision for a Digital Uganda 2040 in 2022 with a costed plan; no source found reports any report on progress.
UGA.summary:
Governance and finance. The Vision for a Digital Uganda 2040 names a Digital Transformation Program Working Group of heads of ministries, departments and agencies to coordinate delivery, with the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance leading, and lists budget appropriations, concessional loans and grants as financing measures.

Standing. The Ministry published the Vision in September 2022 with a foreword by President Museveni; a newer Digital Transformation Roadmap was launched by the Government on 17 August 2023.

Text. The Vision is published on the Ministry's site.

Period. The Vision sets a 2040 horizon with targets for 2025, 2030 and 2040, and the Roadmap covers 2023/24 to 2027/28.

Delivery plan. The Vision carries a cost implementation matrix putting first-phase financing to 2030 at UGX 6.08 trillion, with a results framework of 2030 targets.

Reporting. The Vision has the working group prepare quarterly, semi-annual and annual implementation reports and run annual performance reviews.

Last twelve months. The Vision sets a mid-term evaluation in FY2028/29 and a final evaluation in FY2039/40.

Not found. No report against the Vision has been found, and its governance rows date from September 2022. The Digital Transformation Roadmap has no adopting act or public text on record.

ZAF.short: South Africa has a final draft digital masterplan dated 2021, not public, with its 2020-2025 period ended; no source found reports its adoption.
ZAF.summary:
Governance and finance. The final draft of the ICT and Digital Economy Masterplan for South Africa is dated 22 February 2021 and credits Genesis Analytics and Knowledge Executive as authors.

Standing. Economist Impact says South Africa has published numerous draft versions of the masterplan. The department's 2023/24 plan, approved 31 March 2023, lists a Digital Economy Framework and Strategy still to go to Cabinet.

Text. The Economist Impact profile says in a footnote that the plan is not publicly available. The text held is the final draft of February 2021.

Period. Economist Impact titles the masterplan 2020-2025.

Delivery plan. The final draft has a Priority Action Plan in section 6, with an appendix of actions, some with named executors and time limits of three or five years.

Reporting. The Portfolio Committee's report on the Department of Communications and Digital Technologies for 2024/25 states that implementation of the Digital Economy Masterplan was not achieved against the department's target for the year.

Last twelve months. The latest row held on the masterplan is the Portfolio Committee's report for 2024/25, dated 2025.

Not found. No row says the masterplan was approved or adopted, and Economist Impact says the final version is not public. Its 2020-2025 period has ended, and no governance facts have been found.

ZMB.short: Zambia adopted a public national digital transformation strategy in 2023, running to 2027, with no cost stated; no source found reports progress against its targets.
ZMB.summary:
Governance and finance. The National Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2027 makes the technology and science ministry the coordinating agency, responsible for quarterly monitoring and reporting. It is to be financed by the Government with cooperating partners, with no amount given.

Standing. A 2023 journal study says the strategy was adopted in 2023. The Ministry of Technology and Science published it on 12 October 2023.

Text. The strategy's full text is hosted on the Ministry of Technology and Science's site, from October 2023.

Period. The strategy states its period as 2023-2027, a five-year implementation framework.

Delivery plan. It sets out interventions with numeric targets, indicators and lead institutions, for example 998 communication towers and 200 district digital transformation centres.

Reporting. The strategy's results framework carries targets for 2026.

Last twelve months. Freight News described the strategy's five pillars on 3 September 2026.

Not found. No report on progress against the strategy's targets has been found, and the delivery plan states no cost. No change in the last twelve months is on record.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe's Smart Zimbabwe 2030 Master Plan was launched in 2024 and runs to 2030; no delivery plan or results are known.
ZWE.summary:
Governance and finance. The ICT Minister opened the regulator's POTRAZ Strategic Formulation Workshop in Mutare on 4 November 2025.

Standing. ICT Minister Tatenda Mavetera launched the Smart Zimbabwe 2030 Master Plan on 7 March 2024, with the National ICT Policy 2022-2027 and the Broadband Plan 2020-2030, as the strategy for a digital economy by 2030. A successor, the National Digital Roadmap for 2026 to 2030, began its formulation at a regulator's workshop in November 2025.

Text. The ministry publishes the Smart Zimbabwe 2030 Master Plan, which sets out its pillars and the institutional arrangement to coordinate ICT across the economy.

Period. The Master Plan runs to 2030. The National Digital Roadmap now being drafted is meant for 2026 to 2030.

Delivery plan. The launch report describes the Master Plan as working through sector pillars, with ministries to develop programmes and projects; no dated actions or costs are given.

Reporting. No results against the Master Plan's targets are reported; the latest row on national digital strategy is the roadmap workshop of 4 November 2025.

Last twelve months. The Strategic Formulation Workshop of 4 November 2025 started the process.

Not found. No delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and no results against the Master Plan's targets, have been found. The roadmap now being drafted is not yet adopted, and the coordinating body the Master Plan sets up is on record only from 2019.

AGO.short: Nothing found names digital accessibility for persons with disabilities or says there is none, so no stage is set.
AGO.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether information and digital services are made accessible to persons with disabilities.

BDI.short: Nothing found since 2023 names digital accessibility for persons with disabilities, so no stage is set.
BDI.summary: Not found. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether information or digital services are being made accessible to persons with disabilities.

BEN.short: Accessible digital services or assistive technology were delivered to persons with disabilities in 2024; no audit is published.
BEN.summary:
Accessibility rule. No source found says digital accessibility for persons with disabilities is under way or in service. The nearest held fact: La Nation reports the government set up three digital classrooms for visually impaired learners (Cotonou-Sègbèya, Parakou, and one other) with screen readers, braille printers and braille displays, and 31 pupils of CEG Sègbèya trained at Sègbèya in 2023-2024. A later answer places the country above that step.

Delivered. La Nation reports the government set up three digital classrooms for visually impaired learners (Cotonou-Sègbèya, Parakou, and one other) with screen readers, braille printers and braille displays, and 31 pupils of CEG Sègbèya trained at Sègbèya in 2023-2024.

Audited. No source found since October 2023 gives the results of an accessibility audit of public websites or digital services. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

Not found. No source found since October 2023 gives the results of an accessibility audit of public websites or digital services.

BFA.short: Work to make information and digital services accessible to persons with disabilities was under way in 2025; a rule in force is not on record.

Accessibility rule. TZA.short: An audit of how accessible public digital services are was published in 2025.
TZA.summary:
Accessibility rule. The Tanzania Bureau of Standards recognised TCRA for implementing the newly introduced Tanzania Standard on accessibility of communications and ICT products and services for persons with disabilities. TCRA says its iPRIS Change Initiative on adopting assistive technologies for persons with disabilities is 80 percent complete and due to be finalised within six months. The Tanzania Bureau of Standards circulated for stakeholder comment, by 2025-04-14, a draft Tanzania standard on requirements for communications and ICT products and services accessibility to persons with disabilities (EDC 6, 3227).

Delivered. TCRA has integrated assistive technologies into its website to improve accessibility, and its FURSA SANA and FUTA DELETE KABISA campaigns used sign language interpretation and braille in digital skills training for persons with disabilities in Dar es Salaam, Mtwara and Dodoma.

Audited. A study by Catherine G. Mkude of the Open University of Tanzania evaluated 42 Tanzanian e-government websites against WCAG 2.2 using SortSite, finding an average of 3.64 pages per site with accessibility errors, mostly Level A, with the National Identification Authority portal fully compliant and the NHIF service portal widely non-conformant.

Not found. Nothing further is asked of this indicator.

USAASA opened a public consultation on updating the 2010 ministerial determination on universal access and service, with a review of accessibility for people with disabilities among its issues.

Delivered. No source found since October 2023 says accessible digital services or assistive technology were delivered. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

ZWE.short: Accessible digital services or assistive technology were delivered to persons with disabilities in 2026; no audit is published.
ZWE.summary:
Accessibility rule. Ministry spokesperson Taungana Ndoro said the Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education is scaling up inclusive education for learners with disabilities through assistive tools, accessible buildings and specialised teacher training. A later answer places the country above that step. 2 facts are held on the subject: no news story or official notice read for this study says more about it, the documents the earlier cell cited were not read, and the systems themselves were not examined.

Delivered. Harare Institute of Technology hosted a two-day Zimbabwe University Libraries Consortium workshop training librarians from more than 22 state universities on assistive technologies (screen reader, Braille and reading devices), with equipment funded by a USD 220,000 grant secured by the consortium for its member libraries (HIT, 2026-06-10). In March 2026 the government-commissioned National Information Access Centre at Zimbabwe Open University opened with an inclusive library equipped with assistive technologies, and the vice chancellor said it has smart boards and assistive devices for students with disabilities.
