AGO.short: Angola cut its 2026 communications programme budget by 30.5% on 2025; no spending figure has been found and no fund is known.
AGO.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The 2026 budget sets 159.2 billion kwanza for the communications expansion and modernisation programme, down 30.5% from 229.3 billion in the 2025 budget. The digital lines held for both years total 9,912,523,594 kwanza for 2026 against 9,854,246,545 for 2025. The 4G expansion line falls from 107.8 to 62.7 billion kwanza, and the cybersecurity programme is cut 54%, from 70.5 to 32.3 billion kwanza in the proposed 2026 budget.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The 2026 budget gives 375,466,178,608 kwanza to 52 digital lines. A supplementary credit of 275 million US dollars was opened in the 2026 budget for the Ministry of Territorial Administration's citizens' database plan.

Not found. The money for digital transformation was lower in the latest budget than in the one before.

BDI.short: Burundi's 2026/27 budget raised its digital lines 7.3% and a universal service fund paid for connectivity projects; no source found reports actual spending.
BDI.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The digital lines held for both years total 3,236,082,542 Burundi francs for 2026/27 against 3,015,773,158 for 2025/26, a rise of 7.3%. The budget for 2026/27 gives 80,666,493,781 francs to 74 digital lines.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The Fonds de Service Universel des TIC is funded by a 1% levy on operators' turnover under decree 100/054 of 29 March 2024 and its 2025/26 plan pays 4,811,751,000 francs for three pilot Villages Numériques. Its 2026/27 plan pays 11.4 billion francs for internet connectivity to public health facilities, secondary schools and community telecentres, reaching 75 health facilities and 75 secondary schools after a first 25 of each.

Not found. No budget execution report, settlement law, audited accounts or fund account from the last three years gives what was actually spent.

BEN.short: Benin cut its 2026 digital budget 6.3% from 2025 and published 2025 spending on digital lines; no source found reports any fund or levy.
BEN.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The 2026 digital budget of 27.2 billion CFA francs is 6.32% lower than the 29.034 billion approved for 2025, mainly through a 12.22% fall in external financing. The state's published tables put spending on digital lines for 2025 at 10,487,000,000 francs. The 2026 figure is 9.7 billion francs of operating costs and 17.4 billion of capital across three programmes. By 30 April 2026 77,247,968 francs of the Numérique programme's 12,372,151,413 had been ordered for payment.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The 2026 budget execution table gives the Numérique programme 12.4 billion francs in credits, part-paid by a loan tranche, and the ministry's piloting and support programme 2,184,235,167 francs.

Not found. The money for digital transformation was lower in the latest budget than in the one before.

BFA.short: Burkina Faso's digital lines held in both years fell 11.1% in the 2026 budget; no source found reports any fund or levy for digital programmes.
BFA.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The digital ministry's 2026 annual work plan is budgeted at 61 billion CFA francs, but the digital lines held for both years total 6,174,786,000 francs for 2026 against 6,947,413,000 for 2025, a fall of 11.1%. The execution report to 31 December 2025 shows the ministry's domestic investment ordered for payment at 2,094,406,682 francs. For 2024 the infrastructure programme shows 272,081,258 francs spent, 19.6% of the 1,387,136,000 voted. On 16 April 2026 the Council of Ministers authorised 9,113,100,000 francs of procurement for the ministry's specific projects, financed by the 2026 state budget.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The 2026 finance law appropriates 1,187,169,000 francs in domestic payment credits to the electronic communications infrastructure programme and 1,916,611,000 francs to the digital transformation and ecosystem programme.

Not found. The money for digital transformation was lower in the latest budget than in the one before.

BWA.short: Botswana's 2026/27 budget cut the communications ministry's development money; an access fund paid for centres in 2025. No source found reports full-year 2025/26 spending.
BWA.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The Ministry of Communications and Innovation's development budget for 2026/27 is 473,200,000 pula, down 11.5% on the revised 2025/26 figure and 44.6% on the 2025/26 appropriation. The digital lines held for both years total 1,040,522,175 pula for 2026/27 against 1,055,985,797 for 2025/26. The budget documents publish 1,057,424,684 pula as spent on digital lines for 2024/25.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The Universal Access and Service Fund Trust was established in April 2014 and is financed by a levy of up to 1% of licensed operators' annual gross turnover. Two primary-school Digital Centres, each costing 1.59 million pula, were launched on 28 November 2025 through the fund.

Not found. Nothing found shows the state's money for digital programmes higher in the latest budget than in the one before.

CAF.short: Central African Republic's 2026 budget raises digital lines 15 per cent; no source found reports no fund is shown paying and spending.
CAF.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The digital lines held for both years total 4,384,800,000 CFA francs for 2026 against 3,804,800,000 for 2025, up 15.2 per cent. The 2026 budget holds 51 digital lines worth 5,881,925,000 CFA francs. The 2026 draft proposes 300,000,000 CFA francs from domestic financing for urban optical fibre loops, and the 2025 finance bill carried 1,400,000,000 CFA francs of domestic money in support of the regulator ARCEP. It also proposes 118 million CFA francs, financed domestically, for six months of 2024 salary arrears at the state's digital development agency.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The nearest held fact is the 2026 budget's 51 digital lines, 5,881,925,000 CFA francs in all.

Not found. No fund, levy or assigned tax is shown created, collecting or paying, and no pledge to pay for digital programmes at home is shown with an act following it.

CIV.short: Côte d'Ivoire's 2026 digital ministry budget rose 37 per cent and a telecom levy paid in 2024; no source found reports the levy's law.
CIV.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The 2024 settlement law records 23,434,278,284 CFA francs spent in 2024 on programme 22126, Economie numérique et poste. The digital ministry's 2026 budget of 83.275 billion CFA francs is described as a 37% increase, and programme 22126 rises from 19,033,679,859 CFA francs in 2025 to 45,991,319,076 in 2026. The digital lines held for both years total 148,105,376,640 CFA francs for 2026 against 157,659,408,117 for 2025, down 6.1 per cent.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. Programme 23237 is an earmarked account funded by a levy on telecom operators; the 2026 finance law appropriates 33 billion CFA francs to it. In 2024 the levy funded the ANSUT rural-technology account, and collection fell short, so the 32.3 billion voted was cut to 27,676,208,542 CFA francs.

Not found. The law that creates the levy is not named in the documents held.

The national digital cadastre programme is named at 874,046,000 CFA francs in that bill, against 1,567,500,000 in the 2025 finance law and 1,203,574,000 in the 2024 finance law, both from domestic revenue. COG.short: The 2026 budget raises the digital programme 30.5% to 30.1 billion CFA francs, and a SIM-terminal tax funds digital; its yield is unknown.

CPV.short: The 2026 budget cuts the digital ministry to 174 million Cape Verdean escudos from 370 million; the universal service fund stays flat; payouts unknown.

DJI.short: The state digital agency's 2026 budget fell about 29% from 2025, while the digital line held for both years rose; no fund is known.
DJI.summary:

The 2026 budget of ANSIE, the state digital agency, is 396.1 million Djibouti francs, down from 556.7 million in 2025, a fall of about 29% that the record ties to a separate cybersecurity authority. The budget gives 485,686,344 Djibouti francs to the one digital line held for 2026, and the digital lines held for both years total 485,686,344 for 2026 against 456,943,040 for 2025. DZA.short: Algeria's 2026 budget gives money to 10 digital lines and the state pays for universal service mobile coverage; no source found reports the prior year.

The state pays for the 201-site Mobilis 4G universal service programme, more than 27.3 billion dinars, about 204 million dollars, through the fonds d'appui du service universel, under a specification approved on 4 August 2026, with the fund set up by decree 18-247 of 2018; the document says it is not Mobilis's own investment. On 7 September 2026 the regulator launched a tender for mobile coverage of 3000 small localities, financed wholly by the state through the universal service mechanism. A similar 1,400-locality 4G programme is being completed.

EGY.short: Egypt's digital budget lines rose 24.4% in 2026/27 over 2025/26; no fund, levy or assigned tax for digital programmes is known.

For 2025/26 the Minister of Planning told the House of Representatives that 13 billion pounds of public investment is allocated to the ICT sector, of which 9 billion comes from the general budget. No figure for what was spent has been found.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The nearest held fact is a ministry document, seen by Bloomberg, saying Egypt intends to allocate up to 860 million dollars a year from the general budget from 2026/27 to 2030 for data centres, computing and AI.

Not found. No fund, levy or assigned tax is shown created, collecting or paying for digital programmes.

ERI.short: Nothing found says whether the state budget funds digital programmes or whether a fund or levy pays for them, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not found. Nothing found says whether the state budget gives money to digital programmes, or that a fund or levy pays for them.

ETH.short: Ethiopia's digital budget lines rose 48.2% in 2026/27 over 2025/26; no fund, levy or assigned tax for digital programmes is known.

The same budget appropriates 1,484,839,300 birr to the Ministry of Innovation and Technology and 6,293,131,040 birr to the Artificial Intelligence Institution, 5,600,000,000 of it capital and 693,131,040 recurrent.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The nearest held fact is that the 2026/27 federal budget gives the Artificial Intelligence Institution its money, all from the treasury.

Not found. No fund, levy or assigned tax is shown created, collecting or paying for digital programmes.

GAB.short: The digital ministry's 2027 budget estimate fell to 37.2 billion CFA francs from 53.7 billion in 2026; no source found reports spending.
GAB.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. In the 2027 finance bill, presented to the National Assembly on 25 October 2026, the Ministry of the Digital Economy asks for 37,214,804,386 CFA francs, against 53,711,081,266 in 2026, a fall of about 16.5 billion. In the 2026 budget, the digital lines held for both years total 25,152,318,272 CFA francs for 2026 against 22,855,429,916 for 2025, a rise of 10.0 per cent, from a budget document dated 17 July 2026. The Ministry of Digital Economy, Digitalization and Innovation's own budget, as the minister presented it to the National Transition Assembly in October 2025, rises from 32 billion CFA francs in 2025 to 82 billion in 2026, an increase of 156.2 per cent. The 10 lines held for both years sit within a wider set: in all, the 2026 budget gives 30,511,992,244 CFA francs to 14 digital lines.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The nearest held fact is the budget itself, which names no fund, levy or assigned tax for digital programmes: it lists 14 digital lines for 2026, 30,511,992,244 CFA francs in all, and the ministry's 82 billion CFA francs is the figure the minister presented for 2026.

Not found. Nothing found shows the government saying digital transformation must be paid for from the country's own resources and acting on it: no fund, levy or assigned tax is shown created, collecting or paying. Nothing found gives what was spent.

GHA.short: Ghana's digital lines held for both years rose from 42 million to 258 million cedis in the 2026 budget; no source found reports spending.

A further 138,000,000 of donor money is left out of that figure. The Cyber Security Authority sub-programme receives 25,346,198 cedis for 2026.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The nearest held fact is the 2026 appropriation for ICT Capacity Development, paid wholly from domestic revenue.

Not found. Nothing found shows the government saying digital transformation must be paid for from the country's own resources and acting on it: no fund, levy or assigned tax is shown created, collecting or paying. Nothing found gives what was spent.

GIN.short: Guinea's digital lines nearly doubled in the 2025 budget, and a May 2026 decree created a fund financed by a levy; spending is unknown.

In all, the 2025 budget gives 347,913,391,946 Guinean francs to 113 digital lines. It is to fund technology infrastructure, cybersecurity, training and innovation. Enforcement of the fee follows a six-month transition, and no money is yet reported collected or paid.

Not found. Nothing found shows the government saying digital transformation must be paid for from the country's own resources and acting on it: no fund, levy or assigned tax is shown created, collecting or paying.

GNB.short: The 2026 budget gives 129 million CFA francs to six digital lines, lower than 2025 on shared lines; no source reports spending and any fund.
