AGO.short: Angola adopted its ICT white paper for 2023-2027 by presidential decree in December 2024; no source found says whether its text is public.
AGO.summary:
Governance and finance. The telecommunications ministry, MINTTICS, put the proposed Livro Branco das TIC 2023-2027 to public consultation in 2024, and its minister writes that the policy aligns the sector with the National Development Plan 2023-2027.

Standing. The Livro Branco das TIC 2023-2027 was approved by Presidential Decree 272/24 of 5 December 2024, repealing the Livro Branco das TIC 2019-2022.

Text. The ministry's site carries Presidential Order 129/19 of 22 July 2019, which approved the Livro Branco das TIC 2019-2022, with a download link.

Period. The policy runs from 2023 to 2027, with five objectives targeted by 2027.

Delivery plan. A later decree describes the policy as setting policy measures and strategic actions for the ICT sector on six axes.

Reporting. In October 2025 the ministry reported that the president's State of the Nation message credited the Livro Branco das TIC and its instruments with moving the sector from reform to development.

Last twelve months. A March 2026 article cites the policy as setting plans for a space studies centre, expert training and communications, navigation and meteorology infrastructure.

Not found. No source found says whether the text of the Livro Branco das TIC 2023-2027 is public. Nothing is held on a mandated body, finance, a delivery plan or reporting against the policy, and no dated change to it falls in the twelve months to 30 September 2026.

BDI.short: The national ICT development policy adopted in 2011 ran to 2025; no source says whether a successor is being prepared, so no stage is set.
BDI.summary: Not found. The Politique nationale de développement des TIC (PNDTIC) 2010-2025 reached the end of its period in 2025, and no successor sector policy has been found as announced, in drafting or validated. No delivery plan, report against the policy's targets or event in the last twelve months is held, and the newest facts on the responsible ministry and on finance date from 2021 and 2022.

BEN.short: A digital economy sector policy declaration adopted in 2016 ran to 2021; no source found says whether a successor exists, so no stage is set.
BEN.summary: Not found. The Déclaration de politique sectorielle de l'économie numérique ran to 2021, and no successor sector policy has been found as adopted or in preparation. No mandated body, finance, report against the policy's targets or event in the twelve months to 30 September 2026 is held.

BFA.short: The sector policy published in 2015 ran to 2020; no source found says whether a successor is in preparation, so no stage is set.
BFA.summary: Not found. The newest sector policy on record is the Politique sectorielle de l'Economie numérique et des Postes 2016-2020, which the ministry published in September 2015 and whose period ended in 2020. No source found says whether a successor sector policy has been announced, drafted, validated or adopted, and nothing is held on a delivery plan, reporting or finance for the 2016-2020 policy.

BWA.short: Botswana has a national ICT policy approved by its National Assembly in 2007; no source found reports its period, delivery plan and reporting.
BWA.summary:
Governance and finance. The contents of the National ICT Policy (Maitlamo) of 2007 list a governance structure of an Information Age Council, an ICT Legal Reform Taskforce, an enhanced Department of Information Technology and an e-Governance Structure.

Standing. The National Assembly approved the policy in August 2007, as Government Paper No 3 of 2007, and a report published in December 2025 refers to it as Botswana's existing policy.

Text. The Ministry of Communications, Science and Technology published the full text in August 2007.

Period. The World Bank's 2022 diagnostic says the policy was launched in 2007.

Delivery plan. The same diagnostic says the policy was launched to guide the development of the sector.

Reporting. The December 2025 report gives the policy's aim as faster, cheaper and more transparent government services in support of socioeconomic development.

Last twelve months. The policy of 2007 was still the one named for Botswana in the report of December 2025.

Not found. Nothing found gives the policy an end year, a delivery plan, a report against its targets or a source of finance. Its governance bodies are known only from the 2007 text, and no dated event falls in the last twelve months.

CAF.short: A national digital strategy is held but no ICT sector policy is named; no source found says whether one exists, so no stage is set.
CAF.summary: Not found. No ICT or telecommunications sector policy is named for the country. No source found says whether one has been adopted, is in preparation or does not exist.

CIV.short: Côte d'Ivoire has a national digital strategy for 2021 to 2025; whether it has an ICT sector policy is unknown, so no stage is set.
CIV.summary: Not found. No ICT sector policy is on record for Côte d'Ivoire, whether adopted, in preparation or expired. The only instrument held is the national digital strategy.

CMR.short: A posts, telecommunications and ICT sector strategy was finalised in 2005 with targets to 2015; no source reports its adoption, so no stage is set.
CMR.summary: Not found. No source states that the Stratégie sectorielle des postes, télécommunications et TIC 2005 was adopted by decree or by the minister: it is held as finalised at a seminar in September 2005, and its targets ended in 2015. No successor sector policy is on record as adopted or in preparation, and no text, report against it, responsible body, budget line or activity in the last twelve months is held.

COD.short: DR Congo's 2009 telecommunications and ICT sector policy lapsed in 2014; no source says whether a successor is being prepared, so no stage is set.
COD.summary: Not found. The Document de politique sectorielle 2009 ran out in 2014 without its review, and no sector policy has been found in preparation to succeed it. Its text, the cost of its targets for 2015, reporting, governance and finance, and any movement in the last twelve months are not held.

COG.short: A national ICT policy was drawn up in 2008-2009; no source found says whether its text was ever published.
COG.summary:
Governance and finance. A project coordination unit in the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications in charge of ICT was to monitor implementation of the National ICT Policy, as a project appraisal document of May 2011 set out.

Standing. The government drew up its national ICT development policy in 2008-2009, the minister told the Council of Ministers on 6 March 2019. An appraisal document of 4 May 2011 treats the National ICT Policy as existing.

Text. The 2011 appraisal document does not describe the policy's scope.

Period. The Council of Ministers communique of 6 March 2019 gives no date of adoption for the policy.

Delivery plan. In 2011 a project steering committee was to check project activities against the National ICT Policy.

Reporting. The coordination unit was to monitor the policy's implementation together with the government's ICT strategy, under the 2011 appraisal document.

Last twelve months. The latest dated fact is of 6 March 2019, when the minister said the electronic transactions bill follows the national ICT development policy.

Not found. Whether the policy's text was published, when and by what act it was adopted, the period it covers, and whether it has a delivery plan or any reporting. Nothing dated in the last three years says who runs or funds it.

COM.short: A telecommunications and digital sector policy, which the minister said in 2022 was being implemented; no source found reports its text and adoption date.
COM.summary:
Governance and finance. The minister for posts, telecommunications and the digital economy said in September 2022 that the country was implementing its sectoral policy.

Standing. The Politique sectorielle des télécommunications et du numérique is adopted: the minister told the ITU's plenipotentiary conference in September 2022 that Comoros was in the process of implementing it. The ministry's mission page, dated to 2016, refers to a "new sector policy" without saying that it was adopted.

Text. The ministry's mission page names the new sector policy beside the Comores numérique strategy.

Period. The ministry's page, dated to 2016, calls the sector policy new, and the minister described it as being implemented in September 2022.

Delivery plan. The ministry's page places the government's action within the new sector policy and the Comores numérique strategy.

Reporting. The minister's statement to the ITU conference says the sectoral policy is being implemented.

Last twelve months. The minister's statement that the policy is being implemented dates from September 2022.

Not found. No text of the policy has been found, and nothing gives its adoption date, its period, a delivery plan, a report against it, a mandated body or a budget line. Nothing on the policy is dated after September 2022.

CPV.short: No ICT or telecommunications sector policy is on record as of 2026; no source found says whether one exists, so no stage is set.
CPV.summary: Not found. No ICT or telecommunications sector policy is on record as adopted, in preparation or absent. A national digital strategy is held instead and is assessed on its own row.

DJI.short: Djibouti's sector policy, adopted in 2014, ran to 2024; no source says whether a successor is adopted or being prepared, so no stage is set.
DJI.summary: Not found. The Schéma stratégique intégré (SSI) 2014-2024, approved by a law published in February 2015, ended in 2024, and no successor sector policy is on record as adopted or in preparation; no text, dated action plan, report or finance has been found for it. The Politique nationale de développement des TIC, which the minister named in July 2025, has no adoption date, period or text on record.

DZA.short: Algeria has a post and telecommunications ministry action plan, reported in 2023; no source says whether a sector policy exists, so no stage is set.
DZA.summary: Not found. No ICT or telecommunications sector policy is on record as adopted or in preparation, and no dated statement that the country has none has been found. The one sector instrument on record is a ministry's action plan.

EGY.short: The 2013 national ICT strategy ran to 2017; no source found says whether the strategy to 2030 was adopted, so no stage is set.
EGY.summary: Not found. The National ICT Strategy 2013-2017 reached the end of its period in 2017, and no sector policy has been found as adopted or in preparation after it. The ministry's web page gives the ICT 2030 Strategy a period, to 2030, and nothing else: no source found says whether it was adopted, is being drafted or was only announced, and neither are its text, governance, delivery plan or reporting.

ERI.short: Eritrea had no national ICT policy or development plan in 2009, UNECA said; no source found says whether one has been adopted since.
ERI.summary:
Governance and finance. A UNECA paper on Eastern Africa, published in April 2009, states that Eritrea has no National ICT Development Agency.

Standing. The UNECA paper of April 2009 states that Eritrea has no national ICT policy defining the government's orientation and strategies for development, and its table of 13 states enters "No ICT Policy" against the country.

Text. UNECA, in April 2009, states that Eritrea has no national ICT policy.

Period. UNECA, in April 2009, states that Eritrea has no national ICT policy.

Delivery plan. The same UNECA paper states that no National ICT Development Plan exists for Eritrea.

Reporting. UNECA, in April 2009, states that Eritrea has neither a national ICT policy nor a National ICT Development Plan.

Last twelve months. The UNECA statement that Eritrea has no national ICT policy dates from April 2009.

Not found. The only statement that Eritrea has no ICT sector policy is UNECA's of April 2009, and nothing later confirms or contradicts it. Nothing is held on governance, finance or the last twelve months.

ETH.short: Ethiopia adopted a national ICT policy and strategy in 2016, endorsed by ministers in 2017; no source found says whether its text is published.
ETH.summary:
Governance and finance. The Ministry of Innovation and Technology is mandated under the Communication Services Proclamation of 2019 to develop policy instruments, mobilise resources and guide and monitor the telecom sector. It was formed in October 2018 by merging the Ministry of Communication and Information Technology with the Ministry of Science and Technology. The policy's 2017 revision had financial support from the World Bank.

Standing. The National ICT Policy and Strategy was developed in 2016 and endorsed by the Council of Ministers in 2017.

Text. UNCTAD cites the policy as a 2016 document of the federal government.

Period. The policy revises one first drafted and submitted to the Council of Ministers in 2002.

Delivery plan. UNCTAD lists the interventions through which the policy is implemented.

Reporting. UNCTAD said in September 2021 that implementation was fragmented across projects and sectors.

Last twelve months. In September 2021 the policy was still being implemented.

Not found. Whether the policy's text is published, the period it covers, a delivery plan with dates or costs, and any report against its targets. No domestic budget line is stated, and nothing dated in the last twelve months has been found.

GAB.short: Gabon had formulated a national ICT policy by 2022, a JICA study says; no source found reports its adoption date, text and period.
GAB.summary:
Governance and finance. A JICA baseline study of public service digitalisation in African countries, published in March 2022, states that Gabon has formulated a national ICT policy, the Politique nationale des TIC.

Standing. The JICA study of March 2022 states that Gabon has formulated a national ICT policy consistent with the PSGE Vision 2025, and gives no date of adoption.

Text. JICA, in March 2022, states that the national ICT policy has been formulated.

Period. The JICA study states that the policy is consistent with the PSGE Vision 2025.

Delivery plan. JICA, in March 2022, states that Gabon has formulated a national ICT policy.

Reporting. The same JICA study states that the policy has been formulated, consistent with the PSGE Vision 2025.

Last twelve months. The JICA statement that Gabon has formulated a national ICT policy dates from March 2022.

Not found. The only statement of the policy is JICA's of March 2022, which gives no adoption date. The policy's text, period, delivery plan, reporting, mandated body and finance are not held, and nothing is dated since.

GHA.short: Ghana's telecommunications policy of 2005 is in force with no end date; no source found says whether it reports against its targets.
GHA.summary:
Governance and finance. The National Telecommunications Policy of 2005 makes the Ministry of Communications responsible for defining and reviewing telecommunications policy and the National Communications Authority responsible for implementing it. A guide published on 20 September 2024 says the Ministry of Communications and Digitalization directs communications-sector policy.

Standing. The Ministry of Communications released the National Telecommunications Policy as final on 10 January 2005. A report published on 8 October 2025 recommends updating it and the ICT for Accelerated Development Policy of 2003, and calls both outdated.

Text. The full 33-page text is on the National Communications Authority's website.

Period. The policy states no end date for itself and provides for the ministry to review and amend it.

Delivery plan. The policy sets dated actions and targets with no costs, among them 25% penetration and universal access by 2010.

Reporting. The policy gives the Ministry of Communications the monitoring of progress.

Last twelve months. The report of 8 October 2025 still names the 2005 policy as Ghana's.

Not found. No report against the policy's targets, no cost for its actions and no source of finance has been found. No sector policy has been found as adopted or in preparation to succeed it, and no dated event falls in the twelve months to 30 September 2026.

GIN.short: A digital sector policy letter was announced in a national strategy published in 2024; no source found says whether drafting has begun.
GIN.summary:
Governance and finance. The national digitalisation strategy, published in June 2024, puts the drafting of the Lettre de politique sectorielle du numérique under the ministry it calls MPTEN, with the executive, and costs it at USD 50 thousand.

Standing. The letter is announced as initiative 1.1.8 of that strategy, to be drafted. The government adopted the Politique et stratégie nationales de développement des TIC in 2010.

Text. The strategy lists the letter as a document still to be drafted.

Period. The strategy allows six months for the drafting and gives it no date. An earlier national information and communication infrastructure plan covered 2001 to 2004.

Delivery plan. The 2010 policy set six aims and proposed one computer for each secondary pupil, higher-education student and teacher, with no cost or dates stated.

Reporting. UNESCO's profile of 2023 reports later initiatives launched in line with the 2010 policy.

Last twelve months. The latest dated fact on the letter is its listing in the strategy published on 11 June 2024.

Not found. Whether drafting of the sector policy letter has begun, and any text, period, delivery plan or report for it. The text of the 2010 policy is not held, and nothing on the letter is dated in the twelve months to 30 September 2026.

GMB.short: The Gambia has an ICT for development policy statement adopted for 2018 to 2028; no source found says whether its text is public.
GMB.summary:
Governance and finance. The ICT4D Policy Statement 2018-2028 appears in a 2025 presentation by the Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy on data governance in The Gambia.

Standing. The ministry's presentation lists the statement among the country's existing policies, strategies and legal frameworks, and a Principal Assistant Secretary at the ministry named it in October 2026 among The Gambia's ICT policies.

Text. The presentation sets out the statement's nine priority areas.

Period. The statement runs from 2018 to 2028, as the ministry's presentation titles it.

Delivery plan. The presentation gives the statement's priority areas beside the ministry's other policies and strategies.

Reporting. The head of the Gambian delegation said in October 2026 that the country had already built gender considerations into the statement.

Last twelve months. The statement was on the ministry's list of policies in 2025.

Not found. No source holds, links or quotes the statement's text, and none says it is unpublished. Nothing is held on a delivery plan, reporting against targets, a mandated body or finance, and no dated event falls in the twelve months to 30 September 2026.

GNB.short: An ICT strategy was in preparation in 2021, when the regulator produced a preliminary report; no source found says whether it was adopted.
GNB.summary:
Governance and finance. The regulator, ARN, produced the preliminary report on an ICT strategy in December 2021.

Standing. An ICT strategy was in preparation in Guinea-Bissau in December 2021, when the regulator issued a preliminary report on it.

Text. The strategy appears as a preliminary report of December 2021, cited for its data in the Guinea-Bissau Digital Economy Diagnostic.

Period. The same diagnostic also cites a "Preliminary ICT strategy report 2022" alongside the December 2021 report.

Delivery plan. By December 2021 the work on the strategy had reached a preliminary report, which the regulator ARN produced.

Reporting. The Guinea-Bissau Digital Economy Diagnostic, published in 2022, takes data from the regulator's preliminary ICT strategy report.

Last twelve months. The regulator's preliminary report dates from December 2021, and the diagnostic citing it from 2022.

Not found. The one source cites the regulator's preliminary report without giving the strategy's scope or saying it was adopted, and nothing dated since shows whether drafting continued. No text, period, delivery plan, reporting, responsible body or finance has been found.

GNQ.short: No ICT or telecommunications sector policy has been found; no source found says whether one is adopted or in preparation, so no stage is set.
GNQ.summary: Not found. No ICT or telecommunications sector policy has been found as adopted or in preparation, and no dated statement that the country has none has been found. No mandated body, finance, delivery plan, report or event in the twelve months to 30 September 2026 is held.

KEN.short: Kenya has a national ICT policy adopted in 2019 and gazetted in 2020; no source found reports its period, delivery plan and reporting.
KEN.summary:
Governance and finance. Research ICT Africa's report of September 2026 says the Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy is responsible for policy formulation and sector coordination, with the Communications Authority as regulator.

Standing. The ICT Sector Policy Guidelines 2006 were reviewed and updated to a National ICT Policy in 2019, and the policy was gazetted in 2020 as Gazette Notice No. 5472.

Text. The policy was published in a special issue of the Kenya Gazette, and the September 2026 report cites it to a page on the ministry's website.

Period. The draft artificial intelligence policy of July 2026 lists the National ICT Policy 2019 among the instruments in place.

Delivery plan. The Communications Authority's consultation of September 2026 says the policy directs government agencies to promote and license private investment in carrier-neutral data centres.

Reporting. A 2022 review of the Digital Literacy Programme says the policy sets objectives for scaling up ICT in education.

Last twelve months. An analysis published in July 2026 names the ICT policy among Kenya's existing instruments.

Not found. Nothing found gives the policy an end year, a delivery plan, a report against its targets or a domestic budget line. Sources give both 2019 and 2020 as its year, and no dated event falls in the last twelve months.

LBR.short: Liberia's ICT policy, adopted in 2019, ran out in 2025 and a 2025-2030 successor is in draft; no source says when it will be adopted.
LBR.summary:
Governance and finance. The National ICT Policy 2019-2024 gives the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications overall coordination, implementation, review and oversight, and the national digital strategy published in February 2026 says its governing board, chief information officer and council of chief information officers were put in place. On money, the policy says the Executive ensures resources are available to the ministries concerned.

Standing. The government adopted the policy in 2019, and the President signed it that year.

Text. The full text is on the ministry's website.

Period. The policy set itself five years, 2019 to 2024, and was extended to 2025. The ministry's draft of its successor, the National ICT Policy 2025-2030, dated 7 January 2025, lists it as expired.

Delivery plan. The policy carries a summary of measurable targets with timelines of one to five years after adoption.

Reporting. An appendix to the national digital strategy reviews the policy's initiatives and says its targets have not been met, among them internet access at 50% of clinics and hospitals.

Last twelve months. The national digital strategy, published on 3 February 2026, says the successor policy has been drafted and is in consultation, with approval targeted for the last quarter of 2025. A press release of 8 September 2026 lists a draft National ICT Policy.

Not found. No adoption of the National ICT Policy 2025-2030 is on record. A budget line for the 2019-2024 policy is not held.

LBY.short: Libya has a telecommunications and informatics strategy for 2023 to 2027, in use in 2025; no source found says whether its text is published.
LBY.summary:
Governance and finance. The General Authority for Communications and Informatics (GACI) is the authority competent to regulate and develop the telecommunications and information technology sector, and it is the body that announces work done under the strategy.

Standing. In October 2025 GACI announced root servers in Tripoli and Benghazi as implementing the National Telecommunications and Informatics Strategy 2023-2027.

Text. The Ministry of Telecommunications and Informatics says the strategy aims to develop digital infrastructure and the sector's efficiency.

Period. The strategy covers 2023 to 2027, and the ministry gave the same years in October 2026.

Delivery plan. At a GACI workshop in February 2026, officials stated the aim of drafting legislation and a guidance manual for data centres and cloud computing.

Reporting. GACI presented the root-server launch of October 2025 as the strategy being carried out.

Last twelve months. Root servers entered service in data centres in Tripoli and Benghazi in October 2025. On 15 February 2026 GACI held a workshop in Tripoli on regulating data centres and cloud computing, within the national communications strategy.

Not found. No text of the strategy has been found, and no source says whether it is published. No adopting act or date, delivery plan, budget line or report against the strategy's own targets is held.

LSO.short: Lesotho has a communications policy adopted in 2008 with no end year; no source found reports its delivery plan and reporting.
LSO.summary:
Governance and finance. The Lesotho Communications Policy 2008 makes the Lesotho Communications Authority the regulator for telecommunications, broadcasting and postal services, with the Minister setting basic policy. A 2025 tender notice says the ministry will review the policy with the authority.

Standing. The government adopted the policy in 2008. Before it came the Lesotho Telecommunications Policy 1999 and the ICT Policy for Lesotho 2005. The Lesotho ICT Policy 2021 was in draft in March 2022.

Text. The Ministry of Communications, Science and Technology published the full text, which the government's website hosts.

Period. The policy states no end year or review date.

Delivery plan. The policy states no budget line for its own implementation and provides for a Universal Service Fund drawing up to two percent of operators' net operating income.

Reporting. The National Digital Policy of December 2024 says the monitoring system planned under the ICT Policy for Lesotho 2005 was never established.

Last twelve months. The ministry sought consultants in mid-2025 to review the 2008 policy and draft a Lesotho Communications Policy (2025), with bids closing on 21 July 2025.

Not found. No delivery plan and no report against the 2008 policy has been found, and its finance is known only from the 2008 text. The ICT Policy 2021 is held only as a draft and the 2025 review only as a tender, and nothing is dated in the last twelve months.

MAR.short: A telecommunications sector policy note adopted in 2019 ran to 2023; no source says whether a successor is being prepared, so no stage is set.
MAR.summary: Not found. The Note d'orientations générales du secteur des télécommunications à horizon 2023, adopted on 26 December 2019, ran to 2023, and no successor note has been found as adopted or in preparation. No report against its targets, no finance for it and no event in the twelve months to 30 September 2026 has been found.

MDG.short: A national ICT for development policy dates from 2004, with targets assessed in 2022; no source says whether its text is public or still open.
MDG.summary:
Governance and finance. The MPTDN formulated the Politique nationale des TIC pour le développement in 2004 with support from UNDP.

Standing. A JICA study of March 2022 describes the 2004 policy as the Malagasy government's main ICT policy.

Text. The JICA study reports the policy as setting seven strategic objectives.

Period. The policy's targets run to 2015 for the digital network and to ten years from 2004 for users and engineers.

Delivery plan. The targets include a digital network covering every fivondronana by 2015, 10 million ICT users and 30,000 ICT engineers. The policy states no cost.

Reporting. In March 2022 JICA assessed progress against the policy's objectives: legal and regulatory reform was relatively advanced, while network extension and the training of ICT engineers were behind for lack of funds.

Last twelve months. The latest account of the policy is JICA's of March 2022.

Not found. The policy's text, an act adopting it and a stated period are not held, so no source found says whether the 2004 policy is still open. No mandated body or finance since September 2023 has been found, and no event in the twelve months to 30 September 2026.

MLI.short: A national ICT policy was adopted in 2005; no source found says whether its text is public and what period it covers.
MLI.summary:
Governance and finance. The Politique nationale des TIC 2005 names financing as one of its six priorities, alongside the legal framework, infrastructure, content and applications, media, and cooperation.

Standing. The Government adopted the national information and communication technology policy in 2005. It followed the Déclaration de politique sectorielle des télécommunications, which the Government adopted in 2000.

Text. The national digital economy strategy of November 2014, Mali Numérique 2020, sets out the 2005 policy's six priorities.

Period. The policy dates from 2005.

Delivery plan. The 2000 telecommunications declaration set the country's telecommunications objectives and an action programme. The 2005 policy is built on six priorities.

Reporting. Mali Numérique 2020 states in 2014 that the Government adopted the policy.

Last twelve months. The policy was adopted in 2005, and the telecommunications declaration before it in 2000.

Not found. No text of the 2005 policy has been found, and no source says it is unpublished. No period, delivery plan, results report, mandated body or budget line has been found for it, and nothing is dated within the last twelve months; its adoption is known only from a 2014 document.

MOZ.short: Mozambique's Information Society Policy was adopted in 2018 with no end date; no source found says whether results against its targets are reported.
MOZ.summary:
Governance and finance. Resolution 19/2018 gives the National Institute of Electronic Government (INAGE) the task of mobilising the money, materials and staff for the policy. The policy says its implementation depends on internal and external finance and private investment, and names no budget line. In 2022 INTIC said its work aimed to implement the policy.

Standing. The Council of Ministers approved the Política para a Sociedade da Informação on 20 March 2018 by Resolution 17/2018, in force from 21 June 2018. It revokes the Política de Informática of 2000.

Text. The full text is printed in the Boletim da República, I Série, no. 122, of 21 June 2018.

Period. The policy states no end date and no review year.

Delivery plan. The policy says an Operational Plan sets the actions, those responsible and the calendar for each five years of the Strategic Plan, and states no cost. Resolution 52/2019 approved the 2019-2028 Strategic Plan to put the policy into operation.

Reporting. INTIC's activity report for 2022 says its efforts that year aimed to implement the policy and its Strategic Plan.

Last twelve months. In April 2026 Mozambique told a UNCTAD ministerial roundtable that the policy, approved by Resolution 17/2018, aims at widespread adoption of ICT; the statement names no change to it.

Not found. No report against the policy's own targets has been found, and the Operational Plan that carries its actions is not held. Nothing dated in the past three years says which body is responsible for the policy or how it is financed.

MRT.short: A sector policy declaration was adopted in January 2013; no source found says whether its text is public and whether it is still in force.
MRT.summary:
Governance and finance. The ministry's presentation, published in April 2019, names better regulation of the sector as one of the declaration's four pillars.

Standing. The Déclaration de politique sectorielle is adopted: the ministry's presentation states that a new sector policy declaration was adopted in January 2013.

Text. The ministry's presentation gives the declaration's four pillars as competition and investment, consumer protection, the sector's spillovers for the economy, and better regulation.

Period. The presentation dates the declaration's adoption to January 2013.

Delivery plan. The presentation sets the declaration out as four pillars, the first of them competition and investment.

Reporting. The ministry's presentation, published in April 2019, describes the declaration as new and as adopted in January 2013.

Last twelve months. The ministry's account of the declaration dates from April 2019.

Not found. The text of the declaration is not held. Nothing gives its period, a delivery plan, a report against it, a mandated body or a budget line, and nothing on it is dated after April 2019.

MUS.short: A national ICT policy issued in 2007 ran to 2011; no source found says whether a successor is being prepared, so no stage is set.
MUS.summary: Not found. The National ICT Policy 2007-11, issued in September 2007, ended in 2011, and no successor sector policy has been found as adopted or in preparation. The National ICT Strategic Plan it relies on, any report against it and any event in the twelve months to 30 September 2026 are not held.

MWI.short: Malawi has a National ICT Policy dated 2013 with its text public; no source found says whether the 2022 draft policy was adopted.
MWI.summary:
Governance and finance. The Digital Government Strategy of September 2019 says it will assist the Ministry of Information in implementing the targets in the National ICT Policy.

Standing. The National ICT Policy 2013 is listed in the policy framework of a 2025 management plan for the government data centre. A UNCDF scan of May 2023 calls it outdated and in need of updating, and the Presidential Delivery Unit produced a draft National ICT and Digitalization Policy in 2022.

Text. An essay of March 2026 links a copy of the 2013 policy's text in the ITU national strategies repository.

Period. The 2022 draft is titled 2022-2026.

Delivery plan. The Digital Government Strategy of 2019 lists an action to update the National ICT Policy, owned by the Ministry of Information and the Department of E-Government.

Reporting. The same strategy says the government carried out an ICT sector review during 2013-2017.

Last twelve months. A GSMA report of August 2026 lists the National ICT Policy 2013 among the prior policies on which current digital strategies build.

Not found. No source found reports the act and date that adopted the National ICT Policy 2013, and no period is given for it. No delivery plan of the policy and no report against it has been found, nothing on its governance is dated within three years, and no source found says whether the 2022 draft was validated or adopted.

NAM.short: Namibia launched a national ICT policy in January 2026; no source found reports its text, end year, delivery plan and budget.
NAM.summary:
Governance and finance. The National ICT Policy 2026 sets out clear roles for the institutions responsible for implementing and monitoring ICT development, The Namibian reported in January 2026.

Standing. The Ministry of ICT launched the policy at Opuwo in January 2026. It follows the Overarching ICT Policy 2009, which the National Broadband Policy gazetted on 14 August 2020 says it is built on, and the National ICT Policy / Broadband Policy, which the ITU's repository lists among Namibia's strategies.

Text. The Namibian reported the policy's launch on 29 January 2026.

Period. The minister said at the launch that the policy would guide the ICT sector over the next five years. The ITU's repository gives the earlier National ICT Policy / Broadband Policy a time frame of 2018 to 2022.

Delivery plan. The 2026 policy gives institutions their roles in implementing ICT development.

Reporting. For the earlier National ICT Policy / Broadband Policy, the ITU's repository records training programmes as evidence of implementation.

Last twelve months. The ICT minister launched the policy in January 2026.

Not found. The text of the National ICT Policy 2026 is not held, and nothing found links to it or quotes it from an official site. Its period has no end year, and no delivery plan, report against it or budget line is on record.

NER.short: A telecommunications and ICT sector policy was adopted in 2013 and ended in 2020; no successor sector policy is known, so no stage is set.
NER.summary: Not found. The Document de politique sectorielle des télécommunications et des TIC 2013-2020 ended in 2020, and no successor sector policy has been found as adopted or in preparation; an update was instructed in July 2017 and no updated policy has been found. Nothing is held on the policy's text, on a mandated body or its finance, or on any event in the twelve months to 30 September 2026.

NGA.short: Nigeria's telecommunications policy of 2000 is still in force and is being rewritten in 2026; no source reports its finance and reporting against its targets.
NGA.summary:
Governance and finance. The National Telecommunications Policy 2000 assigns policy formulation to the Ministry of Communications and regulation to the Nigerian Communications Commission, and sets up a National Frequency Management Council in the Ministry.

Standing. The Minister of Communications' preface of May 2000 presents the policy as approved by the President, and the Commission's consultation paper of 9 February 2026 calls it the subsisting sector policy, in force for twenty-five years.

Text. The Ministry of Communications published the full text, in seventeen chapters, in May 2000.

Period. The consultation paper states no end date for the policy, whose Chapter 16 provides for review from time to time.

Delivery plan. The consultation paper proposes to add an implementation matrix with milestones, dependencies and responsible parties, which the 2000 text does not have.

Reporting. Chapter 16 of the policy names annual reports among its three implementation instruments, beside implementation machinery and a national forum.

Last twelve months. In February 2026 the Commission published fifteen proposals for rewriting the policy and invited comments by 20 March 2026, and in May 2026 it held a review workshop with regulators, operators and investors.

Not found. No report against the policy's own targets has been found, and no source of finance is stated. The committees set up to review the policy belong to the rewrite, which is still being drafted and has not replaced the 2000 text.

RWA.short: Rwanda has an ICT sector plan for 2024-2029, published in 2025; no source found says whether results against it have been reported.
RWA.summary:
Governance and finance. The ICT Sector Strategic Plan 2024-2029 commits the Ministry of ICT and Innovation and its affiliated agencies to deliver its programmes. The ministry convened the sector working group's review of the plan under the finance ministry's guidance on 22 November 2024.

Standing. The ministry published the plan, dated 1 January 2025 on its cover, as one it is committed to implement. A sector review of 22 November 2024 was convened to validate it.

Text. The plan is a PDF on the ministry's own site.

Period. The plan covers the financial years 2024/25 to 2028/29. The plan before it covered 2018-2024.

Delivery plan. The plan's contents list an implementation plan and a section on cost and financing, with budget allocated across priority areas. The November 2024 review sets out its targets, among them 1.5 million citizens trained in coding and ICT skills and 50,000 digital jobs.

Reporting. The sector review for 2023/24 reports against the 2018-2024 plan, and put digitised public services at 91% against a target of 100% by 2024.

Last twelve months. After a cabinet briefing on 24 July 2026 the ministry set 30 June 2027 as the date 3G is switched off nationwide, as part of the plan.

Not found. No report, review or evaluation of results against the 2024-2029 plan's own targets is held. No source ties a domestic budget line to the plan, and its costing is known from the contents list only, with no figures.

SDN.short: The National ICT Strategy 2021-2025 ended in 2025; no source found says whether a successor is being prepared, so no stage is set.
SDN.summary: Not found. The National ICT Strategy 2021-2025 ran to 2025, and nothing found records a successor sector policy announced, in drafting or validated. No text, delivery plan or date of adoption has been found, and nothing is dated in the last twelve months.

SEN.short: Senegal validated a sector policy letter for 2025-2029 in February 2025; no source found says whether it has been adopted.
SEN.summary:
Governance and finance. The secretary general of the ministry chaired the final validation workshop for the Lettre de politique sectorielle 2025-2029 in February 2025.

Standing. The Lettre de politique sectorielle 2025-2029 is validated: the final validation workshop with the sector's actors was reported on 10 February 2025, and terms of reference dated July 2026 say the Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital has validated it.

Text. The terms of reference of July 2026 refer to the letter as the ministry's validated sector policy.

Period. The letter covers 2025 to 2029.

Delivery plan. The letter is tied to the National Development Strategy 2025-2029, as the terms of reference of July 2026 state.

Reporting. The terms of reference of July 2026 record the letter as validated by the ministry.

Last twelve months. Terms of reference of July 2026 state that the letter has been validated; the validation workshop was reported in February 2025.

Not found. No adoption of the letter is on record. Its text, a delivery plan, a report against it, a mandated body, a budget line and any dated event in the twelve months to 30 September 2026 are not held.

SLE.short: The 2009 ICT policy, reviewed in 2017, was replaced in 2021 by a national digital policy; no successor is known, so no stage is set.
SLE.summary: Not found. No sector policy is in force: the National ICT Policy approved on 28 October 2009 and reviewed in 2017 was replaced in 2021 by the National Digital Development Policy, and no sector successor has been found as adopted or in preparation. No report against the 2009 policy and no budget line for it have been found, and nothing is dated inside the last twelve months.

SOM.short: A National ICT Policy and Strategy for 2025-2029 was reported approved in 2025; no source found says whether its text is published.
SOM.summary:
Governance and finance. The Ministry of Communications and Technology published a notice on 11 November 2025 for a consultant firm to prepare the National ICT Policy and Strategy 2025-2029. The consultancy is paid from an IDA grant under the Regional Digital Integration Project.

Standing. The minister told the WSIS+20 forum on 9 July 2025 that the Council of Ministers approved the National ICT Policy earlier in 2025. The notice of 11 November 2025 seeks a firm to renew the 2019-2024 policy as a 2025-2029 one, over about four months.

Text. The ministry published the full text of the National ICT Policy and Strategy 2019-2024 on its own site.

Period. The notice gives the new policy's period as 2025 to 2029, after one the Cabinet adopted on 28 November 2019 for 2019 to 2024.

Delivery plan. The 2019-2024 policy set a table of actions and targets, each with a year of delivery, and left the cost of each line to be determined.

Reporting. In August 2025 the minister said the Starlink launch supports the goals of the 2019-2024 policy.

Last twelve months. Expressions of interest for the consultancy were due on 29 November 2025.

Not found. The text of the 2025-2029 policy, a delivery plan for it and any report against its targets. The minister's statement of July 2025 and the notice of November 2025 differ on whether the policy is approved or still to be written. No domestic budget line is stated.

SSD.short: A national ICT policy published in 2012 is public and was said in 2025 to be in implementation; its period, plan and results are unknown.
SSD.summary:
Governance and finance. The minister of ICT and postal services spoke for the policy at the 30th EACO Assemblies in Juba, reported in June 2025.

Standing. The Government of South Sudan published its National ICT Policy in 2012 as a government policy statement. In June 2025 the minister said the government is implementing the revised ICT Policy of 2012.

Text. The policy text is public on the ICT Policy Africa document page as a government publication.

Period. The policy is dated 2012.

Delivery plan. The text sets sector policy for posts, telecommunications and information technology.

Reporting. The minister's June 2025 statement that the policy is being implemented gave no figure or measure against the policy's targets.

Last twelve months. The latest statement on the policy is the minister's, published on 12 June 2025.

Not found. The policy's period, a delivery plan, a mandated body, a budget line and any report against its own targets are not held, and nor is an adopting act: the 2012 date is the publisher's. Nothing is dated in the twelve months to 30 September 2026.

STP.short: An ICT sector strategy was prepared in 2012 and was still awaiting adoption in June 2015; no source found says whether it was ever adopted.
STP.summary:
Governance and finance. The ICT Sector Strategy was prepared in 2012 under the Central African Backbone project, which the World Bank financed; the programme as a whole carried an IDA grant of SDR 9.8 million.

Standing. The strategy was prepared in 2012 after wide consultation with stakeholders. In June 2015 its adoption by the Council of Ministers was still pending.

Text. The World Bank's completion report on the project, prepared in June 2015, names the strategy as prepared and not yet adopted.

Period. The strategy dates from 2012, the year it was prepared.

Delivery plan. The strategy was itself a product of the Central African Backbone project, prepared under it in 2012.

Reporting. The World Bank's completion report of June 2015 records the strategy as awaiting adoption by the Council of Ministers.

Last twelve months. In June 2015 the strategy was still waiting for the Council of Ministers to adopt it, three years after it was prepared.

Not found. Whether the strategy was adopted, dropped or replaced after June 2015. No text, period, delivery plan or report on it has been found, and nothing is dated within the last twelve months.

SWZ.short: Eswatini has an ICT infrastructure policy adopted in 2006 with no end year; no source found reports its delivery plan and reporting.
SWZ.summary:
Governance and finance. Cabinet adopted the National Information and Communication Infrastructure (NICI) Policy in August 2006.

Standing. The policy is adopted. A stakeholder validation workshop endorsed the draft ICT policy in January 2006, and Cabinet adopted it that August as what the document calls the Swaziland National Information and Communication Infrastructure (NICI) Policy.

Text. The government site gov.sz hosts the policy as a PDF, in one file with its Implementation Plan 2012-2016. The document's published date is 1 August 2006.

Period. The policy is published with an Implementation Plan covering 2012 to 2016.

Delivery plan. The Implementation Plan 2012-2016 sits in the same document as the policy on the government site.

Reporting. The policy document records its own adoption in 2006 and its launch in 2007.

Last twelve months. The Prime Minister launched the policy on 3 August 2007.

Not found. No period of the policy's own has been found: the only one on record, to 2016, is the Implementation Plan's. No adopted delivery plan, no report against the policy, no body or budget in the last three years and nothing dated in the last twelve months is held.

SYC.short: Seychelles has a National ICT Policy from 2007 with its text public; no source found says whether it has a delivery plan or reports results.
SYC.summary:
Governance and finance. The National ICT Policy 2007 carries a foreword by the Minister for National Development and sets five focus areas: infrastructure, the legal and regulatory framework, human resources, industry and government.

Standing. The policy is published as the National ICT Policy for Seychelles, and a World Bank report of September 2026 treats it as in force.

Text. The full text is on the SCRA website as a PDF.

Period. The policy states no end year or period; it sets a vision and policy statements.

Delivery plan. The policy says it lays the foundation for a later National ICT Strategic Plan.

Reporting. The World Bank's Seychelles Country Growth and Jobs Report says digital skills are a core pillar of the policy.

Last twelve months. In September 2026 the World Bank named the policy beside the National Development Strategy (2024-2028) as carrying digital skills.

Not found. No delivery plan and no report against the policy has been found, and nothing on a mandated body or a budget line in the last three years. The policy document is undated: 2007 is the date it is recorded as published, and the World Bank report gives no adoption date or scope.

TCD.short: A sector ICT plan adopted in 2017 ended in 2021; no source found says whether a successor is being prepared, so no stage is set.
TCD.summary: Not found. No sector policy is on record as following the Plan Tchad Numérique 2017-2021, adopted or in preparation. No text, delivery plan, report, mandated body, finance or event in the last twelve months is held for that plan, the NICI plan 2007-2027 or the 1997 sector policy declaration.

TGO.short: A digital economy sector policy declaration of 2017 ran to 2022; no source says whether a successor is being prepared, so no stage is set.
TGO.summary: Not found. The Déclaration de politique du secteur de l'économie numérique 2018-2022, adopted in October 2017, reached the end of its period in 2022, and no successor sector policy has been found as adopted or in preparation. Its text, delivery plan and finance are not held, nor is any report against it; the one fact on its steering bodies dates from 2017, and no event in the twelve months to 30 September 2026 has been found.

TUN.short: Tunisia has a national digital strategy but no ICT or telecommunications sector policy has been found, so no stage is set.
TUN.summary: Not found. No ICT or telecommunications sector policy has been found as adopted or in preparation. The instruments held are national digital strategies, a ministry's annual performance plan and a programme, none of which is a sector policy.

TZA.short: Tanzania adopted its National ICT Policy in 2016 and a costed strategy ran to 2020/21; no source found says whether the 2023 review was adopted.
TZA.summary:
Governance and finance. The ICT Commission, under the Ministry of ICT, has the role of ensuring the National ICT Policy is implemented, a November 2024 case study states. The policy's December 2016 implementation strategy names the Government budget, development partners and the private sector as its financing sources.

Standing. The National ICT Policy 2016 was signed by the Minister for Works, Transport and Communication in May 2016 as the Government's revision of the 2003 policy. A June 2025 report cites it as the country's ICT policy. The ministry issued a successor text dated June 2023, which states no adoption date.

Text. The full policy is published as a PDF on the ministry's website.

Period. The policy's implementation strategy covers 2016/17 to 2020/21.

Delivery plan. The strategy estimates that Tsh. 248.2 billion is required over its five years, with a logframe of 22 objectives giving targets, indicators, time frames and responsible institutions.

Reporting. The June 2023 successor text says the ministry will design a monitoring and evaluation system and evaluate after five years.

Last twelve months. In August 2026 The Citizen reported the ICT Commission's director general describing the 2016 policy as the one that followed the 2003 policy.

Not found. The 2016 policy's own period, any report of results against its targets, and a budget line tied to it in the past three years. No source found says whether the 2023 successor text has been adopted.

UGA.short: Uganda has a National ICT Policy of 2014, with a replacement drafted in 2022; no source found says whether the 2014 text is public.
UGA.summary:
Governance and finance. The Ministry of ICT and National Guidance's report for the fourth quarter of 2021/22 shows its E-Services department running the drafting and Cabinet submission of a replacement National ICT Policy, on an output that also covers the National Cyber Security Strategy.

Standing. The Vision for a Digital Uganda 2040, of September 2022, lists the National ICT Policy 2014 among Uganda's key policies, as being reviewed. The final draft of its replacement, dated May 2022, names it among the key policies of the sector's current policy environment.

Text. The final draft of the replacement is online on the website of the consultant who prepared it.

Period. A case study of August 2024 describes Uganda's policy environment as starting with the National ICT Policy of 2003.

Delivery plan. The 2022 draft carries no implementation plan and says the ministry will develop a road map to inform an implementation matrix.

Reporting. The ministry's report of June 2022 says drafting of the replacement was complete and awaiting Cabinet approval. The Ministry of Finance's monitoring report for 2022/23 says stakeholder engagement was finalised, pending submission to the Cabinet Secretariat.

Last twelve months. Terms of reference issued by NITA-U in August 2026 cite a "Draft National ICT Policy, 2022" for the ICT sector's share of GDP.

Not found. No text of the National ICT Policy 2014 has been found, and nothing gives its period, a delivery plan or a report against it. No adoption of the 2022 draft is on record, and nothing dated since 2023 says where it stands.

ZAF.short: South Africa adopted an ICT policy white paper in 2016, and no source says whether it has a delivery plan or reports against its targets.
ZAF.summary:
Governance and finance. In 2019/20 the Department of Telecommunications and Postal Services developed ICT policy and legislation for the sector through its Programme 3, ICT Policy Research and Capacity Development.

Standing. The Department issued the National Integrated ICT Policy White Paper in Government Gazette 40325 of 3 October 2016.

Text. The White Paper is published as a gazette file on gov.za and on the department's website, dcdt.gov.za.

Period. The White Paper's stated main purpose is to unlock ICTs to eliminate poverty and reduce inequality by 2030.

Delivery plan. In 2019/20 the Department pursued its legislative programme in line with the White Paper.

Reporting. The Department's 2019/20 annual report records, against the indicator "ICT legislation and policies in line with the White Paper", that the Digital Development Fund Bill, the Data and Cloud Policy and a framing document for the White Paper's review were developed.

Last twelve months. A World Bank report of June 2026 lists the White Paper among the key anchors of South Africa's policy framework, and a discussion document on universal access of October 2026 lists it as a policy instrument.

Not found. No delivery plan for the White Paper has been found, and no report against its own targets. No source found says how the policy is financed and what came of the review framed in 2019/20.

ZMB.short: Zambia has a National ICT Policy published in 2023 with no end year; no source found says whether results against it have been reported.
ZMB.summary:
Governance and finance. The National ICT Policy 2023 makes the ministry responsible for ICTs answerable for coordinating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating it, with ZICTA regulating the sector. It lists the national budget among seven possible sources of finance and states no budget line or amount.

Standing. The Ministry of Technology and Science published the policy on 11 October 2023 as the government's revision of the National ICT Policy 2006. In December 2025 the policy working group of an ITU event in Lusaka recognised it as the overarching framework governing ICTs in Zambia.

Text. The full text is on the ministry's website as a PDF.

Period. The policy states no end year. It is anchored on Vision 2030 and sets no term of its own.

Delivery plan. A ZDA sector profile of September 2024 says the 2022 to 2026 ICT Policy Implementation Plan lists seventeen investment actions, among them district fibre, a national internet exchange point, regional data centres and rural Wi-Fi, with no costs given.

Reporting. The policy gives monitoring and evaluation of its implementation to the ministry and the Cabinet Office.

Last twelve months. On 12 November 2025 the Ministry of Community Development and Social Services launched guidelines it said were aligned with the policy, TechAfrica News reports.

Not found. No report, review or evaluation against the policy's targets, and no adoption date beyond the text's publication. The implementation plan carries no costs and no budget line is tied to the policy.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe has a public National ICT Policy for 2022 to 2027 with an uncosted action plan; no source found reports results against its targets.
ZWE.summary:
Governance and finance. The 2022 text of the National ICT Policy 2022-2027 names the Ministry of ICT, Postal and Courier Services as coordinator, with a National ICT Policy Advisory Council led by the Minister and a Policy Implementation Secretariat, and ties no budget line or amount to the policy.

Standing. The policy carries a presidential foreword and replaces the policy of 2016-2020, the ICT minister launched it on 7 March 2024, and Cabinet's briefing of 14 July 2026 names it among the frameworks of the national digital agenda.

Text. The full text of the policy, published in 2022, is public.

Period. The policy titles itself for 2022 to 2027, and an article of November 2025 gives it the same period.

Delivery plan. The policy's implementation plan sets out actions by priority area, with responsible bodies and periods from 2023 to 2027, and states no costs.

Reporting. The 2022 text gives the Policy Implementation Secretariat the task of tracking implementation.

Last twelve months. Cabinet named the policy on 14 July 2026, and on 20 July 2026 the head of the statistics agency referred to an ICT Policy for 2026 to 2030.

Not found. No report, review or evaluation against the policy's targets has been found, and no adopting act is named. The policy's bodies and finance are known only from the 2022 text, and nothing found gives the standing or text of the ICT Policy 2026-2030.

AGO.short: A third of the population or more held a national ID in 2025.
AGO.summary:
Share holding an ID. Secretary of State for Justice Osvaldo Amaro said only 16,297,777 citizens hold the Bilhete de Identidade in a country of about 35 million inhabitants, about half the population. It is the only fact held on the subject: no news story or official notice read for this study says more about it, the documents the earlier cell cited were not read, and the systems themselves were not examined.

Everyone holds one. No source found since October 2023 counts 99.9% of the population or more holding a national ID. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

Births and deaths registered. No source found since October 2023 puts birth registration at all births and deaths at 80% or more. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

Not found. No source found since October 2023 says: do two-thirds hold one.

The World Bank says more than 7.7 million people have their NPI as of the end of May 2025, about 52% of the 14.8 million population (divided by the population given, not stated in the document). The WURI-Benin coordinator reports more than 13.41 million people enrolled, stated as 98% of the 2026 population projection.

ETH.short: A third of the population or more held a national ID in 2026.
ETH.summary:
Share holding an ID. The Ethiopia National ID Program reports 49.1 million Fayda enrolments as of 24 August 2026, about 36% of Ethiopia's 135.5 million people (share computed from the held population figure). Ethiopia's national digital ID system is nearing 50 million registrations per the government announcement; against the 135.5 million population given that is about 37%, calculated here, and unaudited. Fayda has recorded more than 52 million registrations as of 9 October 2026 (Biometric Update); against a population of 135.5 million that is about 38 percent (share computed by us).

GAB.short: Fewer than a third of the population held a national ID in 2026.
GAB.summary:

Membership and adoption. Togo's standards body is the Agence Togolaise de Normalisation. ISO's member register lists it as a member body, the full class of membership, on a page read in September 2026. The entry places the agency under the ministry for the promotion of investment, in Lomé, and gives its postal address and telephone numbers. It names no international standard on information technology or data that Togo has adopted as a national one.

Requirement and standard-setting. The register entry gives the agency's membership and its address. A hosting company's information security certificate, announced in March 2026 for its operations in seven countries, Togo among them, is listed below. The announcement does not name the body that issued the certificate.

Not found. No source found names an international standard on information technology or data adopted as a national standard.

TUN.short: Tunisia's standards body, INNORPI, was an ISO member body in 2026; no international standard on information technology or data adopted nationally is known.
TUN.summary:
Membership and adoption. Tunisia's standards body is INNORPI, which sits under the Ministry of Industry, Energy and SMEs. ISO's registry entry, read on 16 October 2026, lists INNORPI as Tunisia's ISO member body. INNORPI also publishes the national standards bulletin, the Officiel de la Normalisation, in which a public inquiry appeared in May 2026, so the member body is active in national standard-setting.

Requirement and standard-setting. The nearest held fact is the same registry entry: ISO lists INNORPI as the member body for Tunisia in 2026, and it names no committee work or rule for public bodies. National standardisation is governed by a 2009 law on the national standardisation system, which is the legal frame within which a requirement on public bodies or committee work could sit.

Not found. No source found names an international standard on information technology or data adopted as a national standard.

TZA.summary:
Membership and adoption. Tanzania's standards body is the Tanzania Bureau of Standards. ISO's member page lists the bureau as a member body of ISO, on a page dated 2026. In February 2025 the bureau's own letterhead described it as a member of ISO and as an agent for ISO. No source found names an international standard on information technology or data that the country has adopted as a national standard, so the membership is the whole of what is held on this aspect.

Requirement and standard-setting. The same ISO page shows the bureau as a participating member of 42 ISO technical committees and as an observing member of 148 others. The page does not say which of these committees deal with information technology or data, so the seats are not counted as standard-setting in that field.

UGA.short: Uganda's 2026 information security policy requires public bodies to comply with the international information security standard; no source found reports its part in writing such standards.
UGA.summary:
Membership and adoption. The Uganda National Bureau of Standards notified its work programme for January to June 2026 to the ISO/IEC Information Centre, under the World Trade Organization's code of good practice for standards bodies. The programme lists the Ugandan standards the bureau planned to develop in that half-year.

Requirement and standard-setting. The National Information Technology Authority's National Information Security Policy 2026, launched on 15 July 2026, describes itself as setting mandatory requirements for ministries, departments, agencies and local governments. It says cloud services, programming interfaces, artificial intelligence and industrial control systems must be deployed and managed in compliance with ISO/IEC 27001:2022, the international standard on information security management, and that organisations must apply the ISA/IEC 62443 standards to industrial control systems. The minister launched the policy with its framework.

Not found. No source from the last three years naming the standards body or a public body as a participating member, chair or secretariat of an ISO or IEC committee on information technology or data is held. No source found states the standards bureau's membership of ISO, or names an international standard adopted as a Ugandan one.

ZAF.short: South Africa's standards body took part in the international information technology standards committee in 2026; no source found says whether it adopts those standards nationally.
ZAF.summary:
Membership and adoption. South Africa's standards body is the South African Bureau of Standards, known as SABS. ISO's membership page lists SABS as participating in ISO/IEC JTC 1, the joint committee on information technology, as of 2026. The same page shows it taking part in the subcommittees on information security (SC 27), biometrics (SC 37) and artificial intelligence (SC 42), three fields that bear directly on government data and digital systems.

Requirement and standard-setting. SABS sits in the working structure where these standards are written: its 2026 participation in JTC 1 and the subcommittees on information security, biometrics and artificial intelligence gives South Africa a place in drafting international standards on information technology. The same page names those subcommittees and does not list any national standard that SABS has adopted from them or any rule requiring public bodies to meet one.

Not found. Nothing found says whether South Africa has adopted an international standard on information technology or data as a national standard, or requires public bodies to meet one.

AGO.short: In 2024, 55.5 per cent of the population used the internet, by the country's own figure.
AGO.summary:
Share of people who use the internet, with its year. INACOM, Angola's communications regulator, reports 55.5% of individuals using the internet in 2024 (indicator HH8); no age range is given. That leaves 44.5 per cent offline. The International Telecommunication Union's series put the share at 34.6 per cent in 2021, 35.8 per cent in 2022, 37.9 per cent in 2023 and 40.7 per cent in 2024. The share is past half and 24.5 points short of 80 per cent, which is four in five. The figure counts a person once, whatever the number of subscriptions they hold, and counts anyone who used the internet in the last three months, from any place and on any device. INACOM reports 48.8% of individuals using the internet in 2023 (indicator HH8); no age range is given. INACOM reports 42.1% of individuals using the internet in 2022 (indicator HH8); no age range is given.

The Instituto de Modernização Administrativa's terms of reference of February 2026 say a seven-month study with 25 public institutions produced a Framework and Roadmap of Interoperability, with organisational, semantic, technical and infrastructure guidelines and a phased roadmap. A regional progress report says the institute completed the framework study and its platform roadmap in the first half of 2026, as the basis for buying the interoperability platform. Neither names an instrument adopting it.

Required and followed. The same study found that 27% of systems across the 25 institutions were interconnected, mostly point to point, with fragmented governance and no common standards. The document names no decree making the framework compulsory. It gives no date by which the framework is to be adopted.

The work is in phase 2, to follow once the deliverables of phase 1 are validated, and the notice states that no drafting had begun.

It describes the Government Interoperability Framework and the interoperability strategy that would set its standards and protocols as still to be developed, in phase 2, which follows once the deliverables of phase 1 are validated. The notice states that no drafting had begun on that date, 3 May 2024.

BEN.short: Benin's interoperability framework, instituted by decree in 2020, governed more than 120 connected systems in 2025; no source names who enforces it.
BEN.summary:

The Cadre d'interopérabilité, published by the state digital agency, is instituted by decree 2020-209 of 18 March 2020 and sets four levels, juridical, organisational, semantic and technical, and five common infrastructure components. A new architecture policy for state information systems, setting principles, technical rules and standards to make public systems interoperable, went to sectoral consultation in Cotonou on 30 June 2026.

Required and followed. The agency's legal note of July 2026 treats the framework as in place. It sets the registration, technical and contractual conditions for connecting to the national exchange platform. A national interoperability committee supervises. In May 2025 Benin told ID4Africa that the exchange platform runs under its interoperability framework. More than 120 systems had been integrated through it.

Not found. No source found names the body that enforces the framework.

In May 2026 the government told the World Health Assembly that its regulatory framework includes the general interoperability framework, beside a personal data protection law; the statement does not say who must follow it or who does.

The Act comes into force by ministerial order. A European Union-funded project running from August 2024 to August 2027 is working with the government to improve and align the National Interoperability Framework, its standards, guidelines and tools.

Required and followed. The project lists a harmonised and operational national interoperability framework for e-government services as an expected result, to be reached by 2027. The Act does not say the exchange framework has been issued. No public body is reported as bound by either text yet.

CIV.summary:

Decree 2021-913 of 22 December 2021 adopts the Référentiel Général d'Interopérabilité des Systèmes d'Information, annexed to it, as the general framework of technical rules for the interoperability of information systems. The annex lists the standards that are recommended, those under observation and those at the end of their life.

Required and followed. The decree was made on the joint report of the ministers for the digital economy and for the public service, who are charged with carrying it out.
