On 3 September 2026 the Head of the Local Government Service presented a programme his office calls LITISIP to give the 261 metropolitan, municipal and district assemblies a secure digital backbone.

What the office does over it. The minister said in February 2024 that the network gives the connected agencies, the assemblies among them, faster communication and access to government shared services. The Ministry of Finance's budget guidelines of 29 August 2025 carry instructions to the assemblies with a part on GIFMIS, the national financial management system.

How the office is connected. The minister said in February 2024 that the network connects government agencies, the assemblies included, by fibre backbone, last-mile fibre and microwave links with satellite backup, on a 10-year indefeasible right of use. At a signing reported on 3 September 2026 the Head of the Local Government Service described the state the Service is moving from as "disconnected offices".

Last twelve months. The Local Government Service signed a memorandum of understanding with Celltel Networks, reported on 3 September 2026, with improved connectivity of local government offices among its expected results.

Local governments connected. The minister's table of February 2024 gives the assemblies 274 of 274 planned sites connected, within 950 of 951 government sites.

Not found. How many of the 261 assemblies the 274 connected sites cover, and how many assembly offices are without a connection in 2026. What LITISIP costs, who pays for it and when it is due, and which systems assembly staff work in over the network.

GIN.short: Commune registry staff worked in a national civil-registration system in 2026, with rural offices on paper; no source found says how many communes are connected.
GIN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Enabel, the Belgian development agency, issued the tender of 27 July 2022 for the internet connection of 10 pilot communes, the notice citing Belgium's bilateral portfolio of EUR 45 million for 2019 to 2023.

What the office does over it. The delegated civil-registry officer of Ratoma commune said, as reported on 2 September 2026, that his office goes on registering births in the digital civil-registration system, which runs from a data centre held elsewhere. Enabel's final evaluation, from fieldwork in April 2026, says civil-status officers and data-entry agents at civil registry centres work in the national civil register's central database, which it calls E-RENEC, with paper still in use in parallel. A policy brief of November 2025 says weak connectivity, high data costs and low digital literacy force rural municipal offices onto manual reporting and paper records.

How the office is connected. That tender was for a service contract for the internet connection of 10 communes, closing on 17 August 2022.

Last twelve months. The relocation of the system's data centre from the Maison centrale disrupted the service to commune offices, on top of a stockout of secure paper lasting about two weeks, as reported on 2 September 2026.

Local governments connected. The tender of 2022 names the 10 pilot communes: the 5 of Conakry, Kassa, Coyah, Kindia, Mamou and Tolo. The evaluation describes E-RENEC as the product of a pilot project and recommends a maturity diagnosis before any national extension.

Not found. Whether the internet connection tendered for the 10 pilot communes in 2022 was delivered, how commune offices are connected today, and how many communes work in the civil-registration system. Who owns and pays for the connection since 2022, and how many rural offices are without one.

GMB.short: All councils had the government's finance system by late 2024 and most used it; capped because no current plan or budget line is known.
GMB.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The rollout of IFMIS, the government's Integrated Financial Management Information System, to the councils is a reform of the Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs, with the system run by the Accountant General's Department. In 2024 it was the first component of the local government pillar of the Public Financial Management Strategy 2021-2025. The ministry's report for the second and third quarters of 2025 says the government lacks funds for a localised IFMIS.

What the office does over it. Most councils were actively using IFMIS in 2024, on the ministry's report. In the second and third quarters of 2025 Kuntaur Area Council was posting live in it and Basse Area Council used it for its accounting.

How the office is connected. By late 2024 Janjanbureh and Kuntaur area councils had working internet connections reaching most of their offices and Banjul City Council had a 100 Mbps connection, the ministry reported. In the second and third quarters of 2025 internet speed and connectivity remained problems at Brikama Area Council.

Last twelve months. The ministry's report for the second and third quarters of 2025 has Kuntaur extending internet across its offices and Brikama installing IFMIS for all its users.

Local governments connected. IFMIS had been implemented in all Local Government Area Councils by the end of 2024, on the ministry's report, which names eight councils. Its report for the second and third quarters of 2025 describes IFMIS in use or being installed at four of them.

Not found. No share of councils connected has been found after 2024, no rural share, and no plan covering 2026 or domestic budget line for the councils' connections. Whether IFMIS works at Kanifing is not held: its mayor said in August 2026 that it had not for two years, and the Accountant General's Department disputes that.

GNB.short: No sector administration, nor the Bissau municipal chamber, is known to have an office connection in 2026, so no stage is set.
GNB.summary: Not found. Nothing found puts a sector administration or the Bissau municipal chamber on a connection. No local elections have been held, and the documents found concern the national backbone.

GNQ.short: In 2024 the government's network did not reach local government offices, which worked largely on manual systems; no source found says whether any has another connection.
GNQ.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The World Bank's digital economy diagnostic of 2024 describes a central network of the government, partly hosted by CNIAPGE. It puts manual working at the local level down to a want of funds and adequate infrastructure.

What the office does over it. The diagnostic states that many ministries at the centre operate on manual systems, and that this is more pronounced at the local level. Data pass between ministries by hand, USB drive or e-mail.

How the office is connected. In 2024 the World Bank stated that the government's central network does not extend to local government branches.

Last twelve months. On 18 December 2025 Gabon's Council of Ministers approved an agreement to interconnect the fibre-optic networks of Gabon and Equatorial Guinea, which are the two countries' national networks.

Local governments connected. The World Bank's statement of 2024 is about local government branches as a whole, which the central network does not reach.

Not found. Whether a local government office holds any connection other than the government's central network, and how many local governments there are to connect. No owner, plan or finance for connecting them, and no event in the twelve months to 30 September 2026.

KEN.short: All 47 counties were on the government network by 2017 and work in national systems; no source found says how many county offices are connected.
KEN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy presents the County Connectivity Project as its own, with two further phases started in 2022. The ICT Authority's plan for 2024 to 2027 states that county governments have not prioritised ICT investment and rely on national government initiatives for their connectivity.

What the office does over it. The Controller of Budget's review of the year to 30 June 2026, as the Daily Nation reports it, has county governments processing payroll in the national Human Resource Information System, which Kenya calls HRIS-Ke, with at least Sh8.3 billion in salaries still paid by manual payroll outside it. The National Treasury's draft payment policy of August 2026 says the Central Bank rolled out internet banking for county governments.

How the office is connected. The ministry states that the counties were connected by secure connections into the national private governmental voice and data network, which it calls NOFBI, the last of them by 2017.

Last twelve months. On 25 August 2026 the National Treasury's Cabinet Secretary announced that all 47 county governments must finish integrating the national electronic procurement platform with its financial management system by 30 September 2026. In the year to June 2026 counties cited connectivity challenges among their reasons for manual payroll.

Local governments connected. The ministry states that Phase I, in 2012 and 2013, connected 28 counties and Nairobi, and Phase 2, completed in 2017, the remaining 18 of the 47 it names.

Not found. The share of county government offices connected: the ministry's 47 of 47 counts counties, and nothing since 2017 gives a figure. Where the staff working in the national systems sit, how those offices are connected, and any plan, finance or connection event dated in the twelve months to 30 September 2026.

LBR.short: A 2019 policy targeted internet access at every county Superintendent office; no source found says whether any is connected, so no stage is set.
LBR.summary: Not found. Whether any county Superintendent office is connected, how, what it does over the connection and how many are. The one target on record, internet access at every Superintendent office, belongs to the national ICT policy for 2019-2024, and no dated statement that the offices lack a connection has been found.

LBY.short: The mayors of 21 municipalities were given access to the ministry's online systems in October 2025; no source found says how many municipal offices are connected.
LBY.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Local Government's digital transformation project director said on 2 November 2023 that official e-mail accounts would be created for the heads of administrative units in the municipalities, inside the ministry's electronic correspondence system, to replace paper correspondence. The system is the ministry's own, run under its digital transformation project.

What the office does over it. In the three local authorities studied by Wynn, Bakeer and Forti, published in 2021, the information systems are isolated in-house or third-party systems on departmental networks, and data is exchanged on paper. Sabratha's finance department uses online services occasionally, to display and update information on the authority's website.

How the office is connected. The study finds internet access at the authorities' offices that is slow, often disconnected or not always available. Sabratha's finance department has fifteen networked computers and an internet connection that is often disconnected, and in Rujban the internet is normally unavailable in community services and unreliable in human resources.

Last twelve months. In October 2025 the ministry gave the mayors of 21 municipalities access to its electronic systems.

Local governments connected. The 2021 study covers three local authorities, Misurata, Sabratha and Rujban, by questionnaire and interviews with eighteen officials, and concludes for the three that access to the internet was not always available. In October 2025 the mayors of 21 municipalities were given access to the ministry's electronic systems, including the local revenue system, which the ministry had launched to six municipalities in May 2022.

Not found. No total or share of Libya's municipalities with a connected office has been found, nor who provides or pays for the offices' internet. The period and the finance of the ministry's strategy are not stated, and the newest fact on the offices' own connection is of 2021.

LSO.short: Two community councils had internet installed under a pilot by 2019; no source found says whether any connection has gone beyond the pilot.
LSO.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The e-Government Project that built and connected two community council buildings is under the Ministry of Communications, Science and Technology, which handed them to the Ministry of Local Government and Chieftainship Affairs on 31 July 2019. The project is financially supported by the African Development Bank.

What the office does over it. The 31 July 2019 handover report states that the two buildings have the Internet installed. In January 2018 the secretary of Tenesolo Community Council said e-government would connect the office to internet access and to a data bank in Mohale's Hoek. In September 2025 the civil registration manager for Qacha's Nek said certificate services decentralised to councils fail without transport to carry applications to and from the district office.

How the office is connected. The Minister said on 31 July 2019 that the two buildings handed over under his ministry's project have been installed with the Internet. In January 2018 the head of the national web e-portal said council connections will use the Lesotho government data network.

Last twelve months. On 17 June 2024 the communications ministry's Principal Secretary said its plan is to roll out its 74 digital services by also connecting Community Councils.

Local governments connected. Two community councils, Dinizulu in Thaba-Tseka and Kubake in Maseru district, had the Internet installed by 31 July 2019 under the e-Government Pilot Project begun in 2014. In January 2018 the Minister said the plan is to assist in connecting all the councils.

Not found. Whether any community council beyond the two pilot ones is connected, and how many councils there are in all. What system council staff work in over the connection, and any plan period or financing since 2019.

MAR.short: A revenue system was deployed in 969 of 1,590 local authorities of all tiers by 2020; no source found says how commune offices are connected.
MAR.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Interior Ministry's directorate for local governments is responsible for the programme under which GIR-CT, Rokhas, the civil registry system and Chikaya were rolled out to participating municipalities. That programme, the Municipal Performance Program, is financed by an IBRD loan with AFD co-financing and closes on 31 December 2026.

What the office does over it. More than 100 large municipalities manage the whole local taxation chain in the Integrated Revenue Management System for Local Authorities, GIR-CT, the World Bank reported in August 2025. Rokhas, the platform for issuing building permits and commercial licences, is operational in all participating municipalities, on the Interior Ministry's information of January 2026. In October 2024 the interior minister told communes to prepare and execute their 2025 budgets in GID alone.

How the office is connected. The World Bank's identity diagnostic of 2016 reported no official statistics on computers at the roughly 2,200 commune civil registry offices, and said the municipal councils equip those offices from their own budgets.

Last twelve months. The World Bank's status report of 30 January 2026 counts 59 of 97 participating municipalities with the civil registry back-office system operational.

Local governments connected. GIR-CT was deployed in 969 of 1,590 local authorities of all tiers, 60.9 per cent, as of 19 May 2020, on the annex to the Interior Ministry's circular no. 32. Rokhas has been deployed in over 91 participating municipalities covering 16.9 million people, as of January 2026.

Not found. How commune offices are connected, and whether the state or the commune provides the connection. The share of communes working in these systems against the national total of communes, and any plan with a period.

MDG.short: About 10 per cent of communes had a secure connection to a State finance system, on a 2024 plan; no source found reports the figure's year.
MDG.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Plan National de Décentralisation Emergente 2023-2030, validated by decree on 2 August 2023, makes local governments' secure connection to the State's strategic information systems a product, with the ministries of decentralisation, digital development and finance responsible. It names no source of funds for the product's 23,092,000 thousand ariary. The April 2025 handover was made through PRODUIR, which the World Bank finances.

What the office does over it. The plan's connection indicator is communes with direct access to the Système d'Information Financière Communal (SIFC), a State information system. In December 2025, 336 communes were using the digital civil registration system SIECM. Communes of Greater Antananarivo use the ministry's online building-permit tool.

How the office is connected. The plan measures communes having a secure connection to the SIFC, and costs annual connection fees for 1,000 communes over three years. On 30 April 2025 the decentralisation ministry handed internet boxes and a subscription to all 38 communes of the Antananarivo agglomeration.

Last twelve months. The number of communes using SIECM rose from 75 to 336 in the six months to December 2025.

Local governments connected. The plan, published in June 2024, gives a baseline of 10 per cent of the country's 1,695 communes with direct access to the SIFC over a secure connection, sourced to the finance ministry, with a target of 50 per cent for 2030. The World Bank puts the 336 communes of December 2025 at 40 per cent of the project's target.

Not found. The 10 per cent baseline carries no year and is marked to be verified in the plan, and where those communes are is not stated. How the 336 communes using SIECM are connected is not stated, their count is given against a project target and not the national total, and the 38 communes handed a subscription are all in the capital's agglomeration.

MLI.short: Certain communes were connected by 2014 and a network for local governments was contracted in 2022; no source found says how many communes are connected.
MLI.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Council of Ministers of 1 June 2022 adopted a draft decree approving the contract for the Projet d'Accès au service de télécommunication des collectivités territoriales, awarded to SIMO TELECOM for CFA 9,407,295,000 over twelve months. Its communiqué states that the project is entirely financed by the Agence de Gestion du Fonds d'Accès Universel.

What the office does over it. The 2022 project is to put telecommunication infrastructure in place at the level of the collectivités territoriales and to give the Administration its own secure, autonomous network.

How the office is connected. The ministry's draft Mali Numérique 2020 strategy of November 2014 counts the connection of certain communes as a result achieved under the government's 2005 national ICT policy, beside the administration's intranet and the equipping and connection of certain schools.

Last twelve months. The contract for the collectivités' telecommunication network was approved on 1 June 2022, to run twelve months.

Local governments connected. The November 2014 strategy lists the connection of certain communes among the few results obtained under the 2005 policy.

Not found. How many communes are connected, whether any lies outside the capital, what their offices do over the connection and who pays for it are not stated. No office is said to be on the network contracted in 2022, and nothing is dated in the last twelve months.

MOZ.short: In 2026 the government network reached public institutions in 141 districts, with expansion planned; no source found says how many local government offices are connected.
MOZ.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The European Union's action document of June 2026 describes GovNet as the government's own network, with INAGE, the national e-government institute, managing e-government platforms and data centres. Its 2026 action plans to expand GovNet in selected districts, in support of the national Internet for All 2030 strategy, at a total estimated cost of EUR 7.1 million, of which EUR 5 million is the EU budget contribution.

What the office does over it. Local administrations, with schools, health and justice facilities, are still hardly providing digital public services, so citizens rely on in-person procedures, the document of June 2026 states.

How the office is connected. On the same document's account of June 2026, GovNet has connected about 1,000 public institutions and organs at central level and across 141 districts, and underinvestment in middle- and last-mile infrastructure leaves many local administrations insufficiently connected.

Last twelve months. The EU's annual action plan for Mozambique for 2026, dated 17 June 2026, carries a EUR 7.1 million Team Europe action to expand GovNet in selected districts.

Local governments connected. As at June 2026 the EU document gives GovNet's reach as about 1,000 public institutions across the central level and 141 districts, and says many local administrations remain insufficiently connected. In February 2020 the municipal component of the state finance system was being piloted in Maputo, Matola and Boane.

Not found. No source puts a local government office on GovNet, names the basic tier or gives a count or share of local governments connected. No use over a connection is stated for any local government office, and the only finance on record is the donor's.

MRT.short: Communes run budgets in a national finance system, deployed in 90% of 232 regions and communes in 2023; no source found says how offices are connected.
MRT.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The PEFA assessment of public financial management of January 2025 names the local finance directorate and the directorate-general of local authorities as deploying the system the country calls SIGeL in all local authorities.

What the office does over it. From 2022 the regions and communes began using SIGeL, the integrated local finance management system, for revenue and expenditure, assets, general accounting and reporting, giving the supervising directorates faster and timely access to their financial data, the assessment states.

How the office is connected. Until 2022 the local authorities ran their budgets in the off-line system El Khazin, on the assessment's account.

Last twelve months. At the end of 2023 the two directorates were in the final phase of deploying SIGeL in all local authorities, the assessment of January 2025 records.

Local governments connected. SIGeL was deployed in 90 per cent of local authorities at the end of 2023, against 232 authorities, 13 regions and 219 communes, at the end of 2022, the assessment states, a share of authorities with the system deployed, regions included.

Not found. How the offices of the communes are connected is not held, nor the owner, plan or finance of a connection. The 90 per cent is a share with the system deployed and not a share connected, and nothing dated in the twelve months to 30 September 2026 is held.

MUS.short: All 12 municipal and district councils worked online in a shared ministry system in 2024; no source found says how their offices are connected.
MUS.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Local Government's report for financial year 2023-2024 says the system its councils work in was built in house by a team of the District Council of Moka, extended to the other local authorities by Government decision of 16 March 2020, and is run with a Digital Office at the ministry.

What the office does over it. The same report says all employees of the twelve local authority digital offices do their daily tasks in real time in what the ministry calls the Council Project Management system, and that the local authorities processed 24,393 Building and Land Use Permit applications in the online National Electronic Licensing System in the year to 30 June 2024.

How the office is connected. The 2023-2024 report says the ministry's Digital Office works in real time with the twelve digital offices, whose employees can also work remotely.

Last twelve months. The Prime Minister told the National Assembly on 29 July 2025 that the back end of the Citizen Support Portal connects 583 ministries, departments, local authorities, parastatal bodies and some state-owned companies.

Local governments connected. The ministry's 2023-2024 report says its I-Council project, piloted at Moka from 27 August 2018, took three years to implement in all local authorities, and that 12 of the 12 it counts, five municipal councils and seven district councils, work in the system. Its permit table for the year to 30 June 2025 lists all 12.

Not found. How the council offices are connected, who provides and pays for the connection, and where the shared system is hosted. No plan, finance or rural share is stated, and nothing is dated in the twelve months to 30 September 2026.

MWI.short: District and city councils used internet on the government network in 2024; no source found says how many of the 35 councils are connected.
MWI.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Minutes of consultations with councils in June and July 2024 say the Department of E-Government manages the councils' internet on the government network, and that the Digital Malawi Project provided it, and the government is to take the service into its budget once World Bank funding ends. A Public Private Partnership Commission page published on 28 November 2023 says a connectivity initiative is to give over 500 public institutions fibre internet for ten years.

What the office does over it. The 2024 minutes record council officers logging in to what they call the Boma network with passwords, and councils still waiting for government email accounts. On 31 July 2026 the Minister of Local Government said councils upload project information to the national Constituency Development Fund dashboard.

How the office is connected. The minutes record that Kasungu has 5MB on the Boma network, and that a M'mbelwa district executive member on 11 July 2024 called the internet the project provided to the councils very slow and unreliable.

Last twelve months. GIZ Malawi says the government launched in mid-June 2026 a six-month pilot in which District Council Offices in Balaka and Dowa take on-demand updates to the national social registry.

Local governments connected. The minutes name Kasungu as on the network and record on 25 June 2024 that Dowa was yet to be connected, of the 35 councils the project plan counts. The International Growth Centre's study, researched to early 2022, describes office internet at the four city councils.

Not found. How many of the 35 councils are connected: the one count is of the four city councils in 2022. Nor is it held over what connection councils reach the national systems they work in.

NAM.short: In 2007 one local authority of two surveyed gave some staff e-mail; no source found says how many are connected, so no stage is set.
NAM.summary: Not found. The only evidence of a connection is a 2007 survey in which one unnamed local authority of two installs e-mail for some of its staff. Whether that authority is outside the capital, how many local authorities are connected, and anything since 2007 on governance or on the last twelve months are not held.

NER.short: Broadband was reported extended to 266 communes in 2026; the total of communes and no source found says what their offices do over it.
NER.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Projet Villages Intelligents is run by a project management unit under a steering committee chaired by the national agency ANSI, and is financed by the State of Niger and the World Bank at USD 100 million, closing on 23 October 2026. The communications minister said in March 2025 that a programme to connect all communes awaited the adoption of a national digital policy.

What the office does over it. The Council of Ministers stated on 22 April 2026 that the computerised national civil status register is operational in 102 communes.

How the office is connected. The project extended broadband to communes as public service provision, alongside health centres and schools, and Le Sahel reports the broadband connectivity of the mairies delivered to the town halls by the project.

Last twelve months. The mairies' connectivity was officially received at a ceremony on 6 May 2026, in the presence of the communications minister and the World Bank's resident representative.

Local governments connected. The project told the news agency ANP, in a report published on 15 April 2026, that broadband internet had been extended to 266 communes, 339 health centres and 298 schools.

Not found. No total of communes is given beside the 266, and nothing says that the commune offices themselves are on the connection or what they do over it. The civil status register is not said to be reached online.

NGA.short: 510 local government administration offices were counted on broadband in December 2025; no source found says how many offices there are, and what they do online,.
NGA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The World Bank's BRIDGE project, approved on 6 October 2025, sets a target of 3,428 local government administration offices on broadband by September 2030. The Bank names the Federal Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy as implementing agency; a company in which private investors are to hold the majority, not yet incorporated on 4 August 2026, is to build the fibre. Of the Bank's US$500 million credit, nothing was disbursed at 24 July 2026.

What the office does over it. The Bank's results framework records the offices as connected to broadband internet at 17 December 2025. Local government area offices enter health facilities' monthly paper returns into the national DHIS2, on the Federal Ministry of Health's report for 2021.

How the office is connected. The Bank counts the local government administration offices themselves as facilities connected to broadband.

Last twelve months. The credit was signed on 30 December 2025 and the project declared effective on 27 April 2026. On 22 September 2026 the communications minister cut the delivery timeline from five years to three, with cable laying to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Local governments connected. The World Bank counts 510 local government administration offices connected to broadband at 17 December 2025, the same number as in July 2025.

Not found. How many local government administration offices there are, and so what share the 510 is; where the connected offices are, who provides or pays for their connections and what is done over them. No domestic budget line is stated, and no office is yet connected by the project.

RWA.short: District offices worked in the national civil registration system in 2024 and 2025; no source found says how many of the districts are connected.
RWA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Governance and Decentralisation Sector Strategic Plan 2024-2029, dated 14 November 2024, costs an intervention giving local government entities ICT equipment and internet connectivity, with the Ministry of Local Government among those responsible. The World Bank-funded Digital Acceleration Project, running 2022 to 2026, plans a government network linking institutions at central, district, sector and cell levels, lawmakers were told on 7 July 2025.

What the office does over it. The civil registration system the National Institute of Statistics calls NCI-CRVS was fully operational at district, sector and cell offices for 2025, as it was in 2024. Engineers at City and District One Stop Centers process building permits in Kubaka, launched in April 2025, and sector offices make all their financial transactions in the national financial management system, on the sector plan of November 2024.

How the office is connected. Ministerial instructions of 12 March 2012 prescribe state-procured bandwidth delivered to central and local government institutions over the national fibre backbone, each institution paying the access fee. Cells, the sub-offices below the sector, have no internet connectivity, on the Ministry of Local Government's assessment published in September 2025.

Last twelve months. Births and deaths in communities are registered at the cell, where before they were registered at the sector, the Ministry of Local Government stated in June 2026.

Local governments connected. Connectivity remains a problem especially at sector and cell level in peri-urban and rural areas, a study published in September 2022 found.

Not found. The share or number of district offices connected, and who provides or pays for a district office's connection. Whether the government network planned to link the districts has been built, and any event at a district office in the last twelve months.

SDN.short: A 2022 meeting recommended fibre for localities that ask; no source found says whether any locality office is connected, so no stage is set.
SDN.summary: Not found. No source puts a locality office on a connection, names what an office does over one or counts the localities connected. The one statement held is a meeting's recommendation of 22 November 2022 that Sudatel connect by fibre the localities that ask, at their own cost, with no locality reported connected.

SEN.short: By June 2026, 400 civil-status centres run by communes were linked to the national register; no source found reports the share of communes connected.
SEN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The national civil-status agency ANEC, under the ministry for local authorities, runs the interconnection of the civil-status centres, with the state company SENUM SA installing the network equipment, as stated in August 2025. The NEKKAL programme that interconnected them was financed by the European Union and executed by Civipol and Enabel.

What the office does over it. Agents at the civil-status centres, which the communes run, register and issue acts in the national civil-status register, hosted at three national sites: 108,233 declarations from 1 January to 3 July 2025, on ANEC's figures.

How the office is connected. SENUM SA put network equipment in on site at 383 centres, 235 of them in service and connected to the network, in ANEC's presentation of August 2025. The communal land offices were not yet connected to the internet in November 2025, on a World Bank mission's account.

Last twelve months. NEKKAL's final steering committee reported 400 civil registration centres interconnected on 29 June 2026. SENUM launched the pilot phase of its PRODAP project in six communes on 24 April 2026.

Local governments connected. The application ANEC calls NEKKAL was deployed in 400 civil-status centres, with access to the central database, at 5 November 2025, on its director-general's word. In the 138 communes of the World Bank's land project, no municipal land bureau was equipped and operational with access to the land information system at 21 November 2025.

Not found. No share of communes connected has been found: no source sets the 400 civil-status centres against a count of communes, and ANEC's director general said on 27 April 2026 that in some centres the circuit was never completed and elsewhere it is very slow. Who pays for the centres' links after the donor programme closed is not stated.

SLE.short: All 21 councils had internet and a national accounting system live in early 2026, the finance ministry says; no source found says who pays afterwards.
SLE.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Finance reports the roll-out to the councils as its own work and procured the councils' internet service itself, on a contract signed on 12 August 2025 and charged to a World Bank grant. The National Digital Development Strategy of December 2022 sets 2027 for extending broadband to all government institutions, local councils among them.

What the office does over it. PFM Smart, the ministry's name for a web-based, real-time accounting system, went live in all 21 local councils in the first quarter of 2026. At Freetown City Council in 2025 transactions were processed live and payment instructions printed from the system.

How the office is connected. The roll-out included the provision of an internet facility for 21 local councils and a local area network at 21, by the ministry's report. The ministry hired a provider of internet services for the local councils, to support the accounting system. In 2023 seven councils outside Freetown reached the internet through individually provided modems.

Last twelve months. In the first quarter of 2026 the system went live in all 21 councils, with solar panels and batteries installed at 18. The internet contract is shown as completed on 18 November 2025, ahead of a planned 26 February 2026.

Local governments connected. 21 of 21 local councils, by the Ministry of Finance's count for the first quarter of 2026. In 2025 one council, Freetown City Council, was live.

Not found. The ministry's report gives no rural share, states live transactions only for Freetown City Council, and counts 21 councils in one place and 22 in another. The internet contract names no number of councils served, and no source says who pays for the service afterwards or names a domestic budget line.

SOM.short: A 2022 report says finance systems are implemented in all municipalities; no source found says how their offices are connected.
SOM.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The National ICT Policy and Strategy 2019-2024 set the goal that all local authorities of the federal government and the member states have internet access by its third year, with costs left to each agency. It made the ICT Department of the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Technology responsible for connectivity in government.

What the office does over it. The World Bank's Digital Economy Diagnostic of 2022 says the web-based financial management systems of the federal government, Puntland and Somaliland, which it names SFMIS, PLFMIS and SLFMIS, have each been implemented in all ministries, departments and agencies, state-owned enterprises and municipalities.

How the office is connected. The 2019 policy lists local authorities among the rural public services whose connectivity is to be built in a co-ordinated way.

Last twelve months. The policy that set the target for local authorities ran from 2019 to 2024.

Local governments connected. The 2022 diagnostic says the finance systems are implemented in "all" municipalities of the federal government, Puntland and Somaliland.

Not found. No source says how any municipal office is connected, or that municipal staff work in the finance systems at their own offices, and no count or total of municipalities is given. Nothing on record is dated within the last three years.

SSD.short: One county office of eleven assessed had its own satellite link in 2021; no source found says how many of the country's counties are connected.
SSD.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Maban County has two satellite terminals, one for the Office of the Commissioner and one for the Health Department, on an assessment of eleven local governments that the International Organization for Migration (IOM) carried out from September to December 2021.

What the office does over it. The Commissioner's office in Maban has a satellite terminal, IOM found in late 2021.

How the office is connected. The Maban office is connected by a satellite terminal of its own, as of 2021. In Renk and Rubkona the only terminal is the Health Department's, and the Commissioner's office and every other department have none. Baliet, Fashoda, Leer, Pariang, Pibor, Raja, Wau County and Wau Municipality have no terminal and report a need for one across all departments.

Last twelve months. IOM's assessment of the eleven locations dates from September to December 2021.

Local governments connected. One of the eleven local governments IOM assessed in late 2021, ten counties and Wau Municipality, has a satellite terminal at the Commissioner's office, and ten have none.

Not found. No count of connected offices across all the country's counties, no use named for the Maban terminal, who pays for it, and nothing on governance or on any event since 2021. The one assessment held omits Maban from its own recommendations section.

STP.short: No source found says whether any district council office is connected as at 2026, so no stage is set.
STP.summary: Not found. Which institutions are on the government network, and whether any district council is. The digital governance strategy is held cut off before its network chapter.

SWZ.short: One town council, Ezulwini, reported its own office internet line in the year to March 2024; no source found says how many councils are connected.
SWZ.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Digital Eswatini Project is implemented by the Ministry of Information, Communications and Technology and financed by USD 65.0 million of World Bank loans and credit approved on 15 June 2026. Town councils meet their ICT costs from their own budgets, in Ezulwini's accounts for the year to March 2024 and Mbabane's for the year to March 2023.

What the office does over it. Ezulwini Town Council moved to Microsoft Office 365 for business email, installed virtual conferencing equipment and ran its telephone lines over the internet line in the year to March 2024. In Mbabane the council's IT Section has automated municipal activities, mail tracking among them (year to March 2023).

How the office is connected. Ezulwini Town Council carries its five office telephone lines over the office's internet line (year to March 2024). The Municipal Council of Mbabane pays for internet among its utility services (year to March 2023).

Last twelve months. The House of Assembly gave a second reading on 21 September 2026 to the three Bills enabling the project's loans. COMESA reports that from January to June 2026 the project was in preparation, with its infrastructure assessment begun.

Local governments connected. One urban local authority, Ezulwini Town Council, reports on its own office's internet line (year to March 2024), and the capital's council reports paying for internet at its offices (year to March 2023). Thirty-eight Tinkhundla centres are set to benefit from broadband, with rollout expected in 2027.

Not found. No share or total of local governments with a connected office is published, and no Tinkhundla centre is reported connected. No national or shared system is named as worked in over the councils' connections.

SYC.short: All 27 listed district administrations had a government email address in 2025; no source found says how their offices are connected.
SYC.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Office of the President's government directory places the district administration offices under the Ministry of Local Government and Community Affairs, as from 1 March 2025.

What the office does over it. Each of the 27 district administration offices has its own office mailbox on the government's gov.sc domain, from anseauxpinsda@gov.sc to takamakada@gov.sc, as from 1 March 2025.

How the office is connected. The directory gives each district administration office a gov.sc mailbox beside an office telephone number (1 March 2025).

Last twelve months. The directory lists the district administrations and their mailboxes as from 1 March 2025.

Local governments connected. The directory's table of district administrations lists 27 districts, Praslin's two and La Digue among them, and gives every one of the 27 an office mailbox on gov.sc (1 March 2025).

Not found. How the district administration offices are connected is not stated, and none is said to be on the government network. No total of districts, no system the offices work in, and nothing on governance or on the last twelve months is held.

TCD.short: Internet kits and subscriptions were handed to 23 communes in 2026; no source found says whether the links are in service and the total of communes.
TCD.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The World Bank's appraisal of the Chad Digital Transformation Project, dated 4 September 2024, names the Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Economy as implementing agency, puts its financing at an IDA grant of US$92.2 million equivalent within a US$120 million total, and provides for last-mile connectivity to selected public institutions, local government offices among them. The 2027 budget orientations, reported on 4 August 2026, provide for generalising the public finance system SIGFiP to the collectivités territoriales.

What the office does over it. The national agency ANATS said, in a report published on 3 June 2025, that its civil registration system links municipalities, among other points, which send their data by SMS to the agency for validation.

How the office is connected. The finance ministry stated on 19 May 2026 that the equipment handed to communes under the project it calls PATN included Starlink Business kits with antenna, router and Wi-Fi, monthly internet subscriptions and Wi-Fi access points.

Last twelve months. The finance ministry reported on 19 May 2026 the official handover of the kits and subscriptions, with computers, printers and copiers, made with the World Bank's support at a ceremony chaired by the Secretary of State for Finance and Budget.

Local governments connected. The 23 communes that are provincial capitals received the equipment, the finance ministry stated on 19 May 2026.

Not found. Nothing says that a commune's link is in service, and no national total of communes is given beside the 23. The municipalities sending civil registration data are not counted or placed, and nothing says a connection is provided to their offices.

TGO.short: A birth-records platform was at pilot in four communes in 2026 and town hall fibre had not begun; no source found says how town halls connect.
TGO.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The digital ministry's resettlement plan of July 2026 names the ministry's project unit as promoter of the fibre extension that is to reach town halls, under the Projet d'Accélération Numérique du Togo, a 100 million dollar project with a target of 136 town hall buildings, implemented with the World Bank. KfW's records show a EUR 20 million grant committed in 2024 and a EUR 15 million grant committed in 2025 to connect town halls, hospitals and schools to the fibre network.

What the office does over it. Under a pilot in Vo prefecture, Togo First reported in May 2026, the mairie reaches in the platform Naissance Keva the newborn's data entered at the maternity, to draw up the birth record. In Lacs 1, UNDP reported in May 2021, the Kadodo application shares data in real time between health centres and the town hall's civil registry.

How the office is connected. The government's site said on 7 February 2026 that the town hall digitalisation project it calls PDiMa is to connect the 136 municipal buildings themselves.

Last twelve months. The Vo pilot has been deployed since February 2026, and the final resettlement plan for the Maritime region's fibre works was issued in July 2026, with the operator still to be recruited.

Local governments connected. The platform is a pilot in the four communes of Vo prefecture. The July 2026 plan states that the fibre works to the 136 town hall buildings had not begun.

Not found. Nothing says how any town hall is connected, and no figure is given for town halls connected by means other than the planned fibre. Outside the pilots, the one commune on record as working online is Lacs 1, in 2021, with no total.

TUN.short: Sixteen municipalities worked in a national permit system in 2026; no source found says how many municipalities have a connected office.
TUN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Communication Technologies' performance plan for 2025 makes the connection of public bodies' sites to the integrated administrative network an indicator of its digital development programme, targeting 98 per cent in 2025 and 100 per cent from 2026. It lists the network for the municipalities among the projects financed through the communications development fund.

What the office does over it. Since 24 June 2026 municipalities issue building permits in the national platform Tunisia calls Taamir, from the application to the final signature. The Centre National de l'Informatique states that municipalities and municipal arrondissements work on the centralised national civil status database it calls Madania.

How the office is connected. The Centre National de l'Informatique states that workstations installed in municipalities are connected to the servers of the state's data centre. The 2025 plan names RNIA3 as the administrative network for local collectivities and municipalities.

Last twelve months. On 24 June 2026 the Municipality of Tunis issued the first building permit handled entirely online and Taamir's extension to 16 municipalities began. On 31 August 2026 the Ministry of the Interior launched a remote service for translated birth extracts whose requests go directly to the municipality of registration.

Local governments connected. Taamir was extended to 16 named municipalities on 24 June 2026. The 2025 plan estimates that 71 per cent of the public bodies' sites programmed for the administrative network were connected in 2024, counting ministries, local collectivities, municipalities and sectoral networks together.

Not found. The number of municipalities whose offices are connected, and the total of municipalities to set the 16 against. How the municipal offices working in Taamir are connected, and how many municipal offices are on the administrative network.

TZA.short: In 2025, 174 district councils worked in a national loans system and councils are on the government network; no source found reports the share connected.
TZA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The e-Government Authority's roadmap of February 2024 sets out a strategy to expand GovNet to all facilities of local government authorities, ministries, departments and agencies. The Digital Economy Strategic Framework 2024-2034 targets 184 local government authorities on a structured office network and GovNet by June 2026. African Business reported in August 2026 that the World Bank-financed Digital Tanzania Project supports the extension of broadband to local government offices.

What the office does over it. The deputy minister for regional administration and local government said district councils process, disburse and collect repayment of the ten per cent special-group loans in the state-run system Tanzania calls WEZESHA. The Controller and Auditor General reports that local government authorities issued bills through the revenue system TAUSI in the year to 30 June 2025.

How the office is connected. The e-Government Authority states that local government authorities, with ministries, departments and agencies, are connected on GovNet, the government communication network.

Last twelve months. On 1 May 2026 the Geita Regional Commissioner directed District Executive Directors and other employers to pay for employees' internet from internal revenues, after the trade union congress said many public employees in the region buy internet bundles with their own money.

Local governments connected. 174 district councils were authorised to issue loans through WEZESHA between July 2024 and December 2025, after a pilot in 10. The e-Government Authority's roadmap of February 2024 gives 265 ministries, departments, agencies and local government authorities on GovNet, as one figure.

Not found. The share of councils whose own offices are connected: the 174 district councils come with no total, and the 265 bodies on GovNet are not divided between central bodies and local government authorities. How the offices of the councils working in the national systems are connected.

UGA.short: In 2022, 60.6 per cent of districts, municipalities and town councils answering a survey had office internet; no source found reports the share of all.
UGA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. NITA-U, the state's IT authority, was the internet provider of 70.1 per cent of connected local governments in its 2022 survey. The Uganda Communications Commission reports that the fourth National Development Plan, for 2025/26 to 2029/30, sets a target of extending high-speed internet to local government offices. On 6 December 2023 Parliament authorised borrowing of up to RMB 1,050 million from the Export-Import Bank of China for Phase V of the national backbone.

What the office does over it. A gender ministry study states that as of July 2022 all local governments had been migrated to the Integrated Financial Management System. NITA-U's 2022 survey found that local governments used the internet mostly for email, 90.9 per cent, and for services to the public, 74 per cent.

How the office is connected. In NITA-U's 2022 survey local governments gave staff internet over institution wireless networks and institution-owned USB modems.

Last twelve months. On 22 September 2026 the Ministry of Local Government launched its web-based accounting tool, which it calls SCART, in Hoima city's two divisions and supplied a laptop and a router for it. On 1 December 2025 the President launched the backbone's extension in Kanungu District, to connect the district headquarters and sub-counties.

Local governments connected. NITA-U's National IT Survey, of January to April 2022, found that 60.6 per cent of the local government administrations that answered it had institutional internet access; 95 of 128 sampled districts gave full data, with 17 municipalities and 10 town councils.

Not found. The share of all local governments connected, any share later than 2022, and the rural share: the survey's figure counts those that answered. A domestic budget line for connecting local governments, and how the lower local governments using SCART outside Hoima are connected.

ZAF.short: Municipalities across the Eastern Cape have worked in a shared disaster system since 2025; no source found says how many municipalities' offices are connected.
ZAF.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Mangaung Metropolitan Municipality told the National Council of Provinces in November 2025 that its network upgrade is its own project, run under a council-approved ICT governance framework, and that it has adopted a three-year ICT strategic plan naming broadband as an outcome. It said that it faces limited resources and an inadequate budget for ICT.

What the office does over it. The State Information Technology Agency said in July 2026 that municipalities across the Eastern Cape are operational on its Provincial Disaster Management Application System. The Road Traffic Infringement Agency names the integration of municipalities with the national traffic information system among the upgrades behind the AARTO rollout. Mangaung has moved its email to a cloud platform, migrating 900 user accounts beside 600 already there.

How the office is connected. By November 2025 Mangaung had appointed a service provider to upgrade its network infrastructure across its seven towns, with the first phase under way, and was still appointing an internet service provider for last-mile connectivity.

Last twelve months. The Eastern Cape disaster system went live on 21 November 2025, with training for provincial and municipal users. AARTO entered its second phase in July 2026, expanding to 62 municipalities.

Local governments connected. One metropolitan municipality, Mangaung, reports an upgrade of its own network. Interviews with nine managers of rural local municipalities in Limpopo, published in 2025, found that only communication had been digitally transformed, through social media and Microsoft Teams.

Not found. A share or a count of municipalities connected against the national total, and how the offices working in the Eastern Cape system and the rural Limpopo offices are connected. Whether Mangaung's last-mile provider has been appointed, who pays for its upgrade, and the years its plan covers.

ZMB.short: Government counted 93 of 116 councils on its network in 2025 and all 116 in March 2026; no source found reports the rural share.
ZMB.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The National Electronic Government Plan 2023-2026 commits to extending the Government Wide Area Network to the 116 district administrative centres and local authorities. It names the Electronic Government Division as the network's deployer and says implementation will depend largely on domestic financing through annual budget allocations.

What the office does over it. Smart Zambia's national coordinator said on 24 March 2026 that data entry into the Constituency Development Fund system was under way across councils. A survey of 2023 found every local authority it covered undertaking e-procurement on the national e-GP platform, and 70% reporting constraints including unstable internet.

How the office is connected. The budget address of 26 September 2025 says Government connected local authorities to the Government Wide Area Network. SMART Zambia said on 7 July 2026 that all local authorities in North-Western Province were on it over fibre.

Last twelve months. Smart Zambia called the connection of all 116 councils complete on 24 March 2026, and announced North-Western Province's local authorities connected on 7 July 2026.

Local governments connected. Each government count puts at least 93 of the 116 councils on the network, the finance minister's figure of 26 September 2025. Smart Zambia's chief technical officer said on 24 March 2026 that all 116 were connected, as did its national coordinator in a briefing published the next day. An article of 26 August 2026 reports one council, Sinazongwe, given high-speed internet under an initiative that seeks to connect all 116.

Not found. The rural share of the councils connected, and whether the 116 stated in March 2026 included Sinazongwe and the North-Western Province councils reported connected later that year. Whether council staff enter Constituency Development Fund data at their own offices, and a budget line for council connections.

ZWE.short: Government handed over 250 satellite kits for local authorities in 2025; no source found says whether any council office is connected.
ZWE.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The government, through the Ministry of ICT, Postal and Courier Services, donated 250 Starlink satellite kits to the Ministry of Local Government for local authorities, reported on 24 July 2025, with deployment, management and maintenance left to the councils. Manyame Rural District Council's chief executive said in April 2026 that its US$491,039 digitalisation programme, connectivity included, is funded from the approved council budget.

What the office does over it. Masvingo's Minister of State for Provincial Affairs said the Starlink kits given to schools, clinics and local authorities in the province in the first half of 2026 improved internet connectivity and access to digital services.

How the office is connected. Local authorities in Masvingo Province received Starlink kits in the first and second quarters of 2026. For the 250 kits handed over nationally in July 2025, installation and use were still to come.

Last twelve months. Manyame Rural District Council began in December 2025 a programme of phased investment in software, hardware, connectivity and training, due to be complete by December 2026. In the first half of 2026 104 Starlink kits were distributed in Masvingo Province.

Local governments connected. The provincial minister gives Masvingo's 104 kits as one total for schools, clinics and local authorities. In October 2021 a network link from councils to the National Data Centre had been piloted in four councils.

Not found. Whether any local authority's office is connected and working over its connection, and how many are: no installed or activated kit is reported, and Manyame's connection is not said to be live. A plan naming the connection of local authorities, and who pays the kits' subscriptions.

AGO.short: A finance ministry system recording municipal payers and fees was put in all 164 municipalities by 2021; no source found says how many record in it.
AGO.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Finance launched and runs the Portal do Munícipe under Presidential Decree 47/18. In November 2021 its Secretary of State presented it as a ministry tool, run with the ministry's SETIC-FP IT service, that the municipalities use.

What is recorded. In November 2021 the Portal held the records of residents and their households and tracked the whole cycle of fees, licences and fines billed by local administrations, with payment by the state's single payment reference.

Where the record is held. The ministry describes the Portal as a centralised system reached over the web, with revenue deposited in a Treasury sub-account. In August 2019 it let central bodies see the amounts local administrations collect.

Last twelve months. The ministry officially launched the Portal on 10 November 2021 across the 164 municipalities.

Local governments recording. The Secretary of State for Finance said on 10 November 2021 that the Portal was implemented in all 164 municipalities, with telecommunications problems in some. In August 2019 the ministry said it had created the technical conditions for it in 152 of 164.

Not found. No share or count of the municipalities whose staff record in the Portal. Nothing dated after November 2021, so the system's current plan, finance and progress are not shown.

BDI.short: Thirty communes collect local revenue electronically by 2026, recording payments only; no source found says where the record is held and the share of communes.
BDI.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Interior ministry's revised budget for 2025/26 carries a line of 2,000,000,000 BIF from the domestic state budget for extending the digitalisation of revenue collection in the communes. The digitalisation master plan adopted on 10 May 2023 includes an initiative to digitalise communal tax collection. One platform in use, IBB M+, is run by Interbank Burundi, a bank.

What is recorded. In Kayanza in June 2025, 48 of the commune's 54 collectors used point-of-sale machines, with the revenue transferred digitally to the commune's account. In May 2026 IBB M+ took payments from traders by phone or through agents, notified a commune officer of each transaction and kept the data to follow revenue.

Where the record is held. In 2021 the Direction of Communal Finances was considering an IT solution to replace the manual collection of communal taxes.

Last twelve months. Butihinda commune trained its planning and accounting staff on IBB M+ on 5 May 2026, for use from the 2026–2027 budget year.

Local governments recording. The Interior ministry's third-quarter execution report for 2025/26 lists 30 communes digitalised in communal revenue. A UNDP mission of June 2025 reported the E-Taxe system operational in communes such as Kayanza.

Not found. No register of payers is described in any system, and where the electronic record is held is not stated. The 30 communes carry no total, so no share of communes is given.

BEN.short: Twelve of 77 communes were selected in 2019 for cash-desk software that records payments; no source found says whether they were equipped and use it.
BEN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The PAACOL project, which equips communes with cash-desk software, is coordinated by the AIMF and implemented with the ANCB, the communes' association. In September 2019 its 743 million CFA francs came from the European Union, the AIMF and the ANCB.

What is recorded. The project's single cash window for non-tax revenue has software that records each payment, as described in September 2019.

Where the record is held. The software is networked within the commune, so that information is shared among the communal actors concerned.

Last twelve months. The project, begun in 2017 for three years, was to equip its selected communes during 2019/2020.

Local governments recording. In September 2019 the project had selected 12 of Benin's 77 communes to be equipped with the cash windows.

Not found. Whether the 12 selected communes were equipped and their cash desks went into use. Nothing dated after September 2019.

BFA.short: State tax services run tax billing and collection (2021); no source found says whether any collectivité territoriale keeps a digital record, so no stage is set.
BFA.summary: Not found. Whether any collectivité territoriale keeps its own digital revenue record. No source on local government revenue records has been found.

BWA.short: One city council has an online rates payment channel (2024); no source found says whether any council keeps a digital record, so no stage is set.
BWA.summary: Not found. Whether any council keeps a digital revenue register or receipt record. Nothing found says the national tax system collects any council revenue.

CAF.short: Bangui agreed with a private firm in December 2025 to digitise its municipal revenue; no source found says whether the system is in use.
CAF.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Under an agreement signed with the Mairie de Bangui in December 2025, BMI-WFS, a firm under Ivorian law, is to run the city's digital collection system.

What is recorded. In late 2020 municipal agents began a door-to-door census of traders in central Bangui, to build a taxpayer database with an individual sheet showing what each owes.

Where the record is held. In December 2020 a city-centre trader told RFI that Bangui town hall had no computerised file of taxpayers and that its collectors issued paper receipts.

Last twelve months. The agreement to digitise Bangui's municipal revenue was signed on 12 December 2025 in the presence of the Minister of Territorial Administration and Decentralisation.

Local governments recording. The agreement of 12 December 2025 covers the municipal revenue of Bangui, the capital, and names no other commune.

Not found. What the system agreed for Bangui will record, where it will be held and whether it is in use. No commune outside the capital is named, and no plan or finance is stated.

CIV.short: A ministry-built register system was in a 22-commune pilot of 201 in December 2025; no source found says whether any commune records in it.
CIV.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Directorate General of Decentralisation and Local Development (DGDDL) developed the SYGIDAN Recettes software in its own services and directs the PAMREC project. In April 2024 the project was financed by the African Development Bank and the Ivorian State, together 3,003,901,293 FCFA.

What is recorded. In April 2024 the DGDDL's director described SYGIDAN Recettes, then at pre-validation, as digitalising all of a commune's revenues, with traceability each time a tax is collected. The project's design of July 2021 registers taxpayers and records payments, balances, arrears and penalties.

Where the record is held. The tool is to centralise the data from all the actors collecting local revenue. The 2021 design was to connect it to the systems of the tax directorate, the Treasury, the DGDDL or the Court of Auditors.

Last twelve months. On 9 December 2025 the DGDDL handed the commune of Assinie-Mafia its taxpayer database, within the PAMREC pilot.

Local governments recording. The African Development Bank's appraisal of July 2021 places the pilot in 22 of 201 municipalities. In April 2024 the tool was to be deployed to the 22 communes and then distributed to all from January 2025.

Not found. No fact says the system is in use in any commune, and no count of communes recording is given. Whether the distribution to all communes announced for January 2025 took place.

CMR.short: A platform for traders to register and pay local tax was presented in 2023 for two councils; no source found says whether any council uses it.
CMR.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The AIMF, the association of French-speaking mayors, reports that FEICOM presented Inform'All City, a platform for collecting local tax from informal traders, on 21 March 2023.

What is recorded. On the platform, as presented in March 2023, informal traders register and pay their local tax, against a site the commune assigns them.

Where the record is held. The platform is built so that, with traders registered and paying on it, councils collect remotely.

Last twelve months. The platform, to be deployed first in two councils, was presented on 21 March 2023.

Local governments recording. In March 2023 the platform was to be deployed first in the councils of Yaoundé II and Douala III, in the political and economic capitals, with no wider count given.

Not found. Whether the platform was deployed in the two councils or in any other, and where its record is held. Nothing dated after March 2023 shows a commune keeping a digital revenue record.

COD.short: Tools to track revenue and register taxpayers were being assessed with 20 decentralised territorial entities in 2024; no source found says whether any uses one.
COD.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The digital tools for the decentralised territorial entities are supported by USAID's Good Governance Activity, launched in July 2023, whose July 2024 workshop was co-hosted with COREF, the national public finance reform committee.

What is recorded. A workshop of 23–24 July 2024 was to standardise and assess tools for tracking revenue, registering taxpayers and budgeting.

Where the record is held. The tools under assessment in July 2024 were for the public financial management of the decentralised territorial entities themselves.

Last twelve months. The Good Governance Activity held its workshop on the tools on 23–24 July 2024.

Local governments recording. In July 2024 the activity worked with 20 decentralised territorial entities in four provinces: Haut Katanga, Lualaba, Tshopo and Haut Uele.

Not found. What the tools record, where the record is held and whether any entity uses one. The tier of the 20 entities, the tools' owner and any plan are not stated.

COG.short: A state platform for local governments' revenue was validated in February 2026; no source found says whether any local government yet records on it.
COG.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Plateforme de dématérialisation des recettes des collectivités locales (PDRCL) was given to the state's Agence congolaise des systèmes d'information (ACSI) by the 2025 finance law. ACSI's procurement notice of 4 September 2025 lists equipment for it from the agency's 2025 investment budget, with the Ministry of the Interior as client.

What is recorded. The finance ministry said in February 2026 that the platform has a back-office module for local government agents and a market-collector module, Zando collecte, that enrols taxpayers, records revenue by payment mode and tracks each taxpayer's operations.

Where the record is held. The ministry said on 14 February 2026 that the platform brings the revenues of local governments into one information system.

Last twelve months. The platform passed final validation at Kintélé on 14 February 2026 and ACSI presented it to the Mayor of Brazzaville on 30 April 2026.

Local governments recording. The platform was validated after workshops with the communes of Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire. On 24 February 2026 ACSI was preparing its deployment, and in 2026 a pilot was to follow at the Ndjindji central market in Pointe-Noire once municipal staff had been trained.

Not found. No local government is stated as recording on the platform, in Brazzaville, Pointe-Noire or elsewhere. No plan naming the platform has been found.

COM.short: Nothing is held on local governments' revenue records, digital or paper, and no system is named, so no stage is set.
COM.summary: Not found. No source on local government revenue records has been found, and no system of any class is named. Nothing is shown either way, including absence.

CPV.short: Terms of reference for a municipal property tax module were issued in 2025; no source found says what municipalities record today.
CPV.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The finance ministry's special projects unit issued terms of reference in 2025 for the Territory Management modules of SIMple, a planned successor to the municipal information system. The work is funded from a US$15 million World Bank credit for the Harmonization and Improvement of Statistics in West Africa Project.

What is recorded. The planned modules cover the cadastre, property assessment and property tax collection.

Where the record is held. The system the modules are to succeed, SIM 2.0, handles accounting, financial management and budget execution, the allocation of revenues and expenses.

Last twelve months. The terms of reference for the property tax modules were issued in 2025.

Local governments recording. The modules are planned for the municipalities, all of which run SIM 2.0.

Not found. What municipalities record of their revenue, where they hold it and how many of them record are not held. No source says the property tax modules are piloted or live.

DJI.short: In 2020 local authorities could not levy taxes and none collected its own; no source found says how records are kept, so no stage is set.
DJI.summary: Not found. The one source found, on 2020 fiscal data, says local authorities are not empowered to levy taxes and that none of the nine collects its own; no source says how a local authority keeps any revenue record, and none names a system in preparation. Nothing found is dated since 2020.

DZA.short: A 2018 audit found most communes reviewed had no current tax-base census; no source found says how communes record revenue, so no stage is set.
DZA.summary: Not found. No source says how communes keep their revenue records, and none names a revenue system in preparation or on pilot. The one fact held is an audit of 22 communes over 2014 to 2018, which found most had no updated census of their taxable base and does not speak for the country.

EGY.short: A central authority collects the real estate tax, a quarter for local government (2020); no source found reports local records, so no stage is set.
EGY.summary: Not found. Whether any governorate or local unit keeps its own digital revenue record. No source on local government revenue records has been found.

ERI.short: Nothing is held on local governments' revenue records, digital or paper, and no system is named, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not found. No source on local government revenue records has been found, and no system of any class is named. Nothing is shown either way, including absence.

ETH.short: A property tax platform was built for three pilot cities in 2016 and never fully implemented; no source found says whether any city still uses it.
ETH.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. An assessment of the Computerized Property Tax Administration (CPTA) platform is run with the Ministry of Urban and Infrastructure's Urban Revenue Reform Project Office and the Ministry of Finance's Tax Policy Department, with UNECA support, according to LoGRI's project page.

What is recorded. CPTA is a platform for administering property tax, developed in 2016.

Where the record is held. The platform was never fully implemented, LoGRI says.

Last twelve months. The Addis Ababa City Government Revenues Bureau began a property-tax reform pilot in July 2026, covering property identification and valuation, in a move from the land-rent and building-tax arrangement to a value-based property tax.

Local governments recording. CPTA was developed for three pilot cities in 2016, and a national scale-up is planned.

Not found. What the platform records and where the record is held are not held, nor whether any of the three pilot cities still uses it. No plan or finance for it has been found, and nothing on it is dated within the last twelve months.

GAB.short: Libreville's mayor said in July 2026 the city runs its own digital revenue system; no source found says whether any other local government records.
GAB.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Libreville's pilot platform is developed by the company GTI Gabon for the city hall, and the mayor said on 3 July 2026 that the city's system was developed with the public Treasury. Digitax is the platform of the Direction générale des Impôts.

What is recorded. At its launch on 29 July 2025 the Libreville pilot platform was described as resting on a geolocated taxpayer file, online declaration and payment, automatic tax and penalty amounts and a dashboard showing who is up to date on which taxes.

Where the record is held. Under the Owendo agreement of 29 April 2026 the tax directorate will align the municipal agents' taxpayer directory with its own.

Last twelve months. The commune of Owendo signed an agreement with the tax directorate on 29 April 2026 to implement Digitax for municipal taxes. A consultancy presented the Colloc-Pay platform to the Ntoum commune and the Komo-Mondah departmental council on 19 June 2026.

Local governments recording. The mayor of Libreville said on 3 July 2026 that the city has its own operational system digitalising municipal revenue and securing collection. The city hall had launched a pilot of digitised revenue collection on 29 July 2025.

Not found. No local government outside Libreville is stated as recording, and where the record is held is not stated. Whether the system the mayor calls operational is the 2025 pilot is not held, and no plan or finance is stated.

GHA.short: Some assemblies record payers and bills in a shared national system, nine of 260 using it in 2019; no source found says how many do now.
GHA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Office of the Head of the Local Government Service, a state body, runs the training on the revenue software it calls dLRev, under a programme the World Bank supports. GIZ funded the application in 2019. Korle Klottey Municipal Assembly's own system is a company's software as a service, as audited at 31 December 2024.

What is recorded. dLRev holds a register of businesses and properties with their owners, and manages the billing and collection of property rates and business operating permits, as described in 2019. Korle Klottey's system held a property database, payer accounts and bills at 31 December 2024.

Where the record is held. Since 2017 dLRev has been hosted on the national platform of the National IT Agency, with no standalone operation in a district.

Last twelve months. A training of 350 staff of 35 Municipal Assemblies on the software began in February 2026, and about 150 officers in six regions were trained in July 2026. Ga West Municipal Assembly introduced a digital revenue system in one zonal council, with data capture set for April 2026.

Local governments recording. Nine of Ghana's 260 assemblies, 3.5 per cent, used dLRev throughout 2019, by a paper GIZ commissioned. In February 2020 47 of GIZ's 90 partner districts had properties registered in it. The Ministry of Local Government reports that in 2021 it rolled the software out in 114 of the 260.
