How the record is made. The Registrar stated in June 2019 that civil events have been registered online since November 2001 at computerised civil status offices, a national identity number being generated on each birth registered. The record is stored in the Division's single Civil Status Database, the Division stated in 2024.

Last twelve months. The Civil Status Division announced on 2 September 2025 that its CSD System was being revamped, with a transition period in which delays might be met.

Local offices doing the digital entry. The Registrar listed 35 Civil Status Offices by district, two of them in Rodrigues, in June 2019, and described them as computerised.

Not found. No share of offices making the digital entry has been found: the 35 computerised offices of 2019 are a count with no total, and the communique of September 2025 gives no count. No current plan naming the system and nothing dated inside the last twelve months has been found.

MWI.short: Births and deaths were entered digitally at 87 local service points in five districts in 2025; no source found reports the share of local offices.
MWI.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The National Registration Bureau, under the Ministry of Homeland Security, is the body responsible for civil registration. Its 2025-2030 plan costs civil registration at MWK 66.06 billion and names limited domestic budget allocations as a threat to the service. UNDP's basket fund spent USD 2,107,228 on digital identity and civil registration in 2025.

Events registered digitally. In 2025 registration officers at Traditional Authority offices began registering community births and deaths on a mobile application the Bureau calls Nzika. Kits at district registration offices register births and deaths and print certificates, by the plan of September 2025.

How the record is made. The district kits synchronise with the central system over the government network or mobile links, by the same plan. Nzika runs on mobile kits with biometric authentication, works offline and is integrated with the national civil registration system, UNDP reported for 2025. In some remote areas paper had not been fully replaced by 2024.

Last twelve months. Nzika registration moved from pilot to 87 service points during 2025, and national rollout is planned for 2026. On 9 October 2026 UNDP handed over 152 printers.

Local offices doing the digital entry. UNDP counts 87 service points in five districts in 2025, against 415 Traditional and Sub-Traditional Authorities listed for expansion by 2030. The Bureau reported electronic birth and death registration in 142 health facilities in 2025, with no total given. Certificate printers were in 58 health facilities in 2025.

Not found. No share of local offices registering digitally is published, and the health facilities registering births carry no total. The gap in remote areas has no figure.

NAM.short: Local offices enter births and deaths in the national register, as reported in 2024; no source found reports the share of offices doing so.
NAM.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security registers births and deaths on the National Population Registration System, the statistics agency said in April 2024. The system was developed in the country with its own resources, by a UNICEF and UN case study of September 2023. Cabinet approved a civil registration plan for 2015/16 to 2020/21 in 2015.

Events registered digitally. The system's death module was deployed in 2012 and its birth module in 2013. The statistics agency counts 85,853 births and 24,388 deaths registered and captured on it in 2021.

How the record is made. The local civil registration office captures the application on the system and issues the certificate, and the record is available in real time across the 14 regions, the agency said in April 2024. Of births registered in 2021, 68.9 per cent were captured within 14 days, and 89.6 per cent of deaths.

Last twelve months. In December 2025 the ministry said it had deployed its staff to 24 state hospitals to issue birth certificates right after delivery.

Local offices doing the digital entry. Some registration offices in remote areas lack computers or internet connectivity, which delays capture, the statistics agency said in April 2024. Birth and death registration took place at local registration centres and 24 health facilities and hospitals, by the case study of September 2023.

Not found. No count or share of local offices registering digitally is published, and the gap at remote offices has no figure. No civil registration plan later than 2020/21 is named.

NER.short: The digital register ran in 101 of 266 communes in December 2024, a share of communes; no source found reports digital death registration outside Niamey.
NER.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The civil-status system belongs to the Interior Ministry's Direction Générale de l'état civil, des Migrations et des Réfugiés, the ministry said on 11 August 2026. A civil registration strategic plan covers 2023 to 2027. The computerisation announced that day sits under the WURI-Niger project, which the World Bank finances.

Events registered digitally. The ministry's database for the five arrondissements of Niamey holds 72,459 births and 6,524 deaths registered in 2023, by the statistics office.

How the record is made. Events are declared at the centres and passed to the commune, where agents key the acts on machines connected to a server at the ministry's directorate, and each validated act is saved there, the statistics office wrote of 2023. Acts are printed on secured paper from the computerised system, by the government's communiqué of 22 April 2026.

Last twelve months. An ordinance of 22 April 2026 provides for the national civil-status register, and its decree followed on 18 May 2026. On 11 August 2026 the ministry announced the computerisation of all communes and declaration centres and a new platform as works to come.

Local offices doing the digital entry. The computerised system was in production in 101 of 266 communes and communal arrondissements in December 2024, by the statistics office, and the government counted 102 communes on 22 April 2026. Only towns in urban areas had electronic civil registration databases in 2023.

Not found. Digital registration of deaths is not established outside Niamey. Whether the declaration centres in villages and health facilities are computerised is not stated, and the gap between urban and rural offices has no figure.

NGA.short: Births and deaths are entered digitally at ward and local government offices from July 2026; no source reports the share of local offices doing so.
NGA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The National Population Commission runs the registration and its centres, and said in July 2026 that the platform is operated under a public-private partnership with a technical partner. The Registrar General's Department lists a Digital CRVS Roadmap for 2024 to 2026. A 2026 programme to speed up birth registration in Kano State is funded by the Government of the Netherlands.

Events registered digitally. Births and deaths have been registered digitally across the country since 1 July 2026, on the platform the Commission calls VitalReg.

How the record is made. The Registrar General's Department described in July 2026 an officer in ward and local government offices registering the birth on the platform, with real-time reporting of registration data. A registrar in Lagos said in August 2026 that his team takes details on a form when the network fails and calls parents back.

Last twelve months. The Commission says the platform became operational in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory on 1 July 2026, replacing paper registration.

Local offices doing the digital entry. The Registrar General's Department reported 3,372 wards activated and 304 registration workstations deployed at 18 July 2026. The Commission said that month that it has 4,011 registration centres across the 774 local government areas.

Not found. The share of local offices entering on the platform: the wards activated have no total, and the count of registration centres does not say how many of them enter on it. No domestic budget line has been found.

RWA.short: Births and deaths are entered digitally at all categories of registration office in 2025, the statistics office says; no source found reports the rural share.
RWA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The National Identification Agency, under the Ministry of ICT, supervises and coordinates the civil registration system nationally, on the statistics institute's account for 2025. The statistics strategy for 2024/25 to 2028/29 names strengthening the system a top priority. The finance law of 30 June 2026 appropriates RWF 116,184,997 to civil registration for 2026/27, domestically financed.

Events registered digitally. The system the country calls NCI-CRVS registered 356,838 births and 39,355 deaths that occurred in 2025, among the nine events registered through it.

How the record is made. The statistics institute states that in 2025 the system captures events in real time at the site where official registration takes place, as a single point of entry. The Agency states that all civil registers have been available only in electronic format since 17 February 2023.

Last twelve months. Birth registration completeness rose from 90.3% in 2024 to 92.9% in 2025, and death registration completeness from 46.1% to 50.5%. The share of deaths registered within the legal 30 days fell from 96.3% to 89.9% over the same year.

Local offices doing the digital entry. The statistics institute states that in 2025 the system is fully operational at all five categories of registration office: health facilities, cells, sectors, districts and embassies. The Agency counted 3,220 civil registration service points in its procedures of December 2023.

Not found. The statement that the system runs at every category of registration office comes with no count of the offices using it, and no figure gives the rural share.

SDN.short: Births are registered in a national electronic registry, with one local office named in 2026; no source says how many offices enter records, and where,.
SDN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Landinfo's report of March 2023 places responsibility for civil registration with the General Directorate for Civil Registration under the Ministry of Interior.

Events registered digitally. The civil registry centre of South Gezira locality issued an electronic birth certificate at its Al-Hosh office on 17 May 2026. A child's birth is registered in the centralised electronic registry introduced in 2011, on Landinfo's report of March 2023.

How the record is made. Landinfo's report of March 2023 describes a centralised electronic registry in which registration is possible at any civil registry office in the country, a birth being registered there on application against a paper notice of birth.

Last twelve months. The Al-Hosh office resumed work in May 2026 after a stoppage caused by insecurity and displacement, and the governor of Gezira State inaugurated civil registry work in Umm al-Qura locality on 29 April 2026. A lawyer told the BBC in a report of August 2026 that the conflict in Darfur has shut down civil registry offices, and an article of June 2026 states that Khartoum's civil registry has ceased almost entirely.

Local offices doing the digital entry. One office is named as issuing an electronic birth certificate in 2026: the Al-Hosh office, which serves South Gezira locality and its surrounding rural villages.

Not found. Nothing since the war began says how or where the birth record is made, and no total of offices has been found beside the one named. Digital registration of deaths is not evidenced, and no governance fact dates from the last three years.

SEN.short: In 2026 civil-status centres register births in one national system, with 77% of 629 centres digitised; no source found reports the share entering data.
SEN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Agence nationale de l'état civil (ANEC), an agency attached to the ministry of Urbanisme, Collectivités territoriales et Aménagement des territoires, deploys the software under a Plan national de remédiation begun in May 2026. The European Union financed the NEKKAL programme, which held its final steering committee on 29 June 2026, and ANEC's budget for 2026 had not been notified by 17 August 2026.

Events registered digitally. On ANEC's data the system held 14,839,577 births and 487,259 deaths at 17 July 2026. ANEC's director general said on 16 September 2026 that health services can register births in it directly from maternities.

How the record is made. ANEC's data describe 437 centres as connected to one system, which it calls the Logiciel de gestion de l'état civil (LGEC), with 5,610 new acts registered in it on 17 July 2026.

Last twelve months. ANEC's director general said in an interview published on 5 August 2026 that the LGEC had passed its pilot phase. By 16 September 2026 deployment was effective in the Dakar, Thiès, Louga, Diourbel, Fatick and Kaolack regions, with Tambacounda and the southern regions to follow in 2026.

Local offices doing the digital entry. ANEC's director general said on 16 September 2026 that the modernisation process stood at 77% of the country's 629 civil-status centres. ANEC's data at 17 July 2026 put the LGEC in 437 of the 629 centres, 70%, from 98% in the Thiès region to 42% in Kédougou.

Not found. No share or count of centres entering events in the system has been found: every figure is of centres digitised, deployed or covered. Whether deaths are entered at the office at registration is not held, and no rural share is given.

SLE.short: In 2023 births were entered digitally at the registration authority's hospital centres and sent to a central registry; no source reports the number of offices.
SLE.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The National Civil Registration Authority (NCRA), the state agency formed under the 2016 Act, presented the integrated eCRVS and ID management system as its own in May 2024. Its Director General said in August 2023 that the system was developed with European Union support through UNOPS.

Events registered digitally. NCRA told the ID4Africa meeting of 22 May 2025 that over 80% of its integrated civil registration and identity services are digitised, birth and death registration among the services listed. UNICEF's representative said in August 2023 that its support covered the piloting and scale-up of a mobile application for the notification and registration of births.

How the record is made. UNICEF reported in March 2023 that at NCRA's registration centres in hospitals the child's details are entered with the application when the mother registers the birth, then transferred through the central server, which generates the identification number, to the Central Registry System.

Last twelve months. UNICEF said in October 2026 that digital birth registration is now an integral part of Sierra Leone's civil registration system.

Local offices doing the digital entry. The Calabash reported in September 2024 that an NCRA project had distributed 48 laptops and internet modems to 48 selected health facilities across the 16 districts. UNICEF showed NCRA staff registering a birth on a portable digital device in Bombali District in October 2026. UNICEF reported in March 2023 more than 200 babies registered a month with the application at Ola During Hospital in Freetown.

Not found. No count or share of offices entering events digitally has been found, and death registration with the application is not described. No plan covering the present, no domestic budget line and no change in the last twelve months is stated.

SOM.short: By January 2026 local administrations in 30 districts registered births digitally into one central database; no source found reports the total of districts or offices.
SOM.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Law No. 46, published on 5 April 2026, charges a Directorate under the Ministry of Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation with creating and running a digital registration system with a central database. A government roadmap, reported on 11 August 2025, plans to scale the service to every district, subject to funding and infrastructure, and UNICEF, with the government and Germany, supported the foundational work.

Events registered digitally. The ministry said on 10 August 2025 that the platform enables local administrations to register births, deaths, marriages and divorces digitally. OpenCRVS's country page, published in January 2026, counts 28,391 completed birth registrations.

How the record is made. The ministry announced on 10 August 2025 that local administrations in Jubbaland, Southwest, Hirshabelle, Galmudug and Northeastern State register events on the platform and all records are stored in a centralised national database. OpenCRVS's page, published in January 2026, says the system captures births at the point of occurrence in the districts and linked hospitals.

Last twelve months. The platform, which the ministry calls the Unified Digital Civil Registration Service, was launched as a pilot in 19 districts on 10 August 2025.

Local offices doing the digital entry. OpenCRVS's country page, published in January 2026, states that the system operates in 30 districts and is linked to 160 hospitals.

Not found. No total of districts or offices has been found, so no share can be read, and only births are counted as registered. The roadmap carries no period, no domestic budget line is stated, and nothing dated falls inside the last twelve months. Reports of the number of districts differ.

SSD.short: A digital civil registration system was announced in July 2026 and no birth is registered digitally; no source found reports its design and start date.
SSD.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The World Bank's diagnostic of May 2026 gives the Directorate of Civil Registry, Nationality, Passports and Immigration as operator and owner of the planned civil registration system. Its director-general said on 28 July 2026 that implementation would start with support from partners, and named none.

Events registered digitally. The World Bank's May 2026 diagnostic found that birth registration is yet to be implemented and birth certificates do not exist, with about 90 per cent of births in no official register.

How the record is made. Births may be declared at civil registration or identification offices within 45 days, which the World Bank said in May 2026 is uncommon in practice.

Last twelve months. On 24 July 2026 the government announced plans for a digital system recording births, deaths, marriages and divorces. On 31 July the Directorate was reported to be planning to link civil registration with the national ID system, with births declared from health facilities. At the handover of 10 August 2026 the outgoing director-general cited a memorandum of understanding, signed in Nairobi, for an integrated civil registration system.

Local offices doing the digital entry. The World Bank's May 2026 diagnostic lists the Directorate's civil registration system as planned only and describes no office registering digitally.

Not found. No design, procurement, pilot office or start date for a digital system is described, and whether the birth-registration pilot in Juba is digital is not stated. No dated statement that local offices register on paper has been found, and the sources do not agree on whether a costed plan is in force.

STP.short: Births are entered directly in the national database at maternities, as of 2026; no source found reports the share of local offices doing so.
STP.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Direcção Geral dos Registos e do Notariado, an autonomous body within the justice ministry, is responsible for civil registration and developed its system with its own technicians, while the University of Aveiro in Portugal maintains and hosts it, the World Bank said in 2023. The same report found no strategic plan specifically for civil registration and identification.

Events registered digitally. The chief conservator of the civil registry said in March 2026 that births are registered by entering the data directly into the directorate's database. The World Bank said in 2023 that the system the directorate calls SIGA, implemented by 2018, registers births, deaths and marriages.

How the record is made. At the maternities the directorate's technicians and trained nurse-midwives make the registration directly in the system, on computers and printers there, the chief conservator said in March 2026. In the directorate's centres registration is done digitally, connected to servers hosted in Portugal, the World Bank said in 2023.

Last twelve months. In March 2026 the chief conservator said the directorate is eliminating paper by registering births directly from the maternities.

Local offices doing the digital entry. The chief conservator said in March 2026 that registration is done in all the country's maternities. The World Bank in 2023 counted 11 centres for all civil registration services and seven birth registration posts in maternities.

Not found. No share or count of the local offices entering records is published, and nothing says where deaths are entered. No finance fact from the last three years has been found, and no current plan for civil registration.

SWZ.short: Births and deaths were entered in the national register at 14 service centres in 2022; no source found reports the total number of offices.
SWZ.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Civil Registration Department of the Ministry of Home Affairs manages the system, and the register was developed in-house with the government's National Data Centre, which hosts it. A CRVS Strategic Plan 2022-26 was launched in 2022. The World Bank's appraisal of 8 June 2026 allots US$5.5 million to digital ID and civil registration.

Events registered digitally. Births and deaths are captured into the National Population Register on registration, with 47,524 birth and 5,968 death registrations in 2022.

How the record is made. The Central Statistical Office's report for 2022 says the registration officer fills the form by hand and a typist enters it into the register, which the service centres reach over a wide-area network, the registration being complete only once it is in the system.

Last twelve months. The World Bank appraised the Digital Eswatini Project on 8 June 2026, to upgrade the existing ID and civil registration systems. Its document says paper birth and death records are stored locally without centralised backups.

Local offices doing the digital entry. The Central Statistical Office's 2022 report lists 14 civil registration service centres with births and deaths registered in the register that year. The Ministry of Home Affairs' report for 2024/25 gives 15 service centres and 5 hospital registration points. In answers collected from October 2022 to April 2023, Eswatini told an AfDB and COMESA assessment that entry of vital events is electronic in all its civil registration offices.

Not found. No total of local offices has been found for 2022, so the 14 centres are a count without a denominator, and no rural share or office figure from the last two years has been found. The World Bank's June 2026 account of civil records on paper is not reconciled with the 2022 and 2023 accounts of electronic entry.

SYC.short: A computerised record of vital events was kept beside the manual register in 2018; no source found says where it is entered.
SYC.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Civil Status Act as in force on 1 November 2022 makes the Chief Officer of Civil Status, appointed by the President and answering to the Minister responsible for civil status, keeper of the registers of births and deaths.

Events registered digitally. A contributed article in Seychelles Nation of 10 August 2018 states that the Civil Status records were computerised in 1989, and that a computerised record of vital events is kept beside the manual register and updated daily from the occurrences the Civil Status registers.

How the record is made. The Act as in force on 1 November 2022 prescribes the registers as numbered pages kept in duplicate, and its section 107A lets the Chief Officer accept statements, forms and signatures through an electronic medium.

Last twelve months. The Civil Status (Amendment) Act 2021 was assented to on 4 November 2021, to commence on a date the Minister appoints by Gazette notice.

Local offices doing the digital entry. The Act as in force on 1 November 2022 provides a Central Civil Status Office in Victoria and offices at Praslin, La Digue and Anse Royale.

Not found. Where the computerised record is entered, at the offices at Praslin, La Digue and Anse Royale or centrally, and how many local offices enter it. Nothing dated after 1 November 2022 on governance or on change in the last twelve months.

TCD.short: Births were registered digitally at 97 hospital registry points in 2025; no source found reports the total of local offices.
TCD.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The World Bank states that Chad created ANATS in 2016 as the government institution in charge of operationalising the civil registry. ANATS's director general said in November 2023 that digital birth registration follows the validated roadmap for universal birth registration by 2030. Kiosks for birth registration in eleven N'Djamena health centres were being set up with UNICEF support and EU funding in September 2024.

Events registered digitally. ANATS's coordinator of civil registration said in an account published in June 2025 that more than 120,000 children had been registered through hospital-based registry offices since 2023. In August 2026 an opinion piece described digital birth registration at hospital desks in Koukou Angarana and Bol.

How the record is made. The World Bank stated in 2023 that civil registration officers in six hospitals enter the declaration in a mobile application ANATS calls TASDJIL, after which ANATS issues the birth certificate electronically. In the June 2025 account all data is sent by SMS to the national agency, which validates it and returns it for issuance. On 23 September 2026 the N'Djamena town hall cited the still heavy recourse to physical procedures in its civil-status service.

Last twelve months. On 23 September 2026 the commune of N'Djamena launched a project to digitise its civil registry and signed a memorandum with ANATS; an integrated management platform is planned.

Local offices doing the digital entry. The June 2025 account gives 97 digitised hospital-based civil registration points, which the government plans to raise to 600.

Not found. No total of local offices is given beside the 97 hospital points, so no share of offices is established, and nothing says deaths are registered digitally. That the entry is made at the office is said only of six hospitals in 2023.

TGO.short: A digital birth registration platform was piloted at one town hall in 2024; no source found says whether other offices register on it.
TGO.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. WHO's Togo office reports that a national diagnostic of the birth and death registration system in 2024 produced a national roadmap for the digitalisation of civil registration and vital statistics and a multisectoral task force. UNDP Togo states that in 2024 it supported the development, deployment and operation of the digital birth registration platform. The digital ministry is employer of a sixteen-commune digitalisation pilot tendered in July 2026, with German financing.

Events registered digitally. UNDP Togo's annual report for 2024 states that the platform, in its pilot phase at the Golfe 3 town hall, simplified the registration of births and of other civil status acts. On 27 May 2021 UNDP described an application the commune of Lacs 1 calls Kadodo as recording births, deaths and marriages.

How the record is made. WHO's assessment summary for Togo, on data from 2013 to 2018, records the exchange of civil registration data from local to regional and central offices as a paper-based system.

Last twelve months. The territorial administration ministry launched the re-reading of law 2009-010 on the organisation of civil status on 21 August 2026, with support from the OIF and UNECA, and reform proposals are expected before the end of 2026.

Local offices doing the digital entry. UNDP Togo states that in 2024 the platform ran in its pilot phase at one town hall, Golfe 3, and that the civil status centres of the 16 communes of the Savanes region were digitised and trained to use it.

Not found. How the record is made on the digital birth registration platform, and whether the 16 Savanes communes register on it. No total of offices is given beside them, and the roadmap's period is not stated.

TUN.short: Registrars enter births and deaths into the national database after the paper register, all offices connected in 2020; no source found says how many register.
TUN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Births and deaths in the civil register come under the Ministry of Interior, on a 2025 country report. The agreement to rebuild the platform, signed on 19 March 2021, was financed by the African Development Bank and falls under the national plan Tunisie Digitale 2020.

Events registered digitally. The national civil status system, which Tunisia calls Madania, holds births and deaths as well as marriages and divorces in a centralised database, on a 2025 report. It held 18.53 million birth acts and 4.14 million death acts as of 2018.

How the record is made. The registrar writes each event by hand in the paper register and then records it directly in the central database, where it is available nationwide the next morning, on a 2020 account.

Last twelve months. On 20 November, 4 December and 11 December 2025 workshops trained civil status officers and heads of municipal districts from 72 municipalities on the system, organised by the Ministry of the Interior and the National Institute of Health.

Local offices doing the digital entry. All civil registration offices have interconnected computer systems and all municipalities have access to Madania, an IDRC chapter of 2020 states, counting 350 principal offices and 170 subsidiary offices, annexes and mobile units.

Not found. No source gives the share or the number of offices that make the entry in Madania. Nothing on how the record is made or on offices is dated after 2020, and no plan or finance fact later than 2021 has been found.

TZA.short: In 2024 57% of mainland registration centres were active, entering births by phone; no source found reports capped because a current plan or domestic finance.
TZA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. On the mainland the Registration Insolvency and Trusteeship Agency (RITA), the statutory registrar of births and deaths, introduced the Civil Registration System in 2017 and runs it. Its Strategic Plan for 2021/22 to 2025/26 names that system for all its birth and death registration. For 2018/19 RITA reported a treasury allocation of USD 510,768 against a requirement of USD 27.5 million.

Events registered digitally. RITA's platform, which it calls e-RITA, registers births, deaths, marriages, divorces and adoptions, on its 2025 presentation. The system held 18,464,255 births as of September 2024 and 977,761 deaths registered since 2017.

How the record is made. At the under-five registration centres, which are ward offices and health facilities, officers record a birth by hand in a register and then enter the same details into the online system by phone, the national audit found in October 2024.

Last twelve months. Zanzibar's registration agency reported a 2025/2026 improvement of its system, with streamlined workflows and a unified mobile app. On the mainland RITA extended its system to all districts in October 2024.

Local offices doing the digital entry. RITA's monitoring plan, as the 2024 audit reports it, counts 6,341 of 11,053 under-five registration centres as active, 57 per cent of them. In Zanzibar the agency states in 2026 that registration runs on its own platform in all 11 districts.

Not found. The 57 per cent is centres RITA counts as active, not a count of centres entering digitally, and no later figure gives a total; Zanzibar's offices are not counted. No domestic finance fact later than 2018/19 and no plan running past June 2026 has been found for the mainland system.

UGA.short: District offices enter births and deaths into the central register, in most districts in 2020; no source found says how many offices do so.
UGA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The National Identification and Registration Authority (NIRA), under the Minister of Internal Affairs, holds all of Uganda's civil registration systems, it said on 18 July 2026. Its Strategic Plan III for 2025/26 to 2029/30 was finalised in 2025/26, and its 2026/27 budget estimate of UGX 155.948 billion is all Government of Uganda money.

Events registered digitally. NIRA's system, which it calls the Mobile Vital Records System, registered 498,439 live births and 22,182 deaths in 2024, on the statistics bureau's figures. On 18 July 2026 NIRA said it had built a births and deaths module on its identity system that issues an identity number once a birth is notified.

How the record is made. A paper notification form is entered into the web-based system at district offices and health facilities, and each entry is recorded directly in the central register, on a 2020 brief.

Last twelve months. In 2025/26 to 31 December 2025 NIRA registered 123,526 births and 9,935 deaths.

Local offices doing the digital entry. The system was used in at least 112 of 135 districts and in 222 of the 5,230 health facilities that handle births, an IDRC brief said in 2020.

Not found. No share or count of offices making the entry has been found, and nothing on offices or on how the record is made is dated after 2020. The new births and deaths module is reported with no offices and no date of going live.

ZAF.short: Births are registered online at 242 equipped health facilities, as of March 2026; no source found reports the share of local offices registering digitally.
ZAF.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Department of Home Affairs itself rolls out the online birth registration system to health facilities, on its 2024/25 annual report. Its amended annual performance plan for 2025/26 targets nine health facilities and allocates R21 million to the rollout.

Events registered digitally. The department reports that its online birth registration system was available at 242 health facilities by the end of 2024/25. Its Annual Performance Plan 2026/27 schedules the digitalising of death registration for 2028/29.

How the record is made. The National Department of Health states for 2024/25 that births are registered and certificates issued at the health facility, by Home Affairs officials posted there, through an online system. Home Affairs stated in September 2025 that births are captured onto the National Population Register at local offices and health facilities from the paper Notice of Birth form.

Last twelve months. The department reported progress on online birth registration in the fourth quarter of 2025/26. The Portfolio Committee on Home Affairs reports that the 2025/26 target of automated birth registration at 47 health facilities was missed and the rollout deferred to 2026/27.

Local offices doing the digital entry. The Annual Performance Plan 2026/27 counts 242 health facilities equipped with online birth registration systems, beside 325 front offices and 220 mobile offices. The National Department of Health counts 299 health facilities able to register births at the end of 2024/25, against 1,445 public health facilities with maternity wards.

Not found. No share of local offices registering births digitally has been found: the counts are of health facilities equipped, and how the front offices make the record is not described. No digital registration of deaths has been found, and no figure for the last year's progress.

ZMB.short: Births are registered in a national system deployed in eleven districts in 2026; no source found says how many local offices enter records themselves.
ZMB.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Minister of Home Affairs and Internal Security describes the Integrated National Registration Information System, INRIS, as the ministry's civil registration system, in a 2026 statement to the National Assembly. The Eighth National Development Plan 2022-2026 commits the Government to operationalise it. The Minister puts the cost of the exercise at K1,069,366,200, and in December 2025 World Bank financing under the Digital Zambia Acceleration Project was put to a contract for the CRVS core modules.

Events registered digitally. The Minister states that enrolment has commenced in the INRIS districts, including registration of births and issuance of birth certificates using the system. The ministry said in December 2025 that about 1.3 million citizens have been enrolled on INRIS and over 500,000 births and deaths registered.

How the record is made. A September 2025 preprint states that death notification forms on paper are carried weekly from local offices to provincial or national headquarters for entry into INRIS. The Lavushimanda district officer said in September 2026 that the district office is implementing digital civil registration through INRIS.

Last twelve months. The Lavushimanda district office registered over 3,000 children under five in the four months to September 2026.

Local offices doing the digital entry. The Minister's 2026 statement has INRIS deployed in eleven districts. A CDC Foundation case study of 2025 says the expansion of INRIS has brought access to civil registration services to 81 of 116 districts. In October 2023 INRIS was rolled out in 79 districts.

Not found. No count of local offices that enter events in INRIS themselves has been found, and the accounts differ on whether entry is made at the office or at provincial or national headquarters. No source of funds is stated for the current exercise, and nothing dated in the last twelve months shows a national advance or retreat.

ZWE.short: Births are entered digitally at computerised offices; at least 93 of 282 offices were computerised in 2026, and no source says how many register digitally.
ZWE.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Registrar General's department presents the computerisation of its provinces, districts and sub-offices as its own decentralisation programme, in July 2026. UNICEF says Zimbabwe developed a strategic action plan for civil registration and vital statistics for 2023-2027. The Appropriation (2026) Act appropriated ZiG 1,470,460,000 to the Civil Registration programme, and the ten sub-offices announced in August 2026 are funded by China and delivered by UNICEF.

Events registered digitally. UNICEF Zimbabwe stated in July 2025 that at the computerised sub-office at Mpilo Hospital mothers register newborns and obtain a birth certificate before discharge.

How the record is made. UNICEF Zimbabwe stated in July 2025 that the computerised registry offices and sub-offices allow real-time data entry at the office. UNICEF's chief of child protection said on 7 August 2026 that some decentralised sub-offices are not computerised.

Last twelve months. In October 2025 the Minister of Home Affairs and Cultural Heritage announced plans to computerise sub-offices across the country. On 7 August 2026 UNICEF and the government announced a China-funded project to computerise, digitalise and solar-power 10 sub-offices in eight districts.

Local offices doing the digital entry. The Deputy Registrar General said on 22 July 2026 that all 10 provinces and 63 districts have been computerised and more than 20 of 209 sub-offices. UNICEF Zimbabwe named, in July 2025, digital registration as operational at Mpilo Hospital, Kariangwe in Binga, Bubi, Manama Mission Hospital, Mahusekwa, Murambinda and Epworth.

Not found. No count of offices registering births digitally has been found: the Registrar General's count is of offices computerised, and what a computerised office does is not stated. No source found says where the digital record is held, and no digital entry of deaths has been found.

AGO.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2026.
AGO.summary:
Mobile money in service. EMIS, Angola's interbank services company, manages the MULTICAIXA Express app and KWiK instant transfers, per an EMIS executive director at the 2026-10-12 CyberSecur Summit. Minister Jose de Lima Massano said on 9 July 2026 that mobile and digital payments in Angola grew about 56% year on year by the end of the first half of 2026. Expansão reports EMIS data that digital wallets originated Kz 212.7bn of the Kz 557.4bn moved over Kwik in the first half of 2026, and that wallets were authorised to open e-money accounts about two years earlier.

Between providers. EMIS describes the STI as account-to-account interoperability between bank and non-bank payment service providers, and KWiK processed 4.48 million transfers worth Kz 123.85 billion in August 2026. Expansão reports EMIS data that wallets sent Kz 209.6bn to bank accounts and banks sent Kz 2.8bn to non-bank payment providers over Kwik in the first half of 2026.

National switch. Expansão reports Kwik, launched by the Banco Nacional de Angola in June 2023, carries instant transfers between banks and digital wallets, with Kz 557.4bn moved in the first half of 2026. KWiK, reported by EMIS, handled 3.14 million transfers worth 74.6 billion kwanzas in February 2026 across wallets and banks, with 12.3 million registered accounts.

Not found. Nothing further is asked of this indicator.

BDI.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2026.
BDI.summary:
Mobile money in service. BurundiPay, the national instant payment system run by the BRB, had about 224,000 users and about BIF 4.29 billion in cumulative transactions on 4 August 2026, with customers paying from bank accounts or e-wallets. BurundiPay lets users pay and transfer funds in real time from bank accounts and mobile wallets, the BRB says. Burundi Pay, the national instant payment system, has been operational since March 2026, per the central bank's deputy governor.

Between providers. On BurundiPay 17 institutions (5 commercial banks, 10 microfinance institutions, 2 payment institutions) are live, and customers can transfer money and pay instantly from bank accounts or e-wallets, per the BRB. The BRB says BurundiPay already allows exchanges between banks, microfinance institutions and mobile wallets locally.

National switch. BurundiPay is described as the national instant payment system run by the BRB, live since 5 March 2026 and launched publicly on 23 April 2026. BurundiPay is described as the national instant payment system connecting commercial banks, microfinance institutions and payment service providers in a single network, also reachable by USSD.

Not found. Nothing further is asked of this indicator.

BEN.short: Payments between mobile money providers or with banks were in service in 2026; no source found reports a national switch.
BEN.summary:
Mobile money in service. Mobile Money has become the standard for transactions and that the Xedo platform integrates Mobile Money settlement for Beninese merchants. Arcep reports 11,649,735 active mobile financial services accounts at 31 December 2025, led by MTN Mobile Money (51%), Celtiis Cash (27%) and Moov Money (22%). Fraternité reported mobile money agents serving Moov Money and MTN MoMo customers in Cotonou, with deposits and withdrawals in service. The World Bank restructuring paper says 219,391 users of digital financial services through mobile money were recorded under the Digital Rural Transformation Project.

Between providers. Transfers from banks can credit mobile money wallets in seconds and the reverse, in real time, via PI-SPI, which the article says now connects banks and mobile money 100% in UEMOA. BCEAO reports 80 participants connected to PI-SPI on 2 April 2026: 59 banks, 9 e-money institutions, 11 microfinance institutions and 1 payment institution, on one interoperable platform. Le Grand Ouémé reported in November 2025 that Moov Money customers can send instant transfers between their wallet and bank and microfinance accounts on PI-SPI.

National switch. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

Not found. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts.

BFA.short: Payments between mobile money providers or with banks were in service in 2026; no source found reports a national switch.
BFA.summary:
Mobile money in service. Orange Money Burkina Faso's director general says the service has about 100,000 points of sale in the country, and SONAR Assurance signed a convention on 18 September 2026 to sell policies and take premium payments through it. Burkina24 reports Orange Burkina Faso's Max It app, relaunched on 18 September 2026, offers Orange Money mobile money to subscribers of all networks, per Orange's Abdramane Diallo. Wave Burkina offers digital finance used for payment, money transfer and savings by traders, farmers and young entrepreneurs, per its representative at an ANPFI training launch.

Between providers. Burkina24 reports Max It is interconnected with almost all the country's banks for transfers between bank accounts and Orange Money accounts, per Orange's Abdramane Diallo. LeFaso.net reports that the BCEAO's PI-SPI interoperable instant payment platform, launched 30 September 2025, connects banks, e-money institutions and payment institutions, with 80 connected by 24 June 2026.

National switch. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

Not found. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts.

BWA.short: Payments between mobile money providers or with banks were in service in 2025; no source found reports a national switch.
BWA.summary:
Mobile money in service. Mmegi reports Orange Money, Mascom's MyZaka and BTC's Smega as mobile money platforms, and FNBB's eWallet as a service through which customers receive money. Mukuru launched a Visa-branded Companion Card linked to its Mukuru Wallet in Botswana, where Mukuru Wallet customers already manage money by phone and Mukuru is a registered Electronic Payment Service Provider. Mmegi reports Orange Money is Botswana's most dominant mobile money service and has added Visa 3D Secure for its virtual cards with Paymentology. FinScope 2024 found 75% of Batswana use mobile money, and 33% of unbanked adults already use it.

Between providers. Mobile money in Botswana is now interoperable with traditional bank accounts.

National switch. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

Not found. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts.

CAF.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2023.
CAF.summary:
Mobile money in service. Telecel Money mobile money is in service in the Central African Republic, with many ENERCA subscribers already paying electricity bills through it before the official launch on 4 August 2026, according to Telecel and ENERCA. Orange Centrafrique provides its Orange Money mobile payment infrastructure, described as widely used across the country, to pay the DPI import fee, per the finance ministry's chief of staff. Orange mobile money transfer and mobile payment services operate in Batangafo, but have been down for nearly a month, per local testimony reported by Corbeau News.

Between providers. The CEMAC QR Code standard, launched 29 July 2026 across six states including the Central African Republic, lets a client with a bank account, mobile money wallet or microfinance account pay by scan whatever their institution. AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY gives all-to-all interoperability between banks, microfinance institutions and mobile money operators in the six CEMAC states including the Central African Republic.

National switch. AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY also provides domestic instant payment functionality connecting banks and mobile money wallets in each CEMAC state, including the Central African Republic.

Not found. Nothing further is asked of this indicator.

CIV.short: Payments between mobile money providers or with banks were in service in 2026; no source found reports a national switch.
CIV.summary:
Mobile money in service. APAnews reports the fintech PUSH in Cote d'Ivoire has over 700,000 individual accounts and over 20 million transactions worth more than CFAF 600 billion, with an interoperability and merchant-payment agreement signed with Orange Money. Africtelegraph reports that Orange Money, MTN Mobile Money and Wave have converted millions of Ivorians to mobile money transactions, which merchants, metered taxis and ride-hailing platforms have largely adopted. SimoCash, launched in May 2026, carries payments and money transfers over mobile money networks such as Orange Money in Cote d'Ivoire.

Between providers. SimoCash lets funds move directly from one mobile money operator to another, Orange Money being named as one. Fraternite Matin reports PI-SPI, launched by the BCEAO on 30 September 2025, lets users transfer instantly between bank accounts, mobile money wallets and microfinance accounts, with 80 institutions connected.

National switch. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

Not found. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts.

CMR.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2023.
CMR.summary:
Mobile money in service. Tech Africa News reports that Looping Binary has launched LBPay in Cameroon, a platform to send and receive money, manage wallets and pay bills and airtime. Cameroon has two licensed payment institutions, Orange Money Cameroun and Mobile Money Corporation (which runs MTN Mobile Money), per DGTCFM data updated July 2026, and mobile money had 30.99 million accounts in 2024 per BEAC. MTN Cameroon's Mobile Money Corporation runs MoMo accounts on which it presented MoMo Helep Pro, offering employees digital advances up to 100,000 FCFA repayable in 30 days, and a Bulk Payment system for instant mass payments, per Le Jour.

Between providers. Tech Africa News reports that LBPay lets users transfer funds across different mobile money networks. BEAC says the QR code launched 29 July 2026 lets any bank or microfinance mobile app read any merchant's code regardless of institution or CEMAC country.

National switch. AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY also provides domestic instant payment functionality connecting banks and mobile money wallets in each CEMAC state, including Cameroon.

Not found. Nothing further is asked of this indicator.

COD.short: Payments between mobile money providers or with banks were in service in 2026; no source found reports a national switch.
COD.summary:
Mobile money in service. TechAfrica News says Flash's FlashApp offers over 27 financial services in the DRC including mobile money, to more than three million customers. Visa's Godfrey Sullivan says M-Pesa mobile money wallet top-ups in DR Congo are settled in stablecoins in the background via Visa Pay with Onafriq. Biometric Update reports almost 30 million citizens in the DRC have a mobile money account, though cash still dominates. MainMoney's director general said at least 29 million Congolese hold a mobile money account, and MainMoney, a palm-vein payment terminal, was launched in Kinshasa on 29 April 2026.

Between providers. About $88 million has been channelled into the formal banking sector through wallet-to-bank transfers over the past year, according to Vodacom Congo's CEO. Onafriq supported the Visa Pay launch in the DRC in Q4 2025, which it says brings interoperability between mobile money and card networks at scale.

National switch. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

Not found. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts.

COG.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2023.
COG.summary:
Mobile money in service. ACI reports Yano, launched 14 September, lets users send and receive mobile payments as a gateway to mobile money operators, which hold the funds. Kerry Payments Brazzaville was authorised by ARPCE as a payment aggregator connecting businesses to mobile money operators, banks and microfinance institutions operating in Congo. A school management platform shown to over 200 principals in Brazzaville integrates school fee payment through Airtel Money, per Tech Review Africa. GIMAC said that in the first half of 2026 payment institutions and mobile money operators, including those of Congo, dominate GIMACPAY transaction volumes.

Between providers. Yano's product manager says the platform lets users pay and be paid by mobile payment regardless of telephone operator, via QR code or link. The CEMAC QR Code standard, launched 29 July 2026 across six states including Congo, lets a client with a bank account, mobile money wallet or microfinance account pay by scan whatever their institution.

National switch. AfricaNenda says GIMACPAY also provides domestic instant payment functionality connecting banks and mobile money wallets in each CEMAC state, including the Republic of Congo.

Not found. Nothing further is asked of this indicator.

COM.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2026.
COM.summary:
Mobile money in service. The PFSS-RRC names Mvula and Huri Money as mobile-banking operators that make the transfer payments to households in Comoros. The central bank says Komor Switch connects banks, financial institutions and mobile money services in the Comoros. AXIAN says it has an established presence in mobile financial services in the Comoros through MVola, separate from the newly licensed digital financial institution. ITWeb reports AXIAN says it already has a presence in mobile financial services in the Comoros through MVola, separate from the newly licensed institution.

Between providers. The central bank says Komor Switch allows instant real-time transfers between banks and mobile money. Al-Watwan reports the president launched Komor Switch, a national platform connecting all banks and mobile money services and making interoperability between banks and mobile banking possible.

National switch. The central bank describes Komor Switch as the national payment infrastructure interconnecting all banks, financial institutions and mobile money services. Al-Watwan reports Komor Switch is a national platform connecting all banks and mobile money services, launched officially by the president.

Not found. Nothing further is asked of this indicator.

CPV.short: Mobile money or e-money was in service in 2024; no source found reports payments between providers.
CPV.summary:
Mobile money in service. The Televinti4 mobile app, launched in 2021 and run by SISP, lets users make transfers, QR Code and Token payments, pay bills and top up phones, and about 15,600 people use it, under 5% of roughly 329,000 Vinti4 network users, per Expresso das Ilhas. A study presented at a Banco de Cabo Verde forum names one operator already in the e-money market, Banco BAI/Makeba, while recommending against building a new e-money entity from scratch (2021, before the three-year window).

Between providers. No source found since October 2023 says payments between providers, or between wallets and banks, are in service. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

National switch. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

Not found. No source found since October 2023 says payments between providers, or between wallets and banks, are in service.

DJI.short: Mobile money or e-money was in service in 2024; no source found reports payments between providers.
DJI.summary:
Mobile money in service. Djibouti Telecom's D-Money officially launched its new smartphone application on 26 September 2024, open to all Djiboutians since 21 September, for money transfers, bill payment and online purchases of services. The Ministry of Communication says Djibouti Telecom's D-Money, a recently launched mobile money service for transfers, payments, bill payment and airtime through agents and an app, already has thousands of subscribers, including three ministers who opened wallets (2020, before the three-year window).

Between providers. No source found since October 2023 says payments between providers, or between wallets and banks, are in service. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

National switch. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

Not found. No source found since October 2023 says payments between providers, or between wallets and banks, are in service.

DZA.short: Payments between mobile money providers or with banks were in service in 2026; no source found reports a national switch.
DZA.summary:
Mobile money in service. The CNESE president said Algeria has widened the use of electronic payment and payment by mobile phone in recent years. Alger 16 reports DZ Mob Pay mobile payments launched officially in early 2025, with 126,114 individual accounts and 18,294 merchant accounts by mid-2026, in rollout with seven pilot banks. Algérie Éco, citing GIE Monétique, says interbank mobile payment DZ Mob Pay launched officially in January 2025 and had 95,014 personal accounts and 14,283 merchant accounts at end December 2025. We Are Tech says mobile money transfers rose sharply in 2025, supported by applications such as BaridMob and Wimpay.

Between providers. Alger 16 reports interbank QR code and P2P payments under DZ Mob Pay run on the interoperability of the national mobile switch put in service in June 2024. Algérie Éco, citing GIE Monétique, says DZ Mob Pay interbank payments rest on the national mobile switch put in service in June 2024, with seven pilot banks.

National switch. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

Not found. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts.

EGY.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2025.
EGY.summary:
Mobile money in service. An analyst says a mobile wallet transfer moves e-money within the service provider's ecosystem, and InstaPay moves value between existing bank accounts. Ahram Online describes Instapay as a state-backed mobile application for electronic payments, licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt and in operation. NTRA reports 57.01 million telecom-operator mobile wallets in Egypt in H1 2026, with 2.22 billion transactions worth EGP 2.96 trillion. Youm7 reports 57.01 million telecom-operated mobile wallets in H1 2026 (up 23%), with 2.22 billion transactions worth EGP 2.96 trillion, per the NTRA H1 2026 report. Orange Egypt says its Orange Cash wallet had about 10 million users in October 2026.

Between providers. NTRA reports 78% of wallet deposit transactions in H1 2026 were made from the wallet holder's bank account via InstaPay. Youm7, citing NTRA, says InstaPay bank-account-to-wallet transfers made up 78% of wallet deposits by count and 58% by value in H1 2026.

National switch. The InstaPay instant payments network, launched March 2022, handles personal, commercial and account-to-wallet transfers, with over 1.1 billion operations, per banking expert Walid Adel.

Not found. Nothing further is asked of this indicator.

ERI.short: Mobile money or e-money was in service in 2026; no source found reports payments between providers.
ERI.summary:
Mobile money in service. The Fintech Times says mobile wallets linked to state-owned EriTel are emerging as the primary entry point to digital financial services in Eritrea, still limited in functionality. Himbol's guide says its M-Nakfa mobile money service is active, with cash-in/cash-out, person-to-person, merchant and utility payments, under Bank of Eritrea licensing and supervision. 2 facts are held on the subject: no news story or official notice read for this study says more about it, the documents the earlier cell cited were not read, and the systems themselves were not examined.

Between providers. No source found since October 2023 says payments between providers, or between wallets and banks, are in service. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

National switch. No source found since October 2023 says a national switch connects wallets and bank accounts. The nearest held fact: the one given above.

Not found. No source found since October 2023 says payments between providers, or between wallets and banks, are in service.

ETH.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2026.
ETH.summary:
Mobile money in service. Capital says Ethio Telecom's telebirr is the dominant mobile-money operator with more than 60 million subscribers, and Safaricom Ethiopia's M-Pesa has also expanded. President Taye Atske Selassie said mobile money and mobile banking accounts reached 257 million and carried more than ETB 24 trillion in the first nine months of 2026. ZooryaPay, a licensed payment platform, processed over ETB 120 billion in merchant transactions in the past year, per the report. Team Shega's diagnostic says Ethiopia has opened more than 135 million mobile wallets and grown its agent network fifteen-fold in four years. M-PESA Ethiopia lets customers withdraw cash at supported Awash Bank ATMs from the M-PESA app, with Tech Africa News reporting real-time processing. NIDP names Telebirr and M-Pesa as mobile wallets harmonised with Fayda.

Between providers. Capital says telebirr and M-Pesa are both connected through EthSwitch, which provides interoperability linking banks, payment-service providers and merchants. The ETTA/Visa devices interoperate fully with Ethiopia's national switch and existing financial institutions. M-PESA says its wallet customers can withdraw at Awash Bank ATMs, and expects this to strengthen interoperability between financial services.

National switch. Capital describes EthSwitch as Ethiopia's national payment switch linking banks, payment-service providers, merchants and the mobile-money platforms. EthSwitch is described as Ethiopia's national payment switch, linking banks, payment institutions and other participants with instant-payment infrastructure and interoperable QR payments.

GAB.short: A national switch connected mobile money wallets and bank accounts in 2023.
GAB.summary:
Mobile money in service. Gabon already has substantial mobile money use, according to Biometric Update. L'Union says Madigipaie is a national QR code digital payment platform for transactions between merchants and users, working with several banks, whose rollout to merchants the economy minister asked Libreville's mayor to support on 3 July 2026. Moov Gabon issued 1,969,325 transactions worth 68.1bn FCFA and Airtel Gabon 1,950,401 worth 55.8bn FCFA in H1 2026, per GIMAC statistics. Droit Medias Finance reports payment institutions in the CEMAC execute local transfers onto customers' e-money wallets for inbound remittances. The article refers to growing mobile money in Gabon, per Biometric Update.

Between providers. BEAC says the QR code launched 29 July 2026 lets any bank or microfinance mobile app read any merchant's code regardless of institution or CEMAC country. AGO.short: In 2024, 1.3 per cent of rural people had electricity.
AGO.summary:
Rural access to electricity. In 2024, 1.3 per cent of rural people had electricity, by the World Bank's rural electricity access series. The series gives no figure for the years just before, so no source found says whether it is rising or falling. It is 25.7 points short of 27, the next line. The study's lines are 27, 53, 80 and 95 per cent of rural people, the frame's own cuts, and the latest figure for 2023 or later sets the stage, so a fall is a fall. The figure counts rural people with any electricity, from the grid or off it, not how reliable or affordable it is. The series is the one Tracking SDG7 publishes, built from household surveys and modelled between them, so a country's own survey can give a different figure. The 80 per cent line is the Agenda 2063 figure for households, applied here to rural people, and 95 per cent is universal access.

AGO.short: Satellite broadband licensed and on sale by 2026, on two satellite networks.
AGO.summary:
Licensed, on sale, and from more than one network. Q-KON and SISTEC launched a Luanda Point of Presence for the Twoobii OneWeb LEO service, which SISTEC says it uses to deliver connectivity to enterprise and financial-sector clients in Angola. Mercury signed a multiyear agreement with Eutelsat to supply low-earth-orbit satellite connectivity in Angola to businesses, public institutions, telecom operators and offshore clients; the document gives no subscriber figures or consumer sale. Agence Ecofin reports Angola is among 16 countries where Starlink's availability map shows 'Starting in 2026', meaning coverage or regulatory authorisation pending. INACOM, the regulator, authorised the Luena-based startup NomaTech (Weza Tchisseque Tchamy) to install infrastructure and sell internet access over the ANGOSAT-2 satellite network to individuals, institutions and businesses. Together these place satellite broadband licensed, on sale and sold on two satellite networks, which answers the first three of the study's four questions. Prices and speeds are given where a source states them; they set no stage.

Subscribers counted by the regulator. Nothing found gives a regulator's count of the subscribers to the service. Only a count the regulator publishes, from the past three years, answers this question; counts given by an operator or an analyst do not.

Not found. No source found gives a subscriber count for satellite broadband published by the regulator in the last three years.

BDI.summary:
